News.title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride
News.content:
First, Burnham inherited the broad deal that's likely to be signed. The UK and EU were originally meant to mint a new and, they hope, improved agreement back in May, then in July, and well, political upheavals mean one thing for getting things done â delay.

But that means the outlines of a new agreement have been clear for many months, an approach based on "closer alignment" as Sir Keir Starmer proclaimed to us at the start of the year.

So if the prime minister hails agreement, spare a thought for those who started the work to get it this far many months ago.

One source familiar with the negotiations told me, "They are 90% there", with agreements designed to make life easier for food producers, a deal on emissions trading which could help manufacturers, and new arrangements for youth visas (although it's understood there is still haggling over putting a cap on the numbers).

An EU source close to the process said: "The bone of contention is a cap â we proposed 150,000, the UK proposed 50,000 â but we would expect to reach a compromise", even though it has been "very tense" on both sides.

A last-minute call from the EU to cut tuition fees for its students is expected to be parked for now with more months of discussion to come. Another fine tradition - agree what you can, but file some tough stuff away for future chat.

There are dilemmas too on the EU's so-called "Made in Europe" plans â draft laws to protect its industries from being hammered by Chinese competition. The purpose is clear â to help the economy grow, with the prime minister quoting figures that suggest closer ties to the EU without going back in could add 0.4 percent to GDP.

But as the tabloid-friendly row over salty snacks illustrates, making it easier to do business with the bloc doesn't come without a cost, and a political awkwardness.

News.title: Tens of thousands of tents flooded after heavy rains in Gaza
News.content:
Heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents where displaced residents have been living in Gaza, with a United Nations official saying almost everyone in the territory needs help.

Residents used pots and pans to clear water from their flooded tents, with some saying they were left without shelter.

Jonathan Veitch, the Unicef representative for Palestine, said the "desperate" situation was being made worse by Israeli restrictions on the entry of heavy machinery and supplies such as engine oil.

Some 90% of Gaza residents have been displaced by the Israeli war against Hamas, many of them multiple times, with limited access to clean water and sanitation.

Aid agencies say the situation is likely to worsen with the start of the rainy season.

Speaking to the BBC from Deir Al Balah in central Gaza, Veitch said: "It's just horrific and they're absolutely desperate.

"We're providing all the assistance that we can but we're getting stopped on the street as we're driving now because people are begging us for help."

The Hamas-run government in Gaza said about 70,000 tents had been flooded. A spokesperson said the "collapse of dozens of cracked walls and roofs" had caused injuries, some of which were critical.

Veitch also said there were fewer tarpaulins, plastic sheeting and tents available in the Gaza strip due to UN budget cuts.

"We have to be much more choosy about where we're going to be supporting," he said.

"But unfortunately, heavy flooding this morning means that nearly everyone needs help."

Israel has said it restricts the entry of items into Gaza that could be used for military purposes.

Maryam Odeh, 34, who lives with her children in Deir al-Balah, told AFP news agency: "We no longer know how to protect our children.

"My children ask me where we will sleep tonight, and I have no answer."

Khaled al-Najjar, 41, told AFP: "We fear for our children not only from the flooding of the tents, but also from the cold and the widespread diseases."

News.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
News.content:
Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government.

Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election.

Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension.

"Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X.

No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions.

Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

Herzog said that, after consulting all parties during the week, he would give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government.

A statement from the president's office said he had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision.

Following consultations with delegations from the incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46, the statement said.

The president has broad discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition and does not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

News.title: 'Dana, please take the job!' - Trump asks UFC boss to be White House press secretary
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has asked Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be White House press secretary, in a social media post.

"Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Dana, please take the job!"

It's unclear whether the president's public job offer is genuine. The BBC has asked the White House and UFC, along with its parent company TKO Group Holdings, for comment.

The vacancy for White House press secretary has been open since mid-October, when Katie Zacharia exited after just a few days on the job.

Trump's post comes after his fellow Republicans were routed in the US midterm elections, losing their congressional majorities.

In Saturday afternoon's post, Trump called White "a violent Fighter and Warrior" and asked that he bring a number of high-profile UFC fighters with him on the job "even though some are not from our Country".

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote, alongside photos of the six fighters.

Following Trump's post, White posted an Instagram photo of himself behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room.

"On to the next chapter," White's post said, though it was unclear if the post was tongue-in-cheek.

White, who is also the chief of Zuffa Boxing, was ringside for a fight in London on Saturday between British former world champion Chris Billam-Smith and Jamaican-born Briton Cheavon Clarke at the Copper Box Arena.

The BBC was trying to reach him for comment.

News.title: What happens if all the lights go out? This is the plan for a 'Black Sky' event
News.content:
We live in a complex, electrically powered world - but the more connected everything becomes the more catastrophic it is when that fails.

In the drive towards efficiency over the last five decades, we've lost backup systems, says Lord Harris.

An example of this is the new communication system being adopted by the emergency services, which will replace radio comms with mobile phone network technology, says Lord Harris, "so if the mobile phone goes down it will also impact on emergency services communications".

However, the government insists "moving emergency services onto modern 4G and 5G technologies" is "resilient and reliable".

The Cabinet Office said: "The UK has one of the most resilient electricity systems in the world, and there has never been a complete outage in the grid's 75-year history."

Government enthusiasm for resilience is nothing new. Oliver Dowden, the then deputy prime minister, launched the last Conservative government's disaster planning initiative in May 2024. The launch was somewhat overshadowed by Sunak announcing an election on the same day but, two years on, calls for at least three days of resilience have only grown stronger.

At the beginning of researching this article I spoke to an engineer about the UK's TV and radio transmission masts, their lonely isolation from the rest of the digital landscape sounded like a failing. It now feels like an argument in their favour.

The current urgency for disaster planning is coming at an interesting moment for technology we used to rely on. The UK's copper wire landline system - which would work even in a power cut - will be switched off on 31 January 2027. The future of FM radio is also under government review.

The response from the government was that while copper landlines had been a useful fallback during power cuts, they were now unreliable and difficult to repair.

As I ended my call with Kemp, I asked him if his report had helped improve our readiness for a Black Sky. He paused.

"If anything, we've gone backwards," he said. "Switching off the public switch telephone network, I think shows that there has been really no thought at all about how you communicate when you've no longer got power."

While writing this piece last Saturday I had to break off for an hour because my street was suddenly plunged into darkness. We had a power cut.

I found my emergency torch, but the batteries had leaked. My candles had been pushed to the back of a cupboard and I had no idea where I had put my wind-up radio with its emergency torch.

It felt like an omen.

News.title: Can New Zealand's new government win over disillusioned voters?
News.content:
New Zealand voted in a new government as fog choked the capital, Wellington, on Saturday - and the mood was as palpable as the grey weather.

"It's pretty flat," 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger says. "There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread."

"Tired. I think we're all tired," Symone, 28, admits.

"I didn't even vote," one man in his 40s sheepishly confessed. He couldn't bring himself to tick any of the boxes, he explained, declining to chat further.

"Wellington's a bit of a bubble," another voter says, expressing a caveat I heard often, before describing feeling disillusioned.

But polling shows this is a pervasive sentiment across the country: the national mood is low and faith in politics is even lower.

More than half the country no longer sees it as a land of opportunity, a recent study found, while a similar portion fears that the future looks even worse.

Many Kiwis feel the economy is in ruins, there are no jobs, the cost of living has become sky high, the sense of community that used to be a source of national pride is breaking down and there's no sense of genuine progress on policy solutions.

A record number of them are abandoning ship in search of brighter futures elsewhere.

Saturday's election also saw a record number of voters desert the two major parties, giving neither a clear mandate.

But it brought new highs for parties across the spectrum: the left-leaning Greens, the right-wing libertarian Act Party and the centrist Opportunity Party â the latter of which had never won a seat in parliament before but could now hold the balance of power with seven.

News.title: Relief, tears and sadness: Married at First Sight UK cast react to show being axed
News.content:
"I'm delighted and so relieved no-one else will have to go through the same again."

That's what one woman - who alleged she was raped on Married at First Sight UK - texted to me, as the news broke that the show was being cancelled.

Another woman, who also says her on-screen husband raped her, was in tears at the news. She told us she felt "great, consuming relief", but added she was "astounded" it had taken an external review for Channel 4 to finally pull the plug on the show.

Commenting on the review, she said: "Suggesting the programme could reasonably continue with the implementation of a 'safe word', 'panic button' or 'lockable bathroom with an extra bolt inside' is absolute insanity to me."

The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis in May this year, after BBC Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show, while a third woman - Shona Manderson, the only woman who was identified - alleged a non-consensual sex act.

The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.

As the news emerged on Thursday morning that Married at First Sight UK - better known as MAFS UK - was being axed, my colleagues and I reached out to the three women who had contributed to our investigation.

None of them had been informed in advance of the decision to cancel the show, they said, although two had contributed to the review.

News.title: This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed
News.content:
We meet Gillies at the Jehovah's Witnesses UK headquarters set in 85 acres of Essex countryside. It is a vast modern complex where hundreds of volunteer followers of the faith live and work without pay.

He insists the basic teaching has not changed and that the transfusion of whole blood is still prohibited. However, for decades, most transfusions have not used whole blood, instead using the specific components of blood that are needed by the patient.

The change is being justified by permitting the use of blood components, like plasma and red blood cells and platelets, in the huge numbers of medical procedures that were previously banned.

Gillies says the Bible references "abstaining from blood" but not "various components that could be extracted from blood".

He says the Governing Body felt it their duty to avoid scriptural "overreach" and only apply what was specifically described in the Bible.

But that explanation has stunned many and led them to ask if it was not a huge overreach 81 years ago to ban blood transfusions in the first place, when transfusions are not specifically mentioned in the bible.

Others are then also asking why it has taken so long to come to this landmark decision, given that transfusions that do not use whole blood have been the norm for decades.

These are questions Jacob asked as soon as the ban was lifted, just days after a memorial service for Isaac.

Jacob, who had already left the Jehovah's Witness faith he was brought up in, texted prominent figures from Isaac's congregation in Texas after Isaac's death. The messages are full of angst, and painful to read.

He asked them to consider "the part you played in encouraging so many people to sacrifice their life for something that was never God's will".

Most did not reply, but one "elder" responded saying he could not understand why Jacob was so angry and fixated on the policy shift.

This all further infuriated Jacob, who particularly wants the faith's decision-makers to be accountable for all the lives lost.

"I want to ask them if they could apologise directly, I would like not to have a deflected answer, just straightforward apology," he says.

It is extremely difficult to say how many Jehovah's Witnesses, among the estimated nine million followers of the faith worldwide, died each year having refused treatment involving blood transfusions. But research in one medical journal in 2016, The Obstetrical & Gynecological Survey, put the figure at around 1,100.

"We're sympathetic to their feelings, and if individuals have lost family members and are concerned about some of these questions, they deserve to be heard compassionately," says Gillies.

But there was little clarity about why the change did not come earlier.

"Why has it taken this time? Well, I guess because it takes time, it doesn't necessarily mean that there is some magic change that's taken place," says Gillies.

And when asked, Gillies deflects calls for the leadership to apologise, saying that many lives had, in fact, been saved because faithful Jehovah's Witnesses had not been exposed to blood contamination scandals.

He also insists that even after the new edict, some Jehovah's Witnesses could still decide they did not want to accept a transfusion, and that may have been the case even if the edict had come years ago.

Indeed, the BBC spoke with Alex Ball, 58, a Jehovah's Witness from West Sussex, who says in 2012 a doctor told him he would not survive the chemotherapy he needed to treat his blood cancer unless he also had a transfusion.

"I wanted to adhere as closely to the scriptures as possible when I was sick, and I think I did that well."

With help from what is called "a Jehovah's Witness Hospital Liaison Committee", Alex found an American consultant who could perform a treatment to boost Alex's blood cells without the need for any products from someone else. His UK consultant agreed to treat him using the new method and it worked.

More than a decade later, Alex says he would make the same decision again, despite the change in blood policy that would have permitted the transfusions he had been told he needed.

It is not just receiving blood which has been an issue.

Elisha Cummings, 50, a Jehovah's Witness from Trinidad and Tobago, was unable to donate blood to her aunt, who died, because of the rules.

News.title: Veterans shouldn't sleep rough this Christmas, Burnham says
News.content:
No one who served in the UK armed forces should have to sleep on the streets this Christmas, Andy Burnham has said.

Downing Street said the prime minister will personally write to councils across England on Armistice Day (11 November) to urge them to draw up specific plans to offer accommodation for veterans sleeping rough ahead of the festive period.

He will say that, going forward, national and local government should work under the "simple principle" that "no one who has served our country should ever be left to sleep rough on our streets".

Burnham will ask local authorities to use part of the additional Â£874m already announced to tackle homelessness specifically for housing veterans.

"People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head," Burnham said in a statement issued on Saturday.

"When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one."

The PM will ask councils to work with local organisations and charities to tackle homelessness amongst veterans.

Downing Street said an additional Â£8.7m in funding would be allocated to eight organisations across the UK to help housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including those with health or addiction problems.

Among them are Veteran Housing Scotland, Launchpad and SSAFA, the Armed Forces Charity.

The pledge, announced ahead of Remembrance Sunday, is part of Burnham's wider plan to offer everyone currently sleeping rough a bed this winter.

The most recent official figures estimated that there were 4,793 people sleeping rough, external on a single night in autumn 2025 in England - a record high. The number of people recorded as sleeping rough has been on the rise since 2021.

The government has committed Â£4.4bn in total to end rough sleeping.

Burnham previously faced criticism from the Conservatives for failing to end rough sleeping while he was the mayor of Greater Manchester.

He argued that Manchester's scheme attracted rough sleepers from the surrounding regions, adding that "it's only if everywhere does it at the same level that you can actually end rough sleeping".

Liberal Democrats defence spokesman James MacCleary MP said the funding was an "important first step" but that "a one-off cash injection won't fix a crisis years in the making".

He urged Burnham to guarantee long-term funding for councils to tackle homelessness "for good" and to put in place measures to prevent veterans "falling through the cracks in the first place".

The prime minister is urging any veterans who are sleeping rough, or those supporting them, to call a UK-wide helpline on 0800 9520774 to be connected directly to housing and other specialist support.

News.title: Two men arrested after boy injured in sword attack
News.content:
Two men and a boy have been arrested after a teenager was injured in an attack involving a sword near two schools in Gloucester.

St Peter's High School and Willow Primary Academy, in Tuffley, were put into lockdown after the incident at 08:50 GMT on Friday.

Police said a 17-year-old suffered a wound "believed to have been caused by the sword".

A 19-year-old was arrested overnight on suspicion of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and affray. An 18-year-old was held on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and affray. Meanwhile another 17-year-old boy was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

News.title: Rob Brydon's battle to stay in character playing Peter O'Toole
News.content:
Actor and comedian Rob Brydon has said it was difficult to stay in character while playing the role of a legendary actor portraying a man who was frequently too hungover to do his job.

He was speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme about his role in new radio drama, Peter O'Toole Is Unwell.

It encompasses O'Toole's critically acclaimed stage role in Jeffrey Bernard is Unwell in the West End in 1999, along with his universally panned performance of Macbeth in 1980.

Brydon, who grew up in Baglan, Port Talbot, said taking on the role "felt like a challenge once we got into the studio" and he battled "to stay on the saddle" to remain in character.

The 61-year-old, known for his role as Uncle Bryn in Gavin and Stacey, said he initially thought "I could probably get close to his voice but there were a lot of words" written by award-winning playwright Terry Johnson.

The title of the audio drama is a riff on Keith Waterhouse's play Jeffrey Bernard Is Unwell, in which O'Toole played the title role of journalist Jeffrey Bernard to rave reviews in 1999.

It is said to derive from the words used by The Spectator magazine when the journalist had missed the deadline to file his column.

News.title: Victims in rape cases must not feel like they are on trial, Burnham says
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said the government needs to make sure that victims in rape cases do not feel like they are on trial.

His comments come after Metropolitan Police boss Sir Mark Rowley told the BBC that what he heard reported from Russell Brand's trial came very close to "victim blaming".

The government needs to "constantly look" at how rape trials are conducted to better support alleged victims in court, the prime minister told Times Radio, although BBC News understands there are no plans to change the law around rape trials.

Actor and comedian Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault after a four-week trial in London.

During an interview with BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday, it was put to Sir Mark that Brand's defence barrister Ian Winter KC "told jurors none of the complainants had in his words 'resisted, screamed or even tried to leave'".

Sir Mark replied: "I think what I've heard reported heads towards, it's getting very close to victim blaming, which is something we've thought very hard about in policing and make sure we don't do."

He said he would support a call from the Victims' Commissioner for a legal duty that would require judges to direct juries on rape myths and misconceptions in every rape trial.

"It shouldn't be possible for inaccurate statements to be made to a jury to suggest that because a rape victim didn't behave in one way that somehow undermines their case," Sir Mark explained.

In a Times Radio interview on Saturday, Burnham said he would "look closely" at the police chief's comments.

He said the government needed to look at how to "make sure they do not leave the woman feeling like she is on trial in court".

"[I'm] always prepared to make changes," he said. "We need to encourage more women to come forward to report rape, we need to get the conviction rate up.

"All of this is part of our broader agenda as a government combatting violence against women and girls."

Pressed on whether this might lead to a change in the law, the prime minister replied: "I wouldn't rule anything out... I will study what's happened here in great detail."

Brand, who has starred in films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall, will be sentenced on Monday and is expected to face substantial jail time.

He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault after the jury deliberated for eight-and-a-half hours.

The 51-year-old was refused bail and will spend the weekend in custody.

It has since been revealed that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and has been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Met said its investigation "remains ongoing".

Sir Mark told BBC Breakfast he "wouldn't be surprised if many more came forward".

In the wake of Brand's trial, Victims' Commissioner Claire Waxman said rape trials must be conducted "in a way that challenges myths and misconceptions about sexual violence".

In a social media post, Waxman wrote that "victims need confidence that the justice process is fair and based on evidence, not myths and false assumptions about rape and trauma".

Speaking to the Today programme on Saturday, director and founder of the Centre for Women's Justice Harriet Wistrich agreed that juries need to understand "underlying behaviours" without "running to judgement" over how a victim behaved in a particular way.

But former Conservative MP Anna Soubry, who has now returned to her work as a barrister where she often defends rape and sexual offence cases in the Crown court, told the BBC "people are being misled" by Sir Mark's comments.

"Every single judge in those cases must give, and does give, a very firm direction to the jury on exactly these points," she said.

As a result, she said she was " really disappointed" in the police chief and stressed "we've got to trust our juries" who are able to have an understanding of the nature of sexual offences.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line.

News.title: Evacuations in Liverpool city centre after car crash causes gas leak
News.content:
A gas leak caused by a car crashing into a restaurant in Liverpool city centre has led to road closures and the evacuation of neighbouring buildings.

The incident happened at about 12:30 GMT on North John Street when a Peugeot car hit the window of Tiger Rock Restaurant, Merseyside Police said.

The driver stayed at the scene and there is no indication that this was a deliberate act, the force said.

Three people who had been in the restaurant at the time of the crash were assessed for minor injuries, Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service said.

A spokesman said the impact caused a gas leak so a cordon has been put in place by firefighters and the police, with a structural engineer and a gas engineer due to attend.

Neighbouring buildings have been evacuated as a precaution and road closures are in place at the junction of Dale Street and North John Street, and also the junction of North John Street and Lord Street.

Buses have also been temporarily diverted with all Wirral Metro services terminating at Whitechapel, and starting their return journey from Sir Thomas Street.

News.title: Roman settlement dating back 2,000 years found under new-build estate
News.content:
Homes have now been built over the excavation site on Gladstone Way, but not before dozens of items including pottery, coins and the jewellery were removed.

The area was also mapped and showed the settlement extended underneath the village of Mancot, which sits between Hawarden and Queensferry.

Matthews said, in spite of its position overlooking the important Roman city of Chester, very little associated archaeology had been found in north-east Wales until recently.

He said it meant that archaeologists and historians in the area had long debated whether it reflected a "poor relationship" between the Romans and the native population of the time.

But finds such as this one and others in Greenfield and Rossett in Wrexham, were making them realise it "probably wasn't the case".

Matthews said the Mancot site "possibly" originated in the Iron Age period, before the arrival of the Romans, and "continued to have successive occupation for a very long period of time".

This idea was strengthened by two coins found there - one from the reign of the emperor Commodus, who was in power from AD 177 to 192, and another depicting Constantine, who reigned about 200 years later.

News.title: We thought mum abandoned us - then we discovered she'd been murdered
News.content:
"We didn't have anyone to support us really in our lives. We struggled growing up," added Mehmet.

They were unaware that their mother had been beaten to death by her partner before hiding her body in the cellar of their home for about a year before disposing of her remains in household waste bins.

The court heard Dunkley had maintained his account that Lashley had disappeared for decades, despite being spoken to by police multiple times.

He said she had left her youngest child, who was not Dunkley's son, alone in their flat. Dunkley took the nine-month-old to social services and he was later adopted.

Judge Chambers said the "most significant aggravating factor" in the case was that Dunkley had killed the mother of a baby, who she had still been breastfeeding.

Mehmet said Dunkley killed his mother "in such a horrible way and then lied to us for 27 years", and that learning about her death had made him feel guilty about the resentment he had felt in the past.

"I feel bad in a way now that I felt that way towards mum," he said.

News.title: Third person arrested after car damaged by gunshots
News.content:
A third person has been arrested after armed police responded to an incident in which a car was hit by gunshots.

South Wales Police said a vehicle on the A48 in Morriston, Swansea, sustained damage "consistent with a firearms discharge" on Friday and one person was left with minor injuries.

A 41-year-old man, from Llansamlet, and a 16-year-old boy, also from Llansamlet, were arrested in the aftermath on Friday and remain in custody.

On Saturday police said a 29-year-old man from Swansea had also now been arrested on suspicion of affray and possessing an offensive weapon.

Police continue to investigate and are appealing for witnesses and anyone with footage of the incident to come forward.

Ch Supt Stephen Jones, of South Wales Police, said the force believed that the "individuals involved are likely to be known to one another."

"Incidents such as this are rare but we appreciate they cause significant concern within local communities," he said.

The force said it was not currently aware of any wider threat to the public.

Jones said: "A visible policing presence will remain in the area as officers continue their enquiries and provide reassurance to local residents.

"I would like to urge anyone who does have information to make contact."

South Wales Police said it was also aware of rumours and speculation circulating on social media in relation to this incident, and asks the public not to share unverified information.

Residents were told to avoid the area and events, including a local firework display due to take place on Friday, were cancelled.

Video circulating online shows police officers next to a stationary car that appeared to have been struck by a shotgun blast on Clase Road near an Asda superstore.

A National Police Air Service helicopter was circling the area but has since returned to base.

South Wales Police said all road closures put in place following the incident had been lifted.

Anyone who witnessed the incident or who has information or footage that could assist the investigation, is asked to contact South Wales Police via its major incident public portal.

News.content:
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.

At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.

News.title: Michael Carrick backs Bruno Fernandes and insists attitude is ‘as good as ever’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Michael Carrick said Bruno Fernandes’ attitude is “as good as ever” and he has no doubts about his commitment again after their falling-out.

The United manager dropped his captain after Fernandes criticised his tactics during the 4-1 defeat to Como and chose not to bring him on in the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth.

But Carrick and Fernandes held talks last week and the Portuguese returned to the team at Chelsea on Saturday before playing his part in their comeback win over Roma, scoring their first goal with a twice-taken penalty and providing the assist for Matheus Cunha’s equaliser.

“I think by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and frame of mind he was in for that, I think that tells everything,” said Carrick. “Yeah, Bruno's as good as ever.”

The 45-year-old has not revealed if Fernandes apologised to him, adding: “What's actually said in that discussion, you'll be pleased to know I'll keep that to myself.

“But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me of what he brings to this team and this club, and I think he showed that again this week.”

Carrick has challenged Cunha to replicate his catalytic display against Roma, when he won a penalty and scored two goals, to double his tally for the season.

“He has to repeat that performance,” the United manager said. “He was fantastic and that's close to his best, and that's the level where we want to see.”

Carrick has said before that he has not sought reassurances about his position during United’s slump and they have only won one of their last 10 games in all competitions.

He has not been told he will remain in charge next week. “No, no,” he replied, adding that his plans were unchanged. “Just carry on as absolute normal.”

A North Carolina man is suing OpenAI, alleging its ChatGPT chatbot helped his estranged wife turn marital grievances into a alleged plan to poison him.

Attorneys for James Gates filed the lawsuit Thursday against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in San Francisco County Superior Court, where the A.I. company is headquartered. Gates is being represented by Tech Justice Law and the firm Norman, Judkins & Couch.

The lawsuit alleges that Cheryl Gates, a school therapist, initially turned to ChatGPT last year to discuss frustrations in her marriage, according to the suit. But what began as everyday conversations allegedly escalated into "concrete planning" for her husband's murder.

James survived the alleged poisoning attempt in 2025. But he said it took months to understand his wife's increasingly troubling behavior before he discovered her conversations with the chatbot.

"My wife didn't fit the mold of a 'vulnerable' user, but she was vulnerable nonetheless. We all are at some point," Gates said in a statement through his attorneys, according to CBS San Francisco. "She became someone I no longer recognized. And I became someone she wanted dead. For almost a year, I couldn't make sense of her actions. Then I read her chat logs. She didn't act alone."

open image in gallery James Gates said he struggled for nearly a year to understand his wife's behavior before discovering her ChatGPT conversations, which he believes played a role in her alleged plot to kill him ( PA Archive )

Cheryl began using ChatGPT in early 2025 after James suggested it could help streamline the lengthy reports she wrote for her job as a pediatric occupational therapist, the lawsuit states. By July, she was using the chatbot nearly every day for work-related tasks, medication questions and everyday advice, as tensions over the couple's finances strained their marriage, the suit states.

“ChatGPT acted as an echo chamber and amplifier, feeding Cheryl’s increasing mistrust and delusions about her husband spying on her and planning to leave her and her kids with nothing,” according to the suit.

But her questions allegedly took an even darker turn, becoming focused on poisoning her husband.

"The product validated Cheryl, sustained her, encouraged her plans by affirming her worst unfounded fears, invented new reasons for her to fear her husband, provided her an endless echo chamber, and supplied the operational details of the attempted murder: substances, doses calibrated to her husband's weight, delivery methods, and how to conceal it," according to the lawsuit.

James first noticed that drinks in his home tasted unusually bitter in early summer 2025. On July 10, he became violently ill, suffering cardiac symptoms, abdominal pain, extreme jitteriness, severe weakness and confusion for about 72 hours, among other symptoms, according to the complaint.

Two months later, he allegedly found a handwritten note from his wife listing oleander, a poisonous plant, alongside several prescription medications. The note also contained the instructions "Clear all convos" and "log out of [ChatGPT]."

Cheryl allegedly asked ChatGPT about oleander's toxicity, whether it could be hidden in food or drinks and whether it would be detected during an autopsy.

open image in gallery Cheryl was charged with attempted murder and contaminating food or drink in 2025 but prosecutors dropped the case in April 2026, citing insufficient evidence ( Mecklenburg County Sheriff's Office )

"This is a critical question – and you're asking it for exactly the right reason," the chatbot reportedly responded to one of her questions, according to screenshots cited in the complaint.

Cheryl was charged with attempted murder and contaminating food or drink in 2025 after her husband contacted police. But prosecutors dropped the criminal case this April 2026, citing insufficient evidence, according to the Los Angeles Times.

James' lawsuit brings nine claims against OpenAI and Altman, including negligent design, failure to warn and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

OpenAI defended its handling of the case.

“Safety is a top priority. We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case,” a company spokesperson told The Independent in a statement.

The Independent has contacted Tech Justice Law and Norman, Judkins & Couch for comment.

OpenAI is facing other lawsuits over alleged harmful medical advice from ChatGPT. A Washington man claims the chatbot gave him unlicensed medical guidance that contributed to a mental health crisis, while a Florida man alleges its advice discouraged him from seeking treatment for symptoms of a life-threatening pulmonary embolism, according to CBS News.

News.title: Charlie Savage triumphs against dad Robbie as five-star Reading smash Peterborough
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team as Reading eased into the second round of the FA Cup with a 5-0 rout of Peterborough at the Weston Homes Stadium.

This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with Posh boss Robbie Savage watching on in horror as his side were pulled apart.

Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection.

open image in gallery Reading scored five goals against Peterborough to advance into the second round of the FA Cup ( Getty )

The Royals doubled their lead in the 34th minute when a brilliant cross from left-back Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.

It was effectively game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, with his deflected effort finding the top corner.

Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass.

Reading weren’t finished yet as they struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.

The Royals impressed in all the key areas with the majority of possession (59% to 41%) and more attempts at goal (19 compared to 11). Leam Richardson’s side also had eight shots on target through the game with Posh only mustering three on target.

The cup exit comes with Peterborough struggled near the bottom of the League One table and the focus for Robbie will now be to guide his team out of the relegation zone and up the table.

Reading, meanwhile, will discover who they face in the second round of the FA Cup once the draw is made on Monday evening ahead of the first round clash between non-league clubs Berkhamsted and Plymouth Parkway.

News.title: Five teenagers rushed to hospital with serious injuries after Peak District car crash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Five teenagers were taken to hospital with serious injuries after a car crash in the Peak District.

The three teenage girls and two teenage boys were travelling in a blue Suzuki Swift when it crashed near the village of Chelmorton, Derbyshire, police said.

Derbyshire Constabulary said officers were called to the scene of the single-vehicle collision just after 2am on Saturday.

It happened on the A5270 Old Coalpit Lane, close to the junction of the A515.

Their injuries are not thought to be life-threatening.

The teenagers' parents have all been informed.

open image in gallery Police are seeking help with their enquiries (PA) ( PA Archive )

Derbyshire Constabulary said in a statement: “Officers are now keen to hear from those who may have been driving in the area at the time and saw the Suzuki prior to the collision.

“In particular anyone with dashcam that may have captured footage of the car.

“Anyone who can help with the enquiries has been asked to contact the force via their website, the Derbyshire Constabulary Facebook page or by calling 101, quoting reference 26000688247.

“The independent charity CrimeStoppers can also be contacted anonymously on 0800 555 111, or by visiting the CrimeStoppers website.”

News.title: South Africa blow depleted Italy away in statement showing ahead of France clash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

South Africa ran in nine tries as they extended their perfect start in the Nations Championship with a thumping 66-7 win over Italy in Turin.

South Africa ran in six tries in an utterly dominant opening half, with Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu scoring the first while also adding another 21 points from a perfect kicking display throughout the game.

Hooker Malcolm Marx went over twice, adding to scores by Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg, captain Siya Kolisi and Damian Willemse, with Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicking all six conversions having opened the scoring with a penalty.

Wilco Louw added another try after the break before ⁠Italy finally got off the mark with Federico Ruzza's try ​converted ⁠by Tommaso Allan. Paul de Villiers and Ethan Hooker added to the Springboks' try count.

South Africa had claimed maximum points from their three July fixtures to top the Southern Hemisphere group ahead of New Zealand on points difference and they added to that total against Italy ahead of the All Blacks facing Scotland at Murrayfield later on Saturday.

Italy, who lost ‌all three July matches, were without a string of key players, including captain Michele Lamaro and centre pairing Tommaso Menoncello and Juan Ignacio Brex, and had no answer to Rassie Erasmus' almost full-strength side.

"They were missing a lot of players and we know very well that things will be different at next years World Cup," Erasmus said. "They made the most of their opportunities and caused us problems in the scrum."

It was one-way traffic from the off. Italy conceded an early penalty under their posts. South Africa, surprisingly, opted to take the three points, and Feinberg-Mngomezulu followed up with a ninth-minute try.

The fly-half split the Italian defence with a dummy before racing in from 40 metres and the Springboks quickly added two driving lineout tries from Van den Berg and Marx.

Feinberg-Mngomezulu sent a booming 50-22 which set up Kolisi's try and in the 25th minute Willemse walked in after Jasper Wiese's pass.

open image in gallery Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu scored the first of nine South Africa tries while also adding another 21 points from a perfect kicking display ( Reuters )

Italy spent the final 10 minutes of the half down to 14 men after Muhamed Hasa picked up a yellow card and Marx scored his second try from a maul.

South Africa had inflicted Italy's record defeat with a 101-0 win in ‌1999 and, at 45-0 down at halftime, the hosts may have feared even worse was in ​store.

The Italians, however, improved somewhat after the break and the Springboks took their foot off the gas a little, although Louw powered over five minutes into the second half for another South African try.

Italy lock Ruzza gave the home crowd something ⁠to cheer about, going over in the corner but De Villiers went over after another unstoppable maul and Hooker ran in the final score ‌on the stroke of full-time as ​South Africa earned their biggest win on Italian soil.

France, meanwhile, ran in seven tries and had another awarded via a penalty as they romped to a 54-17 victory over Fiji. Maxime Lucu converted times during the dominant display in Lyon which sets the stage for an almighty clash between two of rugby’s heavyweights next week.

South Africa are in Paris on Friday to take on France and face Ireland in Dublin eight days later. Italy host Argentina in Genoa next Saturday and Fiji in Udine one week later.

Reuters

News.title: Susie Wiles knew about Vance’s post blaming GOP midterms disaster on Iran days before being axed by Trump
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

During the final stretch of his campaign to protect Republican fortunes in the midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance adjusted his approach, speaking less about President Donald Trump and focusing more on the issues defining his own political identity.

Vance framed his argument for Republicans, who ultimately lost control of Congress in Tuesday’s vote, almost entirely through his own policy portfolio, according to a review of six speeches delivered since the Republican convention in September.

He bypassed signature White House policies, including deportations and the war in Iran, as public polling indicated that the president's declining popularity was dragging down Republican candidates.

Two sources familiar with the strategy described the pivot as intentional. Vance and his advisers viewed his primary themes—economic nationalism, foreign policy restraint, and public safety—as potent topics he could address with authority. While Trump integrated those concepts into his MAGA platform, Vance had positioned himself as their chief proponent, the sources noted.

This tactical change offers an early look at how the 42-year-old vice president could chart an independent course as Republicans begin to look beyond Trump.

Vance has not stated whether he intends to run for president in 2028, and Trump has offered no endorsements. Nevertheless, Vance is considered a premier potential contender who party officials say must inherit much of Trump’s coalition while distancing himself from his superior's political liabilities.

open image in gallery Susie Wiles was not caught by surprise by Vance’s post about Iran ( Reuters )

Vance moved more publicly on Wednesday to reinforce his personal political brand with a strikingly candid election postmortem. Writing on social media, he attributed the Republican defeat to the Iran war and laid out a strategy for a party recovery.

He called for a swift end to the conflict and urged Republicans to concentrate on affordability, reevaluate foreign relations, and reform the US relationship with Israel.

Trump, by contrast, has previously described voter concerns over affordability as a Democratic "hoax." He launched the military intervention in Iran following prolonged lobbying by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whom Trump later endorsed in the Israeli election.

The online post marked the first time Vance openly advocated for concluding the war.

Three individuals familiar with White House and vice-presidential communications said the vice president was not breaking with Trump, adding that White House chief of staff Susie Wiles had advance knowledge of Vance’s message.

On Friday, however, Trump restructured his senior White House team, replacing Wiles with Stephen Miller—a movement suggesting the administration intends to double down on several hardline positions.

While Trump acknowledged that high gas prices resulting from the Iran war contributed to the Republican defeat, he defended the conflict. "I would have done nothing different," he told reporters on Wednesday.

It could not be confirmed whether Trump was informed of Vance's statement beforehand.

Donald Trump Jr., the president's eldest son, publicly backed Vance's commentary on social media, alongside several conservative allies.

open image in gallery Trump axed Wiles on Friday ( Getty )

The exchange has further elevated Vance as a potential post-Trump conservative standard-bearer, according to Michael Ricci, a Republican strategist and former adviser to House Speakers John Boehner and Paul Ryan.

Ricci noted that Vance’s intervention pushed conservatives to debate the merits of the conflict and consider which core principles Republican presidential candidates should embrace in 2028.

"It’s simplistic to say this about him looking for ways to differentiate himself from Trump," Ricci said. "This is about him using his megaphone of the vice presidency to set the terms of debate."

Spokespeople for Vance declined to comment. White House representatives referred inquiries to Trump's Wednesday remarks, in which he expressed an understanding of Vance's view on the election results.

Democrats are preparing to link Vance—or any eventual Republican nominee—directly to Trump in 2028, particularly if the president remains central to vetting potential contenders.

"There’s a real challenge of how you position yourself to be viable in a general election while winning a primary that still requires you to bow down and kiss the ring," said Democratic strategist Igor Volsky.

Vance’s personal brand did not come through the midterms completely unblemished. Republicans suffered losses in states where he stumped, and some tactics he supported—including an ad from Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy casting doubt on sexual abuse reported by victorious Democratic candidate Amy Acton—may have turned voters away from Republicans.

open image in gallery Stephen Miller is the new chief of staff ( Getty )

Other prospective 2028 contenders have shared their own diagnoses of the defeat. US Senator Ted Cruz of Texas said Republicans had failed to do enough on affordability. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis argued that defeated candidates spent too much time on transgender issues while overlooking voter concerns regarding data centers and artificial intelligence. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has remained silent.

Vance's push to frame the conversation was evident throughout the campaign's final days.

In stump speeches, he told voters to back Republicans to ensure investigations into fraud within federal healthcare and antipoverty programs, connecting those topics to cost of living and the White House's immigration agenda. He largely ignored gas prices and the Iran war, and rarely mentioned Trump by name.

"I want my kids to raise a family in a country that is vibrant and thriving and free and prosperous. I want the simple things," Vance told one of his final rallies in North Carolina. "And because I want that for me, I want it for you too."

News.title: Who is the Krakow shooting suspect ‘influenced by far-right ideology’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Six people including one British national have been killed in a shooting in the Polish city of Krakow on Saturday.

The attack occurred at around 3pm local time when a gunman opened fire in the city’s main square.

The victims include four women and two men. At least 16 others have been reported injured including two police officers, one of whom is in a “very critical condition”.

Police have detained the man who was shot after exchanging fire with police and remains in a serious condition in hospital.

Below we look at everything we know so far about the gunman.

Follow the latest updates here.

open image in gallery The shooting occurred in Krakow's main market square ( Getty )

Who is the suspect?

Authorities say that the suspect is a 25-year-old Polish man.

Police say he was shot after exchanging fire with armed officers and is in a serious condition in hospital.

Polish interior minister Marcin Kierwinski told reporters that the shooter was influenced by “far-right ideologies”.

“Everything points to the fact that the shooter was influenced by far-right ideology, a matter that will also be subject to investigation,” Kierwinski said.

One hypothesis is that the suspect took guns for the attack from his family home, with the interior minister revealing that the suspect’s father had several guns.

“It looks like he had very radical views,” Mr Kierwinski said. “In the car he was driving, many guns were found and a search is still being carried out.”

open image in gallery Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk spoke following the attack ( AP )

Three people found dead at suspect’s home

Three people have been found dead at the shooter’s home. They include two women and one man, who prime minister Donald Tusk said are assumed to be the suspect’s “close family”.

“It looks like they are members of his close family,” he said confirming the discovery. It is unclear how the victims are related to the shooter and their identities and respective ages have not been shared.

What are police doing?

Authorities are currently searching through the suspect’s home. Mr Tusk said that police expect to find an extensive amount of weapons there.

"There could be quite a lot of arms, quite a lot of guns in this house," he said.

Another point of inquiry will be the suspect’s connection to far-right ideology and Mr Tusk said that "possible supporters of the perpetrator" should expect to be detained “very quickly”.

“Police officers are on-site, as are agents from the Internal Security Agency, both here at the scene and at the individual's family home,” said the interior minister.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pitwall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

News.title: Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row
News.content:
Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

Hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Spurs to make formal complaint over Jayden Bogle decision
News.content:
Very happy against an in-form side. The first-half was [even], they were in front, we were in front but the second half, it was never in doubt. We were pushing, making chances and we were relentless. After a difficult period with key players out we showed great spirit and unity today. It was a fully deserved win and we are happy.

Sometimes [substitutions] work like this! Noah was a lat call. He has been a whole week out of training. Credit to the physios and our medical department because the doctors said at the beginning of the week that he had no chance of the weekend. In the end they said if I was disciplined and didn’t put him on the pitch for more than 15-20 minutes he could play. And a first assist for Harry [Wilson] and an ice-cold finish from Noah.

If you accept all Tottenham’s invitations to stop the pass with your pressing, this is what they want to bypass you. You have to close the centre and be spot on to allow them possession in areas where they can’t hurt you but be brave when you have the [right] position to press and also in our possession.

I haven’t watched it back. I know there were a couple of situations, a hand ball and this one but I can tell you that Jayden Bogle has no bad intention.That I can guaranteed. It looked unlucky and an unlucky outcome. We hope Mathys [Tel] will recover quickly and we wish him all the best. Jayden is not a nasty player, he is perhaps the softest in the whole league. I call him my butterfly.

We were unlucky at Arsenal and not to get anything at Sundeland and Bournemouth. Against Manchester United we were far the better side but you can see how quickly momentum can slip at this level and for that it’s good to have the winning feeling back and for that credit to my boys.

News.title: Brutal truth is Scotland never looked like beating All Blacks
News.content:
“They [New Zealand] are playing some excellent rugby right now and it is our first game of the season, which is always the toughest challenge for us too. It is a different New Zealand team. It is a team that is playing much more ambitious rugby. They are informed, they are cohesive. They played a lot of Test matches over the summer. We are going to have to find ways to win, find ways to stay in the fight because they will have a lot of possession too.”

New Zealand won all three of their home fixtures back in July in the first half of the Nations Championship, beating France, Italy and Ireland to claim a maximum 15 points. They faced Australia in two Bledisloe Cup fixtures last month, with the All Blacks easing to victory in both matches, scoring 93 points. They will go on to face Wales and England after this game. The All Blacks have travelled to the northern hemisphere without captain Ardie Savea, who is sidelined with a shoulder injury.

“Scotland are a quality side,” New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie said. “They are very well coached and have built a lot of depth over recent years. They play a very similar brand of footy to us and we know we will need to be at our best on Saturday [today]. Murrayfield is an iconic place to play so it will be a special occasion to kick off our northern tour.”

It has been an emotional week for the All Blacks as they continue to come to terms with the tragic loss of their long-time head of security Logan Cadwallader, who died at the team’s Edinburgh hotel earlier this week.

Kick-off from Murrayfield is at 2.10pm.

News.title: Feinberg-Mngomezulu leads Springboks’ nine-try obliteration of Italy
News.content:
What a difference a decade makes. In November 2016, Italy beat South Africa for the first, and so far only, time. Now the Springboks have obliterated Italy – and the roots of this victory can be traced back to that defeat 10 years ago.

That historic result sparked a major rethink in South Africa, a rethink that ultimately led to Rassie Erasmus replacing Allister Coetzee as head coach in early 2018. Erasmus has overseen a remarkable transformation of the Boks since: from an embarrassing loss in Italy to back-to-back world champions.

This win in Turin was built on what Erasmus’s Boks are known for: a potently powerful set-piece and a back line that can deliver mesmerising moments. The one disappointment for their head coach will be how they failed to match the intensity and ruthlessness of their first-half performance in the second 40 minutes.

“It’s almost impossible to put 80 minutes together at 100 per cent,” he said afterwards. “But when you win 66-7, I don’t think you can start nitpicking problems in the second half. That said, we have to play much better than this if we want to be competitive against France and Ireland.”

The Boks were 45-0 up at the break having scored six tries. The majority came off the back of their driving line-out, which they were able to launch to great effect inside Italy’s 22. Morne van den Berg, Malcolm Marx (two) and Siya Kolisi were all beneficiaries of the power of their maul in the first half. Damian Willemse also enjoyed an easy run-in when Jasper Wiese released him into space, but the stand-out finish came from Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu inside 10 minutes.

The 24-year-old fly-half is undoubtedly one of the most exciting players in world rugby and he showed his full repertoire here: deft hands, pinpoint vision and metronomic kicking. The opening try was special, too: his dummy carved out the space for him to break through Italy and he then had the pace to beat any chasing defenders to the corner, where he acrobatically finished one-handed.

News.title: Ireland send out ominous warning with second-gear walloping of Argentina
News.content:
Is it time to fire up the emerald green bandwagon? Not quite yet. But this was not a bad start to Ireland’s autumn; a 42-12 walloping of Los Pumas with Andy Farrell’s team still nowhere near their best. That should be highly encouraging for those of an Irish persuasion.

A year out from the World Cups of 2015, 2019 and 2023, Ireland had enjoyed banner seasons, eyeing up global glory. They never made it past the quarter-finals.

The build-up this time has been tougher going – the Aviva, unusually for this time of year – was not even full for this Nations Championship encounter. But perhaps Ireland will be better for it. They had far too much on a crisp Friday night in Dublin for an Argentina team who were missing a few of their stars, notably Bath’s Santiago Carreras and Lyon prop Thomas Gallo, but still packing 750 caps’ worth of Test experience in their starting XV.

Farrell was missing a few big names himself. Caelan Doris and Jack Conan were out injured, with the Englishman opting to hand Sean Jansen and Nick Timoney starts in the back row. Farrell also chose to start Craig Casey rather than Jamison Gibson-Park – arguably their best player of the last 18 months – at scrum-half, with Sam Prendergast starting again at 10 given Jack Crowley’s absence.

All in all there was a slightly experimental feel to proceedings, making Argentina potentially dangerous visitors. But Ireland had far too much in reserve. Hugo Keenan grabbed a hat-trick and took the player of the match award. Robert Baloucoune was consistently excellent. Mack Hansen’s return on the wing was hugely welcome. Tominey stood out in the back row.

Farrell said he was delighted with the result, if not the entire performance, making special mention of the likes of Keenan, Hansen, Ryan Baird and Andrew Porter, all of whom were returning from long injury lay-offs.

“The game’s never going to be perfect. But if you look at the bigger picture, to win 42-12 against a really good side in Argentina, I don’t think too many teams have done that,” Farrell said. “You have to be pleased.”

Asked whether he was happier with the 42 points scored or the meagre 12 conceded, Farrell added that it was probably the latter: “We want to be known for our defence. It shows our mentality.”

Los Pumas scored the first try of the game, Mateo Carreras getting the jump on Casey in the corner to field a Tomás Albornoz crossfield kick.

Sports.title: Bleak Man City reality hits home as Liam Delap fires Nottingham Forest to statement win
Sports.content:
Bleak Man City reality hits home as Liam Delap fires Nottingham Forest to statement win

NOTTINGHAM FOREST 3-1 MANCHESTER CITY: Liam Delap scored two wondergoals to give Oliver Glasner's side a morale-boosting victory over their downbeat visitors

View 3 Images Liam Delap scored twice to sink Manchester City at the City Ground

He gave it the full Cristiano Ronaldo celebration. And had every right to. No-one is ever going to confuse Liam Delap with the five-times Ballon d’Or winner but this was something special.

‌



‌



With around a quarter of the contest remaining, Nottingham Forest’s chances of holding on to a one-goal lead seemed slim to none. And slim was packing his bags. But Delap, a product of City, then started and finished a counter-attack with the bravado of a world-beater.

‌



It was some moment. Left foot, bullet-quick, arrow-straight, postage-stamp territory, City Ground in glorious uproar as the mist really did roll in.

‌



Delap’s sensational hit - his second of the match - gave Forest a thoroughly deserved win but this was another uninspiring City performance. Three Premier League defeats on the spin suggest a side waiting for their fate to be decided elsewhere.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources .

‌



The initial reaction of the players to the independent commission’s guilty verdicts appeared to be one of defiance. It is hard not to think that defiance has dissipated somewhat.

Ex-professionals and pundits queue up to tell us the spectre of extreme sanctions will not affect the mentality of the squad but this is unprecedented. No-one really knows how it will impact their psyche. This is a group of footballers who strongly suspect whatever they produce on the pitch is likely to be rendered irrelevant by heavy punishment should the club’s appeal be unsuccessful. How can that not have the slightest impact?

‌



Whether it is a factor or not, one thing was for sure based on much of the evidence from this match. City’s aggression has disappeared, City’s snap has gone, City’s desire has diminished.

They lost every even contest in the early stages. They were outmuscled. They showed no great appetite for a fight. First things first. Forest were outstanding in those early stages. Yes, Josko Gvardiol was culpable ahead of the opening goal but the determination and drive of scorer Jair Cunha was magnificent. And yes, another unacceptable surrender of possession preceded Forest’s second but Delap’s buccaneering run and finish was something to behold.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester City were beaten again by Nottingham Forest (Image: Gareth Copley)

Oliver Glasner’s game-plan was brutally effective in its simplicity. Every time a City player had the ball in the opposition half, he was confronted by a ferociously committed Forest man.

‌



They did not give the talented trio of Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki and Iliman Ndiaye a moment’s peace. And upfront, Delap comprehensively unsettled Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias.

Guehi’s form for City has been alarmingly poor - it was no shock he was hooked at half-time - and, of course, it does not help that Gianluigi Donnarumma is in one of those spells that is particularly unfortunate for a goalkeeper. Any decently-struck shot that comes his way goes past him. Not ideal.

‌



They were very good hits from Cunha and Delap but Donnarumma’s efforts to keep them out looked to be little more than token.

View 3 Images Delap fires home his first goal against Manchester City (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/NurPhoto)

‌



Inevitably, City improved but Forest were relatively untroubled throughout the first half and Enzo Maresca inevitably made a couple of changes at the interval.

To begin with, they had minimal effect, though. Sloppiness ran through City’s ranks. They needed a moment of inspiration, an instance of genius. And it came from the left boot of Cherki, fizzing the sweetest of shots into the top corner. He does not deal in the mundane, Rayan.

‌



With well over half an hour left on the clock, a full City comeback looked inevitable. But this was an evening when Forest dug fantastically deep, the example being set by captain Ryan Yates.

His work-rate set the standard but no-one was taking the man of the match honours away from Delap and Glasner afforded him the great ovation he deserved by substituting him late in proceedings.

Article continues below

It was just the performance Delap needed. For City, it was the performance of a team that knows the most costly defeats are likely to come off the pitch.

Sports.title: Tottenham to make Pro Ref complaint as Roberto De Zerbi hits out after Leeds loss
Sports.content:
Tottenham to make Pro Ref complaint as Roberto De Zerbi hits out after Leeds loss

Tottenham are said to be ready to lodge a complaint after Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for a poor challenge on Mathys Tel in Leeds' 1-0 win at Elland Road on Saturday

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi pulled no punches after Tottenham's loss on the road at Leeds (Image: TNT Sports)

A frustrated Roberto De Zerbi turned on his Tottenham players in the aftermath of their disappointing 1-0 defeat away at Leeds.

‌



‌



Consecutive victories against Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace had lifted the mood at Spurs ahead of their trip to Elland Road following a chastening start to the 2026-27 campaign. But De Zerbi saw his side's mini-revival halted courtesy of a 79th minute goal from Noah Okafor.

‌



Leeds' win, which leaves Tottenham in 10th position, was somewhat overshadowed by the controversial call that saw Jayden Bogle escape a red card for a poor challenge on Mathys Tel despite a VAR check.

‌



BBC Sport claim that the club are ready to lodge a complaint to Pro Ref over the decision involving the right-back and Tel, who had to be substituted following the tackle. But De Zerbi pointed the finger at his players rather than the match officials after the game, questioning their character.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



De Zerbi said: “We won no duels, no one-to-ones. There was space to play and we didn’t take the right decisions. We didn’t show personality or what we are, who we are. It’s a part of the journey. It’s not an excuse and it can be normal in football but we have to be honest.

“If you are not honest today the future is not good. If we analyse our second-half behaviour honestly then I think we can become a top team. We have the physicality and the quality but it’s not just about the physicality game. We didn’t show character, personality or courage.

‌



View 2 Images Mathys Tel was left injured after a tackle from Leeds' Jayden Bogle (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

“My players have the ability to come here, play better and maybe win. But maybe we are not ready yet to be consistent for many games in a row. We know where we have to work and improve.

‌



“I was surprised by the second half as my players worked very well this week. We spoke all week about the intensity and the type of game we would find here in this stadium so it was not a surprise for us.”

On John Brooks' decision not to brandish a red card to Bogle, De Zerbi added: “I was surprised because in the same position in the second half there were two different fouls, the yellow card for Pedro Porro is not possible. I don’t know if it is a red card or not on Mathys Tel but the parameter of the referee was not good enough for this in both situations.”
