Sports.title: Martin Odegaard spares Arsenal's blushes as champions narrowly avoid Hull City slip-up
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard was the Arsenal hero as Mikel Arteta's men found a way to grind out another victory against a game Hull City side.

Heavily fancied to further their advantage at the Premier League summit at home to last season's Championship play-off winners, Arsenal rather stumbled out of the blocks. They even had to endure some hairy moments at the back early on, including one from a corner after David Raya lost flight of the ball in the air.

The Spaniard had to be alert to ensure Arsenal's imperious defence wasn't breached by the buoyant visitors before the champions wrestled control of the game away as the half wore on, thwarting Elliot Stroud from inside the box with a fine stop.

Though Arsenal belatedly came to life late in the half, the expected breakthrough failed to arrive until the 72nd minute when Odegaard vanquished the growing Emirates nerves.

‌



Odegaard was alive and on the spot to react after Konstantinos Tzolakis repelled a Noni Madueke effort away from goal, thumping the loose ball into the net to tame the Tigers.

There were chances to add gloss to the scoreline in the closing minutes through Noni Madueke. But Odegaard's strike was the clincher.

‌



REF'S FIRST HALF HIGHLIGHT

View 2 Images Arsenal thought they had a penalty following a first half VAR check (Image: Henry Nicholls/AFP)

As a pretty drab first half drew to a close, it seemed, briefly, as though VAR could give the game a much needed spark. Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy in the box and referee Farai Hallam was sent to the pitchside monitor.

Hallam subsequently informed the crowd there was a holding offence after reviewing the incident - before immediately bursting the home fans bubble by revealing Havertz was in an offside position. The fact that was the most notable moment of the first period tells its own story.

‌



GUNNERS DODGE SLIP UP

Arsenal ended last season as the best team in the Premier League and they've started the 2026-27 campaign in a similar vein. But they narrowly avoided a pretty spectacular banana skin by the skin of their teeth here.

Hull were never going to just be a punching bag and kept Raya and Arsenal's diligent defence honest, particular in the early embers of the game. But the Gunners do what champions do - they found a way to win.

ODEGAARD STEPS UP

‌



With Bukayo Saka missing, Arsenal needed a talisman to get them out of jail against Hull. And it was none other than their rejuvenated captain who delivered just when they needed it most.

This was Odegaard's third Premier League goal of the season already. For context, he mustered just one in the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign. This looks and feels much more like the classy operator who had been pulling the Arsenal strings prior to last year's lean spell. And considering Arsenal failed to sufficiently enhance their attacking options in the summer transfer window and are without Saka, a return to form for Odegaard could prove to be priceless.

Sports.content:
Non-league clash postponed as ex-Forest starlet rushed to hospital in warm-up

Truro City's National League South clash at Folkestone Invicta was postponed when City player Yassine En-Neyah suffered a medical emergency in the warm-up

View 3 Images The ambulance drove on to the pitch to take En-Neyah to hospital (Image: Tom Sandberg/PPAUK)

Truro City's trip to Folkestone Invicta was postponed due to a medical emergency for one of the visiting players.

‌



‌



City star Yassine En-Neyah, a Nottingham Forest youth product, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after the episode prior to the National League South clash.

‌



The 26-year-old is said to have collapsed on the pitch before the ambulance drove on to the playing surface in order to take him to hospital.

‌



Both sides released a short statement confirming the postponement, before a further post from Truro confirmed En-Neyah was the player involved and that he was receiving further treatment.

"Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment. We will provide a further update in due course.”

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard sends Michael Carrick sack warning ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard sends Michael Carrick sack warning ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash

Michael Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Manchester United's home game against Aston Villa on Sunday and Steven Gerrard has spelled out the consequences of defeat

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard has assessed Michael Carrick's situation (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Steven Gerrard has warned Michael Carrick that he must beat Aston Villa on Sunday or Manchester United's hierarchy will pull the trigger heading into the international break.

‌



‌



Carrick eased the pressure with a 3-2 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night. It snapped a nine-match winless run in all competitions, but Carrick knows he needs to back it up against Villa.

‌



United come into the weekend 17th in the Premier League table, outside of the relegation on goal difference having taken just seven points from their opening nine games. It represents United's worst start to a league campaign in 40 years and has seen club chiefs identify possible replacements.

‌



Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada have sounded out Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte, but have so far opted to stick by Carrick. They have held fire for now, but the looming two-week break is an obvious concern for the United boss if he can't beat Villa.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Sometimes a performance against a certain opposition in a certain way can give the board a little bit more belief a little bit more hope," Gerrard said on TNT Sports.

"Michael is having a tough time, and I think the next league game is crucial. I think if he can get that win, I think everyone will think this might be the few stepping stones for them to get into better form. But everyone knows what a defeat [in] the last game before an international break could do. If you lose that on the back of not winning a nine in the league, I think it could be tough for him."

‌



Gerrard recently picked out seven United players he believes aren't up to the standard, with the club failing to provide Carrick with backing in the transfer market. The club decided to spend £155million on three central midfielders in the summer transfer window, without recruiting the left-back and striker they desperately needed.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick has been under pressure at Manchester United (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

"They’ve had numerous managers in the last five or six years that haven’t really been able to turn that fortune around," Gerrard added. "I think [Jose] Mourinho came the closest finished second in the league and obviously won in Europe, so it’s a difficult job at the moment because I don’t think it’s just a problem with the manager or the coach and stuff.

"I think it’s a group of players that have been really inconsistent that haven’t given this club enough, and there’s also a lot of problems from above as well. I said recently that Manchester United have got numerous problems not just one and I don’t think Michael Carrick’s the biggest problem there."

Sports.title: Leeds beat Spurs to leave Roberto De Zerbi fuming at red card controversy
Sports.content:
Leeds beat Spurs to leave Roberto De Zerbi fuming at red card controversy

LEEDS 1-0 TOTTENHAM: Jayden Bogle was lucky to stay on the pitch as VAR decided his reckless challenge on Mathys Tel was not worth of a red card

View 2 Images Noah Okafor scored the winner for Leeds against Spurs (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Roberto De Zerbi was left seeing red after Jayden Bogle escaped a card of the same colour in this crushing defeat for Tottenham at Elland Road.

‌



‌



De Zerbi stormed down the tunnel at half time, having seen VAR refuse to deem Bogle's dangerous tackle on Mathys Tel worthy of a sending off.

‌



The challenge, which saw Bogle stand on the Achilles of the Spurs winger and force him to limp out of the game, didn't even result in the Leeds defender getting booked.

‌



And De Zerbi's mood went from bad to worse when substitute Noah Okafor won the game for Leeds in the final 10 minutes, just 97 seconds after going on.

Spurs had arrived in Yorkshire high on confidence following three straight wins. The run had even lifted a team which made a shambolic start to this campaign, into the top half of the table.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And in the process overtaking a Leeds side which had started to struggle, following a bright opening. Daniel Farke's men took on Spurs without a win in their last five league outings.

‌



But the German also knew his side had the longest unbeaten home run in the Premier League. One spanning 23 games and stretching back to March.

And Spurs were fortunate not to find themselves behind inside the opening five minutes. Mateus Fernandes did his best to handle a cross and concede a penalty, before VAR bailed him out, while Ao Tanaka blazed a shot just wide.

‌



Ethan Ampadu then sliced an effort well wide as Spurs continued to hang on. Having weathered the storm, Spurs threatened themselves when a lightening break from Tel down the left resulted in Omar Marmoush shooting straight at James Trafford.

Moments later Mohammed Kudus tested Trafford again, but these were rare moments of quality in a game badly lacking the stuff.

‌



Ten minutes before half time VAR took four minutes to review that challenge by Bogle on Tel. De Zerbi couldn't believe the outcome of the dithering.

Bogle then set up a chance for Lukas Nmecha, who headed straight at Antonin Kinsky from close range. A comical collision between team-mates Ampadu and Tarik Muharemovic kind of summed up the first half.

‌



View 2 Images Tel had to be replaced after the challenge by Bogle (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Things could only get better. And they did. Ampadu had a shot blocked, while Micky van de Ven almost sliced an interception into his own goal.

‌



Dominic Solanke blocked a header from Dominic Calvert-Lewin close to his own line as Leeds continued to push for a breakthrough. Tempers continued to simmer, and De Zerbi was booked after objecting to a yellow card shown to Pedro Porro.

A break from Calvert-Lewin saw him tee-up Tanaka, who ballooned his effort over the crossbar when he should have scored.

‌



Ampadu then had an effort deflected wide, while substitute Conor Gallagher was a whisker from snatching a winner for Spurs at the opposite end.

But with 10 minutes remaining Okafor burst into the box to beat Kinsky and bring Spurs' recent momentum to a shuddering halt.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick laughs off Man Utd claim as Antonio Conte opinion emerges
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick laughs off Man Utd claim as Antonio Conte opinion emerges

Antonio Conte is one of the managers linked with the Manchester United job

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has been under pressure at Manchester United (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has laughed off Sir Alex Ferguson comparisons as Manchester United have been told not to appoint Antonio Conte. The Italian is one of the names linked with the Old Trafford hot seat amid pressure on Carrick following a poor run of form.

‌



Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis in the summer, but the side are currently on a run of seven league games without a win and sit in 17th place in the Premier League table. They are only out of the relegation zone on goal difference.

Former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Conte is keen on the United job, having left Napoli in the summer.

JJ Gabriel breaks silence on Man Utd exit with eight-word explanation for Real Madrid move READ MORE :

Unai Emery sends Jamie Carragher firm message over Aston Villa plans after legal threat READ MORE :

The pressure on Carrick eased somewhat following the midweek fightback against AS Roma in the Champions League. United recovered from 2-0 down to secure a 3-2 victory.

The result has prompted comparisons to the triumph over Nottingham Forest in the FA Cup third round in January 1990, which ultimately saved Sir Alex Ferguson's position. However, Carrick dismissed suggestions that history could be repeating itself.

"It's up to us to take it forward," he said. "As a one-off night, it was a fantastic night. I thought we played really, really well and deserved the game. It was nice to end like that. It was nice for the supporters to end like that and to have that feeling.

"Nothing's done yet. Nothing's achieved yet, and it's one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. But we need more of it, for sure."

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has been linked with the Man United job (Image: Francesco Pecoraro, Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He is, though, not ruling out the prospect of replicating the achievements Ferguson enjoyed at Old Trafford after that victory. "It's not impossible," he added. "Anything's possible.

"You've got to build, you've got to be realistic. You've got to put things in perspective as well. The recent history that we've had and what we're trying to get to, it's not going to happen overnight.

"Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build. There are no shortcuts to it. In the end, that's where you get to, but it's definitely possible."

Amid the pressure on Carrick and the talk around Conte, former Premier League defender Gallas has issued a caution to United regarding a possible appointment. He instead believes attention should be on implementing alterations elsewhere at the club.

Speaking to SeatPick, he said: "I don't know if Antonio Conte can fix Manchester United because from what I understand now the players in that dressing room are completely different from the players 10, 15 or 20 years ago.

"If you bring in Antonio Conte, you know he has a big personality. You know he will ask his players to adapt to his system, but I don't know if the players at Manchester United can do this.

"It's a different generation. Now you have to adapt to the players at this club, not just the players adapting to you. It has to be a compromise. Before, it used to be that the players had to adapt to the manager. Nobody said anything. They had great results. Now life has changed."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"A manager like Conte would have to understand that 'OK I have to adapt to this new generation, and if I do that, at the same time, I will need them to adapt to what I want from them,' and that's why you have to be sure about what you are going into. Manchester United also have to be sure about the manager they are bringing in because the message has to make sense and be understood by the players in the dressing room. Otherwise it will be the same problem again and again.

"Ultimately, the problem with United is the players that they've brought to the club because they aren't at the level to play for Manchester United. With all the respect I have for other clubs, Manchester United are not Coventry City. They are not Crystal Palace. We are talking about Manchester United.

"They should only be signing the best players to play for the club but time and time again they have made big mistakes. Antonio Conte cannot change that. No manager can. You have to look higher up at the club first."

United are back in Premier League action on Sunday when they host Aston Villa at Old Trafford. Villa manager Unai Emery is another name said to be interesting United, but the midlands club won't let their boss go without a fight.

Sports.title: Norris claims Sao Paulo GP pole after treacherous rain-hit qualifying
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid.

On a typically rain-hit day at ever-unpredictable Interlagos, qualifying was suspended for over an hour and 20 minutes after a torrential downpour hit the drivers' first laps of Q1.

The rain eventually eased - but never particularly stopped - to allow running take place and create a thrilling and unpredictable battle for pole.

In the end it was Norris who came out ahead as conditions worsened again in Q3 to seal a third successive Interlagos pole position for the outgoing world champion, on a weekend McLaren had already showed improved form in the dry following car upgrades.

Mercedes' George Russell was second fastest ahead of a race he already knew he carries a five-place grid penalty for an engine change, meaning he could not ultimately achieve pole position whatever he did.

He lapped 0.204s slower than Norris and from second will drop to seventh on Sunday's grid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell was seething after being told to back off at a time when he believed he could have pushed for P1 during the Q3 session in Sao Paulo

But the Mercedes driver was left frustrated not to have topped the qualifying timesheet outright, which he believes he would have done had he not been advised by his race engineer to back out of what turned out to be his final representative timed lap of Q3 when he came up behind Alex Albon's slower Williams.

Russell's engineer, Marcus Dudley, clearly hoped this would pay dividends by giving the Briton a clearer run on his next lap but the call coincided with the rain increasing again, meaning lap times quickly became slower.

Drivers swiftly headed back to the pit lane to mark an effective end to the Q3 battle as they all stayed in the garage as the clock ticked down to zero.

"I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1!" fumed Russell on team radio at the end of the session.

New world champion Kimi Antonelli qualified third but will move ahead of team-mate Russell to the front row alongside Norris.

Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) George Russell, Mercedes*



3) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari**



5) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



6) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



7) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



8) Oliver Bearman, Haas



9) Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin



10) Alex Albon, Williams



*five-place penalty to be applied



**10-place penalty to be applied

Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari but he has a 10-place penalty for an engine change to serve so will drop down into the midfield.

His team-mate Hamilton was also originally supposed to serve the same sanction but a problem with his fresh Ferrari engine in final practice triggered a complete power-unit change and locked him in to a back-of-the-grid start.

He will be joined on the back rows by old title rival Verstappen, who has also taken a new power unit in his Red Bull from Saturday's running.

Both drivers dropped out in Q2, Hamilton in 11th and Verstappen in 16th after opting not to run in the second phase at all in order to save wet tyres for the race, but neither result mattered given their overriding penalties.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen reflected on a wet qualifying session in Sao Paulo.

Ferrari's heavier grid penalties increase Mercedes' chances of closing out the Constructors' Championship on Sunday. They will complete a title double for 2026 if they outscore their Italian rivals by three points or more.

Front-running penalties promote midfield runners up grid

The grid penalties for Russell, Verstappen and both Ferraris - which were all confirmed in the sessions ahead of qualifying - mean Sunday's grid has a different complexion to normal in a season dominated by the 'big four' teams.

Russell and Leclerc's demotions move Liam Lawson - whose future at Racing Bulls remain in huge doubt despite his impressive season - to a joint career-best third on the grid after the New Zealander already impressed in the wet to qualify fifth.

Who has grid penalties at Interlagos? George Russell, Mercedes - 5 places

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari - 10 places

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari - Back of grid

Max Verstappen, Red Bull - Back of grid

Sergio Perez, Cadillac - Back of grid

There were also strong performances in the rain from Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who will start fourth, and Haas' Oliver Bearman, who will line up sixth. With Verstappen at the back, Isack Hadjar will be the lead Red Bull driver in fifth.

Fernando Alonso showed his old mastery of the rain to put under-powered Aston Martin into Q3 for the first time this season, while Williams' Alex Albon also made his first top-10 appearance of a difficult year.

Alonso and Albon will line up in eighth and ninth respectively.

That is just ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri - after he dropped out in Q2 - and Brazilian debutant Rafael Camara in 11th.

Haas' new signing hugely impressed on his F1 debut to make Q2 before blotting his copybook slightly by crashing into the barriers at the end of that second phase.

Arvid Lindblad will line up 12th after his Racing Bulls car was stopped by technical issues in Q2.

Sports.title: Alcaraz sets up US Open rematch with Shelton at Paris Masters
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz cruised through to his first ATP Paris Masters final, defeating Casper Ruud in two sets.

The Spaniard, who fell in the second round in the same tournament last year, beat his Norwegian opponent 6-4 6-4 to earn a showdown with Ben Shelton on Sunday.

Ruud just about kept Alcaraz at bay in two of his first three service games, but the Spaniard then broke to move 4-3 up and closed out the first set with a 130mph ace.

The second stayed on serve until Alcaraz picked the opportune moment to break to go 5-4 ahead and sealed the win inside just 97 minutes.

This is the sixth final the 23-year-old has reached this calendar year, with him also extending his winning streak to eight consecutive matches.

Image: Alcaraz will play in his maiden Paris Masters final

"This tournament has always been really tough for me. I've struggled every time," Alcaraz said on court.

"I've come into this part of the season much fresher, hungry, ambitious, excited about coming to the tournaments and stepping on the court, playing matches and competing. I'm just really happy that I made the final."

Alcaraz entered the semi-final off the back of a dramatic victory over Taylor Fritz, saving two match points on Friday and apologising to the American at the end for, as Fritz put it at the net, being just "too good".

His drop volley winner against Ruud from the baseline encapsulated his form in the French capital.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion will next face Fritz's compatriot, two months on from their memorable US Open meeting.

World No 4 Shelton beat Alcaraz in the quarter-finals at Flushing Meadows in a gruelling five-set thriller.

Image: Alcaraz is on form in Paris

Shelton reached the final of the US Open but was ultimately defeated by Alexander Zverev.

In Paris, he secured another final showdown by beating Luca Van Assche 5-7 6-3 6-4 to face Alcaraz once again.

Watch the Paris Masters live on Sky Sports until Sunday, with the ATP Finals in Turin then running from November 15-22. Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream contract-free.
