Sports.title: Hits and misses: Could Konsa hold off Saliba's return?
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Arsenal’s match against Hull in the Premier League.

Arsenal did not produce a vintage attacking display against Hull but defensively there were few faults. Their seventh clean sheet in 10 Premier League games, and 10th in 16 overall, owed a lot to their centre-backs. Gabriel and Ezri Konsa excelled again.

William Saliba's impending return will put pressure on Konsa to retain his place but on current form he may keep hold of the shirt. Highlights from his display included a last-ditch block on Mohamed Ali-Cho when was suddenly exposed on the break.

There was no self-congratulation afterwards. Instead he berated the referee for a perceived Hull foul, then got on with business. By the end of the game, he had won all seven of his duels and completed all but two of his 53 passes, a picture of composure.

He continues to make an immense contribution since his arrival at the club. Arsenal had one early scare when Elliot Stroud forced a save from David Raya but it is now 444 minutes without conceding a goal in the Premier League for the Gunners.

Martin Odegaard won it but Konsa did his bit too. Saliba, who will build his fitnesby appearing for Arsenal's U21s on Sunday, has his work to do to win back his place.

Nick Wright

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Nottingham Forest and Manchester City.

Oliver Glasner had suggested after Nottingham Forest's loss to Brentford that the time had come to make changes. As it was, only two players came into the team for the game against Manchester City but one of them was particularly significant with skipper Ryan Yates making his first start of the season.

The popular midfielder personified the intensity required, not allowing City any time on the ball and also conducting the crowd in the rare moments when the noise levels dropped. He even helped spark the counter-attack for the dramatic third goal.

Delap was the player of the match but Yates symbolises the spirit that supporters have wanted to see from their side throughout this barren run. The celebrations upon the final whistle made this feel like a big moment. Typical that Yates should be the catalyst.

And that was true even before kick-off because he delivered the team-talk. "I have played more than 500 games as a player," said Glasner. "I have managed more than 500 games as a manager. I have never heard such an inspiring speech to the team." Yates backed it up on the pitch too.

Adam Bate

The question that Manchester City supporters might be asking right now is whether Yates and Xaver Schlager nipping at heels and Jair Cunha pressing up the pitch should have been enough for their side to unravel as they did. Three defeats in a row tells a tale.

"Today we didn't match the intensity, we need to understand the reasons why," said Maresca. "If you make a mistake or you don't win duels, you can concede on transition."

Josko Gvardiol was dispossessed for the first goal, Elliot Anderson was too weak for the second and Marc Guehi made it too easy as well. City look like a side who want to be allowed to play their football but when teams refuse to give them that time then they become unsettled.

Seven wins in a row to start the season suggested that, for all the issues engulfing City right now, it would be a seamless transition under Enzo Maresca on the pitch. But the blueprint for stopping them is now becoming clear. And that should be a major concern.

Adam Bate

Are Spurs back? On this evidence, they are not.

Three consecutive wins had raised hopes that Tottenham may have turned a corner amid talk of a European push.

But the limp 1-0 loss at Leeds, which was fully deserved as Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitted himself, shows the north London side have plenty of work to do - especially in front of goal.

Spurs created just one big chance at Elland Road and were not good enough, even amidst the controversy of Jayden Bogle's red-card escape.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Should Jayden Bogle have seen red for his challenge against Tottenham Hotspur's Mathys Tel - see what the Soccer Saturday panel have to say.

James Trafford's only meaningful save came from Jan Paul van Hecke's stoppage-time header. The defender is Tottenham's top Premier League scorer this season.

Dominic Solanke failed to have a shot despite coming on in the 43rd minute as Spurs mustered an expected goals of just 0.77 to Leeds' 2.02.

Tottenham have had the second-most shots in the Premier League this season, but have only hit 10 goals.

Spurs' goal-scoring issues will be a major area of work over the international break for De Zerbi if he is to truly get Spurs back fighting for European qualification.

Declan OIley

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Leeds’s match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

A superb second-half performance from Leeds was deservedly rewarded by a Noah Okafor's winner over Spurs.

His goal was Daniel Farke's making after he brought him and the man who assisted, Harry Wilson, on together as the pair combined just 97 seconds after entering the pitch.

This is a much-needed win for the Whites, who had gone off the boil after starting the season brightly with eight points from their first four league games to go third.

A first win since mid-September will have Leeds fans dreaming again of a potential European push, with their defence central to this.

The clean sheet against Spurs means Arsenal and Brighton remain the only two teams to have conceded fewer goals than Leeds.

And summer-signing Tarik Muharemovic is at the heart of this solidity, having made a match-high 13 clearances in the Spurs win. In fact, his 85 in total is the most of any player in the Premier League this season.

Elland Road also remains a fortress for Leeds, who are now unbeaten in their last nine Premier League home games (W5 D4).

It just feels like the November international break has now come at the wrong time for Leeds and Farke.

Declan Olley

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Fulham and Newcastle United.

Newcastle's display at Fulham may not have been pretty but it was close to the perfect away performance - and may have been but for VAR.

Matthias Jaissle had come under increasing pressure following four defeats in five. He could not argue with the noise surrounding St James' Park after a double-header with Everton saw them drop out of the Carabao Cup and suffer a limp home league defeat within three days last week.

This was the moment he needed to put out a call to his team to show they were still playing for their manager. And they answered.

Despite Fulham's domination, Newcastle had the better of the chances at Craven Cottage and restricted their hosts to an xG of 0.62, the most frugal of any visiting defence this season.

Jaissle talked of "complete commitment and togetherness" in the Magpies' performance - and it was hard to argue.

He might not have had the victory he desired to diffuse the pressure around his position, but the performance still went most of the way.

Ron Walker

Coventry may end up in the Premier League relegation zone this weekend, but there's so much positivity from Frank Lampard's side that they will be out of it in no time.

Had the two wrong penalty calls gone their way - and the fine margins about Thierno Barry's second goal for Everton also fallen in their favour - they would have surely picked up three precious points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Coventry boss Frank Lampard feels his side were hard done by as they had two penalty appeals turned down as well as conceding their third to a potential handball by Everton's Thierno Barry.

And it would have been deserved too. At the back, Stephen Mfuni and Ethan Pinnock look a perfect blend between youth and experience. Caleb Yirenkyi and Jack Rudoni look to have finally caught up with the demands of the Premier League in midfield. Taiwo Awoniyi is a handful up front.

What let them down on Merseyside was the officials and most importantly VAR - perhaps the biggest difference between Championship and Premier League football in this modern era.

With Crystal Palace and Ipswich to come in their next two home games, Lampard's Sky Blues have to shake this disappointment off quickly. The international break will help with that.

Sam Blitz

Image: Thierno Barry scored twice in quick succession against Coventry to turn the game Everton's way

Who had Thierno Barry down as Everton's answer to Erling Haaland? Well, the numbers are starting to look rather similar.

Barry's double against Coventry took him to 10 goals and three assists in all competitions, already surpassing his entire goal tally from last season. Better still, he has now scored in three successive games for Everton for the first time. Suddenly, the Frenchman is discovering a taste for goals that even the most optimistic Evertonian would have struggled to predict.

However, no player in the Premier League has missed more big chances this season than Barry too, with 13. That's an extraordinary number and suggests his finishing has been anything but clinical. Barry was even seen watching the replays of his goals on the big screen at the end of the win over Coventry where he remarked on how efficient he'd been with his finishing. Even he seemed surprised.

Had he been more ruthless this season, his numbers could be even more spectacular. The challenge now is keeping this remarkable consistency in front goal. If he does, then Haaland may have company in the Golden Boot race.

Lewis Jones

Sports.title: Delap’s Nottingham Forest stunners hand Manchester City third league defeat in a row
Sports.content:
Wait long enough and results will come to reflect performances. Manchester City may have won their first seven league games of the season but they always looked vulnerable, and now have lost three in a row. Nottingham Forest may have been second bottom but, other than the twin curses of missing chances and giving away daft goals, they seemed to be playing reasonably well. Put the two together and the outcome was a dramatic regression to the mean. It turns out the stats were right, after all.

Liam Delap scored twice to remind people just what a good striker he can be. Oliver Glasner, after last week’s anger, can breathe a little easier in his job. And Enzo Maresca remains a paradox, a manager obsessive about control whose teams always seem oddly susceptible to direct running.

After last week’s defeat at Brentford, Glasner said he regretted compromising too much in the early weeks of his reign at Forest. Although he gave no precise details as to what that might mean, he elaborated a little on Thursday, speaking of the need for “trust and respect” in the appropriate balance, suggesting there had been too much trust and not enough respect this season at Forest, too much “Woodstock 69” and not enough “high-performance nature of military”.

Glasner’s brave new uncompromising world was ushered in with just two changes to the starting lineup from defeat at Brentford, Ola Aina and Dan Ndoye dropping out for Daniel Muñoz and Ryan Yates, who both came on at half-time last week. It may have been an underwhelming revolution but it soon worked, Jair Cunha dispossessing Josko Gvardiol and running through to opening the scoring after six minutes, Forest’s first home goal since Morgan Gibbs-White’s strike against Bournemouth 34 minutes into the final game of last season, a drought of 510 minutes.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap cannot contain his delight after scoring again for Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

No side this season had underperformed their xG by such a margin as Forest; they began the weekend third in Opta’s expected table but second bottom of the actual table. To an extent that is a matter of misfortune: defeat at Brentford, for instance, was a result of a cross and a shot that both looped in off Nikola Milenkovic; when you concede one shot on target but two goals, you know you’ve been unlucky. And when, on Saturday, three minutes after Forest had taken the lead, a Jérémy Doku shot hit Milenkovic and, rather than looping agonisingly past Matz Sels, cannoned wide for a corner, Forest must really have known their luck was in.

One of the biggest issues for Forest this season has been the form of Delap. A gruelling spell at Chelsea had seemingly sapped his confidence but, 18 minutes in, he surged from inside his own half, ran, as Cunha had for the opener, between Rúben Dias and Marc Guéhi, and thumped his shot over the dive of Gianluigi Donnarumma. With confidence, it turns out, Delap is a very different player.

View image in fullscreen Jair Cunha celebrates ending Nottingham Forest’s goal drought at home. Photograph: Maddy Grassy/AP

Guéhi’s form, meanwhile, is becoming a major concern for City. With Dias wary of Xaver Schlager running to his right and potentially becoming a passing option, it was surely Guéhi’s responsibility to close Delap down. As it was, the pair left a huge channel, inviting Delap to keep going to score his second goal since joining Forest. Guéhi and Gvardiol were both withdrawn at half-time.

Quick Guide How do I 

If James McAtee had not missed the target with two very presentable opportunities, Forest could have been out of sight by half-time. It was never, though, going to be that easy. Seven minutes into the second half, a long diagonal set Doku in behind Muñoz, and although his cross was half-cleared, Rayan Cherki slammed in a brilliant half volley. In a moment, the mood changed. All the anxiety stored up by two months of disappointing form bubbled to the surface again.

Forest may feel that, after the season they have had, they are owed some luck. They were nearly paid back a slice of that when a Yates shot deflected off Elliot Anderson and dropped on to the back of the bar. But still they had burned through a fair amount, with blocks, brave headers and clearances off the line, when Gibbs-White set Delap away on the counter. A week ago, it would barely have registered as an opportunity but, self-belief restored, Delap swept into the box and drove his finish in off the far post.

Forest are out of the relegation zone and the idea that City might challenge Arsenal for the title, even if there is no points deduction, is beginning to look a little fanciful.

Sports.title: There are very few reasons for Unai Emery to leave Aston Villa for Manchester United | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
On Sunday afternoon, shortly before 4.30, Unai Emery will leave the tunnel at Old Trafford and walk along the touchline towards the bench. Will he glance around the grand old stadium – faded and leaking though it may be in parts – and think that he could have a part in restoring the club to former glories? Will he look at the home bench and imagine himself sitting there – or perhaps more plausibly, scuttling up and down in front of it – as the first Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson to land a league title?

Perhaps not. Emery is, after all, in “advanced talks” to extend a contract at Villa that already runs to 2029. However frustrating he may find the habitual summer churn, he is good at managing it. He feels the right fit for Villa, and that is arguably the most important factor in determining success. Yet all elite managers share a robust self-belief and there is a paradoxical sense that the worse the situation gets at United, the more appealing the job becomes.

Imagine being the manager who does sort it out. Imagine following in that brief lineage of United title winners: Ernest Mangnall, Matt Busby, Alex Ferguson … me? United remain the eighth wealthiest club by revenue in the world; imagine the resources that would be available if they were actually any good.

That is an allure that very few clubs in the world can match, no matter how good they were in the 1890s, and no matter how much the Villa owner, Nassef Sawiris, may dislike the fact. This is a point that cannot be made too strongly. Villa’s threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher was an outrageous attack on free speech. There is no way Carragher’s comment about the food chain of football could be construed as defamatory and, while it’s true he might have made the comment in less provocative terms, swearing is not a crime. This was a classic case of a legal threat being used to quell criticism and those fans – and, worse, journalists – who cheered it on should be thoroughly ashamed. The partisan blindness and persecution complex shared by fans of so many clubs is one of the most depressing features of the modern game.

But it’s also true United’s allure has come to look distinctly tarnished. No matter how bullet-proof a manager’s self-confidence, it would represent a remarkable risk to make the leap from Villa to United at this juncture. In almost every facet, from infrastructure to personnel, the modern Villa are better run than the modern United. And from Emery’s point of view, it’s not just that Villa are well run, it’s that they’re well run in his way.

He has the coaching staff he wants, while the president of football operations, Roberto Olabe, and the director of football operations, Damian Vidagany, are people he trusts and has worked with before. Emery would not have the degree of autonomy he has at Villa at many other clubs. United’s win over Roma on Tuesday may have eased the most immediate pressure on Michael Carrick, but nobody surely thinks that one good half against a depleted Serie A side cures all ills. (The question, obviously, is slightly absurd: nobody surely thinks Carrick is really the problem at United; it’s just that executives tend to get rid of managers because it’s what you do when there’s been a slump in form; it’s how a director acknowledges that he’s recognised there is a problem, while hoping desperately to deflect attention from his own shortcomings).

It doesn’t help that there is a clear precedent from five years ago, when a popular former United player saw his team come from two down to beat a Serie A side managed by Gian Piero Gasperini; Ole Gunnar Solskjær was sacked a month later.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick applauds the fans after Manchester United beat Roma in dramatic fashion. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

The United crisis may have eased, but it is far from over. While Sir Jim Ratcliffe shows off architects’ plans and begs for public money to build a new stadium, Villa get on with building the new Trinity Road Stand. While United’s squad sags under the weight of its many contradictions, a weird mismatch of ill-fitting parts, Villa’s begins to take shape despite making 11 signings in the summer – even if the 3-0 defeat by Barcelona in midweek suggests there is still work to be done. They probably wouldn’t ideally have made such radical changes and would have preferred to keep Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa but, equally, there was an admirable sense of realism at Villa – a recognition of their place in the food chain, you might say – that when Chelsea or Arsenal come calling and offering huge contracts, there’s not much to be done other than to drive the price as high as possible.

Youri Tielemans is another player Villa might have liked to keep, but once United matched his release clause, the deal was done. Although Tielemans probably appreciates his new contract, it’s far from clear it’s been a good move for him from a football point of view, not least because United’s is a midfield that exposes his lack of mobility. Carlos Baleba was signed from Brighton to address that lack of dynamism in the United midfield but there were concerns about his tendency to drift in and out of games even before he suffered a hamstring injury on Tuesday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It even feels as though Villa have been smarter about using United players than United have. Victor Lindelöf was brought in on a free transfer in summer 2025 and has excelled since and while Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho had less of an impact, Villa only signed them on loan. Rashford’s time, which featured four goals in 17 appearances in all competitions, was probably the more eye-catching, but Sancho made 39 appearances in his season at Villa.

In both cases, Villa got value out of a players whose futures were uncertain but without committing to having to take them on full-time.

It’s pretty hard to imagine at the moment, but at some point, United will start heading in the right direction. It may even be that Tuesday’s win prompts a surge of adrenaline that takes them into the top half of the table. For now, though, Villa look by far the brighter prospect, a club on the up, while United are in barely managed decline.

Sports.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
Sports.content:
As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season.

Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents.

“To the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach,” said Arteta. “I need to praise the players and all the staff for the work that they are doing because it’s been very, very demanding. We have a very short time to recover from games but despite that the mentality and the quality of the team has shown: it’s incredible.”

Jakirovic had promised beforehand that his side would go on the front foot. “If you are passive, they will destroy you,” said the Bosnian. But while his bold 5-3-2 formation caused Arsenal’s much-vaunted defence some issues, Hull remain without a league victory since the end of August. “It’s a big experience for us,” was Jakirovic’s post-match assessment. “We can take some big lessons from this but we have shown we can compete at this level.”

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard scores the decisive goal from close range. Photograph: Simon Dael/Shutterstock

Hull made the brighter start as John Egan headed wide from a corner. After losing to Brighton before the last international break, Arteta was taking no chances and reverted to the side that won at Liverpool last weekend. There was no William Saliba on the bench, with the France defender set to play for the under-21s on Sunday instead as he continues his comeback from a back injury.

Quick Guide How do I 

Yet aside from a set piece that resulted in Gabriel Magalhães just failing to connect with Ezri Konsa’s flick-on, the visitors’ low block frustrated Arsenal and they continued to cause problems on the break. Elliot Stroud forced David Raya into a save after Riccardo Calafiori surrendered possession cheaply.

Havertz’s failure to take a shot after being played in by a slide-rule pass from Ødegaard drew groans of frustration. A toiling Arsenal thought all their prayers had been answered just before half-time when the referee, Farai Hallam, was sent to the big screen by the VAR. Nobel Mendy was clearly pulling Havertz’s shirt inside the area yet the German was offside so the penalty was not awarded, even though it probably should have been according to the rules. They state that Havertz must be “attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball” to be penalised and because Mendy’s offence came first, that should have taken precedence, as it did when Newcastle’s Fabian Schär was awarded a penalty against Bournemouth in February 2024.

View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz is pulled back by Nobel Mendy but no penalty was awarded. Photograph: Simon Dael/Shutterstock

Pro Ref has yet to make a statement on the incident and Arteta admitted he had been left confused by the whole episode. “I don’t know what the interpretation is, I’m sure they will make that clear to understand,” he said.

The Arsenal manager’s annoyance levels continued to rise when Havertz could only head straight at Konstantinos Tzolakis on the stroke of half-time. Hull came out for the second half with a similar attitude and Jakirovic picked up a yellow card for protesting against another decision that went against his team. Declan Rice was withdrawn early, although Arteta insisted he was fine afterwards. Noni Madueke found space after a flowing Arsenal move but again his effort was straight down the throat of Tzolakis.

The feeling of desperation was growing. But Ødegaard has made a habit of coming to Arsenal’s rescue this season and the captain was quickest to react when Tzolakis spilled Madueke’s shot to finally break Hull’s brave resistance.

Sports.title: Muniz rescues late point for Fulham against Newcastle after Murphy stunner
Sports.content:
Questions over whether Álvaro Arbeloa and Matthias Jaissle have what it takes to succeed in the Premier League remain unanswered after these two young foreign managers watched their sides grind out a 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage.

Arbeloa’s Fulham lacked fizz, physicality and personality before rescuing a point thanks to a late equaliser from Rodrigo Muniz, while Newcastle displayed little of Jaissle’s high-octane philosophy and squandered the chance to move into the top half after failing to build on a vicious opening goal from Jacob Murphy.

A second consecutive away win in the league was on the cards when Murphy seized on an error from César Palacios and scored in the 80th minute. Jaissle has faced criticism over his tactics and training methods since replacing Eddie Howe just before the start of the season but the German was happy with elements of this Newcastle performance.

The 38-year-old saw “a complete commitment and togetherness in all phases of the game” and was entitled to argue the visitors had the better chances, an impressive feat given there was such little threat from Jaissle’s front two of William Osula and Yoane Wissa.

It remains a big problem for Newcastle, who are paying for their failure to fill the void left by Alexander Isak’s move to Liverpool last year. They witnessed another half-hearted display from Wissa before the £55m striker’s withdrawal in the 61st minute and were hindered by the bluntness of Osula, whose hopes of grabbing a rare goal were somewhat hindered by his failure to register a touch in Fulham’s area.

To make matters worse Osula was also partially responsible for the leveller. Newcastle needed the 23-year-old to hold the ball up but he was outmuscled near the halfway line, allowing Fulham to pounce. Palacios, who had given the ball away for Murphy’s goal, wriggled into the area and combined with another of Arbeloa’s substitutes by smuggling the ball across for Muniz to score his first league goal since August 2025.

Jaissle felt it was a “slapstick” concession. Arbeloa, who likes to play an expansive style of passing football, focused more on Muniz’s impact after the target man’s introduction in place of the smaller Gonzalo García. “Newcastle were marking us man to man,” Fulham’s Spanish head coach said. “They forced us to play long balls and Rodrigo is very strong in this situation. He got his chance. It is very important for us because I need a player like Rodrigo. He can score goals but create so many chances.”

It is encouraging that Arbeloa was willing to be flexible and more direct. However this was a poor game between two sides too close to the bottom three for comfort. Fulham also fretted over Josh King after the 19-year-old went off with a groin injury. The attacking midfielder is set for a scan and will hope not to have suffered any significant damage after earning his first England call-up on Friday.

Thomas Tuchel will be keen to have King available. Newcastle paid a lot of attention to the teenager, with Sean Steur and Nico González sitting deep in midfield, but they could not keep him quiet during the first half. King tested Lukas Hornicek with a volley from 20 yards and later missed a decent headed chance.

View image in fullscreen Jacob Murphy roars in delight after giving Newcastle the lead. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Fulham were not at their best. Oscar Bobb and García went close after an error from Steur but Newcastle were comfortable. Jaissle, who made four changes after accusing his players of not following instructions during last Monday’s defeat by Everton, asked his side to play a patient game and was annoyed when they had a goal ruled out in the 33rd minute. Dan Burn did nothing wrong when he converted a cross from close range, but Wissa was penalised for a holding offence on Timothy Castagne off the ball.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Jaissle called it a soft decision. Newcastle, who saw Bernd Leno twice thwart Harvey Barnes before half-time, moved on and improved in the second half. They pressed with more intensity and created opportunities for Barnes and Wissa.

Fulham had no out ball with García unable to impose himself against Burn and Malick Thiaw. Palacios came on and was at fault when Newcastle broke the deadlock. The Spaniard played an aimless pass across his own half and was punished by Murphy, who seized possession before driving forward to cut inside and crack a brilliant shot past Leno from 25 yards.

It seemed Newcastle were about to ease the pressure on Jaissle. Fulham had other ideas. Arbeloa praised the defiance. Palacios linked with Alex Iwobi and found Muniz. The ball bounced around the six-yard box and Muniz forced it past Hornicek.

Fulham poured forward in search of a winner. Lewis Hall almost restored Newcastle’s lead, only for Leno to deny the left-back. A draw was fair.

Sports.title: Okafor seals Leeds win but Tottenham complain to Pro Ref over Bogle tackle on Tel
Sports.content:
It is almost one year to the day when the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, produced the tactical overhaul many observers believe saved his job. That day, Farke abandoned his trusted 4-3-3 when Leeds were 2-0 down at Manchester City and although they lost the game, the 3-5-2 he reverted to was the bedrock for the success that followed.

To suggest Farke was under similar pressure going into this game would be a stretch, but without a win in five Premier League games it was not unreasonable to suggest the Elland Road natives were getting slightly restless. Defeat going into the international break would have firmly extinguished what had been a positive start, with eight points from the first four.

So how fitting that with the stakes high once again, Farke’s tactical flexibility which he appears to have developed over the past 12 months laid the platform for a much-needed win for Leeds. His decision to go back to 3-5-2 heading into this meeting with Tottenham led to a largely stalemate opening 45 minutes, with the hosts cancelling out an in-form opponent.

But what happened at half-time was significant. Just like a year ago, Farke changed shape and breathed new life into his side. He switched first to a 4-2-3-1 and then into a 3-4-3, with a mountain of pressure ultimately producing the goal Leeds’ play deserved, as the substitute Noah Okafor’s late strike proved to be the difference.

It was a moment that clearly meant as much to Farke as it did the Elland Road faithful, the German punching the air in delight as his tactical tweaks paid off, with another substitute Harry Wilson the man to tee up Okafor for the winner. It was a successful afternoon for Leeds, who can look ahead with optimism once again after a tricky period.

“There’s no replacement for this winning feeling,” Farke said after. “All my credit goes to the boys for a terrific performance against an in-form Spurs side. It was important to be tactically spot on against their processes.”

Spurs may look back on this as a frustrating afternoon. They failed to create enough opportunities to trouble a well-organised Leeds side, but they will consider whether a crucial moment as half-time approached could have shifted the momentum firmly their way, with Jayden Bogle perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

View image in fullscreen Noah Okafor slots home the Leeds winner in the 79th minute. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

Bogle caught Mathys Tel on the achilles, with replays showing a nasty contact that left the forward unable to continue. A lengthy video assistant referee stoppage led many to assume Bogle would follow Jean-Philippe Mateta in seeing red against the same opposition, but it was deemed the Leeds wing-back did not commit serious foul play. It later emerged Tottenham will submit a formal complaint to Pro Ref about the decision not to send off Bogle for the challenge.

In both halves Spurs’ attacking potency let them down and they never really truly tested James Trafford in the Leeds goal as their bid to win four successive Premier League games for the first time in three years came grinding to a halt.

“The second half we didn’t show the same spirit,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “We didn’t show the hunger we need for these types of big games. We have to analyse. Many games like this can be a problem for us.”

There were few clearcut opportunities in the first half, with the Bogle-Tel incident the undoubted talking point. But Farke reverted to a back four after the restart, and it led to a huge spell of Leeds pressure. Both Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ao Tanaka had glorious opportunities, with Spurs struggling to contain Leeds’ new shape.

Quick Guide How do I 

The momentum remained with the hosts as the hour mark arrived, which prompted De Zerbi into a triple substitution to attempt to wrestle back control. The result was almost immediate as Conor Gallagher shot wide while at the other end Sean Longstaff was next to spurn a huge chance for the hosts.

It looked as though it would end goalless but Farke rolled the dice again. His next move was another change of shape with Wilson and Okafor introduced to support Calvert-Lewin. Within two minutes the two substitutes combined and Okafor rifled home past Kinsky to send Elland Road into uproar with a goal – and a result – their second-half performance undeniably merited. Leeds navigated any late drama with minimal fuss.

Sports.title: Manchester City break clear of Chelsea in WSL after Bronze’s freak own goal
Sports.content:
An own goal by defender Lucy Bronze ⁠against Everton cost Chelsea top spot in the Women’s ⁠Super League as ⁠they ​were held to a 1-1 draw at home, allowing Manchester City ⁠to leapfrog them with a 5-0 drubbing of West Ham.

Bronze headed ⁠the ball back across the goal to tee ​up Sandy Baltimore ‌to score ‌from close range in the 28th minute, but ‌five minutes later her attempted clearance rolled into her own net to put Everton level. The visitors held on for a draw as Chelsea dropped points for the ‌first time since the opening day of the season.

Manchester City made the most ​of that slip-up as Bunny Shaw’s superb goalscoring form continued, the Jamaican striker netting a hat-trick as her side cantered to a comprehensive win against West Ham, with Aoba ​Fujino ​and Iman Beney also on target.

The WSL’s top scorer gave City the lead six minutes before the break. City then ran riot after the interval as Shaw grabbed another couple for the match ball while Beney and Fujino scored their first goals of the campaign.

West Ham were happy to sit in and soak up the pressure from their opponents, and Constance Picaud-Inconnu was relieved when she parried Kerstin Casparij’s effort straight back into danger but no one was on hand to tap home. The visitors had the woodwork to thank for not going a goal down when Fujino’s effort hit a post.

It seemed only a matter of time before City made the breakthrough and they did just that five minutes before the break. Hemp stole possession as West Ham tried to play out from the back and the ball was worked to Shaw to finish expertly.

View image in fullscreen Sandy Baltimore opens the scoring for Chelsea against Everton. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

City doubled their advantage eight minutes after the break as Shaw directed Hemp’s cross past Picaud-Inconnu. Fujino hit the crossbar but was not to be denied minutes later to make it 3-0.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Beney added a fourth five minutes after coming on with a deflected strike from the edge of the box. Shaw completed her hat-trick with 16 minutes to play when she latched on to a through ball from Grace Clinton before grabbing her 12th goal from nine WSL games.

Sports.title: European football: Bayern beat Mainz but Neuer’s record-breaking day turns sour
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich secured a 2-1 victory over Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday but the form ⁠of goalkeeper Manuel Neuer will again be in the spotlight after another error almost produced an equaliser for the home side ⁠in the first ⁠half.

Neuer became Bayern’s ​oldest player at 40 years, 225 days, overtaking Bernd Dreher, but was forced off with a recurrence of a foot injury ⁠that had kept him out of recent matches, replaced before half-time by Jonas Urbig.

Neuer was left flailing at a cross that resulted ⁠in Mainz’s Lee Jae-sung putting the ball in the back of the net with Bayern ​leading 1-0, though the effort was ‌ruled out for offside.

Neuer’s mistake ‌against Augsburg last month, which resulted in the fastest-ever Bundesliga goal after eight seconds ‌by Robin Fellhauer, was the latest in a growing number for the keeper once regarded among the best in the world.

According to Sofascore using Opta data, that error was his fifth that led to a goal in his previous 17 Bundesliga games, or one every 3.4 matches. In 248 appearances before that, he made just 10 ‌such errors, or one every 24.8 games.

Neuer has played twice since that Augsburg fixture, which ended 2-2, missing four games with the foot injury. ​He returned for this week’s 2-0 Champions League win at Atlético Madrid.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane was not on the scoresheet but provided two assists. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

The Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane could not find the net against Mainz but did provide two assists for Joshua Kimmich and 18-year-old Lennart Karl as Bayern extended their unbeaten away run in the league ⁠to 31 games.

They maintained their lead at the top of the Bundesliga ​from Borussia Dortmund with ​both clubs on 21 points from ​nine games. Bayern have a superior goal difference.

Dortmund were given a ​scare by promoted Elversberg ‌but won 2-1, ​thanks to two ​goals from Felix Nmecha.

Third-placed RB Leipzig, who are three points behind the leaders, won 5-2 at home to Augsburg, while Jonathan Burkardt scored a 93rd-minute equaliser for Eintracht Frankfurt as they drew 2-2 at Paderborn in a battle between two mid-table sides.

Werder Bremen missed the chance to climb into the top four when they lost 1-0 at Stuttgart, where an early goal from Maximilian Mittelstadt settled the contest.

Later on Saturday, Real Madrid can move level with Barcelona overnight at the top of La Liga by winning at Valencia; the leaders visit Atlético on Sunday. In Italy, a win for Roma at home to Sassuolo would put them a point behind their fellow Stadio Olimpico tenants, Lazio – the leaders visit Napoli on Sunday lunchtime. In France, Paris Saint-Germain can cement their place at the top of Ligue 1 by beating Troyes at home.

Sports.title: Truro City game at Folkestone called off after Yassine En-Neyah has medical emergency in warm-up
Sports.content:
Truro’s National League South game at Folkestone Invicta was called off after the visitors’ midfielder Yassine En-Neyah had a medical emergency and was taken to hospital.

The 26-year-old was transported to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford for treatment but is now responsive, according to an evening update from the Cornwall club.

“He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation,” a Truro City statement read.

“The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City’s medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

“Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.”

En-Neyah joined Truro from Waterford in 2023, having once been on the books at Nottingham Forest. The Morocco-born player was raised in Ireland and spent time in the youth systems of Corduff and Bohemians, before he joined the Forest academy in 2017.

Truro lie third in the National League South table, four points behind the leaders Ebbsfleet United but with a game in hand.

Sports.title: Fans left baffled as FA Cup clash marred by intense fog covering entire ground
Sports.content:
Football fans couldn't believe what they were watching as Altrincham's FA Cup tie against Notts County.

Or, given the intense fog that encapsulated the stadium, what they were not watching.

4 This was the view fans were left with watching on TV

4 This was the view of the penalty shootout

The contest finished 2-2 at full-time, sending it to extra time and then eventually penalties.

In the end, it was Notts County who won 3-2 in a crazy shootout as both teams missed spot kicks in the conditions.

TNT Sports commentator Adam Summerton did his best to cover the action as even the managers of both teams were questioning what was going on.

The prize for County is a place in the second round of the FA Cup as they ended the National League team's run.

Pictures on the broadcast of the match left several fans baffled as to how it was not stopped due to the conditions.

One fan on X said: "Maybe the camera makes it worse but how is this Altrincham vs Notts County still playing in this fog is ridiculous."

Another added: "I’m amazed anyone could see that Notts County equaliser at Altrincham."

A third said: "Nice to see the BBC are using the screens that VAR use during a game for the Altrincham vs Notts County match."

An additional supporter proclaimed: "Altrincham v Notts County is currently being played in a cloud."

A fifth continued: "The coverage of Altrincham v Notts County is farcical. You can’t see the other side of the pitch."

4 Fans at the ground saw the funny side and used their phone cameras to try and create some light

4 Banks thought he'd won it Credit: Getty

How did Altrincham v Notts County unfold?

Making it to the second round of the FA Cup is a big deal with the dream of a big Premier League tie just one win away.

And despite the terrible conditions, both sides put on a show.

It was the League One side who opened the scoring as former Newcastle United winger Callum Roberts set up Jacob Bedeau.

But a man who was in the ninth tier, Lucas Weaver, hauled Alty level.

He got on the end of a lovely pass by Matty Kosylo into the box, squared up his man, jinked inside and drove a low shot in at the near post.

The shock looked to be on in the 59th minute as Lewis Banks got the end of an excellent cross from the left.

Banks' first header was saved, but he tapped in the rebound.

However, as the fog became worse, Roberts hit a low first-time curling shot from the edge of the box.

But the teams couldn't be separated in normal time with a penalty shootout required.

James Belshaw was the hero for the League One side with two saves in the shootout before Rosaire Longelo stepped up to slam home the winner.

Sports.title: Arsenal equal all-time club record with victory over Hull
Sports.content:
Arsenal have matched their best ever start to a Premier League season following Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull.

The Gunners provisionally stretched their lead at the top of the table to six points with a hard-fought victory over the Tigers at the Emirates Stadium.



3 Martin Odegaard was quickest to react to fire Arsenal's winner against Hull Credit: AFP

Mikel Arteta’s side were made to wait until the 72nd minute for their winner courtesy of Martin Odegaard.

The Arsenal skipper was on hand to slot home from close range after Noni Madueke’s effort was parried into his path by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

The win took the Gunners up to 27 points from their ten league games this season – a record-equalling best for the club.



Arsenal’s previous points return from the same number of games came in the 2022/23 season.

That season, the north London club agonisingly missed out on the Premier League title to Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City.



City and Arsenal enjoyed an enthralling title race only for Guardiola’s men to pull ahead and claim the title by a five-point margin.

But it is reigning champions Arsenal who lead the way while having momentum in their favour in this season’s race for the crown.



Sergej Jakirovic’s Hull side put up a valiant fight at the Emirates and were looking good for what would have been an impressive point on the road.

VAR controversy

The match was plunged into confusion late in the first half when Kai Havertz was denied what appeared to be a clear penalty.

The Arsenal forward had shirt pulled by Hull defender Nobel Mendy only for referee Farai Hallam to wave away the appeals.

3 Referee Farai Hallam made the call not to award the penalty Credit: Getty



3 Mikel Arteta's side are on the right track for success this season

Hallam was subsequently instructed to consult the pitchside monitor where it was concluded that Havertz was in an offside position at the time he was impeded.

But it all proved insignificant in the end as Arsenal extended their unbeaten home run in all competitions to 11 games.

That sees the Gunners claim top spot going into the International break with key fixtures to come in the lead up to Christmas.



Next up for Arteta's side in the Premier League is a trip to Newcastle where they have won just once in their last four visits.

Further testing clashes follow with title rivals Manchester City, Brentford to play before the north London derby against Tottenham.

Arsenal also face home matches against Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid in the Champions League.



﻿

Sports.title: William Saliba left out of Arsenal squad for alternative appearance this weekend
Sports.content:
William Saliba left out of Arsenal squad for alternative appearance this weekend

William Saliba is set to play for Arsenal's Under-21s against Aston Villa on Sunday, Mikel Arteta has confirmed.

The defender has not played this season since suffering a back injury with France at the World Cup, but was named on the bench in the Gunners' win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday.

4 Saliba was involved in an Arsenal matchday squad for the first time this season against Slavia Prague on Wednesady Credit: Getty

While Saliba did not feature in the Champions League victory, his presence led to hopes he could feature against Hull on Saturday.

Saliba absence explained

However, Saliba was not selected for the home clash, but it has now been revealed his absence isn't a cause for concern.

Gunners boss Arteta confirmed that was not due to any setback, but rather a plan to get the Frenchman back up to full fitness.

Saliba will take his next steps towards a return by being involved for Arsenal's Under-21s when they host Villa on Sunday.

Explaining this, Arteta said: “He needs some minutes.

“Obviously, the Champions League allows you to bring more players into the bench, but we believe that it’s the best thing to do, to play some minutes on the weekend with the Under-21s and then be fully fit for the international break.”

With the international break up next, means that Saliba will now have to wait until November 21 to make his return to the pitch.

The 25-year-old was not included in Zinedine Zidane's second France squad, as they prepare to face Italy and Turkey in the Nations League.

That's despite Arteta previously suggesting he would have been comfortable with Saliba being called up for international duty.

Selection headache?

Saliba's imminent return will come as a major boost for Arsenal, with the defender establishing himself as indispensable in recent years.

4 Saliba has yet to kick a ball for Arsenal this season Credit: Getty

4 The Frenchman has been out injured for over three months Credit: Getty

Widely considered one of the top-flight's best defenders, his rock-solid partnership with Gabriel played a key role in the Gunners' Premier League title victory last season after a 22-year wait.

The centre-back pair conceded just 27 league goals across the entirety of last term and Saliba was named in the PFA team of the year for the fourth consecutive time.

However, the France star might not find that he walks straight into the starting XI, with Arteta now facing a selection headache.

Saliba's absence led to the Gunners' £55million move for Ezri Konsa this summer, who has impressed since his arrival from Aston Villa.

The England star has made an immediate impact, most recently helping Arsenal keep three consecutive clean sheets in the Premier League.

This has led Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand to suggest that Konsa should move to right-back once Saliba returns.

4 Ezri Konsa has quickly established himself at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Konsa has previously impressed when deputising in the role - doing so for England at the World Cup - and this would allow Arteta to accommodate all of his defensive talent.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand said: "I think Saliba is one of those guys that you have to find room for in the team. He's that good, he's top.

"I said to my son yesterday, 'watch Ezri Konsa', because everything he does is efficient. That's a great problem for Arteta to have.

"I wouldn't be surprised if Konsa goes back to right-back once Saliba comes back. I wouldn't be surprised because Konsa is top."

Sports.title: Wantaway Man United kid JJ Gabriel outlines Ballon d’Or ambition in Spanish media interview
Sports.content:
Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel is targeting future Ballon d’Or success and has hinted at an imminent move to Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old forward recently signalled his intention to leave Manchester United by handing in a shock transfer request.

3 Gabriel was said to be unhappy with his lack of game time at United Credit: Getty

A host of clubs have reportedly shown an interest in the starlet with talkSPORT reporting earlier this week that Real Madrid were leading the chase for his signature.

Gabriel appeared to drop his biggest hint yet regarding possible move to the Santiago Bernabeu by giving an exclusive interview to Spanish outlet Marca.

The youngster has not trained at United’s Carrington Training Centre since September and has instead spent his time training in Madrid.

In the interview with Marca, Gabriel discussed his favourite club between La Liga giants Real Madrid and Barcelona while discussing his future objectives.

Pressed on what his preferred club is, Gabriel replied: “Obviously Madrid” - to the amusement of his watching father Joe O'Cearuill.

A switch to the club is expected to be confirmed in January with Manchester United possibly netting a compensation of as little at £300,000 for the teen sensation.

Gabriel went on to reveal his personal ambition of one day winning the Ballon d’Or.

The decorated award handed out to the best player in the world has not been won by a Real Madrid player since Karim Benzema in 2022.

The Frenchman was the last active La Liga player to have won the award with Vincius Junior narrowly missing out in 2024 and Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal coming up short behind Harry Kane in this year’s edition.

“My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or,” Gabriel explained, having already made his mark on the UEFA Youth League with a hattrick prior to his transfer request.

3 Gabriel is hoping to one day follow in the footsteps of fellow Englishman Harry Kane by winning the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

Manchester United sources insist they have not entered into discussions with any club over a transfer but it appears that a move to the Spanish capital is imminent.

The forward is expected to start his Real Madrid career in the club’s Castilla team that functions in Spain’s third tier.

He will also feature in the UEFA Youth League.

Why does Gabriel want to leave Manchester United?

Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United due to frustrations over his development pathway. His camp have reportedly pinpointed a perceived delay in his integration into the first team.

The star’s representatives have lost faith in the long-term project at Manchester United, claiming the club has declined compared to Europe's current elite.

Gabriel was named the Premier League’s Under-18 Player of the Season last year aged just 14 years old.

3 Gabriel has been lauded for his superb displays across United's youth teams Credit: Getty

He went on to break records playing for United’s various youth teams and became the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s.

Sports.title: VAR chaos as Arsenal penalty refused for offside but rules expert says it should have stood
Sports.content:
VAR chaos as Arsenal penalty refused for offside but rules expert says it should have stood

Martin Keown blasted the farcical nature in which Kai Havertz was denied a penalty against Hull City.

Havertz had his shirt pulled by Hull defender Nobel Mendy as he looked to break clear late in the first half of Arsenal's 1-0 win over the Tigers.

2 Havertz pleaded his case to the official but to no avail Credit: AFP

Why did Arsenal not receive a penalty?

The incident was initially dismissed by referee Farai Hallam, but he was quickly instructed by VAR official Michael Oliver to review the incident on the pitchside monitor.

However, a review quickly showed that Havertz was in an offside position when Mendy tugged on his shirt, meaning the pitchside review would ultimately be redundant.

That's exactly how it played out when Hallam announced his decision to the Emirates Stadium crowd.

Hallam initially admitted Mendy's foul was indeed worthy of a penalty, sparking cheers from Gunners fans.

But those quickly subsided when he explained that because Havertz was in an offside position at the time, it was a moot point.

Martin Keown reacts to the non-penalty

The entire process left Gunners great Keown, who was on commentary duties for talkSPORT, furious.

"He should never have been asked to go to the VAR monitor, should he," Keown said.

"They should have determined that already if he was offside. That's ridiculous."

Keown added: "Wouldn't you have decided all of that in the VAR room before you ask the referee to go and look at it? It's ridiculous. I'd really love to hear the true story on that one."

Co-commentator Alex Crook added Liverpool fans would have felt Havertz's non-penalty would be 'karma' given Alexander Isak did not receive a penalty when Jurrien Timber committed a similar offence last Sunday.

2 Referee Farai Hallam was at the centre of controversy by not awarding a penalty Credit: Getty

Were Arsenal robbed of a penalty against Hull?

But in a further twist to the decision, BBC football rules expert Dale Johnson explained that Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty.

He said: "A player who is in an offside position only becomes active when they commit an offside offence.

"Kai Havertz must be 'attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball' - otherwise the shirt pull by Nobel Mendy takes precedence. The foul comes before any offside offence.

"Havertz did not commit an offside offence, and this should have been a spot-kick to Arsenal regardless of the offside.

"We saw this a couple of seasons ago between Newcastle and Bournemouth. Fabian Schar was just offside but pulled back as he moved to run onto a free-kick delivery. A penalty was awarded after a VAR review."

Regardless of whether a penalty should or should not have been awarded, Havertz has developed an uncomfortable habit of being offside.

By straying beyond Hull's defensive line, Havertz has been flagged offside a league-leading 15 times this term, seven more than Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin who sits second on the leaderboard.

Sports.title: Xavi Simons gives one-word reaction as Tottenham fear ‘bad’ Mathys Tel injury
Sports.content:
Xavi Simons has asked football fans to play a game of spot the difference.

Simons, who is recovering from an ACL tear sustained in April, watched on as Spurs slipped to a 1-0 loss away at Leeds on Saturday.



3 Spurs' three-game win streak was snapped by Leeds Credit: AFP

But one moment in particular caught Simons' attention and left him baffled as to how no further action was taken.

What sparked Xavi Simons' reaction?

Spurs players and fans, including talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara, blew up deluxe when Leeds defender Jayden Bogle avoided a red card for an ugly challenge on Mathys Tel in the first half.

Replays showed Bogle planted his foot on the back of Tel's ankle, with the Spurs flyer requiring medical treatment following the miscued tackle.



Although a five-minute VAR check ensued, Bogle escaped a red card while Tel had to be substituted.

How severe is Mathys Tel's injury?

Unfortunately for Tel, the challenge could leave him sidelined for a period of time.



Speaking after the contest, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitted it was a 'bad injury'.

"Now we have to make the medical check, and in the next day we will know what is the problem."



For Simons, he could not believe Bogle remained on the pitch given he committed a similar foul on Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk last season but was sent off.

The incident happened during Liverpool's 2-1 win over Spurs last December.

Simons was initially shown a yellow card for the challenge by referee John Brooks.

3 De Zerbi admitted he is worried about Tel's injury sustained against Leeds Credit: Getty



However, Brooks was instructed to review the tackle on the pitchside monitor, and it wasn't long before Simons' yellow card was upgraded to a red one.

It was the first red card of Simons' senior career and saw him immediately receive a three-match suspension.

What did Xavi Simons say about Jayden Bogle's challenge?

Given the similarity in tackles but variation in punishment, Simons expressed his frustrations on social media.

Simons shared screenshots of both challenges to his Snapchat story along with the caption: "Difference?"



Simons wasn't the only Spurs player to express their befuddlement at Bogle not being punished.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Spurs skipper Micky van de Ven said: "When I saw the impact from the side, I knew straight away.

3 Bogle has been sent off just once in his professional career Credit: Getty

"I went to the referee and said, 'This is a hard challenge.'

"I think it says enough that they're going to check it. So when the VAR needs so long to check it, you can always call the ref to have a look by himself."



Why did Jayden Bogle avoid a red card?

Despite Spurs fans wincing with every replay of Bogle's tackle, VAR official Tony Harrington backed up referee John Brooks' initial call not to send the Leeds ace off.

"I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card," Harrington said.

"There's a lack of speed going into the challenge and he's stepping into the tackle.

"Confirming a reckless challenge."

Sports.title: ‘Horrendous feeling’ – James Trafford reveals how bad it got at Man City
Sports.content:
‘Horrendous feeling’ – James Trafford reveals how bad it got at Man City

James Trafford has revealed he left Manchester City for Leeds this summer for the sake of his mental wellbeing.

The England international sealed a dream return to the Etihad in the summer of 2025, two years after he first departed to join Burnley.

4 Trafford has kept four Premier League clean sheets in 10 games for Leeds this term Credit: Getty

However, disaster struck weeks later when the Citizens then signed Italy star Gianluigi Donnarumma in the same window.

This immediately saw Trafford relegated to second-choice, despite appearing set to become City's No.1 when he first joined.

It meant that after starting the first three matches of the campaign, Trafford made just one further Premier League start in the following 35 games.

The 24-year-old then left the Etihad for Leeds in a club-record £45million move in the summer transfer window.

Since then, Trafford has been a standout performer in the top-flight and started for England over Jordan Pickford during the most recent international break.

Trafford: I lost myself at City

With Trafford flying high at Elland Road, the goalkeeper has now opened up on his struggles during his year back at Man City, and admitted a move away for first-team football was crucial.

On his time at City, Trafford told Football Daily's The Football Interview: "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing.

"You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up.

"I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny.

He continued: "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing.

4 Despite a lack of Premier League minutes, Trafford was City's first choice goalkeeper in domestic cup competitions last term and lifted two trophies Credit: Getty

4 Gianluigi Donnarumma's European pedigree immediately saw him replace Trafford as Man City's No.1 Credit: Getty

"Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous.

"I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve."

Despite his limited playing time, Trafford insisted there were valuable lessons from his final season at City, where he started in both of their Carabao Cup and FA Cup final victories at Wembley.

"Going into any season, I always have the highest of hopes and always the belief that it will go the best way it could," he added.

"Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens.

"In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year.

4 Trafford has earned four England caps to date Credit: Getty

"There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

In the same interview, Trafford shares his hopes at making the England No.1 shirt his own, having served as back-up to Jordan Pickford at the 2026 World Cup.

His strong form for Leeds was rewarded in the last international break, where he started in back-to-back Nations League games.

On his hopes of becoming England's No.1, Trafford said: "It's my aim and it's something I've always dreamed of.

"I always believe that one day I could be. Every day I try to keep improving to put myself in the best position to be England's number one one day.

"I think everyone in the goalkeeping department with the national team wants to be number one because it's an amazing position to be in."

Sports.title: Newcastle star Amar Dedic breaks silence on run-in with police after bow-and-arrow incident
Sports.content:
Newcastle star Amar Dedic breaks silence on run-in with police after bow-and-arrow incident

Newcastle star Amar Dedic has compared himself to a Lord of the Rings character after being questioned by Northumbria Police earlier this week.

Dedic was quizzed by officers on Wednesday for being in possession of a bow and arrow in public.



2 Amar Dedic was embroiled in a bizarre bow and arrow incident with police on Wednesday Credit: Getty

The Magpies’ summer signing was stopped by police in the Darras Hall estate in Newcastle, and officers seized the weapon at the scene.

They were responding to a report of two men walking alongside a reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area of the city.

Six police cars, consisting of some armed police, arrived on scene to question Dedic and his friend.



Bizarrely, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett who were in the area, stopped by to help Dedic.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: "Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.



“Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

"At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use, and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing."



Dedic's response

The Bosnia and Herzegovina international has now commented on Newcastle’s Instagram post commending the star for his recent international call-up.

The post on X read: "Amar Dedic has been named in the Bosnia and Herzegovina squad for their games against Sweden and Romania over the international break. Congrats, @amar_dc!"

Commenting on the post, Dedic posted a GIF of Legolas, an elf from Lord of the Rings.

2 Dedic posted the GIF which has now been deleted Credit: NUFC X



The GIF depicts the character with a quiver of arrows over their shoulder.

Fans were quick to comment on Dedic’s post which was later deleted by the player.

Prior to deleting the GIF, Dedic had garnered over 20,000 likes and 300 replies from fans seeing the humour in his reply.

Newcastle are not expected to take any disciplinary action against the player with police enquiries continuing.



Dedic joined the Magpies from Benfica in August on a five-year deal in a £30million deal.

The right-back has so far made 13 appearances for the club, registering four assists.

Sports.title: Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
This run will not be about the verdicts. This cannot be about the verdicts. Footballers do not care about these things, the stuff out of their control. Besides, all of them are earning cut-price transfers elsewhere were Manchester City to suffer relegation anyway. And cut-price fees mean bulkier salaries. So to them the current climate, the circumstances around City – their recent history and their immediate future – does not overly matter. Sure, there might be the odd one who is slightly more philosophical and inquisitive about appeals and appendices but the majority won't be giving it much or any thought. City insist on their innocence publicly and privately; until that changes, their players and Enzo Maresca carry on regardless. There were the usual jeers here, there were ditties about cheating, but that surely cannot affect them. Instead, the performances over the past few weeks, this a third consecutive Premier League defeat and now sinking six points adrift of Arsenal, cannot be excused by the findings of an independent commission. The problems are football problems. This is a squad who appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game. Namely how to build from the back – and that is prompting individual mistakes. It happened against Ipswich Town and at Aston Villa. On the river Trent, it was no different. The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story. Man City are a squad who now appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story Three defeats in a row have seen Enzo Maresca's side slip six points behind leaders Arsenal Too many errors. Too much arm waving. Too much feeling sorry for themselves when decisions go elsewhere. Oliver Glasner is not stupid, he will have seen examples of this play out in parts of City's victories as well as reverses. As Liam Delap raced into the corner to celebrate his second with 17 minutes left – a huge day in his career against the club which moulded him – Glasner was dashing down the touchline with unbridled joy. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Nottingham Forest (5-2-2-1): Sels 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 65, 6), Cunha 8, Milenkovic 8, Murillo 7, Williams 8; Yates 8 (Sangare 79), Schlager 8; McAtee 7 (Ndoye 65, 6), Gibbs-White 7; Delap 9 (Jesus 87) Manager: Oliver Glasner 8 Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Nunes 46, 7), Gvardiol 4 (O'Reilly 46, 6); Anderson 5; Ndiaye 6, Cherki 6, Fernandez 4 (Foden 78), Doku 6; Haaland 5 Manager: Enzo Maresca 5 Referee: Sam Barrott 6 Att: 30,762 Forest displays have deserved more than their points total so far and this was vindication for their fifth manager in 14 months, who suggested he fancied sampling Nottingham’s nightlife afterwards. Delap was exceptional, some personal redemption after criticism. The way in which Glasner nudged James McAtee further forward, stationed higher from the off in order to pressurise the visitors, spoke to an idea that City arrived here ready to be ruffled and have been wearing a look of fragility. By the time this was eight minutes shy of half time and McAtee was nicking possession from Elliot Anderson, drawing a foul that sparked another onslaught on Gianluigi Donnarumma's box, Forest were already two clear – and had been for some time. Phil Foden warmed up on the touchline, laughing and hugging with Callum Hudson-Odoi. Forest preyed on City insecurities. A midfield structure that is simply not working at the moment, easily railroaded. A defence allergic to the basics and an epidemic of individual mistakes – either as a result of nervousness or blase attitude on the ball. Straight to the mistakes. A real collection, these: the first in the fifth minute and the others 13 minutes afterwards. Jair Cunha wheeled away after picking Josko Gvardiol's pocket, meandering forward into the box and side-footing into the far corner largely unchallenged. Gvardiol seemed to have the air of a man who felt invincible when gathering possession before being eased off it. Later, as Delap thundered forward 45 yards unchecked to hammer past Donnarumma, you wondered about the communication between these City players. Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye left things to each other near halfway, Xaver Schlager gave his thanks – finding Delap – and the City academy graduate bulldozed clear. Marc Guehi waved him through, Ruben Dias dithered and Maresca bowed his head. Liam Delap was exceptional for Nottingham Forest, some personal redemption after criticism Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes. Dias looked aghast at Guehi, who was then hooked at the break alongside Gvardiol. Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both stood in the centre circle, hands on hips. It later emerged via replays that Anderson had been arguing with Abdukodir Khusanov in the build-up to Forest's opener as well, proof that City were nowhere near close to producing what was expected when on the ball in their own half. Glasner had the weapons at his disposal to make this work but even the Austrian must have been surprised at the way in which they tickled City's soft underbelly. They had not scored at the City Ground all season. All change when owner Evangelos Marinakis made his first trip to see a game since Glasner's appointment, which felt particularly handy, with Yates having delivered a spinetingling dressing room speech pre-match. Anger permeated the eyes of some City players as the whistle went. Cherki stormed down the tunnel, animatedly discussing how to play through Forest with Fernandez when they re-emerged. Their lifeline came after 52 minutes, a Ryan Yates deflection from Jeremy Doku's cross sitting up for Cherki to hammer home a half-volley off the bar. Doku soon almost squeezed another effort past Matz Sels and the mood shifted, City briefly creeping menacingly like the monsters they are portrayed as. Maresca had introduced Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, with both affecting the upturn. An admission of selection errors, perhaps, although O'Reilly is managing an ongoing back issue and is set for therapy on it over the international break. City will need some of that as a collective. Delap won the ball inside his own third, gliding past Anderson, and Forest's explosive counter ended with Delap spearing a shot in off the post after Morgan Gibbs-White carried possession unopposed for 60 yards. Delirium, Glasner darting to the corner flag. The quirk of this is that City's failings mean Manchester United drop into the bottom three. MARESCA'S VERDICT: Maresca criticised Manchester City’s lack of fight but insisted that City created enough chances to leave with something despite admitting his players were physically second best. ‘In the first half we were not good enough - we didn't match the intensity that these kind of games require,’ Maresca said. ‘If you are not able to win the second balls then you struggle. You have to match the desire to win second balls and duels, otherwise it is not good. When you lost balls the way we did and cannot recover immediately, it’s a matter of winning duels.’ Maresca has a two-week international break to rake over the issues affecting his side and believes time away could do the squad good. The Italian added: ‘When you lose a game you always want to go again immediately to try to win games but I think that this international break, the last one until March, is also good for the players. ‘We didn't match the intensity. We need to understand the reason why and try to avoid the next games. There is no panic. We need to understand but no panic.’ Maresca revealed that defenders Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol asked to come off at half time with injuries, while Forest out-ran his team by 6km on the night. ‘If you want to win against City, you need to do this,’ Oliver Glasner said after recording his first home win. ‘Credit to Liam, these strikes are something you have or you don't have. ‘It can be a turning point but we have to prove it. The way we performed today should give us confidence.’ City winger Jeremy Doku could not explain why they could not deal with Forest before half time. ‘We are used to playing every two days - that's not a reason,’ Doku said. ‘If you ask me for the reason for our first half I don't know. ‘We reacted too late. We need to be fresh minds, start again and analyse what we can do better and move forward. The international break comes at the right moment for us to analyse and come back refreshed.’ JACK GAUGHAN
