Sports.title: Now go after the rest of the cheating Aussies: Usman Khawaja's explosive claims bring more shame onto a team who were cowardly as well as complicit - they must surely be punished and captain Pat Cummins cannot escape, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Now go after the rest of the cheating Aussies: Usman Khawaja's explosive claims bring more shame onto a team who were cowardly as well as complicit - they must surely be punished and captain Pat Cummins cannot escape, writes OLIVER HOLT

Usman Khawaja is adamant about it. ‘It was all of us,’ he writes in his soon-to-be-published autobiography. ‘Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us…If you read my story, if you read what I’m saying, I have numerous times said it’s us, the team. This is the team. It’s not Steve, Davey and Bangers. It’s all of us.’

His revelations about the Sandpapergate cheating scandal that rocked world cricket in 2018 and cast captain Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft as scapegoats will detonate another explosion under the Australia cricket team as they are about to head into an Ashes year. Those revelations will turn a dark episode in Australia’s cricket history even darker.

The three players’ admissions of their part in using sandpaper to tamper with the ball during the Third Test of the series between South Africa and Australia at Newlands in Cape Town brought shame on the country.

A particularly tearful mea culpa from Smith at a subsequent press conference has been used to mock him and Australian masculinity ever since.

Each of the three players received bans from Test cricket for their part in the scandal but Khawaja’s revelations not only reopen the wounds of the grisly episode eight years after they thought they had banished it but also raise the possibility of Australia’s bowling attack being decimated before they fly to England for the Ashes series in the summer.

The significance of Khawaja’s revelations lies primarily in his allegations that Australia had experimented with the same ball-tampering tactics at the previous Test in Port Elizabeth but also in the fact that the majority of the team dodged responsibility for the cheating even though Khawaja says they were all complicit.

Cameron Bancroft (left), Steve Smith (right) and David Warner took the blame for Sandpapergate but Usman Khawaja has now revealed the whole team knew of the cheating

The rest of the team, pictured here in the Sandpapergate Test, must surely be punished

That second revelation strikes at the heart of the ethos of Australian cricket because it destroys the idea of ‘mateship’ within the ranks of the side.

What Khawaja is saying is that the majority of the team let three others take the fall when they should have stood together as one. They failed to do that. They let their mates swing.

One of those men who stood back and watched as Warner, Smith and Bancroft were thrown to the wolves was Pat Cummins, now the Australia captain. If what Khawaja says is true, then how can Cummins’ authority over the team remain? If what Khawaja says is true, then how can a man who did not stay true to the spirit of the Baggy Green retain the respect of the players he leads?

If what Khawaja says is true, then surely it will be incumbent on Cricket Australia to impose bans on the rest of the players in that Cape Town Test. Warner and Smith were both suspended from Test cricket for a year. The same sanction, presumably, may now be visited on the rest of the side.

Team sport, after all, ought to be about collective responsibility and that responsibility is something that those four bowlers, who still constitute the majority of the Australian attack now, dodged together.

They are very much in the line of fire now as Australian cricket stumbles into a new crisis.

Part of Khawaja’s motivation appears to be guilt that he did not stand up for his mates when he should have done.

He has watched, he writes in the autobiography, as Warner has ‘copped it’ over and over again for his part in the cheating and resolutely refused to implicate others. Warner, he suggests, has chosen secret honour. Others have not.

Khawaja (left) has decided to spill the beans in his soon-to-be-released autobiography and now serious questions must be asked of captain Pat Cummins (right)

But there will surely be wider repercussions for the Australian game now. In 2021, Australia’s bowlers in the Newlands Test – Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon – released a statement in which they denied any knowledge of a foreign substance used to change the condition of the ball.

‘We feel compelled to put the key facts on the record again,’ the bowlers’ statement said.

‘We did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball until we saw the images on the big screen at Newlands.

‘And to those who, despite the absence of evidence, insist that 'we must have known' about the use of a foreign substance simply because we are bowlers, we say this: The umpires during that Test match, Nigel Long and Richard Illingworth, both very respected and experienced umpires, inspected the ball after the images surfaced on the TV coverage and did not change it because there was no sign of damage.’

Those words will be picked over relentlessly in the next few weeks as Khawaja’s revelations are released in extracts in the Australian media.

Smith said he was left traumatised by the Sandpaper gate scandal in 2018 - pictured here with his father as he made his tearful public apology in Sydney

‘Same old Aussies, always cheating,’ is the common refrain of the Barmy Army during Ashes contests and it will be sung with renewed gusto now as one of the sport’s most infamous cheating scandals brings even more shame on Australia.

‘At the end of the day,’ Khawaja said, ‘I still think it’s the right thing to do for particularly those three guys (Warner, Smith and Bancroft). And I think most of the guys in the team, at some level, will be relieved that we can finally move on.’

It is a nice idea but the reality is that Australian cricket has been plunged into a new world of pain.

Sports.title: Non-league footballer in stable condition after collapsing in warm-up and rushed to hospital, leading to match being abandoned
Sports.content:
Truro City's match against Folkestone Invicta was abandoned due to a medical emergency on Saturday after a footballer collapsed during the warm-up.

Yassine En-Neyah, 26, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing while preparing with his team-mates on the pitch. It was later confirmed he was in a stable condition.

The former Nottingham Forest academy youngster had been named among the substitutes to face Folkestone in the National League South game in Kent.

A club statement on Saturday read: 'Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.

'Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.'

The club added a welcome on Saturday night, saying: 'He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation.

Truro City's clash with Folkestone Invicta has been abandoned due to a medical emergency

Yassine En-Neyah - pictured before the game - was named on the bench to face Folkestone

Club Statement:



Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.



Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.



We will… pic.twitter.com/IyiF2VIFMz — Truro City FC (@TCFC_Official) November 7, 2026

'The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

'Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.'

Truro City's players had earlier gathered around the rear of the ambulance where En-Neyah was being treated to shield him from view.

The Moroccan-born former Republic of Ireland youth international began his career at Nottingham Forest, making his professional debut in January 2020 as a substitute during an FA Cup third-round clash against Chelsea.

After being released by Forest in 2021, the winger has played for multiple non-league sides including Shelbourne, Waterford and Maldon & Tipree.

Having briefly represented Truro in 2023, En-Neyah returned to the Tinners for a second spell in 2024, where he has remained since.

When he signed his new Truro contract last season, En-Neyah admitted he didn't think twice about the decision to stay.

'Truro's been my home for the last couple of seasons and it was a very easy decision,' he told BBC Radio Cornwall.

'I feel home so I just want to continue working hard and help the club achieve greater things.

'It wasn't a case of having to think about it, it was just a matter of getting it done and continuing to work hard and do well for the club and for myself.'

Sports.title: Donald Trump offers UFC chief Dana White press secretary job in bizarre replacement for fired Katie Zacharia
Sports.content:
Donald Trump offers UFC chief Dana White press secretary job in bizarre replacement for fired Katie Zacharia

President Donald Trump has offered the role of press secretary to UFC supremo Dana White in a bizarre turn of events in Washington.

Trump called White a 'violent fighter and warrior' who he wants to be at the helm of his press briefings following the turmoil of the midterms and Democratic 'bluenami.'

In a post on Truth Social, the president wrote: 'I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States.

'I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris[son].

'We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!'

White posted an image of himself behind the press podium with the caption 'on to the next chapter' and reposted Trump's post on his Instagram Story.

It's unclear if the UFC boss, who has been a staple figure in the MAGA world since Trump's first administration, will take up the role. The White House hung up on the Daily Mail reporter who asked for clarity on the matter.

White is set to meet with the president in the Oval Office on Monday, TMZ reported.

Trump is currently without a press secretary after he ousted Katie Zacharia last month, who was in the coveted White House position for just five days.

After a disastrous first press conference and another train wreck interview, Trump made the decision to remove MAGA diehard Zacharia from the post back in October.

President Donald Trump attends the UFC 314 event alongside UFC President and CEO Dana White

Dana White is seen with the president in Colorado Springs, Colorado, on February 20, 2020, ahead of a 'Keep America Great' rally

'You don't have to do this if you don't want to,' Trump said he told Zacharia. 'Honestly if I were you I'd reconsider.'

Her tenure was shorter than Anthony Scaramucci's famously brief 11 days as White House communications director in 2017. She previously only lasted six weeks as a communications adviser at Homeland Security earlier this year.

Zacharia was made press secretary after Karoline Leavitt announced her resignation in August, after serving in the role since the beginning of Trump's second administration.

Leavitt, known for her sharp tongue and quick answers to the fiery White House press corps, stepped down to focus on being a mother after welcoming her daughter to the world earlier this year.

White, who is worth a reported $500 million, is close friends with Trump and held his UFC 250 event at the White House earlier this year.

The controversial job offer was also extended to various UFC fighters, including Russians Makhachev and Nurmagomedov.

White and Trump have been allies for years with the first UFC event under his leadership taking place at the Trump Taj Mahal in Atlantic City in 2001 - an event Trump described as 'the most unbelievable thing I've ever seen'.

It's unclear if the UFC boss, who has been a staple figure in the MAGA world since Trump's first administration, will take up the role. The White House hung up on the Daily Mail reporter who asked for clarity on the matter

White, who is worth a reported $500 million, is close friends with Trump

White speaks during an election night event for Republican presidential nominee Trump at the Palm Beach Convention Center on November 6, 2024 in West Palm Beach

The friends shake hands at a Keep America Great rally on February 20, 2020

Trump later asked White to speak at the Republican National Convention in 2016, where he eventually won the presidential nomination for the first time. Despite pleas from his inner circle to reject it, White took to the stage.

When Trump ran for president in 2016, White was one of the loudest voices in his corner.

'Everybody said, "Don't do it. Don't do it",' White told TIME earlier this year.

'It was about more than "You don't want to get into politics." The bigger one was "He's never gonna win." And I was like, "Well, whether he wins or not, the guy's been a good friend to me".'

Trump was interviewed for the piece and commented: 'He's a very good speaker, very inspirational-type speaker. I know guys who are successful, they can't speak.'

And after January 6, 2021, when corporations and celebrities distanced themselves from Trump en masse, White stood firm.

He didn't scrub Trump from the promotional material, but instead he walked Trump into arenas and made him visible at a moment when visibility was a statement.

Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was ousted from the position in just under a week. The ordeal happened weeks out from the midterms - which ended up being a disaster for the GOP

Trump is currently without a press secretary after he got rid of Zacharia last month

Leavitt, known for her sharp tongue and quick answers to the fiery White House press corps, stepped down to focus on being a mother after welcoming her daughter to the world earlier this year

White also played a huge role in helping Trump regain the White House in 2024. He reveals he had a 'philosophy' that if Trump 'stayed on Fox News, he couldn't win the election'.

Instead, he gathered up podcasters and influencers to expose a new audience to the now-president that powered him back to the presidency.

Trump appeared on shows with the Nelk Boys, Will Compton and Taylor Lewan of 'Bussin' with the Boys', Adin Ross, Theo Von and, most notably, Joe Rogan.

When asked how significant White was to Trump's campaign to beat Kamala Harris, he replied: 'Very important. He introduced me to people I never heard of, young kids.

'I mean, I was being interviewed by 20-year-old kids. I'm saying, "Where the hell did you meet these people?" They're called influencers.

'But I did a lot. I became friendly with some of them. They're nice kids, and they do have a big audience, and everything helps.'

Sports.title: Commentators haven't the foggiest idea what's going on: Thick mist ruins FA Cup clash for TV viewers - and fans use phone torches to see the action!
Sports.content:
Commentators haven't the foggiest idea what's going on: Thick mist ruins FA Cup clash for TV viewers - and fans use phone torches to see the action!

'Peak FA Cup', was the verdict from TV viewers watching (or trying to watch) the clash between Notts County and Altrincham as thick fog obscured the action.

Those tuning in on TNT Sports were baffled by what was actually happening in the game when the mist descended at Moss Lane.

Commentators saw the funny side, with Adam Summerton chuckling, saying: 'Your guess is as good as mine at the minute,' when asked by his partner what was going on.

As the match progressed, the foggy conditions only worsened and it became difficult for the players to see far in front of them, let alone those trying to spectate in the ground and at home.

Even though the conditions appeared to simply be deep fog, one local claimed it was smoke from local firework parties causing the white-out.

They wrote: 'It is smoke from the bonfire night fireworks and bonfires. I live round the corner, it is literally just smoke. All you can smell in the air is smoke.'

The fog is closing in at Moss Lane! 🌫️



Conditions are getting tricky for Altrincham and Notts County 👀



📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/gTM9e3KA2w — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 7, 2026

Fog descended on the FA Cup clash between Altrincham and Notts County and TV viewers could hardly tell what was going on

Fans pulled out the torches on their phones in a light-hearted bid to see more of the action

Despite the lack of quality action for fans to watch at Moss Lane, plenty of them saw the funny side and even took out their phone torches in unison to try and cut through the gloom.

Those at home poked fun at the scene, with one posting: 'Can you ask the ref that if it goes to pens they bring the goal closer to the cameras so we can watch them?'

Another wrote: 'Where's the orange ball? I miss those days!'

Not everyone could see the humour in the situation, with one user on X writing: 'I'm sorry but this is ridiculous it should be abandoned. You could be miles offside.'

The game itself went to penalties, which caused further problems for the commentators, who had to largely base their reactions on the crowd directly behind the goal.

Ultimately, Notts County survived a scare from the non-league outfit and won 3-2 in the shootout.

Rosaire Longelo netted the final spot-kick to fire the Magpies into the second round of the FA Cup.

They'd had to fight back from 2-1 down in normal time after Lucas Weaver and then Lewis Banks put Altrincham in front.

Callum Roberts scored to make it 2-2 and neither side could find a winner in extra-time, meaning an already memorable game was settled in a fitting and dramatic fashion.

Sports.title: Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE

Just when Newcastle looked set for victory after Jacob Murphy had borrowed Amar Dedic's bow to arrow them into a late lead, they turned the weapon on themselves.

After a week in which Dedic, Bosnia's answer to Robin Hood, had made headlines when pursued by police for wandering around the Northumberland countryside with his hunting gear, the Geordies were ready to rob the good folk of west London after Murphy found the target ten minutes from time.

Less than three minutes later and they were picking the arrow from their own foot. William Osula failed to protect possession and allowed Fulham to enter the penalty area. Then, with the ball bouncing around the goalmouth, it was home substitute Rodrigo Muniz who pounced to punish Newcastle's scruffy defending.

'Slapstick', visiting boss Matthias Jaissle later called it.

The German also said that his team deserved to win but you got the impression he was relieved to emerge without defeat, especially as the performance was improved on the back of a run of four losses in five.

Newcastle's second-half spirit also showed a response to a week of noise centred on dressing-room unrest, not to mention Dedic's police drama.

Jacob Murphy thought he had won it for Newcastle after scoring late on at Craven Cottage

Rodrigo Muniz netted moments later after sloppy defending from Newcastle, earning a 1-1 draw

Matthias Jaissle's side were much improved but must cut out the errors to win matches

And Jaissle was right in that his team could have left with three points had master archer Harvey Barnes not missed a hat-trick of chances.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno 7; Castagne 6 (Tete 77, 5), Affengruber 6, Bassey 6, Robinson 5; Berge 6, Charles 6; Bobb 6 (Sessegnon 78, 6), King 7 (Palacios 72, 5), Iwobi 6; Garcia 4 (Muniz 65, 8) Subs not used: Lecomte, Andersen, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, Kevin Scorer: Muniz 83 Manager: Alvaro Arbeloa 6 Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 7; Dedic 6, Thiaw 7 (Schar 85, 6), Burn 7, Hall 6; Nico Gonzalez 5 (Miley 61, 6), Steur 7 (Fernandez-Pardo 74, 5); Murphy 8, Wissa 6 (Willock 61, 5), Barnes 6; Osula 5 (Elanga 85) Subs not used: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Bazoumana Toure Scorer: Murphy 80 Manager: Matthias Jaissle 7 Referee: Rob Jones Attendance: 27,367 MOM: Murphy

The winger is the player to whom they'd want those opportunities to fall, too. But twice before half-time, when denied by Bernd Leno from close range, and then again when lashing wide after the break, he failed to give his side the advantage.

Murphy corrected his team-mate's finishing when capitalising on a loose pass from Cesar Palacios and slamming into the bottom corner from 25 yards, but that joy was short-lived.

In truth, there hadn't been much joy to behold all afternoon. The draw keeps both sides in the bottom half of the table, and that is where they will likely stay.

The first half, in particular, had very strong last-on-Match-of-the-Day vibes.

Newcastle thought they had a 33rd-minute lead when Dan Burn stole in at the near post to flick home from Murphy's low cross.

What the officials had spotted at the far post was linebacker Yoane Wissa pinning defender Timothy Castagne, and so playing Burn onside. It was the right call, even if Jaissle disagreed

'I learned that word here, a 'soft' decision. In my eyes, it was not right,' he said. 'But I was pleased with our complete commitment and togetherness.

'We grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on. We showed the fundamentals.'

DEDIC-ATION

Dedic twice came close to creating goals with teasing crosses from the right, and you wondered if he would have mimicked Barnes' trademark archer celebration had they been converted.

He was kept away from the media post-match, but Jaissle did say: 'He played well, right? It (the bow & arrow incident) didn't affect him. He was not aware of the rules. We don't need to make a big deal out of it.'

KING CONCERN

Fulham's Josh King was included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday, the club's first Three Lions call-up in eight years. He, however, now needs a scan on a tight groin before learning if he's fit enough to feature.

Did the 19-year-old play like a would-be England international? He was his side's best player in the first half, even if that was a low bar to hurdle. One volley would have raised the roof had it gone in, so sweet was the connection from 20 yards. Lukas Hornicek needed every inch of his 6ft 6in frame to dive and save. And that, too, was a recurring theme, Newcastle's reliance on the big Czech to bail them out when giving up chances.

Like Newcastle, however, Fulham simply weren't good enough to take them.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break. There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation. But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch. If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot. In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke. The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise. Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6) Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly Booked: Manager: Mikel Arteta 6 Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6) Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz Booked: Coyle, Gourna-Douath Manager: Sergej Jakirovic 7 Ref: Farai Hallam 7 For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition. Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack. It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull. Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting. Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend. It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them. Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious. Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London Arteta tells wasteful Arsenal to be more 'chaotic' Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City. Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors. 'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta. 'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that. 'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic. 'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.' Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy. The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor. Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position. On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty. 'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it. 'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.' By Isaan Khan The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick. A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right? Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective. None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak. Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour. By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening. First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner. Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

Sports.title: Furious Tottenham set to complain to authorities after Jayden Bogle escapes red card in Leeds' 1-0 win at Elland Road
Sports.content:
Tottenham are to issue a formal complaint over the decision not to show a red card to Leeds defender Jayden Bogle after his challenge on Mathys Tel at Elland Road.

Video replays showed Bogle catch the Spurs forward on the back of his left ankle in the first half of Saturday’s lunchtime kick off but despite a lengthy review by the VAR, referee Jon Brooks was not sent to the pitchside monitor.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0 through a Noel Okafor goal.

Spurs, who will lodge their protest with Pro Ref, may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta in the previous Saturday’s clash at the Tottenham Stadium for his foul on Micky van de Ven.

On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card but it was upgraded after a video assistant referee review.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC that the Leeds defender was ‘fortunate’ not to be dismissed.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0

Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for this foul on Micky van de Ven in the previous Saturday’s clash

‘Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent,’ Cann said. ‘He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch.’

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi was more critical of his own players afterwards, but did say of the decision: 'I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor.

'If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve.'

The decision will be reviewed by the Key Match Incidents Panel in the coming days. Mateta is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card he received in their 2–0 defeat to Tottenham.

Sports.title: Australia star says ALL players knew about sandpaper scandal in bombshell claim
Sports.content:
Australia star says ALL players knew about sandpaper scandal in bombshell claim

Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has lifted the lid on the sandpaper scandal of 2018, claiming the whole team new about the cheating against South Africa

View 3 Images Usman Khawaja has lifted the lid on the sandpaper scandal (Image: Darrian Traynor/Getty Images)

The entire Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball against South Africa in 2018, despite the scandal being pinned on three people.

‌



‌



That's according to ex-Aussie batter Usman Khawaja who has come clean in an explosive interview ahead of the release of a new book. The use of sandpaper in the Cape Town Test saw Cameron Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith take the rap for the blatant cheating.

‌



TV cameras caught Bancroft, a junior member of the team, using sandpaper to help generate reverse-swing in the third Test. Bancroft served a nine-month ban, while captain Smith and vice-captain Warner were banned for a year.

‌



The rest of the team denied any knowledge of the cheating and bowling quartet Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon released a statement in 2021, hitting out at those questioning their integrity. Their claims of innocence are now set for fresh scrutiny after Khawaja's comments.

Mary Earps announces birth of 'secret' baby with partner in adorable video post READ MORE :

Former champion boxer Josh Frederiksen dead at 36 after tragic skydiving accident READ MORE :

“It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,” he told the Sydney Morning Herald. “In an ideal world, I don’t want to do this. I don’t want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth. The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now.

“Maybe I thought Davey (Warner) would have exposed it, or someone else would have talked about it more. I just didn’t think it was going to come down to this.”

‌



A spokesperson for Cricket Australia told the Press Association: “There has been a great deal of speculation in the eight years since the 2018 Cape Town Test, including extensive media coverage throughout last month’s series in South Africa.

View 3 Images Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft facing the music in 2018 (Image: Ashley Vlotman/Gallo Images/Getty Images)

‌



“During this time there has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case. All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process.”

Khawaja also slammed Cricket Australia's decision not to interview him while investigating the scandal. "I was sitting next to Cam Bancroft that whole Test match, and I didn’t get interviewed," he said. "I thoroughly feel that I didn’t get interviewed because they knew that I wanted to take it as a team, because they knew I was ready to tell the truth if I was interviewed.

‌



"And I was waiting for my phone to ring. It just never rang, and then the penalties were given, and I couldn’t believe it."

View 3 Images Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon and Mitchell Starc claimed no knowledge of sand paper (Image: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

‌



Khawaja played 88 Tests for Australia and has decided to bare all in his new autobiography, Sabr, which is likely to cause fresh turmoil in the country. The former batter claims he wanted the entire team to front up and accept culpability at the time, rather than allowing Bancroft, Smith and Warner to shoulder the blame.

“Even in the change rooms when I was talking to them after the game, I said, ‘Take this as a team. We did this as a team’," he added.

Article continues below

“I’m not doing this for any other reason than I think it’s the right thing to do. I’ve always felt like there’s more to life than just cricket, and these guys, in some respect, deserve that justice. And it just doesn’t feel like anyone’s going to give it to them.”

Sports.title: Unai Emery sends Jamie Carragher firm message over Aston Villa plans after legal threat
Sports.content:
Unai Emery sends Jamie Carragher firm message over Aston Villa plans after legal threat

Unai Emery is convinced he can achieve big things at Aston Villa as he prepares to sign a new contract in the wake of comments from Jamie Carragher that sparked a backlash

View 3 Images Unai Emery has big ambitions at Aston Villa (Image: Javier Borrego/Getty Images)

Unai Emery has insisted that he can win the Champions League with Aston Villa in eye-catching comments which follow the club's legal threat towards Jamie Carragher.

‌



‌



Carragher caused a stir by suggesting that Emery would be a good fit to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager. His comments - plus a subsequent sweary message to angry Villa fans - prompted Villa to take the extraordinary step of threatening the Sky Sports pundit with legal action.

‌



The former Liverpool defender was forced to issue an apology, but has since doubled down on his opinion that Villa are some way behind United in the hierarchy of global football. Writing in the Telegraph, Carragher said it was "beyond doubt" that United eclipse Villa on every conceivable metric.

‌



"It did not strike me as controversial to suggest that when a club of United’s size wants Aston Villa’s managers or players, traditionally they get them," he added.

‌



Emery is poised to show his commitment to Villa by signing a new contract and, speaking ahead of a trip to Old Trafford with his side on Sunday, insisted he can achieve his dreams by staying put.

“Aston Villa won [the European Cup] in 1982. They were favourites at that moment? I think not,” Emery said. “ Leicester won the league 10 years ago. In football, everything can happen. Of course, the favourite teams, they are (competing for) the Premier League and Champions League.

‌



“With Villarreal, we played in the semi-final four years ago. We were close. Borussia Dortmund played three years ago in the final. They are teams not favourites, but sometimes they are having their opportunity to fight for this title.

“In the Premier League, it is more difficult. We finished two times fourth in the league and in those times we were in December two or three points behind Manchester City and Arsenal. To keep the consistency in 38 matches is the difficult way. But we are working, trying to get our best.

‌



View 3 Images Aston Villa had won all three of their Champions League games this season before losing 3-0 to Barcelona (Image: Gongora/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“Of course, it is very difficult to win the Premier League, very difficult to win the Champions League. I have my dreams, thinking in objectives like that. In all my moments working in all the clubs, I was setting my demand high and my objectives high, sometimes achieving and sometimes not.

“Last year, we achieved the Europa League, which is the second competition in Europe. Still being positive how we can continue improving, how we can even not being contender in the Premier League or Champions League, we have to compete and we have to try to get our best. Over the time, we will see how we can achieve our objectives.”

‌



Carragher has argued that, while United are currently below Villa in terms of results, the Red Devils remains a bigger job with greater expectations.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher was threatened with legal action by Aston Villa (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



"United clearly are not at the level of Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and PSG right now," he wrote. "But when any manager goes to Old Trafford, over the course of their contract they will be expected to build a team that will go head to head with those European giants. Anything less is failure. Villa are not judged to that standard.

"Emery is Villa’s best coach since their 1981 title-winner Ron Saunders, but he can take his side to Barcelona, get soundly beaten 3-0, and it will be brushed off as an understandable setback against European aristocracy. United managers cannot suffer that kind of loss without more scrutiny."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury issues response to Oleksandr Usyk trilogy snub
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury issues response to Oleksandr Usyk trilogy snub

Tyson Fury is not giving up hope on fighting Oleksandr Usyk for a third time despite the Ukrainian brutally snubbing his longtime rival

View Image Oleksandr Usyk and Tyson Fury fought twice in 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

Oleksandr Usyk has plans to return to cruiserweight for his next fight - but longtime rival Tyson Fury is not buying it.

‌



‌



The Ukrainian had relinquished his titles earlier this year, but still had plans to stay at heavyweight. Usyk was eyeing up a farewell fight against Deontay Wilder in 2027, but talks fell through. He also also expressed interest in a third meeting with Fury - despite beating the Morecambe brawler twice in 2024.

‌



Fury has long called for a third clash with Usyk and has insisted he should have won the previous two encounters. The 'Gypsy King' will return to the ring next month when he takes on Anthony Joshua. Usyk's future remains up in the air but is expected to fight next year.

‌



And he is hoping for a potential showdown with undefeated sensation David Benavidez. Usyk recently told DAZN: “I cleaned out heavyweight and now I’ll go back to my weight. Now [I weigh] 96/97kg. Today there is change at heavyweight, if I have an opportunity at cruiserweight, I’m back. It’s a big fight because Benavidez is a big champion. When I have an opportunity, I take this opportunity. This is life.”

Fury, though, is not convinced and is adamant that the Ukrainian will only fight again if he is the one standing across the ring from him. Speaking to Michelle Joy Phelps, he said: "I do not think that is going to happen (Usyk moving down to cruiserweight). If it is not me then Oleksandr Usyk will not be fighting again. Definitely not.

Fury has been handed some hope that a trilogy could come to fruition after holding talks with Usyk recently. The Brit offered the Ukrainian the chance to fill in for Joshua should something happen, but Usyk declined.

The 39-year-old is currently enjoying time with his family, but is targeting a potential return in March. “I actually spoke with Oleksandr to say ‘if Joshua does not fight, we will do it.’ And he said he was busy," Fury said. Sports.title: Error-prone Gianluigi Donnarumma could cost Man City with Arsenal boasting rock-solid David Raya
Sports.content:
The more Enzo Maresca protests, the less convincing he sounds.

The Manchester City manager must prefer to answer questions about Gianluigi Donnarumma than the looming question marks over the club's guilty verdict, but only just.

They have been a recurring theme this season - and for good reason. The stats show that Donnarumma has made three errors leading to goals in all competitions this season and there have been plenty of other moments of peril to go with them.

City's giant goalkeeper was beaten at the near post by Ridle Baku's attempted cross due to his poor positioning in their 3-2 win over RB Leipzig on Wednesday. In the 2-1 defeat by Aston Villa 11 days prior, he let Nicolas Jackson's low shot squirm through his grasp.

‌



Sir Alex Ferguson is a painful reminder of Man Utd's glory days 40 years on from his arrival READ MORE :

These are not isolated incidents. In the 1-0 win over Coventry in early September, Donnarumma nearly allowed a routine back-pass from Abdukodir Khusanov over the goalline. He was forced to scramble it off the line in a near-calamitous moment that was the headline of a jittery performance.

And yet Maresca has refused to even entertain the topic as one open to debate. "It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," Maresca said after the Leipzig error. "We recognise that; he knows that it's a mistake, but now it's Nottingham Forest away, we need to be focused on that."

The City boss was echoing his previous comments after the Villa defeat. "Gigio, since we started, is doing well," he insisted. "Like any player or any manager at some point, he is making some mistakes, but it's part of the season.

View 4 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma has struggled at times this season (Image: Maja Hitij/Getty Images)

‌



"They are playing so many games and minutes that sometimes it's impossible not to make some mistakes. He's quite a strong guy. He knows when he makes some mistakes. He doesn't need us to tell him. Sometimes it's so clear, so they recognise that. It's part of the game."

Of course, mistakes are part of the game. But currently they are not a part of David Raya's game: the Arsenal goalkeeper is yet to make an error leading to a goal in the Premier League this season. And in a title race that could be decided by tiny margins, it is a difference worth exploring, even if Maresca doesn't want to.

Donnarumma 'confusing himself'

Former City goalkeeper Joe Hart launched an impassioned defence of Donnarumma on The Overlap Daily, insisting that the Italian was trying to cut out Baku's cross and be a team player when he was beaten by a freak goal. He also pointed out that Donnarumma made a world-class save only he was capable of in the same game.

Yet even the staunch City supporter conceded Donnarumma was "confusing himself" through his positioning and should instead be more focused on preventing "the worst-case scenario", rather than being constantly on the front foot being proactive.

‌



There is another factor that should be laid out in Donnarumma's defence: the age-old truism that a goalkeeper is only as good as his defence. Donnarumma has faced 33 shots on target in the Premier League this season, which is 11 more than Raya.

City, and in particular Marc Guehi, have been error-prone and unusually shaky at the back this season, while Arsenal - with their beefed-up backline thanks to the signing of Ezri Konsa - have been typically resolute. Arsenal therefore have six clean sheets to City's three in the Premier League, having conceded five goals to City's 10.

View 4 Images Marc Guehi has also been at fault for goals this season (Image: Richard Sellers/Getty Images)

Square peg in a round hole

Concerns over Donnarumma are nothing new. As soon as City decided to sign him from Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2025, there were question marks over how he'd fit into Pep Guardiola's playing style. The Italy international is renowned as a fantastic shot-stopper, not a ball-playing keeper of the modern era.

‌



Donnarumma only ended up playing one season under Guardiola before Maresca arrived, but those question marks remain. Despite his repeated defending of his goalkeeper and admission that Geronimo Rulli isn't really an option as a replacement, it is something Maresca is aware of.

"I think a few times tonight it's not Gigio's mistake, it's more the wrong decisions to go back to Gigio," he said after the 2-0 win over Porto in September. "Sometimes we go too many times back to Gigio when we don't need."

View 4 Images David Raya has been rock-solid for Arsenal (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/Getty Images)

Former Premier League goalkeeper Brad Friedel believes that while Raya was recruited specifically to fit Mikel Arteta's style, Donnarumma is more of a square peg in a round hole.

‌



"They're completely different goalkeepers, and it's about how you want to play," Friedel told Mirror Football on behalf of Grosvenor Sport. "I mean, Donnarumma stands at six foot five and Raya's barely six foot.

"I would say Raya is probably better on crosses than Donnarumma, believe it or not, because he has great timing and great spring when he comes out for a ball. I think Donnarumma is a huge presence in goal. If you're a striker and you look up, you're probably thinking, where can I strike to score?

"Whereas Raya is a little bit different. He uses his quickness for his saves. So as a striker, you probably think the corner's free, and then before you know it, Raya's hand's there."

‌



Raya has the edge

"They're completely different goalkeepers," Friedel added. "Playing out of the back, I would say Raya has the advantage. Certain shot-stopping areas, probably Donnarumma has a little advantage because of his size.

"But it's really what you want from your goalkeeper, too. With Raya, he fits perfectly in Arteta's style and system, and looks like a character as well, and he has been a huge part of that.

"With Donnarumma, I don't have that many games to go by yet to know if he's the perfect fit for Maresca's style or not. But he's definitely a quality goalkeeper. But I would probably give Raya a little bit of an advantage over him with everything that I just said, as far as fitting in a system."

Arsenal, it seems, have the best of both worlds in Raya. City, however, may need to adapt their playing style to avoid more costly errors from Donnarumma.

Sports.title: Micah Richards reveals secret torment of dad's shock death and how he's supporting young son
Sports.content:
When BBC pundit Micah Richards commentated live to 20 million viewers on England's World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina this summer, he did it for his dad. He had just received the devastating news of his father, Lincoln’s “unexpected and shocking” death, but says: “I had my dad’s voice in my head telling me, ‘you've got to make the most of this opportunity,’ and that's what I tried to do. I did it for him.

“Everyone grieves differently. If you watch the game back, I kept tapping my foot. All these emotions were going through my body. I was getting myself through it.” Micah, 38, says his dad had been ill for a few years, but does not disclose his cause of death, just saying: “I didn't think it would happen then.”

An electrician, Lincoln also ran a grassroots football team - raising Micah and his seven siblings with the pundit’s mum, Heather, who worked in a social services office. Sadly, the couple separated, but Micah, who is single, says they both encouraged him to play football.

View 6 Images “I had my dad’s voice in my head telling me, ‘you've got to make the most of this opportunity,’ and that's what I tried to do. I did it for him." (Image: BBC)

‌



Starting with kickabouts in Chapeltown, Leeds, where he grew-up, Micah became a star at Man City, winning two Premier Leagues and one FA Cup trophy with the Blues. At 18 he became the youngest defender ever to play for England, and represented Team GB at the London 2012 Olympics.

Now living in Harrogate, North Yorkshire, he says: “My dad took me absolutely everywhere. “He probably missed 10 or 20 games throughout my whole career. He was just amazing. He always said, from when I was young, ‘If you apply yourself properly, you'll make it.’ He said, ‘The minute you take your eye off the ball, then someone will take your place.’ But he always believed that I had the ability to do it. It was just keeping me on track.”

As a teenager, when his friends were all out at clubs and discos, Lincoln told him: “That'll all come. Don't worry about that, just stay focused.” Now, life without his dad, who had been dealing with a drink problem, is tough.

Micah says: “He was the one who always gave good advice. I've got four sisters and three brothers - and I’ve lost count of the number of cousins. If I ever needed advice, he would be the one who I would turn to. But now, essentially, everyone turns to me. I'm like, ‘I'm only 38, I've not got the answers. Just do your best.’ What am I to say?”

‌



View 6 Images A young Micah (left), with brother and dad Lincoln

Despite his success, Micah says he has “wild imposter syndrome all the time.” Advising people just to “show up” if they want success, he adds: “Everyone looks at my career and says, ‘you played for England, won the Premier League, now working for all the big broadcasters.’ But I'm just enjoying the ride.”

Again, he praises his dad for his wise words in keeping him grounded. He says: “My dad always used to say to me, ‘never forget where you come from.’ What he meant by that is, just know if you're earning more money, or if you've got a bigger house, make sure you stay humble. Make sure you're always working hard. Make sure you have compassion with other people.’”

While Chapeltown was a tough area to grow up, Micah adds: “ I never strayed because I was always focused on football.” And now Micah is an ambassador for the Specsavers campaign, Best Worst Team, to support grassroots football. A community-driven initiative, Specsavers searches the UK for rock-bottom, underfunded grassroots and Sunday League football teams that suffer heavy losses, bad luck, or comical on-pitch blunders and gives them a makeover.

‌



View 6 Images Micah as a little lad. He grew up in Chapeltown, Leeds

This year, they’ve picked Bollington United in Cheshire, who will be given professional professional coaching, high-profile assistant managers and football legends, upgraded kits, and media coverage - before being included in an 8-part YouTube documentary series.

Micah, an assistant manager, says: “My job is to get them off the bottom of the table. Grassroots football gave me stability and a focus. It taught me a lot of things in terms of being personable, in terms of sharing. It makes you resilient. All those things that you need in life. It humbles you, too. I was at Oldham Athletic and I was the best player by far. I went to Man City at 14, and I was the worst.”

But he says Oldham gave him the skills to deal with it, without “throwing your toys out of the pram when you’re not getting picked.” He adds: “Grassroots is so important because that is the foundation, that's where it starts.”

‌



Micah says the community element of grassroots football is also important. He adds: “Community's where you've come from, what you are. My community in Chapeltown was absolutely amazing. I still go back to Chapeltown to get that chicken and rice from Maureen's. And the love and affection I get is just amazing.”

View 6 Images Micah in kids' team (bottom row, centre)

Micah rose through the ranks from grassroots to Leeds City Boys, then Leeds United, Oldham Athletic and Man City. He officially retired from professional football on July 26, 2019, aged 31, due to chronic and persistent knee injuries.

He admits: “I was lost when I retired. I thought, ‘What am I going to do, man?’ But football has given me everything in life, so I feel like I have the responsibility now to sort of send the message that football's for everyone.Grassroots or Premier League, you should enjoy it the same way.” He also works with charities, including British Heart Foundation and Shelter. "Helping people makes me proud,” he says.

‌



Fiercely private, Micah has never revealed the name of his nine year old son, or identified the boy’s mum. But he says: “He plays football, and I am one of those dads who doesn’t say a word on the sideline, but inside, I'm raging. It makes my blood boil when he doesn't work hard.”

And other parents expect a BBC-level commentary. Micah says: “When I'm on the side there, people are always looking at me when their son's scored to say, ‘Ooh, that was good, wasn't it?’ I'm like, ‘yeah, it's good! It's fine!’ What, you want me to give some expert analysis on the goal?’ I'm not going to do that! Let the kids have fun.”

View 6 Images Coaching Sunday League side on Specsavers' Best Worst Team Season 5

BBC Sport, and CBS Sports - Micah says his proudest achievement is being a dad. He says: “Having my son makes me proud. That and making my debut at 17 for Man City.”

‌



His prolific career also means Micah has some enviable contacts. But he confesses that there’s one famous woman who he can’t get hold of. Earlier this year, he claimed on The Rest is Football podcast to co-hosts Alan Shearer and Gary Linekar that Spice Girl, Mel B, was once his babysitter. However, she has neither confirmed nor denied it.

He says: “My mum said she did it, my sister did. And I actually tagged her, which I never do, I never tag people in Instagram. It did happen, but I need the confirmation from Mel B.” It’s not like Scary Spice to be silent!

*Micah Richards returns for season five of Specsavers' Best Worst Team, helping grassroots side Bollington United Sunday Blues, in an eight-part YouTube series.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard bemoans 'big' VAR decisions after Coventry suffer Everton defeat
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard bemoans 'big' VAR decisions after Coventry suffer Everton defeat

Coventry tasted defeat in their Premier League clash with Everton, but the newly promoted team will hard done by following a series of decisions that went against them

View 2 Images Frank Lampard was aggrieved by three decisions (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Frank Lampard was left ruing VAR after Coventry were denied two penalties and had complaints over Thierno Barry's decisive goal in their 3-1 loss away to Everton. Lampard's side took the lead on 52 minutes before Everton scored three unanswered goals to go fifth in the Premier League table on Friday.

‌



‌



But Coventry will feel hard done by over three separate incidents. In the first half, Caleb Yirenkyi had his hair pulled by Everton's James Tarowski in the penalty area.

‌



Then in the second period, Coventry striker Taiwo Awoniyi went tumbling over inside the 18-yard box after a tangle with Vitalii Mykolenko. The Sky Blues were also left aggrieved by Barry's second goal of the night that put Everton 2-1 up, with replays showing that the ball may have hit his hand on the way past Carl Rushworth.

‌



Post-match, Lampard told Match of the Day: "A lot of good stuff in the way we played which makes it really difficult to lose the game. Big decisions affected the game, clearly.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"The VAR ones, VAR looked at them. The hair pull on Caleb. Taiwo, I think he gets contact on the edge of the box which is a penalty. Then the second goal for them comes off the player's hand.

"If you're going to check the angles, there is an angle where it flicks in off his hand. VAR looked at it and decided not. The last touch to score is off the hand, in my opinion.

‌



"I've seen a conclusive angle so I can disagree. I understand they are going to back themselves that's fine and it's hard to say it's not a hair pull. It's an in-between kind of hair pull, that's a funny area to be in so I don't get that one either.

"We have to keep working, I'm seeing progression in the team. We have to work hard. There is a good spirit with us and we have to keep improving."

‌



Should Coventry have had two penalties? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images VAR checked Thierno Barry and Everton's second goal (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, Everton manager David Moyes was asked about the incidents and replied: "I've seen the goal, I didn't think it hit his hand.

"I've certainly not seen the hair pull, that's for sure. I think a hair pull nowadays only gets you a booking, doesn't it? I need to see if it was a hair pull in the first place because I've not seen that myself and I didn't even know about it but I will get a look at it and see."

Article continues below

Friday's result means that Coventry could spend the international break in the relegation zone. Their next game is at home to fellow strugglers Crystal Palace while Everton travel to Brentford.

Sports.title: What Man Utd really think of Eddie Howe as 'Julian Nagelsmann's stock takes big hit'
Sports.content:
What Man Utd really think of Eddie Howe as 'Julian Nagelsmann's stock takes big hit'

Manchester United are much less sold' on Eddie Howe than is widely believed to succeed Michael Carrick as manager at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Man United are said to be 'less sold' on Eddie Howe

A fresh candidate to replace Michael Carrick has surfaced amid suggestions that Manchester United harbour reservations about Eddie Howe. Despite the magnificent fightback triumph against Roma in the Champions League, Carrick continues to be under pressure following a dismal beginning to the campaign.

He had been anticipated to face the sack after the 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth before being granted additional time to reverse the club's fortunes following crisis discussions between United's hierarchy. Success against Aston Villa on Sunday ought to secure him more breathing space, while defeat could edge him nearer to the exit.

Several high-profile names have been mentioned in connection with the position, including Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann. Howe is available after departing Newcastle in the summer and would prove a favoured option amongst certain supporters.

Yet according to the Independent, United are 'much less sold' on the former Newcastle United boss than is commonly thought. The same report indicates that Stuttgart manager Sebastian Hoeness is greatly admired, while Nagelsmann's stock has 'significantly dropped'.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Hoeness's reputation has soared after guiding Stuttgart to Champions League qualification and Germany Cup success since taking over a team facing relegation in 2023. Appointing the 44-year-old would draw comparisons with the recruitment of Ruben Amorim, who was on a comparable upward trajectory with Sporting Clube de Portugal before his troubled stint at Old Trafford.

United are said to be intent on breaking their pattern of interim managers should they choose to move on from Carrick. Temporary appointments have become a recurring solution at Old Trafford in recent years.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer initially came in as a caretaker before securing the full-time position, while Ralf Rangnick was recruited to complete the season after the Norwegian's sacking in November 2021. Carrick himself had a stint as interim boss during the latter half of last season.

View 2 Images United are thought to be less keen on Julian Nagelsmann (Image: Getty)

Nevertheless, according to Sky Sports, director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada would favour a permanent appointment rather than another stopgap solution if they opt to replace Carrick, who currently retains the club's support.

Carrick is encouraging the squad to capitalise on the confidence-boosting victory over Roma when they take on Villa.

He said: "It was a fantastic night as a one-off night. It was a good night for us all, but nothing has been achieved yet. It's one moment we need to use to move forward.

"When you watch the game [against Roma] back, the first half wasn't so bad. There were moments when we left ourselves short, and we need to fix them.

Article continues below

"The first half against Chelsea was very good. We're showing signs of improvement, no doubt, and we need to take that forward."
