World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Who is behind Europe’s suspected hybrid attacks?
World.content:
Bomb hoaxes and supermarket cyberattacks are heightening security fears.

Italy says civilian infrastructure in Europe is “under attack”.

A series of bomb threats this week grounded flights and put airports on high alert. No explosives were found, and the threats appear to be false.

But the disruption is not limited to aviation. Hackers have also targeted supermarket freezers in several countries, raising temperatures and spoiling food.

Together, the incidents are raising fears and questions about a wider campaign of hybrid attacks.

Who could be behind these threats? Are they connected? And can European nations come together to counter these acts of aggression?

World.title: Israel’s president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government
World.content:
Former army chief has 28 days to build a coalition that would end Benjamin Netanyahu’s long tenure as prime minister.

Share Israel’s president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form next government on social media

Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, passing over the former army chief’s rival, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Herzog told Eisenkot of his decision on Saturday evening and will formally hand him the mandate at a ceremony on Sunday, the president’s spokesperson said.

Herzog held consultations with political parties this week to decide who he would appoint to form a government after neither side secured a majority in the October 27 general election.

Some 67 lawmakers, including from Arab-led parties, endorsed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, to form the next government, while only 46 backed Netanyahu, the current prime minister.

Eisenkot will have 28 days – with a possible 14-day extension – to build a coalition of at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, the minimum threshold for a government.

In the October election, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Herzog’s decision, said the president “took the predictable route” in selecting Eisenkot, as he had the highest number of recommendations.



“The hard work will begin now for Eisenkot to put together a government that can pass a vote of confidence at the Knesset that: one, will not break too many of the promises he made on the campaign trail; and two, that can survive the opposition of the right-wing bloc led by Netanyahu,” Odeh said.

If Eisenkot fails to form a government within the allotted time, Herzog will nominate another candidate. If the second nominee fails, a parliament majority can back a third candidate, who will be granted a final 14 days.

If, once again, no government is formed, a new election will be called within 90 days, with Netanyahu staying on as a caretaker prime minister.

United against Netanyahu government

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

Ahmad Tibi, a senior member of the Joint List – a coalition of Arab-led parties that holds 11 seats – told Al Jazeera on Saturday that Herzog’s decision was “expected”.

“We were concerned that the president would move towards a national unity government,” he said, referring to a proposed power-sharing agreement between Eisenkot and Netanyahu.

Instead, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate, granting him a “considerable margin”.

Tibi said he believes Eisenkot is headed for a minority government “with external support from the Arab parties”.

While this would not be a “dream government” for Arab-led parties, Tibi prioritised bringing down “the government of Netanyahu, [Itamar] Ben-Gvir and [Bezalel] Smotrich”.

Hours before Herzog’s decision, Netanyahu had warned that a government formed by the opposition bloc with support from Arab-led parties would lead to Israel’s collapse.

“Such a government, dependent on Islamists, will dismantle the state of Israel from within, as is happening in European countries, and far worse than that,” Netanyahu said in a prerecorded video speech, echoing the language of far-right politicians who falsely claim parts of Europe have come under Islamic law.

Netanyahu “described us as supporters of terrorists and terrorism”, Tibi said. “My response to him is this: Netanyahu is the biggest terrorist in Israel and the region, and the foremost supporter of terrorism, particularly Jewish terrorism in the West Bank and the Palestinian territories.”

Al Jazeera’s Odeh noted that although Eisenkot has expressly said he does not wish to form a government with Arab-led parties, “they both share quite compelling reasons to get rid of Netanyahu”.

World.title: More than 140,000 rally as new protests against rising costs sweep France
World.content:
Tear gas fired in Paris and Lyon as interior minister warns authorities are ‘ready and waiting’ for rioters and looters.

Share More than 140,000 rally as new protests against rising costs sweep France on social media

Tens of thousands of people have protested across France for a fourth consecutive weekend, in another show of anger against the government.

About 146,000 people rallied across the country to protest against the rising cost of living on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the Ministry of the Interior said.

Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital.

The demonstrations come just days after an estimated 575,000 people took part in a rally organised by trade unions.

About 70,000 security personnel were deployed across the country on Saturday, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warning that authorities would be “ready and waiting” for anyone engaging in rioting or looting.

Clashes broke out between police and some protesters in the capital, Paris, despite a lower turnout than in previous weeks.

Footage posted online by the CLPRESS news agency showed police charging at protesters and using tear gas in an attempt to disperse the crowds. A police officer was also seen hitting a protester with a baton.

Police said a group of 200 individuals attacked officers as they were arresting a man who had set fire to a rubbish bin in a square in Paris, the AFP news agency reported.

In the southeastern city of Lyon, police also fired tear gas to disperse several hundred people in the city centre who were blocking a road during an unauthorised gathering.

Reporting from the French capital, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler said people working in a variety of jobs attended Saturday’s demonstrations in support of the student-led movement.



“I spoke to one railway worker who told me it was really important to be here today. He said not only was it important to protest against the cost of living, but that it was also important to support young people,” Butler said.

“There is no doubt that the trade unions, who’ve been weakened in recent years, really feel there is a sense of momentum,” she said. “Many of the workers that I’ve been speaking to say this is their time to really press the government for higher salaries and better facilities.”

The demonstrations in France began in September over poor conditions and a lack of resources at French high schools. The protests later expanded to encompass a host of grievances, linked to worsening living standards. The movement continues to be led by France’s students, but people of all ages have been taking part.

This weekend’s protests take place against the backdrop of France’s upcoming presidential election, due to be held in April. Polls put far-right candidate Marine Le Pen of the National Rally first, followed by far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon of the France Unbowed party.

Melenchon unveiled his programme on Saturday to some 17,000 supporters and promised to do the opposite of incumbent President Emmanuel Macron.

He pledged to stimulate the economy by capitalising on consumer spending and “through billions [of euros] that already exist”, adding that these savings “must be channelled towards our country’s ecological and social needs”.

World.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
World.content:
The shooting happened in one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, a busy location which is also a popular tourist destination.

Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich was there with his Polish girlfriend Dominika. The couple were outside St Mary's Basilica, in the corner of the square, when the shooting started.

Jonathan said: "We ran down the side of the church and through the side door and hid with several other people until the gunfire died down.

"A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms - there were two distinctly different noises."

Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle arrived in Krakow yesterday with her friend Jon for a long weekend.

She said they heard shots from their hotel room but were not sure what was happening until their hotel rang them and told them to "stay in our rooms until further notice".

World.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
World.content:
There was no clear winner following New Zealand's election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show.

Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached.

But opposition leader Chris Hipkins, whose Labour Party won 36 seats, showed no signs of conceding, saying the "shape of the next government" will remain uncertain "for a while".

The tight result followed a campaign shaped by the cost of living and unemployment.

Projections show the National Party on 42 seats and Labour on 36. The Greens are on 16, with ACT on 13, New Zealand First on 12, the Opportunity Party on 7 and Te PÄti MÄori, which represents MÄori interests, on 5.

World.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
World.content:
A US State Department statement about its multi-million dollar reward said it was offering the money for information about the Iranian programme, including "facilities, equipment and associated personnel".

It said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA [the International Atomic Energy Agency] on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like [nuclear] centrifuges".

Centrifuges are needed to produce enriched uranium, which can be used to make reactor fuel for civilian use but also for nuclear weapons if enriched to around 90% purity or higher.

There had been mounting speculation that the US might resume significant strikes in Iran after the midterm elections, though Trump told reporters, prior to the polls, that he was in "no rush" to do so.

In an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms, the president also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme.

This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump said.

The president has repeatedly threatened to bomb the suspected underground site on previous occasions.

However, both Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have said public opposition to the war on Iran fuelled heavy losses for their Republican Party in this week's midterm elections, which has led to speculation the White House may no longer seek an escalation in the conflict.

On Friday, Trump insisted that Iran was keen to end the eight-month conflict with the US, stressing the damage to Tehran's economy and military.

"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday that both sides were "reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented" and that it remained hopeful of a deal being agreed.

Iranian negotiators had discussed with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days once the US met its seven conditions.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

World.title: Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
World.content:
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say that at least 25 people, including women and children, have been killed in airstrikes by Saudi Arabia.

There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.

The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.

Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia.

The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.

A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plan landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.

The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.

Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.

A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

World.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
World.content:
The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.

The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.

But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.

He said there was not a "single market Ã la carte" menu from which the UK could pick and choose what elements it wanted to adopt.

Barnier - who led the EU delegation during Brexit talks between 2016 and 2021, and had a three-month spell as French prime minister in 2024 - said the "door is open" within Europe to the UK rejoining as an EU member.

But he insisted that any move to rejoin the single market - which allows for goods to be freely traded without border controls - would require the UK to follow the same terms as other members.

He added that this included compliance with regulations designed to promote the circulation of goods, services, capital and people, referred to collectively within EU institutions as the "four freedoms".

"There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market."

Since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham has suggested he could commit Labour to pursuing a much closer future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member, though he has ruled out major changes before the next election.

His predecessors have struck a series of deals with the EU on different aspects of how the UK and EU interact post-Brexit.

Both sides are hoping to use a meeting in Brussels in 10 days' time to unveil deals on food standards, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.

World.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
World.content:
In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress.

On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job.

One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests.

"Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it."

World.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
World.content:
Prosecutors in Paraguay have charged former president Santiago PeÃ±a over his alleged role in a banking scandal that led to his impeachment.

He has been accused of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

PeÃ±a, who denies any wrongdoing, was forced from office after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

He was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down but rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached PeÃ±a and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

PeÃ±a, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.

The impeachment charges that led to PeÃ±a's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

PeÃ±a's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal.

"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.

The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.

Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday.

An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, AsunciÃ³n.

Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

PeÃ±a's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.

"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," PeÃ±a said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation, adding his priority was "the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system".

Afterwards, senate president Basilio NÃºÃ±ez said PeÃ±a was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".

World.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.

The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.

The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru, which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop.

"I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts; I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay.

"Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," Pope Leo confirmed.

Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

On Friday, he arrived in Monetevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed.

In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone".

He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia the care he received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment.

He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral.

Pope Leo will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.

On Sunday he will travel to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor Pope Francis who did not return during his own papacy.

The Pope said his visit was about being near the people who were looking to the Church for a message of "hope".

World.title: COP31: What Nigeria, other African countries will push for at UN climate summit
World.content:
As world leaders prepare to convene in Antalya, Türkiye, for the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) says it will push for increased climate finance, including an ambitious replenishment of the Green Climate Fund (GCF), among other priorities.

The group said securing adequate and predictable climate finance, particularly grant-based and concessional funding, would be central to Africa’s negotiating priorities at the conference.

This was disclosed by the AGN Chair, Nana Antwi-Boasiako, on the sidelines of the pre-COP31 meetings on Friday.

The AGN is a coalition of climate change negotiators representing all 54 African countries at the UNFCCC and other international environmental negotiations. Nigeria is a member of the group and will negotiate under its umbrella at COP31.

Nigeria’s delegation and technical support is expected to be led by the Nigeria Council on Climate Change Director General, Omotenioye Majekodunmi.

In a speech recorded and published on the AGN’s social media platforms ahead of the formal commencement of COP31, scheduled to hold from 9 to 20 November, Mr Antwi-Boasiako said African countries would seek stronger financial commitments to support the implementation of their climate targets and adaptation plans.

According to him, the continent has made considerable progress in establishing the structures needed to implement the Paris Agreement, but inadequate financing remains a major obstacle.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He cited progress in developing Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), carbon market mechanisms under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, National Adaptation Plans and the Enhanced Transparency Framework.

However, he said many developing countries were struggling to implement their climate commitments because of financial constraints.

“All these issues are structures that are going to support implementation. The key question now is: Where is the money? Where is the financial ambition to help us implement those commitments that we are making as developing countries?” the AGN chair said.

He noted that the group had submitted proposals for agenda items on tripling adaptation finance and replenishing the Green Climate Fund, describing both as critical to advancing climate action across African countries.

He explained that the proposed agenda item on adaptation finance was intended to provide an opportunity to clarify and establish operational arrangements for implementing the decision reached at COP30 in Belém, Brazil, to triple adaptation finance.

The group also wants COP31 to support an ambitious replenishment of the Green Climate Fund next year, describing the facility as particularly important for financing climate action in African countries.

COP31: From consensus to action

COP31 is expected to focus on translating climate commitments into concrete action, with an emphasis on implementation.

The summit will operate under an unusual shared leadership arrangement, with Türkiye hosting the conference while Australia leads the negotiations. Its overarching slogan, “Where Dialogue Becomes Global Action”, reflects the ambition to move beyond climate pledges towards practical implementation.

Beyond the proposed agenda items, the African negotiating bloc is seeking to defend the existing financial obligations of developed countries under the Paris Agreement.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako said Africa was not opposed to expanding the contributor base for climate finance but insisted that such an arrangement must not be used to weaken the obligations of developed countries.

Citing Article 9 of the Paris Agreement, he explained that Article 9.1 establishes the obligation of developed-country parties to provide financial resources to support developing countries, while Article 9.2 provides for contributions from other countries that are in a position to do so.

He argued that developed countries must demonstrate leadership by fulfilling their existing commitments before seeking additional contributions from other countries.

“You cannot abandon your obligations and use something that is not an obligation to replace your obligation,” he said.

The AGN chair disclosed that two policies had recently been adopted at a Green Climate Fund Board meeting ahead of the fund’s next replenishment. One concerns grant-based contributions, while the other addresses the expansion of the contributor base.

The group hopes the replenishment process will demonstrate leadership from developed countries before other countries are encouraged to contribute.

He also identified disagreements between developed and developing countries over climate finance as a major political divide in the negotiations.

While developing countries are demanding credible, predictable and scaled-up grant-based financing, developed countries have cited geopolitical tensions and domestic economic difficulties as constraints on their ability to increase financial contributions.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako, however, questioned the justification for these funding constraints, arguing that developed countries had demonstrated their ability to mobilise substantial resources when other priorities, including energy security, were at stake.

Africa seeks equitable energy transition

The African Group is also seeking progress on the Just Transition Mechanism, insisting that its implementation must reflect the continent’s development realities.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako said the mechanism should go beyond an energy-focused approach to address workers’ welfare, natural resource management, energy poverty and the broader economic implications of the transition.

He warned against an approach that could leave African economies worse off by forcing them to abandon resources they still need for development.

“For the African continent, we think that the transition away from fossil fuels must happen in a more equitable manner. We have a continent that has other challenges. And so we cannot allow our natural resources to be stranded when we need those resources to develop,” he said.

He acknowledged that discussions on the transition away from fossil fuels were continuing but noted that there was no formal negotiated agenda item specifically addressing the issue.

Rather, the discussions were being pursued through a roadmap developed by the COP Presidency outside the formal negotiation process.

The AGN’s position, however, is that countries with higher emissions and greater levels of pollution should lead the transition before other countries follow.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako stressed that the process must be designed to prevent economic hardship in developing countries.

“It is not just energy transition, but transitioning where we are able to make sure that our economies don’t suffer within the transition,” he said.

Climate and trade, other priorities

The African negotiating bloc is also seeking discussions on climate and trade, particularly the implications of unilateral trade measures that could undermine the progress of developing countries.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako said the group was working to secure the adoption of its proposed agenda item to create room for negotiations on the relationship between climate policies and international trade.

He also expressed concern about initiatives introduced under the COP Presidency’s action agenda without adequate consultation with parties.

While the AGN does not oppose initiatives led by the presidency, he said such programmes should not be introduced into formal negotiation texts without proper consultation and party-driven processes.

The group also wants to strengthen the participation of young Africans in climate negotiations through capacity-building programmes that would prepare a new generation of negotiators.

COP31 as foundation for COP32

The AGN described COP31 as an important opportunity to strengthen Africa’s negotiating position ahead of COP32, which will be hosted by Ethiopia next year.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako said the group had commenced pre-sessional coordination meetings in Antalya on 1 November, followed by engagements with national focal points and other African delegates.

The group is also engaging other negotiating blocs within the Group of 77 and China to secure broader support for its proposed agenda items ahead of the formal adoption of the COP31 agenda, scheduled for 9 November.

He said Africa’s negotiating strength depended not only on internal coordination but also on building consensus with other developing countries.

The AGN chair cited the continent’s contributions to the establishment of the Green Climate Fund, the Loss and Damage Fund, and the inclusion of adaptation provisions in the Paris Agreement as examples of the group’s influence in international climate negotiations.

The group also called on civil society organisations and the media to help amplify Africa’s priorities throughout the conference.

Mr Antwi-Boasiako said the outcome of COP31 should provide a strong foundation for the continent as it prepares to host the next climate conference.

World.title: NNPC says its gas supply not cause of low power generation
World.content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed claims that constraints in its gas transportation network are contributing to the decline in electricity generation across the country.

In a statement issued on Saturday by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, the company said its pipelines remain available to transport gas to power plants nationwide without any constraints.

“NNPC Limited confirms that gas transportation network operated by its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), remains available to support deliveries to power generating stations nationwide without any constraints,” the statement said.

It added that NGIC’s operational records do not indicate any transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the current decline in electricity generation.

The clarification comes against the backdrop of a recent statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which identified limited gas availability and reduced water inflows to hydroelectric power stations as factors contributing to lower electricity generation.

“NNPC Limited’s clarification concerns the operational status of NGIC’s transportation network,” the statement noted.

Electricity supply across major Nigerian cities, including Lagos and Abuja, has declined significantly in recent weeks, worsening concerns over the country’s power supply.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The situation has been compounded by high temperatures and extreme heat as the rainy season gradually draws to a close.

The persistent power shortages have placed additional pressure on businesses and households, particularly as petrol prices remain elevated. While many Nigerians continue to struggle with the situation, others are increasingly turning to solar systems and inverters to meet their electricity needs.

On Friday, Nigeria’s Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, attributed the outages recorded across the country to planned maintenance at Egbin Power Station and gas supply constraints affecting some thermal power plants, which have reduced the volume of electricity available on the national grid.

The minister said he and his team were working to return the affected generating units to service in phases, with the first units expected to come back online within the next 48 to 72 hours.

“We are also working with operators to improve gas supply and accelerate repairs to the damaged infrastructure. I thank everyone affected for their patience and will provide further updates as supply is gradually restored,” he said.

NNPC’s gas transportation not a challenge

However, NNPC maintained that the availability of its gas transportation infrastructure was not a challenge, reaffirming its commitment to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation.

“Gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants must be assessed separately from the availability of transportation infrastructure,” the statement said.

The company explained that a comprehensive assessment of the challenges must also consider the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake.

“These factors determine whether gas supplied can be converted into electricity. They should be verified alongside gas supply data to establish the causes of the shortfall,” NNPC said.

The company called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify specific constraints and guide appropriate interventions.

It stressed that accurate reporting across the gas-to-power value chain was essential to resolving the challenges and sustaining public confidence.

“Our focus remains on dependable energy infrastructure and constructive collaboration that helps translate Nigeria’s gas resources into more reliable electricity for Nigerians,” it said.

NNPC added that it remained committed to actualising the federal government’s gas development and monetisation agenda, which it said had contributed to approximately 10 per cent growth in gas production volumes year-to-date in 2026.

World.title: Flamingos make history, beat Japan to win Nigeria’s first U-17 Women’s World Cup title
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos have made history by winning their first FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco.

Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku gave Nigeria a two-goal advantage before Japan mounted a late challenge. Still, the Flamingos held on to secure a landmark victory at the Mohammed VI Football Complex.

The triumph makes Nigeria the first African country to win the U-17 Women’s World Cup, ending the continent’s long wait for the title and giving the Flamingos their best-ever finish in the competition.

Having lost their opening match to Poland, the Nigerian youngsters responded with a remarkable run of victories to reach the final. They completed that recovery in style by overcoming one of the tournament’s most successful teams.

Bashiru, Umejiaku fire Nigeria ahead

The Flamingos began the final with attacking intent, looking to unsettle a Japanese side that had conceded only twice on its way to the championship match.

Nigeria created several opportunities in the opening half. Oluwakemi Adegbuyi tried her luck in the 12th minute, while Umejiaku came close 12 minutes later after getting past the Japanese goalkeeper. However, a heavy touch allowed Japan to recover.

Bashiru also threatened in the 26th minute before Nigeria came agonisingly close to taking the lead when an effort struck the crossbar in the 37th minute.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The breakthrough finally arrived in the 39th minute through Bashiru.

The midfielder unleashed a long-range effort that Japan goalkeeper Kou Kadowaki failed to hold, allowing the ball to slip through her hands and into the net.

It was another important contribution from Bashiru, who had scored twice in Nigeria’s 3-1 semi-final victory over Brazil.

The Flamingos carried their advantage into the break and needed only two minutes after the restart to extend it.

Umejiaku kept her composure to finish in the 47th minute, putting Nigeria 2-0 ahead and bringing the team closer to a historic title.

Japan fight back, but Flamingos hold on

Japan, champions in 2014 and runners-up in 2010 and 2016, refused to surrender their hopes of a second title.

The Asian side increased the pressure as the match entered its closing stages and found a way back into the contest in the 80th minute.

Fuki Ito scored to reduce the deficit to 2-1, setting up a tense finish for the Nigerian team.

With four minutes added, the Flamingos were forced to defend their advantage against Japan’s late attempts to find an equaliser.

But Busari’s players held their ground until the final whistle, triggering celebrations as Nigeria secured the trophy.

A historic campaign

The victory completes a remarkable turnaround for the Flamingos, whose campaign began with a 2-1 defeat to Poland.

Coach Akeem Busari’s side recovered with victories over Puerto Rico and defending champions Korea DPR in the group stage before defeating Mexico in the Round of 16 and Venezuela in the quarter-finals.

Coach Akeem Busari

Their 3-1 semi-final victory over Brazil then secured Nigeria’s first appearance in the final.

The Flamingos had previously finished third at the 2022 edition in India, their best performance before this tournament.

Japan, meanwhile, had reached their fourth final, having won the competition in 2014. They will have to wait for another opportunity to add to that title.

For Nigeria, however, the wait is over. The Flamingos have not only claimed their maiden world crown but also delivered a breakthrough achievement for African women’s football.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino and CAF President Patrice Motsepe were both in the stands to witness coach Akeem Busari-led Flamingos write a new chapter in women’s football.

World.title: Harvest of projects as Mbah begins tour of 68 development centres, commissions smart schools, PHCs
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State, on Friday, began his campaign tour of the 68 Development Centres in the state, commissioning several development projects initiated by his administration in the political wards of Aninri West and Aninri North Development Centres of Aninri Local Government Area.

Mbah said his government’s inclusive development model, which ensures the distribution of projects and opportunities across wards, had ensured that no part of the state was left behind.

In Aninri West Development Centre, the governor commissioned the Amorji, Uhueze and Agbada Nenwe campuses of the Smart Green School, as well as toured the Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centre, Agbada Nenwe, and commissioned the Type 2 Healthcare Facility, Amorji, Nenwe.

Mbah also held stakeholders’ engagements with the people of Aninri West and Aninri North Development Centres at Nenwe and Oduma, respectively, where he interacted with the people, polling unit by polling unit, to get feedback on government projects and policies. The people also used the opportunity to table their needs.

Speaking at the end of his interactive session with the people of Aninri West Development Centre at Nenwe, he emphasised that his administration was not coming to the people with mere promises, but with concrete results.

“Essentially, we have just commenced our engagement with our grassroots. Our aim is to go to all the development centres and have an interactive session with all our stakeholders. We are not coming to our stakeholders and various communities empty-handed. Our model of development in Enugu State is inclusive development. What that means is that there is no electoral ward in Enugu State that does not have the footprint of governance. So, we have not just come; we have also come to say to them, look at what we have delivered with the mandate you gave us to serve you,” he stated.

Mbah said the buildings were not the actual Smart Schools, but the facilities and teaching that go on in them to prepare Enugu children for the global economy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our children have no limits to what they can become and no boundaries as to what they can become. That is the whole idea of Smart Green Schools: to democratise quality learning. We know that if we do not invest in our children today and get them exposed to skills that will prepare them for the workplace of today and tomorrow, all we would have done building roads, conference centres, hotels, and the myriad of projects would not be sustainable, as we will not have children that will maintain them, and it would only be a matter of time before they all hit the rock.

“So, that was why we took education as the most important thing in any nation. If you want development, if you want to end poverty, you must educate your young ones and prepare them for the future,” he stressed.

On health, he said, “We have built 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres across the 260 electoral wards of Enugu State. While some have started full operation, the process of onboarding is ongoing, and you would also find out that in some instances. But the idea is that all the 260 wards of Enugu State will have a functional Type 2 healthcare centre.

“We have also approved the recruitment of 2,250 healthcare personnel because we are not just interested in the structure, but also in making sure that they are well staffed. What we measure our results on is not the blocks; it is based on the number of pregnant women we are able to ensure that they successfully deliver their babies and also based on the number of young ones that we are able to ensure do not die because they are not taking the right vaccinations they need. These are the real outcomes of the blocks that we put across our wards,” he explained.

He reiterated his administration’s commitment to delivering 10,000km of roads to the people of Enugu State by 2031, noting that the administration had expended the bulk of its resources on the education and health sectors in his first term and had so far been able to construct or reconstruct only 1,521km of roads.

“You would have noticed that we have carried the heavy lift of schools and hospitals. The next item for us is to go aggressive on road construction.

“I want to assure you that we have built the biggest asphalt plant in the South East here in Enugu. I have told my team that we are going to get a second asphalt plant installed in Enugu West Zone and another asphalt plant installed in Enugu North Zone.

“Our objective is still to do 10,000 kilometres of roads. We are not yet there. We have only done about 1,521. I acknowledge that we still have a long way to go on that, but rest assured that we will deliver,” he stated.

He promised to support rural communities to enhance their agricultural production.

“Agriculture must be enhanced. We have to end manual ways or methods of farming. We need to migrate you to mechanised farming methods, which is why we are building the farm estates.

“I have also spoken to some of the women here. I have informed them that they need to form clusters of at least 20 or a maximum of 25, where we can now provide them with money to enhance their productivity and equipment to add value to what they produce. So, that programme is going on now,” Mbah added.

At Oduma, Aninri North Development Centre, he also assured the people of the government’s commitment to enhancing livelihoods and productivity in their rural communities.

He said, “Aninri is known for the production of food, and we will assist in making sure that we add value to what you are doing. We will give you equipment to scale up your production. Before the end of the year, the road from Nomeh to Oduma will be completed. It was delayed due to the rainy season. But now that the rain has receded, the contractors will commence the asphalt process.”

He enjoined the people to vote for President Tinubu, himself and all APC candidates to guarantee the ongoing massive development of their communities.

“We call on you to get your PVC. Let us also continue to aggressively go door-to-door, house-to-house, and make sure our neighbours come out for polling unit meetings. Prepare them for the elections on January 16 and February 6. We are going to vote for President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates,” he concluded.

The consultations witnessed a large turnout of residents and stakeholders.

Mbah also used the opportunity to interact with pupils of the Smart Green Schools.

Meanwhile, the Chairman of Aninri Local Government Area, Hon. Ugochukwu Nwanjoku, who received Governor Mbah alongside other stakeholders in the council area, expressed gratitude to the governor for ensuring that Aninri received its fair share of development projects, noting that the administration’s inclusive development model had brought tangible benefits to communities across the local government area.

He assured the governor of the overwhelming support of the people of Aninri in the 2027 general elections, pledging that the council would reciprocate the administration’s commitment to its development with massive votes for Mbah, President Tinubu, and all APC candidates.

“You have demonstrated through the projects we have seen today that you are committed to the development of every part of Enugu State. Aninri is not left behind, and we are grateful. We will mobilise our people to ensure that you receive massive votes in 2027. We will stand with you and the APC from top to bottom,” Nwanjoku said.

World.title: Court restrains Kaduna university unions from strike
World.content:
The National Industrial Court of Nigeria has restrained three workers’ unions at Kaduna State University (KASU) from embarking on a strike or taking any form of industrial action pending the determination of a suit instituted by the university’s management.

The order, issued by Justice E. D. Subilim of the court’s Abuja Judicial Division on November 5, specifically restrained the unions, their officers, agents and other persons acting on their behalf from declaring, commencing, directing, instigating, encouraging or participating in any strike or industrial action.

The affected unions are the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) and the National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT), all operating at the Kaduna State University.

The court also directed the unions to cease giving effect to any strike action pending the hearing and determination of a Motion on Notice before it.

The suit, marked NICN/ABJ/329/2026, was instituted by Kaduna State University, its governing council and the vice-chancellor against the three unions and some of their officials.

Those listed as defendants include NASU branch chairman, Comrade Nina Ochigbo; its secretary, Comrade Dahiru Musa; SSANU chairman, Comrade Sadiya Mustapha; and its secretary, Comrade Nicholas Allen.

The court directed the university’s management to ensure that the originating summons, Motion on Notice, supporting affidavits and a copy of the enrolled order were served on the defendants without delay.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It adjourned the hearing of the Motion on Notice to 18 November

The order was issued under the seal of the court in Abuja on 6 November and signed by Vallari Aaron Masomene, Senior Registrar II.

Seven-day ultimatum over welfare demands

The court intervention followed a fresh threat of industrial action by the three unions operating under the Joint Action Committee (JAC) at KASU.

At a congress held on 2 November, the unions issued a seven-day ultimatum to the Kaduna State Government and the university management, demanding the implementation of outstanding agreements and the settlement of workers’ welfare concerns.

In their statement, the unions demanded the immediate implementation of the 2026 Consolidated Non-Teaching Tool Allowance Agreement (CONTTA), payment of approved wage awards and provision of group life insurance for staff.

They also demanded the payment of the federal government-approved N70,000 monthly transport support for workers for six months and called for respect for the university’s autonomy.

The unions warned that failure to address the demands within the stipulated period could compel them to embark on a warning strike.

They described their action as a demand for fairness, equity, justice, institutional autonomy and respect for agreements reached with workers.

Although they expressed willingness to pursue constructive engagement, they maintained that industrial harmony could not be sustained where negotiated agreements and staff welfare concerns remained unresolved.

Earlier demands included promotion and pension arrears

The latest ultimatum followed months of agitation by the non-teaching unions over what they described as outstanding financial and welfare obligations to their members.

In a communiqué issued in September, the Joint Action Committee called on the Kaduna State Government to implement outstanding agreements and settle accumulated entitlements.

Among their demands were payment of earned allowances, promotion arrears, pension arrears and outstanding wage awards, as well as the implementation of the 25 per cent and 35 per cent salary adjustments.

The unions also raised concerns over excess workload allowances, group life insurance and other conditions of service.

They argued that consistently implementing agreements reached with university-based unions was necessary to protect workers’ welfare, build confidence and sustain industrial peace at the institution.

The September demands came amid a wider labour dispute at KASU, which also involved the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), whose members had threatened industrial action over the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement.

Kaduna government sets up negotiation committee

In a move to address the growing tensions at the university, Governor Uba Sani, in August, approved the constitution of a nine-member negotiation committee to review the demands of ASUU, SSANU, NASU and NAAT.

The committee, chaired by the Commissioner for Education, Professor Abubakar Sani Sambo, has four weeks to examine the unions’ grievances and recommend practical, financially sustainable solutions.

The government said the committee would review outstanding allowances, the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA), and the financial implications of implementing the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement.

The intervention was accompanied by the approval of a one-off ₦300 million payment as Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) for academic staff.

According to the Secretary to the State Government, AbdulKadir Meyere, the payment was part of efforts to address a backlog of more than N800 million in accumulated entitlements and allowances dating back to 2016.

The government also cited the settlement of outstanding withheld salaries, the release of more than ₦300 million for programme accreditation and postgraduate resource verification, and a N50 million monthly standing order for the systematic settlement of outstanding arrears as part of its interventions.

It urged the unions to embrace dialogue, negotiation and collective bargaining rather than resorting to industrial action that could disrupt the university’s academic calendar.

Government approves new salary agreement for lecturers

The government subsequently announced a major intervention in the dispute involving academic staff.

On 12 September, the Commissioner for Education announced that Governor Sani had approved the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU salary agreement for KASU academic staff, effective October 2026.

The approval followed the government’s negotiation committee recommendations. It covered the revised Consolidated University Academic Salary Structure (CONUASS), the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and other applicable salary adjustments and allowances.

READ ALSO: Uba Sani receives human capital development champion award

However, the approval applied only to academic staff and did not, by itself, resolve the separate welfare demands of the non-teaching unions.

The distinction matters because SSANU, NASU and NAAT later renewed their demands, particularly over the non-teaching tool allowance, wage awards, transport support and other outstanding entitlements.

Court hearing fixed for 18 November

With the latest court order, the three unions are barred from embarking on industrial action pending further proceedings.

The 18 November hearing will determine the next steps in the court proceedings and the application filed by the university management.

The development raises fresh questions about resolving the outstanding welfare issues and the prospects of industrial harmony at the state-owned university.

While the Kaduna State Government has previously initiated negotiations and approved financial interventions to address some workers’ grievances, the latest ultimatum suggests significant disagreements remain, particularly over non-teaching staff demands.

World.title: REPORTER’S DIARY: Tasting Chef T’s jollof at Swoop’s Lagos table
World.content:
Jollof rice is hardly just another meal in Nigeria. Its colour, aroma, texture, and level of smokiness are scrutinised, compared and debated, making it a bold choice for any fast-food chain.

That was the dish placed before guests on Friday at Burger King’s Ajose Adeogun outlet in Victoria Island, Lagos, where delivery platform Swoop hosted The Jollof Table, an invited tasting experience.

The event introduced Chef T’s Jollof Combo, a Burger King meal offered for ₦1,000 exclusively through the Swoop app.

Rooted in Nigerian culture

For this reporter, the tasting presented one straightforward question: could the combo deliver the familiar flavour Nigerians expect from a proper plate of jollof rice?

With the expectations that come with the dish, I was curious about how Burger King, an international fast-food brand, had interpreted a meal so deeply rooted in Nigerian food culture.

For many Nigerians, the meal comes with expectations shaped by years of eating it at weddings, birthday celebrations, family gatherings, and restaurants. The smoky aroma from a pot cooked over firewood, the right balance of pepper and seasoning, and rice that is neither too soft nor too hard are often part of the standard.

But with jollof rice, the price is rarely the only thing that matters. After all, jollof is one of those dishes people can enjoy without much explanation, but rarely eat without an opinion.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The experience also offered an opportunity to look beyond the promotional price and assess the food itself. Would the rice stand out? Would the accompanying chicken and plantain complement it? And perhaps more importantly, would the combination leave a lasting impression?

Bringing jollof to the fast-food table

The collaboration brings together Burger King, Nigerian food creator Tolani Tayo-Osikoya, popularly known as Chef T of Diary of a Kitchen Lover, and Swoop, which is making the meal available exclusively through its delivery platform at a promotional price.

Chef T developed the recipe in collaboration with Burger King, aiming for a version of jollof that fits the restaurant’s fast-food offering while retaining familiar Nigerian flavours.

The meal combines seasoned jollof rice with a choice of smoked or spicy chicken and plantain. It is served in branded packaging bearing Chef T’s image.

The partnership is also part of Burger King’s effort to add familiar Nigerian food options to its menu, while Swoop is using the collaboration to attract customers with a discounted offer.

Speaking about the partnership, Steven Osiegbu, Account Management Lead at Swoop, said the platform wants to make popular food experiences more accessible.

“Jollof is one of those meals Nigerians never get tired of, and we’re excited to partner with Burger King and Chef T to bring something special to our customers.

“At Swoop, we’re always looking for ways to make great food more accessible,” he said.

So, how did the jollof taste?

When the meal arrived, the familiar combination of jollof rice, chicken and plantain made it immediately recognisable.

The rice offered a lighter and more restrained flavour than the smoky, pepper-forward party jollof many Nigerians are accustomed to. That difference was noticeable, but it also reflected the challenge of adapting a culturally significant dish into a fast-food format meant to stay consistent across multiple orders.

The chicken and plantain complemented the rice and made the serving feel like a complete meal. Rather than competing directly with wedding or firewood jollof, the combo offered a straightforward, convenience-focused version.

As expected, the meal prompted comparisons and conversations around the table. With jollof, everyone arrives with a personal standard shaped by where they grew up, how their families prepare it, and the celebrations where they ate their most memorable plates.

The ₦1,000 proposition

At its regular price of about ₦2,500, the combo competes with several rice-and-protein options available across Lagos. The promotional price of ₦1,000, however, makes affordability and convenience central to its appeal.

The offer is available through the Swoop app until 30 November 2026, allowing customers to try the collaboration at a reduced price.

READ ALSO: Veteran Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu dies at 71

For Burger King, the partnership represents an attempt to incorporate a familiar Nigerian meal into its fast-food offering. For Swoop, it provides an exclusive product intended to attract users to its delivery platform, while Chef T brings local food knowledge and a recognisable identity to the collaboration.

A table of opinions

By the end of the event, it was clear that no single version of jollof would satisfy every Nigerian palate.

Chef T’s Jollof Combo offers a convenient, accessible take on the meal, supported by chicken and plantain and packaged for the fast-food customer. Those expecting the intense smokiness of party jollof may find it different, while customers mainly after a quick, affordable meal may see it differently.

The tasting ended as most conversations about jollof in Nigeria do without a unanimous verdict. Swoop called it The Jollof Table, but by the end, it had become a table of opinions.

World.title: PDP faction may contest Court of Appeal judgement recognising Wike-backed leadership
World.content:
A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), led by former Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, Kabiru Turaki, has said its legal team is reviewing the Court of Appeal judgement affirming the Wike-backed faction as the party’s authentic leadership.

The faction said its lawyers would advise on whether to challenge the judgement at the Supreme Court after reviewing its legal implications. It, however, expressed optimism that it would eventually be recognised as the PDP’s authentic national leadership.

Mr Turaki disclosed this on Saturday when a delegation of governorship candidates who had obtained nomination and expression of interest forms from his faction paid a solidarity visit to its leaders in Abuja.

The candidates said the visit was aimed at encouraging the faction’s leadership to develop a strategic plan to sensitise and unite party members, particularly at the grassroots level.

The candidates were Sunday Biggs (Plateau), Ladi Hassan (Kwara), Joel Danlami (Taraba), Caleb Myebangara (Adamawa), Isah Muqaddam (Gombe), Lawal Umar (Kaduna), Ibrahim Abdullahi (Kebbi), Yakubu Mu’azu (Jigawa) and Zanna Gaddama (Borno).

Mr Turaki told the delegation that the faction would meet with its legal team to consider its assessment of the judgement before deciding on the next course of action.

“I have listened to you carefully, and I want to inform you, and through you to inform Nigerians, that since our judgement last Wednesday, we’ve instructed our team of lawyers to study, say and advise us accordingly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“And I can confirm to you that immediately after this meeting, we’re going to have a meeting with our legal team and they’re going to tell us the result of their assessment of the judgement of the Court of Appeal,” he said.

The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous judgement delivered last Wednesday, upheld the earlier decision of the Federal High Court dismissing a suit challenging the leadership of the Wike-backed faction of the PDP, chaired by Abdulrahman Mohammed.

The three-member panel was presided over by Ugochukwu Ogakwu, with Laja Balogun and Ruqayyat—Ayoola, who read the judgment.

The suit was instituted by the Board of Trustees (BoT) aligned with the Turaki faction. The board is chaired by Adolphus Wabara, a former Senate president.

The appeal, marked CA/ABJ/CV/1221/2026, was filed by Mr Wabara and seven others against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and six other respondents.

The appellants had asked the court to set aside the Federal High Court judgment and compel INEC to recognise the Interim National Working Committee (NWC) led by Mr Turaki.

They argued that the committee emerged from a National Executive Committee meeting convened after the Supreme Court judgment in April.

However, the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, affirming the position of the lower court in favour of the Wike-backed faction.

Struggle continues

Mr Turaki told the governorship candidates that the faction would continue its efforts to take control of the party through constitutional and legal means.

He expressed optimism that the Supreme Court would rule in its favour, paving the way for its candidates to participate in the 2027 general elections.

He also predicted that the PDP would win the elections if the faction eventually secured recognition as the party’s authentic leadership.

“I want to assure your excellencies and indeed your other colleagues who are not here, and through you also, to assure other candidates, our other respective candidates, that there is indeed going to be a bright sunny day at the end of the tournament. This struggle will continue. We are hopeful that we will win, and that after winning, PDP candidates shall be on the ballot.

“And as soon as we are on the ballot, I want to assure you that Nigerians are waiting for us. We shall be winning the 2027 elections by the special grace of God. So on behalf of PDP, I want to thank you so very much for the continuous support, the solidarity that you’ve been giving to us,” he added.

Mr Turaki thanked the candidates for their support and advice, assuring them that the faction would continue to work with them and other party organs in accordance with the party’s constitution.

He accused unnamed forces of attempting to undermine the party, insisting that the faction would continue to resist efforts to place the PDP in bondage.

“Now, PDP has come to stay, and PDP will continue to fight to free itself from the shackles of bondage that some undemocratic forces and elements are trying to put us in,” he said.

He also urged the candidates to encourage their supporters to remain calm and hopeful despite the court’s decision.
