“I pray that God will grant you a journey back home with mercy, and then try to talk to your people to remain calm. Let them remain calm. Fighting is not for those who are seeing victory in sight. So we should not fight.

“We should remain resolute. We should remain prepared, because even if it is a few days to the date of the election, and the shackles, the bondage of our party are freed, we will get to the polls. And by the special grace of God, we will emerge victorious,” he said.

Candidates call for reconciliation

Speaking earlier on behalf of the delegation, Mr Biggs, the PDP governorship candidate in Plateau State, said the visit was intended to demonstrate solidarity with the faction’s leadership and encourage it to pursue all available legal options.

“The visit was to interact with the INWC to show solidarity with them and to encourage them to undertake a strategic plan aimed at sensitising and unifying the party, especially at the grassroots level.

“Furthermore, to ensure that the appeal to the Supreme Court is pursued with urgency, competence and every necessary legal preparation,” he said.

Mr Biggs also urged the faction to explore reconciliation and constructive engagement with aggrieved members to resolve the party’s leadership crisis.

“We also want them to establish a broader platform for reconciliation and constructive engagement among aggrieved members. The national publicity secretary should ensure that effective communication with party members is regularly held to prevent misinformation, speculation and unnecessary anxiety.

“The party should develop a comprehensive political and organisational strategy to strengthen the party ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he said.

World.title: Let Trump’s Republican Party defeat be a lesson to any arrogant politician!, By Murtadha Gusau
World.content:
In the name of Allah, Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy.

Alhamdulillah. All praise is due to Allah, the Almighty, the Subduer, the One who elevates whom He wills and deposes whom He wills. We praise Him, we seek His guidance, and we ask for His forgiveness. We bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, alone without partners, and we bear witness that Muhammad (Peace be upon him) is His servant and final Messenger.

Dear servants of Allah! I advise you and myself to fear Allah. For indeed, the final outcome belongs only to the mindful. Allah warns us in the Noble Qur’an. He says:

“Say, ‘O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'” [Qur’an, 3:26]

Dear brothers and sisters! Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered a historic landslide defeat in the US midterm elections on November 3, 2026, as a massive “blue wave” delivered control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate to the Democratic Party. This sweeping victory effectively turns President Trump into a “lame duck” for the final two years of his presidency, crippling his legislative power and subjecting his administration to intense congressional oversight.

The defeat was driven by a combination of key state flips, major candidate upsets, and clear voter dissatisfaction with foreign and economic policies.

The scale of the Republican losses stunned political analysts, breaking decades-old voting patterns as Democrats flipped deep-red strongholds.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In arguably the most historic race of the night, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton to claim a Texas Senate seat. A Democrat had not won a Senate election in Texas since 1988.

Democrats broke a nearly three-decade streak by flipping a Senate seat in South Carolina, alongside major Senate victories in traditional Republican strongholds like Iowa and Kansas.

Longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins was ousted by Democrat Troy Jackson in Maine, while Democrat Chris Pappas defeated former Republican Senator John Sununu in New Hampshire.

What Are The Key Reasons Behind The Defeat?

1. The War on Iran and Rising Prices

In his post-election media appearances, President Donald Trump openly conceded that the ongoing US-Israel war against Iran, which significantly drove up American consumer prices, played a massive role in alienating voters.

2. Rejection of Trump’s Agenda

Exit polling indicated that voters overwhelmingly viewed the election as a direct referendum on Trump’s polarising presidency, citing the economy and the state of democracy as their top motivators for voting blue.

3. Weak Endorsed Candidates

Trump partially blamed the losses on the Republican candidates themselves. He distanced himself from several failed campaigns, admitting that voters simply “didn’t like the candidates” he had put forward.

Now with Democrats commanding both chambers, they now hold the power to block Trump’s legislative wishlist, pull back funding, and launch extensive congressional investigations into the White House.

Analysts expect Trump’s iron-clad grip on his own party to loosen as congressional Republicans begin looking ahead to their political survival in the 2028 presidential election cycle.

Here, the core lesson of worldly authority is that power belongs entirely to Allah, and whenever a leader cloaks themselves in pride, their eventual fall serves as a universal sign for those who reflect.

For example, look across history and look closely at our world today. We witness the rise and fall of leaders who believed they were untouchable. When we look at political figures who build their entire legacy on the pillars of arrogance, division, mockery, and absolute pride—such as Donald Trump—their sudden, crashing defeats are not merely political news. They are profound, spiritual realities.

For years, an arrogant leader may believe that their wealth, their media machinery, their passionate crowds, and their temporary power make them immune to failure. They speak as if they control the destiny of nations. They treat the vulnerable with disdain, disregard justice, and mock the truth.

But Allah is Al-Mutakabbir—The Supreme, the Only One Justified in Pride. When a human being attempts to wear the cloak of pride, Allah strips it away to show the creation how fragile man truly is. The transition from the highest seat of worldly power to a sudden, humbling loss is a clear sign. It is a modern manifestation of the ancient truth: No matter how high you rise in the eyes of the world, if your foundation is arrogance, your fall is a decree already written.

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) gave us a definition of arrogance that pierces through every political speech and campaign. He said:

“Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down upon people.” [Sahih Muslim]

When leaders reject absolute truths, manipulate realities for personal gain, and view ordinary citizens as mere tools for their ego, they enter a losing battle against the Divine Law. The Qur’an recounts the stories of Pharaoh, Qarun, and Namrud. They did not fall because they lacked wealth or armies; they fell because they forgot they were merely dust walking on dust.

Any politician, leader, or person of authority who fails to learn from these downfalls is blind to history. Power is a temporary loan, not a permanent possession. Today you are on the throne; tomorrow you are a cautionary tale.

This lesson is not just for the rulers in palaces; it is a mirror for our own hearts.

If a man who controlled nuclear codes and global economies can be humbled overnight, who are we to be arrogant in our homes, workplaces, or communities?

True strength lies in humility and justice, not in loud boasts or oppressive policies.

Do not despair when tyrants or arrogant leaders seem to dominate. Allah gives them respite, but He never forgets.

Respected brothers and sisters! Remember that, your voter’s card is not a mere piece of plastic; it is a sacred trust and amanah, a formal testimony and Shahadah, and a powerful instrument of Amru bil-Ma’ruf wan-Nahyu anil-Munkar: enjoining good and forbidding evil. In the light of Islamic jurisprudence and spiritual accountability, how we use—or neglect—this tool (voters card) will be weighed by Allah Almighty on the Day of Judgment.

And know that the religion of Islam is not a religion restricted only to the corners of the Mosque, nor is it isolated from the affairs of the society in which we live. Allah Almighty says in the Noble Qur’an:

“O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives…” [Qur’an, 4:135]

Dear brothers and sisters! Know that, when you hold your voter’s card, you are holding a great pen that writes the future of your Ummah. In the scales of the Shari’ah, casting a vote is a form of Shahadah and Testimony. When you vote for a leader, you are testifying before Allah that this person is capable, trustworthy, and just. If you sell that vote for a fleeting worldly gain, or if you cast it out of blind tribalism or nepotism for an oppressor, you have borne false witness—a major sin in Islam.

And what of those who stay home out of cynicism?

To withhold your vote when your Ummah needs righteous leaders is to conceal the truth. Allah Almighty warns us:

“…And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it – his heart is indeed sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.” [Qur’an, 2:283]

Rise, claim your card, guard your amanah, and let your vote be a witness for you, not against you, on the Day we return to Him.

Dear brothers and sisters! To truly understand the weight of civic engagement in Islam, we must look at the three dimensions of what a voter’s card represent:

1. The Voters Card as an Amanah, a Sacred Trust

Allah Almighty states:

“Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice…” [Qur’an, 4:58]

The power to choose who governs your resources, protects your rights, and maintains safety is a trust given to you. Abdicating this responsibility allows corruption to thrive unchecked.

2. The Weight of Shahadah, a Legal Testimony

In Islamic law, a vote acts as a recommendation and Tazkiyah, and a testimony and Shahadah.

● Voting for competence means you testify that the candidate will stand up for the poor, fund schools, and secure communities.

● Selling or wasting a vote means bearing a false witness, making the voter spiritually complicit in every act of injustice that politician commits while in office.

3. Continuous Charity or Continuous Liability, the Sadaqah/Jariyah

If the leader you help elect builds hospitals, establishes justice, and alleviates poverty, a share of the reward belongs to you. Conversely, if that leader plunders the land, oppresses the weak, and brings ruin, the psychological and spiritual burden of that systemic evil attaches to those who brought them to power.

It is easy to fall into despair. It is easy to look at the political landscape and say, “My single vote will change nothing. The system is entirely broken.”

But remember the story of the ant in the army of Prophet Sulaiman. When the massive army approached, a tiny ant did not remain silent thinking its voice was insignificant. It called out to save its nation:

“O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Sulaiman and his soldiers while they perceive not.” [Qur’an, 27:18]

Allah Almighty immortalised that single ant’s effort in the Qur’an.

You are not responsible for fixing the entire world by yourself, but you are entirely responsible for the weight of your own hand. When Allah asks you on the Day of Judgment, “When you saw injustice, when you saw the weak suffering, what did you do with the tools (voters card) I gave you?”—your voter’s card will be part of that questioning. Do not let your answer be that you voluntarily chose silence.

And finally, dear brothers and sisters! In the 2026 US midterm elections, Muslim candidates achieved historic victories across federal and state levels, including the election of the first-ever Muslim US Senator. They are as follows:

1. Abdul El-Sayed (Democrat – Michigan)

Made history as the first Muslim ever elected to the US Senate after defeating Republican Mike Rogers.

2. Adam Hamawy (Democrat – New Jersey)

Won the race for New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District, becoming the first Muslim elected to represent New Jersey in Congress.

3. Darializa Avila Chevalier (Democrat – New York)

Won New York’s 13th Congressional District, making history as the first Latina Muslim woman elected to Congress.

4. Ilhan Omar (Democrat – Minnesota)

Successfully secured her fifth term representing Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District.

5. Rashida Tlaib (Democrat – Michigan)

Retained her seat in Michigan’s 12th Congressional District.

6. Andre Carson (Democrat – Indiana)

Won re-election to continue representing Indiana’s 7th Congressional District.

7. Lateefah Simon (Democrat – California)

Won her congressional race in California’s 12th Congressional District.

8. Aisha Wahab (California)

Won her race for the California State Legislature.

9. Nabeela Syed and Abdelnasser Rashid (Illinois)

Elected as the first Muslim state legislators in the Illinois House of Representatives.

10. Mana Abdi, Deqa Dhalac, and Ambureen Rana (Maine)

Made history as the first Muslims elected to the Maine State Legislature.

11. Munira Abdullahi and Ismail Mohamed (Ohio)

Became the first Muslims elected to serve in the Ohio state legislature.

12. Salman Bhojani and Suleman Lalani (Texas)

Achieved history as the first Muslims elected to the Texas Legislature.

13. Nabilah Islam and Ruwa Romman (Georgia)

Re-elected/elected to the Georgia State Senate and House, expanding Muslim representation in the state.

14. Zaynab Mohamed and Samakab Hussein (Minnesota)

Secured legislative seats, bringing Minnesota’s total to 5 elected Muslim state lawmakers.

15. Mauree Turner (Oklahoma)

Became the first Muslim lawmaker elected to the Oklahoma state legislature.

16. Madinah Wilson-Anton (Delaware)

Made history as the first Muslim elected to Delaware’s state legislature.

17. Iman Jodeh (Colorado)

Elected to represent her district in the Colorado state legislature.

We ask Allah to purify our hearts from pride, to grant us leaders who fear Him and show mercy to the people, and to make our final actions our best actions.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace, blessings and salutations of Allah be upon our noble Messenger, Muhammad, and upon his family, his Companions and his true followers.

Murtadha Muhammad Gusau is the Chief Imam of Nagazi-Uvete Jumu’ah and the late Alhaji Abdur-Rahman Okene’s Mosques, Okene, Kogi State, Nigeria. He can be reached via: [email protected] or +2348038289761 or +2348024192217.

World.title: ‘You’ve written your names in gold,’ Tinubu celebrates Flamingos, U-17 FIFA World Cup winners
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos for making history as the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco.

Read Also: Nigeria’s Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win first U-17 Women’s World Cup

The President, who received the cheering news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States, hailed Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the nation and a landmark achievement for African women’s football.

“What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country.

“To our gallant Flamingos, I say congratulations. You have shown courage, discipline, determination and the Nigerian spirit of never giving up.

“I followed your journey throughout this tournament, and after your semi-final victory, you promised to bring the trophy home. Today, you have kept that promise. You believed in yourselves, fought for one another and carried our nation’s flag to the very top of the world.

“Your victory is an inspiration to millions of young Nigerian girls who dream of achieving greatness. You have shown them that with hard work, opportunity and determination, they too can reach the highest levels of achievement.

“Today, Nigeria celebrates you. You have written your names in gold, and your country is immensely proud of you.”

The President particularly applauds Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose goals secured the historic victory, while commending the entire squad for their exceptional teamwork throughout the tournament.

He also congratulates the coaching crew, the Nigeria Football Federation and the National Sports Commission for their contributions to the team’s success.

President Tinubu reaffirms his administration’s commitment to investing in grassroots sports development and expanding opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly girls, to discover, nurture and fulfil their potential.

“Congratulations once again, Flamingos. Thank you for making Nigeria proud.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC
World.content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has said its gas transportation network remains available to supply gas to power generating stations nationwide, insisting that transportation constraints are not responsible for the current decline in electricity generation.

The national oil company said operational records of its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), showed no transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the drop in power generation.

NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja on Friday.

The clarification followed a November 5 statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which attributed the decline in electricity generation partly to limited gas availability and reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations.

However, NNPC said its clarification was specifically about the operational status of its gas transportation infrastructure, noting that gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants were separate issues requiring independent assessment.

The company said gas production had grown by about 10 per cent year-to-date in 2026, attributing the increase to the Federal Government’s gas development and monetisation agenda.

“Gas supply availability is therefore not a challenge as NNPC remains committed to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation,” the statement said.

NNPC further explained that determining the causes of the generation shortfall required an assessment of other components of the gas-to-power value chain.

These, it said, included the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake by power stations.

The company stressed that the factors must be examined alongside gas supply data to establish the specific causes of the decline in electricity generation.

It also called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify constraints and guide appropriate interventions.

NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to developing dependable energy infrastructure and collaborating with stakeholders to translate the country’s gas resources into more reliable electricity supply for Nigerians.

World.title: Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence
World.content:
Former presidential candidate, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has condemned political violence in Nigeria, warning that attacks on political opponents could worsen the country’s already precarious security situation.

Olawepo-Hashim also called on President Bola Tinubu to caution members of his team against actions and statements capable of provoking political conflict.

He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after visiting activist and publisher, Omoyele Sowore, following the reported attack on him in Ekiti State.

Olawepo-Hashim said his visit was motivated by their longstanding relationship, which dates back to their participation in the struggle against military dictatorship and the campaign for democracy.

He warned that Nigeria, already grappling with terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security challenges, could not afford another crisis arising from political violence.

“Nigeria cannot afford to add political violence to the general insecurity in the land.

“Nigeria is already battling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and widespread insecurity. We cannot afford to add political violence to this burden,” he said.

The former presidential candidate welcomed a statement by a United Nations representative expressing concern over the incident and urged other international partners to condemn political violence.

He also urged political leaders to exercise restraint, warning that those who provoke violence might not be the ones to suffer its consequences.

“President Bola Tinubu must call his team to order. Political leaders must exercise restraint and stop actions or rhetoric capable of provoking conflict. Those who recklessly provoke violence may not be the ones who bear its consequences,” he said.

Recalling their history, Olawepo-Hashim said he and Sowore had been comrades since 1989/1990, when they worked together against military rule.

He said he was particularly moved by Sowore’s recollection of how he introduced him to political activism at the University of Lagos.

According to him, Sowore reaffirmed during the visit that he remained undeterred by the reported attack and was determined to continue campaigning for genuine democracy.

Olawepo-Hashim stressed that political disagreements should not be used as justification for violence, urging Nigerians to uphold democratic values and reject actions capable of worsening insecurity and instability in the country.

World.title: Fubara to Tinubu: You stood with us in difficult times; we’ll stand with you
World.content:
Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has pledged the state’s support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, saying the people are ready to reciprocate the President’s support during their challenging moments.

Fubara said Rivers State had not forgotten Tinubu’s intervention and support during the political crisis that rocked the state, assuring him of their backing as he seeks a renewed mandate.

The governor disclosed this in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after welcoming Tinubu to Rivers State for the All Progressives Congress (APC) South-South presidential campaign rally.

He expressed appreciation to the President for his intervention and commitment to restoring peace, stability and development in the state.

“Rivers State has not forgotten your support in our most challenging moments. As you stood with us, we are ready to stand firmly with you as you seek a renewed mandate in 2027,” Fubara said.

The governor said his administration and the people of the state remained committed to building a peaceful, stronger and more prosperous Nigeria.

He also reaffirmed Rivers State’s support for Tinubu, declaring: “Rivers State is with you, Mr President!”

World.title: Tinubu seeks Rivers support, hails Wike-Fubara reconciliation
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has sought renewed support from Rivers State voters ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, commending Governor Siminalayi Fubara and his predecessor, Nyesom Wike, for resolving their political differences.

Tinubu also thanked the people of Rivers State for their support during the 2023 presidential election, saying their votes contributed significantly to his emergence as President.

He spoke on Saturday at a campaign rally organised by the Rainbow Coalition, led by Wike, at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, Port Harcourt.

The President praised Fubara for what he described as maturity, understanding and respect for the intervention of political elders during the political crisis between the governor and Wike.

“During the political crisis caused by a misunderstanding in the family, I intervened on your behalf. I thank Governor Fubara, in particular, for his maturity, understanding, and respect for the wisdom of elders when we intervened.

“Fubara, you will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said.

On the economy, the President defended his administration’s reforms, insisting that they were placing the country on the path to prosperity.

He said the Federal Government was addressing inherited financial obligations, including unpaid pensions and gratuities, to ensure that more Nigerians benefited from economic recovery.

According to him, outstanding pension and salary liabilities in 27 of the 36 states have been cleared, making monthly payments more certain for beneficiaries.

“When those people talk about hunger, remember that I am cleaning up the mess they created. Atiku was one of them. Ask him how he built a private university while in office as Vice President in charge of our economy. Who funded the university for him? It was your money, your effort!” he said.

Tinubu also questioned the moral standing of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), to seek another opportunity to hold public office.

“A man without moral integrity, latitude, and ethics has no business holding public office,” he added.

The President also presented his manifesto for the 2027 election at the rally.

Speaking, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged political leaders and supporters in Rivers State and the South-South to support Tinubu’s re-election, citing the administration’s performance and commitment to the region.

Shettima said Nigeria’s economic indicators were improving, claiming that the country’s foreign reserves had risen from about $3.9 billion to $60 billion in approximately three years.

He also criticised opposition figures, describing Atiku as “intellectually malnourished” and the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as politically irrelevant and mediocre.

Fubara, in his remarks, pledged to mobilise three million votes for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

The governor also declared his support for the Rainbow Coalition and acknowledged Wike’s leadership of the political group.

“Under the guidance and leadership of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, we will deliver not less than three million votes for you,” Fubara said.

He thanked Tinubu for his intervention during the political crisis in the state, promising that Rivers would reciprocate the President’s support.

“Thank you, Mr President, for standing by us at a most difficult time. A good gesture deserves reciprocity. As you have stood by us, we will stand by you,” he said.

Earlier, Wike described the large turnout at the rally as evidence of Rivers State’s support for Tinubu’s re-election.

The FCT Minister said the rally was organised by Rivers residents without mobilisation from other states, insisting that the people had already made up their minds to support the President.

Wike also thanked Tinubu for appointing Rivers indigenes to positions in his administration and cited federal projects in the state, including the Bonny-Bodo Road and the Federal University of Environment in Ogoniland.

He claimed that the President had made no fewer than 47 political appointments from Rivers State, describing the appointments and federal projects as evidence of the administration’s commitment to the state.

The former Rivers governor also accused Rotimi Amaechi, a former governor of the state and ADC vice-presidential candidate, of failing to account for $39 million earmarked for the Karibi Whyte Specialist Hospital project, as well as funds allocated for fumigation in the state.

The rally, held at the 40,000-capacity Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, attracted political leaders and supporters, with the crowd reportedly spilling into surrounding areas.

Those in attendance included First Lady Oluremi Tinubu; wife of the Vice President, Nana Shettima; Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; APC National Chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda; and Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari.

Also present were several governors, Senators Magnus Abe, Adams Oshiomhole and Ifeanyi Okowa, other members of the National Assembly, and the President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Tinubu arrived in Port Harcourt from Akwa Ibom State, where he had earlier attended a political rally and commissioned projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration.

World.title: Trump orders Justice Department probe of Democrats seeking impeachment
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration.

Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterms.

Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.

“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

“This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable,” he said, arguing that there had been “no impeachable acts committed.”

Trump said he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act” and said “imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS.”

With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.

Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.

“Lawyer up,” wrote incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia on X as the results became clear on election night.

Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.

Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so.

The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate — far beyond the party’s numbers.

World.title: Obi condemns attacks on NDC, Obidient Movement members in Delta
World.content:
Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned reported attacks on members and coordinators of the party and the Obidient Movement in Delta State.

Obi described the incidents as disturbing, insisting that political violence, intimidation and destruction of property had no place in a democratic society.

The former Anambra State governor disclosed his position in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday.

He called on the Delta State Government and security agencies to immediately investigate the reported attacks, identify those responsible and ensure they were brought to justice, irrespective of their political affiliations.

Obi said no political ambition was worth the life of any Nigerian, stressing that disagreements should be resolved through peaceful and lawful means.

He expressed concern over what he described as attempts by some individuals to secure political influence through intimidation, fear and violence rather than persuasion and popular support.

According to him, political authority should be earned through the trust of the people and not by intimidating political opponents.

“I unequivocally condemn the attacks against our coordinators, supporters, and fellow citizens who were merely exercising their democratic rights.

“Political violence has no place in a democracy and can never be justified. No political aspiration is worth the life of a Nigerian, and no dispute should be resolved through intimidation, physical attacks, or the destruction of property,” he said.

Obi urged security agencies to guarantee the safety of NDC members and other citizens, adding that the party would not be intimidated or prevented from exercising its democratic rights.

He also reaffirmed his commitment to peaceful political engagement, saying the party’s response to the incidents would remain lawful and non-violent.

The NDC presidential candidate further stressed that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to organise, assemble, express opinions and participate in the electoral process without fear of harassment.

” No political party or individual has exclusive ownership of the democratic space. Every Nigerian is entitled to organise, gather, express their views, and freely elect their leaders,” he added.

Obi expressed solidarity with those affected by the reported attacks, saying Nigeria’s future should be built on justice, liberty, peace and respect for the dignity of every citizen.

World.title: Atiku to Tinubu: 2027 conversation is how to repair damage your govt caused
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has told President Bola Tinubu that his administration’s failures will cost him re-election in 2027, challenging him to defend his record in office rather than attack his investment in education.

Read Also:

*Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP

*Any Nigerian that’s not lazy will have food on the table – Yari

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, said Nigerians had endured enough hardship under Tinubu’s leadership, insisting that the next presidential election would be about reversing the damage “inflicted on the country through rising poverty, insecurity, unemployment and a crushing cost-of-living crisis”.

In a statement on Saturday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku also defended his investment in the American University of Nigeria, AUN, insisting that his educational venture began before he became Vice President in 1999.

“The answer is simple: my investment in education predates my time in public service.

“In 1993, I was laying the foundation for ABTI Academy. That Academy has since grown into the American University of Nigeria,” Atiku said.

He accused Tinubu of attempting to undermine his record in education because he could account for his own business and political journey.

Turning to the economy, the former Vice President said Tinubu had no business seeking another mandate when millions of Nigerians were struggling with the consequences of his policies.

“A president who has plunged the country into a crushing cost-of-living crisis has no business asking Nigerians for another mandate. The real conversation about the 2027 election is how to repair the damage your government has done,” Atiku said.

He also challenged the President’s insistence that Nigeria could not return to fuel subsidy, questioning the benefits of the economic reforms to ordinary Nigerians.

“You say Nigeria cannot return to subsidy and must move forward. But you cannot even tell Nigerians where you are taking them. Forward into deeper poverty, mounting debt, insecurity and mass unemployment?” he asked.

Atiku accused the administration of creating widespread poverty and being insensitive to the plight of struggling Nigerians, citing a reported comment by Tinubu’s campaign Director-General that hungry Nigerians were lazy.

“You created poverty, then insult the people suffering from it. You attack my Affordable Life campaign, but the people you are really attacking are the millions of Nigerians desperate for relief from your failed leadership,” he said.

The ADC candidate said his proposed alternative would include a transparent, production-based fuel subsidy tied to local refining, alongside deliberate social welfare investments to support economically vulnerable Nigerians.

“By the grace of the Almighty and with the mandate of the Nigerian people, I will restore a transparent, production-based subsidy tied to the local refining of fuel.

“Nigerians will benefit directly through lower energy costs, including the prices of petrol and diesel,” he said.

He also promised to end what he described as the opaque management of funds meant for vulnerable Nigerians.

Atiku accused Tinubu of wanting him off the ballot at all costs, but insisted that he would contest the 2027 presidential election.

“You want me off the ballot at all costs, but the will of the Nigerian people will prevail. I will be on that ballot, and I will beat you decisively,” he declared.

The former Vice President concluded that Tinubu’s record in office, rather than the opposition’s campaign promises, would be his biggest obstacle in the next election.

“After three and a half years in office, you have no achievements to campaign on. Your own record of failure is the strongest campaign against you,” Atiku said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Nigeria’s Flamingos Win Historic 2026 U17 Women’s World Cup, Beat Japan 2-1
World.content:
* Become first African to win the competition

Kunle Adewale

Nigeria’s under-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, etched their names into football history Saturday, defeating former champions Japan 2–1 at the Mohammed VI Football Complex to lift the 2026 FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup.

With the victory, Nigeria becomes the first African nation to win the tournament since its inception in 2008.

Led by head coach Akeem Busari, the Flamingos entered the showpiece having already broken ground as the first African side to reach the final, surpassing their previous best finish of a bronze medal in 2022.

After a fiercely contested opening half-hour against a disciplined Japanese side making their fourth final appearance, Nigeria broke the deadlock in the 39th minute.

Midfielder Awawu Bashiru—who had starred with a brace in the semi-final against Brazil—unleashed a long-range strike that slipped past Japanese goalkeeper Kou Kadowaki to give the Flamingos a 1–0 lead at the break.

Nigeria wasted no time doubling their advantage after the restart. Just two minutes into the second half, forward Oluebube Umejiaku latched onto a through ball and lifted a composed finish over the onrushing Kadowaki in the 47th minute to make it 2–0.

Desperate to reclaim a title they last won in 2014, Japan responded with a triple substitution and mounted heavy late pressure.

The Young Nadeshiko eventually pulled a goal back in the 80th minute through setting up a tense finish in front of a crowd that included FIFA President Gianni Infantino and CAF President Patrice Motsepe.

Despite Japan’s late surge, Nigeria’s backline—marshalled by goalkeeper Sylvia Ijirigho and defender Omowunmi Sunday—held firm through stoppage time to seal an unforgettable triumph for Nigerian and African women’s football.

World.title: Deputy Speaker Kalu Reassures Item Community on Tertiary Institutions
World.content:
Item Community in Aba, Abia State, on Friday received assurances from the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, on the establishment and sustenance of tertiary institutions attracted to Bende Federal Constituency.

Kalu attended the community’s cultural day in Aba, Abia State after participating in the day-long APC Presidential campaign in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

On his arrival, he was received by a large crowd singing the mandate anthem of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Item is a large community with three of the 13 electoral wards in Bende Federal Constituency, which the Deputy Speaker represents at the National Assembly.

The cultural day drew attendees from different political backgrounds.

Exemplified by their excitement, the crowd thanked the President for the University of Medical and Health Sciences and the Federal College of Education attracted by the Deputy Speaker and sited in Bende Federal Constituency.

Responding to their call for support, Kalu donated hugely towards the construction of Item civic centre in Aba.

He also assured the people of more dividends of democracy, including construction of more classroom blocks, roads and health centres.

He said: “I love Ndi Item. The President loves Ndi Item. That is why he signed the bill for the establishment of a tertiary institution in Item. We will build more classrooms for primary and secondary schools in Item. We will construct more roads for the people.”

Speaking on culture, Kalu said it is a uniting force and a value-sustaining element through which heritage is passed from one generation to the next.

He said the ways of the fathers should always be promoted, especially those that conform with the norms of a dynamic society.

World.title: Mbah Tours 68 Devt Centres, Commissions Smart Schools, PHCs
World.content:
*Promises more democracy dividends

Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State, on Friday, began his campaign tour of the 68 Development Centres in the state, commissioning several development projects initiated by his administration in the political wards of Aninri West and Aninri North Development Centres of Aninri Local Government Area.

Mbah said his government’s inclusive development model, which ensures the distribution of projects and opportunities across wards, had ensured that no part of the state was left behind.

In Aninri West Development Centre, the governor commissioned the Amorji, Uhueze and Agbada Nenwe campuses of the Smart Green School, as well as toured the Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centre, Agbada Nenwe, and commissioned the Type 2 Healthcare Facility, Amorji, Nenwe.

Mbah also held stakeholders’ engagements with the people of Aninri West and Aninri North Development Centres at Nenwe and Oduma, respectively, where he interacted with the people, polling unit by polling unit, to get feedback on government projects and policies. The people also used the opportunity to table their needs.

Speaking at the end of his interactive session with the people of Aninri West Development Centre at Nenwe, he emphasised that his administration was not coming to the people with mere promises, but with concrete results.

“Essentially, we have just commenced our engagement with our grassroots. Our aim is to go to all the development centres and have an interactive session with all our stakeholders. We are not coming to our stakeholders and various communities empty-handed. Our model of development in Enugu State is inclusive development. What that means is that there is no electoral ward in Enugu State that does not have the footprint of governance. So, we have not just come; we have also come to say to them, look at what we have delivered with the mandate you gave us to serve you,” he stated.

Mbah said the buildings were not the actual Smart Schools, but the facilities and teaching that go on in them to prepare Enugu children for the global economy.

“Our children have no limits to what they can become and no boundaries as to what they can become. That is the whole idea of Smart Green Schools: to democratise quality learning. We know that if we do not invest in our children today and get them exposed to skills that will prepare them for the workplace of today and tomorrow, all we would have done building roads, conference centres, hotels, and the myriad of projects would not be sustainable, as we will not have children that will maintain them, and it would only be a matter of time before they all hit the rock.

“So, that was why we took education as the most important thing in any nation. If you want development, if you want to end poverty, you must educate your young ones and prepare them for the future,” he stressed.

On health, he said, “We have built 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres across the 260 electoral wards of Enugu State. While some have started full operation, the process of onboarding is ongoing, and you would also find out that in some instances. But the idea is that all the 260 wards of Enugu State will have a functional Type 2 healthcare centre.

“We have also approved the recruitment of 2,250 healthcare personnel because we are not just interested in the structure, but also in making sure that they are well staffed. What we measure our results on is not the blocks; it is based on the number of pregnant women we are able to ensure that they successfully deliver their babies and also based on the number of young ones that we are able to ensure do not die because they are not taking the right vaccinations they need. These are the real outcomes of the blocks that we put across our wards,” he explained.

He reiterated his administration’s commitment to delivering 10,000km of roads to the people of Enugu State by 2031, noting that the administration had expended the bulk of its resources on the education and health sectors in his first term and had so far been able to construct or reconstruct only 1,521km of roads.

“You would have noticed that we have carried the heavy lift of schools and hospitals. The next item for us is to go aggressive on road construction.

“I want to assure you that we have built the biggest asphalt plant in the South East here in Enugu. I have told my team that we are going to get a second asphalt plant installed in Enugu West Zone and another asphalt plant installed in Enugu North Zone.

“Our objective is still to do 10,000 kilometres of roads. We are not yet there. We have only done about 1,521. I acknowledge that we still have a long way to go on that, but rest assured that we will deliver,” he stated.

He promised to support rural communities to enhance their agricultural production.

“Agriculture must be enhanced. We have to end manual ways or methods of farming. We need to migrate you to mechanised farming methods, which is why we are building the farm estates.

“I have also spoken to some of the women here. I have informed them that they need to form clusters of at least 20 or a maximum of 25, where we can now provide them with money to enhance their productivity and equipment to add value to what they produce. So, that programme is going on now,” Mbah added.

At Oduma, Aninri North Development Centre, he also assured the people of the government’s commitment to enhancing livelihoods and productivity in their rural communities.

He said, “Aninri is known for the production of food, and we will assist in making sure that we add value to what you are doing. We will give you equipment to scale up your production. Before the end of the year, the road from Nomeh to Oduma will be completed. It was delayed due to the rainy season. But now that the rain has receded, the contractors will commence the asphalt process.”

He enjoined the people to vote for President Tinubu, himself and all APC candidates to guarantee the ongoing massive development of their communities.

“We call on you to get your PVC. Let us also continue to aggressively go door-to-door, house-to-house, and make sure our neighbours come out for polling unit meetings. Prepare them for the elections on January 16 and February 6. We are going to vote for President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates,” he concluded.

The consultations witnessed a large turnout of residents and stakeholders.

Mbah also used the opportunity to interact with pupils of the Smart Green Schools.

Meanwhile, the Chairman of Aninri Local Government Area, Hon. Ugochukwu Nwanjoku, who received Governor Mbah alongside other stakeholders in the council area, expressed gratitude to the governor for ensuring that Aninri received its fair share of development projects, noting that the administration’s inclusive development model had brought tangible benefits to communities across the local government area.

He assured the governor of the overwhelming support of the people of Aninri in the 2027 general elections, pledging that the council would reciprocate the administration’s commitment to its development with massive votes for Mbah, President Tinubu, and all APC candidates.

“You have demonstrated through the projects we have seen today that you are committed to the development of every part of Enugu State. Aninri is not left behind, and we are grateful. We will mobilise our people to ensure that you receive massive votes in 2027. We will stand with you and the APC from top to bottom,” Nwanjoku said.

World.title: Tinubu: Atiku Part of Those Who Created the Mess I’m Clearing
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has said that the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar was part of those that created the mess his government was cleaning up now.

Atiku was vice president between 1999 and 2007 during the administration of President Olusegun Obasanjo.

Tinubu stated this Saturday during the presidential campaign rally of the All Progressives Congress (APC) held in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

He said when he was helpless, the people of Port Harcourt supported him and gave him the mandate.

The President stated: “I look very helpless. But you stood out to support me, give me the mandate. The mandate that I used to govern till today, you are a positive contributor. I must thank you for going out there to vote and vote massively for APC. Today again, I return here to say thank you. And seek your support for the second term.

“I’m seeking that support because you believe in me. You believe that I care for you, particularly the young youth. Your education, your welfare, your skill is extremely important to me, to Nigeria. I assure you this, we have started the golden age. The prosperity is here.”

Tinbu said when he took over, 27 out of 36 states were unable to pay salaries, saying that meant a lot for the families that depend on the salaries and to many households

He stressed that ever since, his administration had reversed the ugly trend, saying the country was on the move for prosperity.

Tinubu stated: “Those people, talking of hunger, we are clearing the mess they created. Atiku was one of them.

“Ask him how he built the university while he was in office as vice president — in charge of our economy. Who built the university for you? Is it your money? Is it your effort? A man without moral integrity, latitude and ethics for the office.”

The president described the Minister of Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike as a development partner of his administration, saying he is doing a wonderful job.

He commended Wike for maintaining peace and stability during the civic crisis, created by misunderstanding in the family.

Tinubu added: “To me, I intervene on your behalf, Similayi Fubara. Your excellency, the host governor of the day. I want to thank you specifically for the maturity, understanding, and respect for the wisdom of elders.

“When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat. Fubara you will not regret what you have done. As long as all of us are alive.’

Tinubu said the 2027 elections are about the youth of Nigeria.

He stated: “This election is about you (youth). It’s not all about me. Your future depends on this election. It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it.

“The weapon you have against poverty. Is to elect progressive development of our economy. That is what I’m pursuing. The people that governed before, they left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of Naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included.

“We are sharing prosperity already. A retired engineer is receiving a gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving a pension right now, a retired teacher is receiving a pension right now.”

Also, Vice President Kashim Shetima said River state is the true definition of political alliances, it is River State.

He recalled that four years ago, Rivers people gave the ruling party their trust and they have not withdrawn it and also stood by it.

Shettima added: “Good people of Rivers State, you chose to stand by us when the easier choice was to stand elsewhere. We ask you to make that choice again. We ask you to renew your mandate again. We have traveled too far to abandon the Rivers people. We have worked too hard to surrender again.”

The vice president berated those he referred to as political charlatans on the other side of the divide making efforts to demonize President Tinubu instead of celebrating him.

Shettima said the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar and his Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) counterpart, Peter Obi are no match for Tinubu.

He described Obi’s performance as Governor of Anambra state for eight years and Chairman of a bank as mediocre.

Shettima noted: “I dare say, without any fear of equivocation, that President Bola Tinubu is a decent man. When he assumed office as President, three and a half years ago, our economy was seemingly on the verge of collapse. We were on the road to Caracas. Instead of demonizing his successor with his predecessor, the president had the moral courage, had the conviction, to take the bull by the horn.”

Speaking, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Abubakar Yari said the ruling party has set a target of 2.3 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers State.

He also expressing confidence in the state’s capacity to deliver an overwhelming victory for the President in the 2027 elections.

Yari noted that the state has approximately 3.3 million registered voters, out of which 2.8 million have collected their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

He stressed that the figures present a strong electoral opportunity, adding that Rivers State was among the states expected to deliver between 75 and 80 per cent of the votes for President Tinubu.

Yari commended the people of Rivers State, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and other stakeholders for the massive mobilisation and support for the President.

He described the emerging political alliance as a working rainbow coalition, expressing optimism that the growing unity across political divides would strengthen Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Taking a swipe at the opposition, Yari highlighted Tinubu’s record as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, particularly his foundation for sustainable revenue generation.

He recalled that Lagos State’s internally generated revenue stood at about ₦600 million when Tinubu assumed office, but has since grown to over ₦100 billion monthly under successive administrations, including the current government of Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

Yari expressed confidence that the same vision and institutional foundations that transformed Lagos State could be replicated at the national level, adding that the policies and reforms being implemented by President Tinubu would benefit future generations.

Yari urged Nigerians, particularly the people of Rivers State, to sustain their support for the President, expressing confidence in a strong electoral outing in 2027.

On his part, the National Chairman APC, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda described the Tinubu-Shettima presidential ticket as one of the most formidable political combinations in Nigeria’s democratic history.

He declared that Tinubu deserves another term to consolidate the bold reforms and transformative development initiatives of his administration.

Yilwatda noted that the Tinubu-Shettima ticket represented a combination of political experience, courage, capacity and tested leadership, capable of steering Nigeria through its current challenges towards sustainable economic growth and national prosperity.

His words: “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country.

” He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria.

“President Tinubu has confronted enormous challenges since assuming office, and rather than surrendering to them, he has taken decisive steps to address the structural problems that have constrained our national development for decades.

“He inherited a country facing serious fiscal and economic difficulties, including unsustainable fuel subsidy expenditure, revenue constraints and mounting obligations. His administration has demonstrated the political will to confront these challenges through difficult but necessary reforms.”

Yilwatda noted that the removal of the fuel subsidy, the unification of the foreign exchange market and other economic policy adjustments were important components of the administration’s efforts to rebuild the economy, strengthen public finances and establish a more sustainable foundation for long-term growth.

He acknowledged that the reforms had come with significant adjustments for households and businesses but maintained that the administration was committed to addressing their impact through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions, infrastructure investments and policies designed to expand opportunities for Nigerians.

Yilwatda urged Nigerians not to lose sight of the long-term objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda, insisting that the country must sustain the reform trajectory to enable the administration to consolidate its policies and deliver greater economic benefits.

He described President Tinubu as a reformer and performer whose leadership vision places national development above political convenience, adding that the 2027 election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to choose continuity, stability and the consolidation of ongoing reforms.

The chairman commended the political leaders, stakeholders and members of the Rainbow Coalition for recognising the importance of national unity, political cooperation and continuity in the pursuit of Nigeria’s development.

According to him, the emerging political consensus in Rivers State reflects a broader recognition that the success of the Tinubu administration is in the collective interest of Nigerians, irrespective of their political affiliations.

“Come 2027, we want to continue with this reformer and performer as our President. That is why the coalition and the people of Rivers State, irrespective of political party, have decided to work together for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Yilwatda said.

The chairman expressed confidence that Rivers State would deliver overwhelming electoral support for President Tinubu, predicting that the state would become a major stronghold of the President’s re-election campaign.

World.title: Navy Rescues Seven Victims of Bayelsa Boat Mishap, Uncovers 117,000 Litres of Stolen Crude Oil
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy, in collaboration with local divers and members of the Abedigbene Fishing Community, has rescued seven passengers following a boat mishap in the waters around Abedigbene, in Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the incident involved a passenger boat travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa, which reportedly had eight people on board.

“Following a distress report from a local fisherman, personnel of Forward Operating Base (FOB) Formoso, deployed at Labrador Lagosgbene Houseboat, promptly mobilised to the scene and commenced search and rescue operations with the support of local divers and community members.

“The rescued passengers included the Bayelsa State Commissioner for Trade, Industry and Investment, Dr Ebieri Jones, an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, and five other passengers,” Captain Folorunsho said in the statement.

He said the survivors were taken to the houseboat, where they received first aid, with preliminary assessments indicating that none had sustained visible injuries.

He, however, regretted that one passenger, identified as a police officer, remained missing, while search and rescue efforts continued to locate the officer.

He said, “On 6 November 2026, the Commissioner and the six other survivors were conveyed to Yenagoa to reunite with their respective families.

The Commanding Officer of FOB Formoso commended the personnel for their prompt response and professionalism, while acknowledging the invaluable support of the local divers and host community.

Captain Folorunsho noted that the successful rescue further highlighted the importance of collaboration between security agencies and coastal communities in strengthening maritime safety and protecting lives.

Meanwhile, the Forward Operating Base (FOB) Bonny deactivated three illegal refining sites in Awokiri Community, Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, uncovering approximately 117,000 litres of stolen crude oil.

The naval spokesperson said the operation was conducted following credible intelligence indicating the activation of new illegal refining sites in the area.

“During the operation, the naval team discovered 16 dugout pits, nine of which contained approximately 115,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil. An additional storage tank contained about 2,000 litres, bringing the total volume to approximately 117,000 litres. Four other pits contained water, while three were freshly excavated. The identified sites, pits and products were handled in accordance with extant regulations.”

Folorunsho said the operation underscored the Nigerian Navy’s sustained commitment to combating crude oil theft and illegal bunkering through intelligence-driven operations.

He added that by dismantling illegal refining infrastructure and disrupting criminal networks, the Service continued to protect critical oil and gas assets and safeguard the nation’s economic interests.

World.title: Navy Sustains Zero Piracy Incidents in One Year, Secures Nine Convictions of Crude Oil Thieves
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy has said that between November 2025 and November 2026, it sustained Nigeria’s zero-piracy status and secured nine convictions for offences relating to crude oil theft and pipeline vandalism.

The Service also disclosed that, within the period under review, it deactivated 168 illegal refining sites, destroyed 363 dugout pits, arrested 259 suspects and seized four vessels suspected of involvement in crude oil theft.

The Director of Naval Information, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, in a statement marking Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abba’s first year in office, further revealed that the Service recovered over 7.48 million litres of stolen crude oil and illegally refined petroleum products within the year.

Folorunsho said the Nigerian Navy recorded significant operational, infrastructural and institutional achievements during Vice Admiral Idi Abba’s first year as Chief of the Naval Staff, strengthening its contribution to maritime security, the protection of national assets and national development.

He said, “A major operational initiative was the activation of Operation Delta Sentinel in January 2026 to strengthen efforts against crude oil theft, illegal bunkering and other maritime crimes. The Navy also commissioned three high-speed patrol vessels, NNS Oloibiri, NNS Mambila and NNS Gurara, in June 2026 to enhance maritime surveillance, operational reach and response capabilities.

“The Service also advanced infrastructure development and personnel welfare through the construction and commissioning of over 36 projects, including accommodation, medical, office and multipurpose facilities. In addition, it commenced the development of a 200-bed Reference Hospital at Navy Town, Asokoro, Abuja. Through the Chief of the Naval Staff Special Intervention Quick Impact Projects (CNS-SIQIP) and other community initiatives, the Navy completed over 93 community development projects.”

These projects, he said, included 18 solar-powered boreholes, the renovation of 11 school buildings, the construction and equipping of 11 healthcare centres, and the provision of electricity infrastructure in three communities.

“On human capacity development, the Nigerian Navy graduated and inducted its inaugural batch of 328 Nigerian Navy Marines. The personnel were deployed to reinforce ongoing operations, particularly against asymmetric threats in northern Nigeria, while training for a second batch continued,” the Naval Spokesperson said.

Furthermore, the Navy strengthened regional maritime cooperation through its participation in exercises, including Obangame Express 2026, Coastal Grip 2, Grand African Nemo 2026 and Crocodile Lift.

World.title: Nigeria Deepens Defence Ties with Germany
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), has assured the German Government that Nigeria remains committed to honouring existing military agreements and deepening strategic defence cooperation with its international partners.

General Musa gave the assurance when he received a high-level delegation led by the Ambassador of Germany to Nigeria and ECOWAS, His Excellency Stefan Rössel, at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters in Abuja.

Welcoming the Ambassador and his delegation, the minister assured them that the ministry would ensure the optimal deployment and maintenance of all defence support equipment provided to the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

According to a statement by the Minister of Defence’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, General Musa also pledged that all operational and administrative concerns raised during the meeting would be addressed expeditiously.

Reflecting on previous fruitful engagements during his tenure as Chief of Defence Staff, Musa expressed Nigeria’s profound gratitude to Germany for its sustained technical assistance, particularly the provision of critical medical facilities for Nigerian troops over the years.

Earlier, Ambassador Rössel extended his heartfelt condolences to the minister, the Armed Forces and the people of Nigeria over the recent Nigerian Air Force plane crash. He explained that his visit was aimed at reinforcing bilateral relations, strengthening security cooperation and exploring new avenues for operational support.

Both leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment to advancing a robust and mutually beneficial multilateral defence architecture.

World.title: Abia Moves to Harness AGOA’s Benefits, Hosts 1st Africando Conference in Umuahia
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

As part of efforts at harnessing the United States economic development programme, the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), the Abia State Government has announced the hosting of the 2026 African Diaspora Conference and Expo (Africando).

The conference scheduled for November 17-19, at the state capital, Umuahia, is expected to bring together African and US businessmen and women, educators, government policymakers and administrators, trade and investment experts, bankers and representatives from international organisations, with the aim of improving trade and expanding markets for African products in the international marketplace.

Speaking with journalists in Abuja yesterday, the Chief of Staff to Governor Alex Otti, Mr. Caleb Ajagba, attributed the choice of Abia State as host of the Africando, to the transformation of the state to an industrial hub, in the current administration.

He recall that Governor Otti, on assumption of office decided to prioritize the issue of infrastructure, security, power supply, manpower development and entrepreneurial capacity in other to exploit the potentials of the state and people of Abia.

According to the Chief of Staff, Abia’s manufacturing base, particularly in Aba, offered opportunities for international business partnerships and investment.

Stating that, “Aba is a place where anything can be manufactured”, Ajagba disclosed that Africando aims to provide necessary resources to small and medium scale businesses.

The Chief of Staff added that besides making funds available for acquisition of equipment, the Otti’s administration had put in place policies and programmes that would create an international market for products.

He disclosed that the government as part of measures at encouraging participation at the conference has made registration easy for those interested.

Ajagba also promised that the state government would work with the organisers to ensure the conference delivered practical economic benefits to businesses and the state.

Also speaking, the President, Foundation for Democracy in Africa, Mr. Fred Oladeinde, disclosed that plans were underway to establish a trade centre and civil society network to facilitate access to international markets, investment opportunities and business partnerships for local enterprises.

According to him, the proposed platforms would work with the Abia Global Chamber of Commerce, Nigerian-American Chamber of Commerce, Nigerian Association of Women Entrepreneurs and other partners to strengthen trade connections.

Oladeinde said manufacturers and entrepreneurs in Aba, a major commercial and manufacturing centre, stood to benefit from improved access to markets across Nigeria and West Africa.

He added that the initiative would support advocacy for a long-term extension of the AGOA, following its reported two-year extension to December 2028.

Oladeinde said the expo’s theme, ‘Deepening U.S – Africa Commercial Ties in the Area of AfCFTA and AGOA’, would provide an opportunity to examine how existing trade frameworks could translate into greater commercial opportunities for African businesses.

He said discussions would cover eight sectors, including agriculture, consumer goods, financial services, insurance and healthcare.

Meanwhile, he disclosed that outstanding Africans would also receive the Medal of Glory Award during the event.

Also, the proposed trade centre and civil society network are expected to be unveiled during the three-day expo in Umuahia.

World.title: Rassie Erasmus gets sweet birthday wish from old school
World.content:
Springbok coacj Rassie Erasmus receieved a special birthday message from his old school. Images via IG

Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus received a special birthday wish from his alma mater, Hoërskool Despatch, this week.

The rugby hero turned 54 on Thursday, 5 November.

RASSIE GETS EXCITING BIRTHDAY WISH FROM OLD SCHOOL

On their social media accounts, Hoërskool Despatch – the Eastern Cape High School where Rassie Erasmus matriculated more than 30 years ago – posted a special birthday wish to the Springbok coach.



In the clip, learners of the Afrikaans medium school performed an upbeat war cry for the rugby hero who turned 54 years old this week.

The school shared: “We are incredibly proud of you, your achievements and the inspiration you are to our learners, our community and South Africa”

Rassie responded to the post with a comment that read: “This is so special! Love Despatch and all of you. Blow the flame high ❤️ Despatcher for life”.

PASSION FOR RUGBY

While attending Hoërskool Despatch, Rassie Erasmus developed a passion for rugby.

In 2018, his former coach, Coenie Strumpher, told SABC News that the rugby hero was an exceptionally talented schoolboy.



He shared: “He was so talented. It didn’t matter in which position he played.”

His former coach, Coenie Strumpher, told SABC News in March 2018 that Erasmus was an exceptionally talented schoolboy.

He recalled moving him from eighthman to flyhalf, saying: “He was so talented. It didn’t matter in which position he played.”

Rassie went on to play professionally for the Free State Cheetahs and Gauteng Lions, before making his Springbok debut in 1997.

He had 36 test match appearances and played until 2001. As the national team coach, he’s helped the Springboks win back-to-back World Cup titles in 2019 and 2023.

Now dubbed the unofficial “best rugby coach in the world,” Rassie once played alongside legends like Joost van der Westhuizen, Breyton Paulse, Percy Montgomery, and Nick Mallett.

World.title: Eldorado’s ‘Cookie Lyon’ sends message to ‘haters’ after being voted out
World.content:
Former Patriotic Alliance (PA) ward councillor Juwairiya Kaldine – who calls herself “Cookie Lyon from Eldorado Park” – has vowed to make a “comeback” after the party was defeated by the Democratic Alliance (DA) in this week’s local government elections. Kaldine has represented Ward 18 since 2021.

PA’s ‘COOKIE LYON’ COUNCILLOR VOWS TO FIGHT BACK

This week, PA president Gayton McKenzie confirmed that the party had lost its five-year stronghold on Eldorado Park’s Ward 17 and 18, the latter occupied by ward councillor Juwairiya Kaldine.

The ward was defeated by DA’s Fazel Jaffer, who was once a PA member.



The news came as a shock to fans of Kaldine, who is affectionately known as Eldo’s “Cookie Lyon”, named after a fearless female character played by actress Taraji P Henson, on US streaming series Empire.

The 34-year-old has helmed Ward 18 since 2021.

Known for her no-nonsense approach, the PA councillor shared a post on her social media platforms acknowledging her defeat.

She posted: “My comeback will be greater than my setback, may the name ‘Juwairiya Kaldine’ remain in the history books of South African politics, and may it remain in the mouths of all my haters”.

Kaldine, who has bragged about being “the most talked about ward councillor in South Africa”, made headlines in 2024 over an alleged voice recording accusing the PA of being funded by gangsters and drug peddlers. The allegations were disputed by McKenzie, who claimed that the recordings were “doctored”.

‘ACCEPT DEFEAT GRACIOUSLY’

Meanwhile, Gayton McKenzie has called on PA members to “accept defeat graciously”, after losing wards 17 and 18 in Eldorado Park.



The 51-year-old claimed that he had been “inundated with conspiracy theories and allegations” about the party’s “shocking loss of both wards”.

He shared in a Facebook post: “I hereby wanna make it public that we accept defeat in both wards and wanna congratulate the DA. We should not be sore losers.

“The people made their choice, and instead of blaming the people, we should go and do some introspection. The numbers we had were totally wrong.”

WHAT’S NEXT FOR ELDORADO PARK?

Ward 18 in Eldorado Park, Johannesburg, to the DA’s Fazel Jaffer.

World.title: Actor Roderick Jaftha’s worrying post: ‘My body has collapsed…’
World.content:
Actor Roderick Jaftha has sparked concern with one of his latest Facebook posts about experiencing poor health. The TV star is known for his roles in soapies such as Generations, Villa Rosa, and Rhythm City, and in films including Kings of Jo’Burg and The Emissary.

In recent years, the veteran TV star has faced financial setbacks, appealing to the public for donations to buy food and pay his rent.

RODERICK JAFTHA’S WORRYING FACEBOOK POST

On Friday, 6 November, Roderick Jaftha sparked concern with a post about ailing health.



The 63-year-old shared a picture of himself lying in bed with the caption: “Comes a time when you have to face your mortality. This morning, I finally broke. Years of stress buildup finally caught up with me. My body collapsed, my blood pressure shot through the roof. I could hardly move. Yet and still, I have to march on. “

He continued: “Seeing the worried look on my kid’s faces strengthened me. Made me more determined than ever to win this fight. I’m so close. Either to victory or death”.

In recent days, Roderick has shared posts about going through “dire personal circumstances” and “suffering in silence”.



‘NO AMOUNT OF FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT HELPS’

In the comments section, Roderick Jaftha’s Facebook followers urged him to remain hopeful and positive

When one follower commented about the increase of thespians suffering from poor health and financial strain, the actor responded: “Perhaps we need a minister that can fix things, amongst other solutions.

He added: “It’s not about political affiliation for me. Someone needs to take a hard look at the dealings and shenanigans that are going on behind the scenes, crippling the industry”.



When another claimed actors and sports stars “need classes in financial management”, Roderick clapped back: “Your comment comes from a place of ignorance as to how this business works”

He went on to elaborate: “Even when you’re making money, with few exceptions, it’s not much. The bulk of the money goes to producers and channels. We do not get paid residuals, as is the case in most countries. The work itself can also be fleeting in nature. The government taxes us 25% of every cent we earn. Medical aid and pension are your own responsibility.

“Now let’s say you get a year contract on a show. Let us also say your fee is of such a nature, that you are able to save and live within your means. As soon as that contract ends and is not renewed, you are forced to dig into your savings. You could conceivably be unemployed for the next year. By the time you get another job, the process starts all over again. Most of us are constantly starting from scratch.



He added: “No amount of financial management helps you. I know, I’ve tried. Add to that, not qualifying easily for a bond or vehicle finance, by virtue of being a contract worker. It’s a nightmare.

In 2024, Roderick Jaftha appealed to the public for donations to buy food for his family and pay his rent. Later, reports emerged that the Minister of Sport, Arts, and Culture, Gayton McKenzie, donated R5 000 to assist the artist.

World.title: Eswatini’s Princess Ntsandvweni marks 12th birthday by giving back
World.content:
Princess Ntsandvweni Dlamini from the Kingdom of Eswatini opted to celebrate her 12th birthday by giving back to the community of Hosea, a rural part of the country.

The young royal is the eldest daughter of King Mswati III and Queen Sindiswa LaFogiyane. She previously drew attention for performing the traditional kutsamba dance alongside her mother at the Umkhosi Wemaganu ceremony.

PRINCESS NTSANDVWENI CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY AT HOSEA

The birthday celebrations kicked off with the handover of a newly built three-bedroom house to 65-year-old Lillian Mbamba in Ondiyaneni, Hosea.



The house, a gift from the King, reflects his ongoing commitment to uplifting communities in Eswatini.

The event was attended by members of the royal family, residents, and Deputy Prime Minister Thulisile Dladla.

Other local leaders who attended included Chief Mlotjwa of KaLiba and Shisel­weni Regional Administrator Themba Nhlan­gan­iso Mas­uku.

Masuku warmly welcomed the royal visit and expressed his appreciation for the gifts and donations shared with the community of Hosea.

The birthday celebrations continued in KaLiba, where school learners cheerfully sang the birthday song to Princess Ntsandvweni. Her younger sister, Princess Nolikhwa, stood beside her as she cut her cake.
