Princess Ntsandvweni then donated pairs of school shoes and socks to 61 learners, while 100 food parcels were distributed to families in need, a thoughtful gesture that brought smiles to many faces.

Upon completion of the houses, two underprivileged families are set receive newly built homes in Hosea.

PRINCESS NTSANDVWENI EARNS PRAISE

Kokolu543: The way you and your sister are so respectful. [I] bumped into you and her at Gables. [When I] greeted you, bodyguards and all, [I] thought you weren’t going to respond. But you did, and respectfully so. Thank you for blessing the less privileged. God bless you, boNkhosi.

Nokwazi Motsa: One thing about our Princesses [they are] well-raised. Keep it up, guys. You can humble yourselves, shem.

Si_phe_sihle5: Wonderful work, Princess, God bless you.

ESWATINI ROYALS DEVOTED TO SERVING COMMUNITIES

Beyond the glitz and glam associated with royalty, the Eswatini royal family has remained devoted to serving the people of the country through various charitable initiatives.

In June 2026, the communities of Timphisini and Ntfonjeni were blessed by the generosity of Prince Sicalo Dlamini, son of King Mswati III and Queen Nomsa LaMatsebula.

Through his Sicalo Foundation, he donated essential parcels to over 3000 elderly people and schoolchildren in the area.

World.title: Teen rugby prodigy dies after battle with meningitis
World.content:
Frans van der Bergh, a 13-year-old rugby prodigy from Springs, has died of suspected meningitis. His death was confirmed by his mother, Jeanine, in the Facebook group, Bid vir Frans.

The teen from Laerskool Christiaan Beyers recently took part in the U13 Craven Week in Bloemfontein.

SPRINGS RUGBY TEEN DIES OF MENINGITIS

In the Facebook group Bid vir Frans, the mother of Frans van der Bergh confirmed his passing on Wednesday, 4 November.



His school, Laerskool Christiaan Beyers, and his rugby club, Valke Laerskole Rugby, also shared a heartfelt tribute to him.

The 13-year-old reportedly contracted meningitis after developing a severe sinus infection several weeks ago.

Frans, who was treated in the ICU of Glenwood Hospital in Benoni, suffered from seizures after developing an infection near his brain. He was administered strong antibiotic medication.

Before his death, a neurosurgeon decided against performing surgery on the teen.

After his death, his mother, Jeanine, confirmed that she had decided to donate Frans’s organs, six of which went to children in dire health circumstances



Jeanine shared in the Facebook group: “Frans has always had an incredibly big love for the people around him. His heart was full of caring, love and a desire to make a difference in the lives of others.

“Even though our hearts break into a million pieces, we find comfort in knowing that our son’s love for others will live on even after his passing.

“My Frans, you always wanted to make a difference in this world. And just look, my child.. You are going to give six other children a chance at a future”

His memorial service will be held on Thursday, 12 November

In June, Frans van der Bergh and the Valke rugby club participated in U13 Craven Week in Bloemfontein. He also played on the first team at his school, Laerskool Christiaan Beyers, where he won several trophies.

WHAT ARE THE SYMPTOMS?

Meningitis in children is a serious condition involving inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It can develop rapidly, particularly bacterial meningitis, and is a medical emergency requiring urgent treatment.

The symptoms include:

High fever with cold hands and feet

Stiff neck

Severe headache

Vomiting or nausea

Confusion and lethargy

Seizures

According to the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD), there were 65 confirmed cases of invasive meningococcal [bacterial] disease recorded in South Africa in the first two quarters of 2026.

World.title: IEC confirms time for 2026 Local Government Election results announcement
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has confirmed when the official results of the 2026 Local Government Elections will be announced. Image: X @IECSouthAfrica

The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has confirmed when the official results of the 2026 Local Government Elections will be announced.

The commission plans to announce the election results on Sunday, 8 November from 18:00.

ELECTIONS 2026 | Result: DA wins Nelson Mandela Bay metro



The announcement will bring the national counting process to its formal conclusion following several days of voting, counting and results capturing across the country.

South Africans are now awaiting the final outcome of an election that has delivered significant political shifts, particularly in several major metropolitan municipalities.

Latest numbers

As at the time of publishing, 99% of the votes around the country have been tallied.

The ANC are on track to record the greatest number of votes – but will receive a record low amount of around 30.84%.

In the most recent 2021 elections, the ANC garnered 45.59%.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) will finish second with around 24.6% (21.66% in 2021), with the MK Party in third with roughly 9.66%.



The MK Party were formed in 2023 and therefore did not contest the 2021 elections.

Coalition negotiations expected to follow

The 2026 elections have produced several closely contested councils, with smaller political parties potentially holding the balance of power.

The formal announcement of results will provide the basis for the next stage of negotiations as political parties seek to establish municipal administrations.

For voters, the announcement will confirm the final outcome of an election that will determine who governs South Africa’s municipalities over the next five years.

World.title: 5 wards recounted by IEC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has ordered the recount of votes in five wards.

The affected wards are in the City of Tshwane, Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality, Thaba Chweu Local Municipality and Breede Valley Municipality.

IEC Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Mosotho Moepya says the assigned seats in the provisional results may change as a result of the recount.

ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula said on Saturday that it had lodged disputes with the IEC and was able to win back wards from their disputes. Other parties, including the MK Party have also lodged disputes with the Commission that are being investigated.

World.title: 'This has been a catastrophic outcome' - Fikile Mbalula
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - "This has been a catastrophic outcome for the ANC," says secretary-general Fikile Mbalula.

Speaking on the sidelines of the preliminary local government results on Saturday. Chief Electoral Officer Mosotho Moepya said that the IEC hope to have the final results on Sunday.

Mbalula said the interim results in the country's municipalities and metros are catastrophic for the liberation movement.

Mbalula says while the party will not be making any hasty decisions, they will put the elections outcome to the national conference in 2027.

The ANC lost control of six of the country's eight metros. They have retained Buffalo City in the Eastern Cape and Mangaung in the Free State. uMkhonto weSizwe Party has retained eThekwini, while the Democratic Alliance has retained majority votes in Cape Town, Nelson Mandela Bay, Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane.

Despite this, the ANC still has majority of the votes nationally, with more seats than votes in most metros. Mbalula says they are not in a hurry to have coalition talks. Instead, they are considering the option of being a 'principled' opposition party.

World.content:

According to the party's Tony Yengeni, they are ready to start talk with 'Black' parties.

The coalition negotiators will consist of Duduzane Zuma, Dali Mpofu, Willies Mchunu, Tony Yengeni, Mxolisi Phakati, Lindi Mtshali and Thanti Mthanti

World.title: 'Cat' Matlala to testify before Madlanga Commission on Monday and Tuesday
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Alleged crime boss Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala is expected to appear before the Madlanga Commission on Monday and Tuesday.

Matlala, who remains behind bars facing several criminal charges, is expected to be questioned about government tenders and alleged criminal networks.

The Commission aims to conclude Phase Two of its inquiry this month before moving on to Phase Three.

The next phase will include the return of KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi to the witness stand.

The inquiry will then compile its final report, which is due to President Cyril Ramaphosa by 25 January 2027.

World.title: IEC processes hundreds of objections ahead of election results announcement
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Electoral Commission says it is working to ensure credible local government election results.

IEC officials are processing hundreds of election-related objections, including the MK Party’s call for an audit of the eThekwini results.

Voter turnout currently stands at 45 percent, while the commission says it has experienced no technical glitches during the week.

The IEC is expected to announce the results on Sunday, once all objections have been considered.

"I know that our voter turnout numbers are sitting at 45 percent. This is a very good number in terms of, you know, the checks and balances, the controls to say where you stay; that's exactly where you need to vote," said the IEC's Vusi Vuma.

"So we did not have any glitches technically, and we are looking forward to tomorrow when the commission will be announcing the results. At this point, we are currently busy with objections.

"The objections closed yesterday; we received hundreds of them, and it's part and parcel of the process. We're going to process each and every one of them, and make sure that, you know, by the time we announce the results, everyone is happy."

World.title: France braces for protests as Yellow Vests urge 'mass disobedience'
World.content:
PARIS - French unions and student groups are set to take to the streets for another day of protests on Saturday, while the Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris despite a ban by authorities.

The demonstrations follow weeks of youth-led unrest and nationwide strikes that drew hundreds of thousands of workers protesting over the rising cost of living.

They come less than six months before voters elect a new head of state to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in the opinion polls.

Student groups and trade unions have called for an authorised march in central Paris "against the high cost of living and in support of young people".

Yellow Vests activists, however, have refused to join, instead calling for a separate rally at Place de la Concorde, near the lower house of parliament and presidential palace, despite a ban by authorities.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 police officers and security forces would be deployed across the country.

"If there are any rioters or looters... we'll be ready and waiting for them," he said.

The demonstrations have been largely peaceful, but there have at times been clashes with police or vandalism on their sidelines, including on October 17, when France saw its worst rioting in years.

On Thursday, hundreds of thousands of striking workers took to the streets across France in mostly orderly protests, although clashes between demonstrators and police broke out in several cities.

-'Mass disobedience'-

The Yellow Vests movement, which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron's government over planned fuel-tax hikes, has called for its banned rally to go ahead.

"We are calling for mass disobedience," said Benjamin Ball, a member of its coordinating committee.

Authorities are determined to prevent a repeat of the rioting and looting that marred the October 17 demonstrations, although the interior ministry said Thursday's protests had "generally gone well" despite 642 arrests.

The police response has faced criticism for being heavy-handed, with dozens of internal investigations launched into allegations of brutality against demonstrators.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has said he will discuss wages and purchasing power with representatives of trade unions and employers' organisations on Monday.

"The only thing that will bring the protests to an end is a response to the demands that have been put forward for several weeks by workers, civil servants, young people and pensioners," an inter-union coalition said on Friday.

The unions are calling for an increase in the minimum wage, which has not received any discretionary boost since 2012, across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people.

With the European Union's second-largest economy under pressure to rein in debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters.

World.title: Cyberattack shuts down internet fan fiction library
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - One of the world's most popular fan fiction libraries has been dark for over a week after a cyberattack forced it offline, leaving millions of fans without access to their favourite stories.

Since October 29, anyone trying to reach Archive of Our Own -- known to devotees as AO3 -- has been met with a message saying the site is down for maintenance.

"It's all over my social feed. People are in withdrawal," Johanna Sarriot, a writer and co-founder of pop-up romance bookstore Love Love Books in Los Angeles, told AFP.

Fan fiction refers to stories written by amateur authors using characters and worlds from already-existing books, films or TV shows.

Contributors rewrite endings, invent romances or give minor characters their own adventures, then share them online for free.

Once a niche hobby, it has become a launchpad for the publishing industry, generating breakout smashes like E.L. James's "Fifty Shades of Grey," which began as "Twilight" fan fiction, and Ali Hazelwood's bestseller "The Love Hypothesis," which sprang from the "Star Wars" universe.

Launched in 2008, AO3 has become the genre's main home, with more than 11 million registered users and nearly 18 million works stored on the platform.

In 2019, it won a Hugo Award for Best Related Work, one of science fiction's most prestigious prizes.

"We wanted to make sure that there was a place for fans to engage in non-commercial creativity in ways that wouldn't barrage them with ads, censor them to placate advertisers, sell their data, or do anything but provide a space for fandom," said Harvard Law School professor Rebecca Tushnet, who helped found the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) which runs the site.

- 'AO3 is not gone' -

Romance fans have been among the hardest hit by the outage.

World.title: Mudavadi urges Western Kenya to unite, says region cannot remain on sidelines
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi. [File, Standard]

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi has urged Western Kenya to unite ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying the region must strengthen its political representation to have a greater say in national decision-making.

Speaking during a UDA delegates' meeting in Shitoto village, Mumias East, Kakamega County, he said Western Kenya could not afford to remain on the sidelines while decisions affecting the country were being made.

"2027 is the moment we must change the narrative. We must make sure that we are at the table where decisions are made. We cannot afford to remain spectators when the future of our country and our region is being determined," he said.

Mudavadi said parliamentary influence depended on numbers, arguing that electing more MPs would give the region a stronger voice in key parliamentary committees, including the Budget Committee.

"Parliament exercises authority in its own right. We want more MPs so that we can have a say in the Budget Committee and other important committees. These positions are secured through numbers, and numbers matter when decisions affecting the country are being made," he said.

Turning to the opposition, Mudavadi described its leaders as divided and challenged them to present clear manifestos outlining what they would offer Kenyans.

He said the divisions within the opposition would work in President William Ruto's favour as he seeks re-election in 2027, expressing confidence that he would win in the first round.

"We want Ruto to win without a petition. We want to thrash them in the first round," he said.

World.title: Family identifies two security officers involved in Abshir Abdi abduction
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

LSK president Charles Kanjama leads members in a protest over the disappearance of lawyer Abshir Abdi. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The family of Nairobi lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi has identified two security officers alleged to have taken part in their kin's abduction, even as his colleagues threatened mass protests to push for his release.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) said the two names have been forwarded to the police to aid in investigations and demanded that the office of the Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, speed up the probe into the abduction.

"One is named Siad and the other is Hussein, and we want them released for investigation, arrest, prosecution, conviction, sentencing and imprisonment," said LSK.

The revelation came during a demonstration led by (LSK outside the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police and other towns yesterday .

Abshir was forcibly taken on November 1 along Muchai Road, his vehicle was pursued and intercepted by armed individuals in two vehicles before he was seized.

While state security agencies have denied holding him in custody, court filings and colleagues suggest his abduction may be connected to his professional work representing clients in high-profile cases involving senior police officers.

Furthermore, the LSK presented additional names of security personnel linked to the incident, demanding immediate legal action against Chief Inspector Vitalis Kibet, Inspector Kennedy Kimani Karanja, Siad Mohammed, Abdurahman of the Anti-Terrorism Police Unit (ATPU), and KDF officer Ali Hussein.

The leadership voiced their frustration over the state's inaction and the alarming pattern of extrajudicial actions targeting officers of the court. Representatives insisted that lawyers must be allowed to execute their duties without fear of intimidation, torture, or abduction.

"We demand that the officers involved be handed over, arrested, prosecuted, and convicted. We will stand in the courts, in the streets, and in the boardrooms until abductions come to an end," they said in a statement.

The LSK has issued a stern ultimatum to the police command, including the president, DIG Gilbert Masengeli, Inspector General Douglas Kanja, and senior commanders. If Abshir is not released safely and the identified suspects are not formally charged in court by Monday, the LSK warned it will initiate private prosecutions itself.

Furthermore, the society threatened to bring activities to a complete shutdown and demand the immediate resignation of Kanja, Masingeli and Minister for Security Kipchumba Murkomen, carrying their demonstrations to Parliament and State House if necessary.

As court proceedings continue under a habeas corpus application at the Milimani High Court, the legal fraternity remains resolute: the protest at Jogoo House is merely the beginning of an unyielding campaign for justice and the rule of law.

In Nakuru, lawyers protested within the Law Courts, calling for his production.

“It is shocking that one of our colleagues was picked and today we do not know where he is. Unless we voice our concern, there will be complete lawlessness in the country,” said LSK member Ekaterina Handa. “Our lives matter and silencing lawyers is silencing justice. we will not relent until we get justice.”

Rift Valley LSK Chair Wangari Mwangi said it was shocking that the alleged abduction was captured on CCTV.

She rubbished the narrative that the missing lawyer was involved in a crime syndicate, maintaining that he should have been arrested and charged in court. [Additional reporting by Daniel Chege]

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: New Zealand in political limbo after knife-edge election
World.content:
New Zealand voters face weeks of political limbo after a knife-edge election left the country’s conservative coalition government at risk of losing its majority following just a single term in office.

Saturday’s preliminary results show Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National-led coalition with a two seat majority. But the margin is so tight, a small variance in the final tally could yet leave the opposition left-wing bloc with a chance to form a government.

Luxon told supporters gathered in Auckland that while it looked like his party had a pathway to form the next government, the race remained “too close to call.”

He said the country would need to wait until the Electoral Commission delivered the final official results on November 27 for certainty. Coalition negotiations could then drag on for weeks before a government is formed.

Preliminary numbers show the right-wing coalition grouping has 67 seats in the 131-seat parliament.

Should it fall short of a majority, Luxon would likely need to turn to the progressive centrist Opportunity party, which will enter parliament for first time, for support. Prior to the election he had ruled out working with the party.

The center-left Labour party received the highest share of the popular vote under the country’s mixed-member proportional voting system by a tiny margin, but a stronger performance in individual electorates has delivered National more seats in parliament.

Labour Leader Chris Hipkins made light of Saturday’s inconclusive results as he addressed supporters in Wellington, saying: “Tonight, New Zealand has spoken. It may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you’ve said.”

Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins attends an election night watch party, in Upper Hutt, New Zealand. Hollie Adams/Reuters

Hipkins – who served briefly as prime minister in 2023 – did not concede, telling the crowd that “every vote matters. And every vote must be counted.”

The opposition grouping of center-left Labour, the leftist Greens and indigenous party Te Pati Māori is projected to have 57 seats. But the bloc could have a path to power if it picked up some additional seats in the final count, and if it secured the support of Opportunity.

Struggle for reelection

The incumbent coalition – the country’s most right-wing in a generation – took power in 2023, capitalizing on an electorate looking for change in the wake of the Covid-19 pandemic.

But its struggle to secure an emphatic victory this time signifies the level of public discontent over living costs, stubbornly high unemployment rates and concerns over healthcare.

Luxon’s center-right National party emerges a diminished force, crashing to just 29.3% of the popular vote, down from 38% in 2023, according to the preliminary count.

A person places his vote in a ballot box at a voting place on election day in Auckland, New Zealand. Alex Robertson/AP

Its coalition partners, the right-wing-libertarian ACT party and the nationalist New Zealand First Party, increased their vote share to 11% and 10% respectively, putting them both in a stronger position to dictate terms in pending coalition talks.

The stronger-than-expected result for New Zealand First and ACT, and National’s weakened position, raises the prospect of the coalition moving further to the right in a second term and further embracing culture-war policies.

On the campaign trail the ACT vowed to end affirmative action schemes at the country’s medical schools, while New Zealand First promised sweeping immigration changes and voiced support for a review of the ban on gay conversion therapy.

Luxon, would also have a complex job filling key cabinet posts in a second term, with a raft of senior lawmakers from his National party, including finance minister Nicola Willis and parliament’s speaker Gerry Brownlee, losing their seats.

Voters turn to minor parties

Swing voters turned away from National and Labour, which have dominated Wellington politics for nearly a century, opting to support minor parties entrenched further to the right and the left, as well as Opportunity in the center.

It’s political newcomer leader Qiulae Wong, 38, who applied for the party’s leadership by responding to a job  a year ago, told supporters they had voted “to change New Zealand politics for good.”

The Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong poses for a portrait outside Parliament in Wellington, New Zealand. Charlotte Graham-McLay/AP

The party, which secured 6% of the vote, becomes the first total outsider party (not involving established political figures) to enter parliament since the country moved to a mixed-member proportional voting system in the mid-1990s.

Depending on the final vote tally, Opportunity, which positions itself as both business-and climate-friendly, could yet find itself in the kingmaker position – with both the right and the left groupings vying for its support.

World.title: ‘Like a bolt from the blue’: Israel’s president shocked by Trump announcing end of aid
World.content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said it was “like a bolt from the blue” when President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday, the day of the midterm elections, that he would end US aid to Israel.

Herzog brought up the issue during a meeting with the Yashar party, led by Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

“The issue of the American aid worries me greatly, and it also fell on me like a bolt from the blue. We have an (memorandum of understanding) with the US that is supposed to last until 2028 and this is one of the major goals, and therefore a government must be formed and not go to repeated elections,” he said.

Trump said aid to Israel would end this year, two years ahead of the formal end of the memorandum of understanding (MoU), which provides Israel with $3.8 billion per year to purchase American weaponry.

But he offered few details in the announcement, which was made in an Election Day phone interview with Fox News. Netanyahu has not made any public comment on the announcement.

“It’s a bad talking point because when you say, ‘Why don’t we give everybody $4 billion?’ Israel’s our number one; we give them more than anybody else, and they no longer need it,” Trump told Fox.

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee said he was looking for clarification on what would happen. In an interview with Israel’s Channel 12 News, he defended military aid, which has grown increasingly unpopular in both the Democratic and Republican parties.

“Americans need to know the value of the relationship,” he said. “It’s not about what Americans are putting into it. It’s about what they are getting out of it. Maybe we haven’t done a good job helping the American public to recognize and be grateful for the partnership with Israel, which has benefited their lives every day.”

Huckabee also disagreed with Vice President JD Vance, who said on X that the relationship with Israel contributed to Republican losses in the midterms. A staunch support of Israel, Huckabee said, “I don’t think support for Israel is toxic in the conservative wing and the Republican Party.”

A task for Herzog

While Herzog navigates Trump’s announcement the US is cutting off $4 billion in aid to Israel, he faces a crucial task following elections in his own country.

Eisenkot emerged with a majority of the incoming Israeli Knesset’s backing after the conclusion of the president’s meetings with the elected parties, following Israel’s election late last month. Herzog held two days of consultations with representatives of all of the parties elected to the incoming Knesset.

Netanyahu secured the backing of only 46 seats after one of his ultra-Orthodox allies refused to endorse him, leaving him far short of the 61-seat majority needed. Eisenkot secured the backing of lawmakers holding 67 seats, but 19 of those are held by Arab-led parties, complicating his path to oust Israel’s longest-serving leader.

Herzog must now decide who gets the mandate to form the next government, a decision he said he will make Sunday. “The results of the consultations may appear clear, but the authority vested in me by law is to determine who has the ability to form a government, and that is not entirely clear,” he said after meeting all the parties. In a statement Thursday evening, Eisenkot’s party made it clear it expects to receive the mandate to form a government.

“The decision of the people and the clear parliamentary majority leave no room for doubt: Israeli citizens chose change and expressed absolute no-confidence in outgoing Prime Minister Netanyahu and his government,” the Yashar party said. Netanyahu, the statement continued, “has no mandate, no majority, and no trust of the people.”

Whoever is chosen will have 28 days to negotiate with other parties over cabinet posts, budgets and policies. A 14-day extension is possible. If he fails, the mandate passes to another candidate for another four weeks. If he fails too, the Knesset gets a short window to put forward another candidate. If it cannot, the country automatically returns to the polls. Until Israel has a new government, Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister.

Netanyahu, who lost his parliamentary majority, is still challenging the election results and claims the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties through bribery, foreign funding and fraud. The opposition says he is trying to delay the swearing in of the Knesset Tuesday, and to prevent plans to replace the Knesset speaker with a lawmaker from the opposition.

World.title: Hegseth’s ‘fight, fight, fight’ video pours fuel on impeachment flames
World.content:
In seeking to fend off impeachment, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth may have strengthened his critics’ case for it.

In an ardent social media video Thursday, Hegseth vowed, “We Stand, We Fight” amid rising speculation he may become a scapegoat for the Republican disaster in midterm elections shaped by the unpopular Iran war.

President Donald Trump told reporters that the former Fox News anchor was doing a “fantastic job” at the Pentagon, even as expectations rose that the lame-duck GOP-led House of Representatives may vote to impeach the secretary next week.

Apart from Trump, few in Washington are willing to publicly defend Hegseth, especially after an electoral rout which showed the public’s disdain for a war the defense secretary has enthusiastically waged. So Hegseth took matters into his own hands with a video seemingly aimed at a single viewer: Trump.

The defense secretary tapped into Trump’s anger at his own impeachments in his first term, apparently positioning himself as a fellow victim of what the president sees as political chicanery. “It’s all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that,” Hegseth said.

The video was released at a volatile political moment with Washington rocked by the midterms results and as Trump’s inner circle splits over the war. It followed a another stunning social media post in which Vice President JD Vance pinned the GOP debacle Tuesday on the war and warned that those who supported it had lost the Senate for six years.

Turmoil in the administration underscored a wider point: It’s now clear that Trump lost the political front of the Iran war, whatever the strategic and military score. The Islamic Republic’s endurance after the initial US and Israeli onslaught inflicted a huge political cost on Trump, which was transmitted through soaring gasoline prices.

The result is that a president who broke his promise to avoid foreign wars will now spend the last two years of his term penned in by bumper Democratic majorities in Congress. Since the president isn’t going anywhere, political logic suggests that another high-profile figure may carry the can.

But Trump told reporters that he was not considering firing Hegseth, praising him for the US raid in Venezuela to extract then-dictator Nicolás Maduro earlier this year and for his Iran war leadership.

Still, Hegseth seems increasingly in danger of emulating Donald Rumsfeld, the defense secretary cut loose 20 years ago after voters dealt a huge midterm election defeat to Republicans because they wanted to punish another president, George W. Bush, for another unpopular war, in Iraq.

Trump can barely afford uncertainty over the Pentagon’s leadership since he’s facing an urgent dilemma over what to do next in the Iran war. There was growing speculation before the election that he’d escalate the conflict once votes were counted to try to force Tehran to negotiate or capitulate.

Doing so now would leave him isolated after the public abandoned him over the war and as schisms widen in his Cabinet. But backing away would force Trump to admit an embarrassing defeat, since Tehran is defying the US victory he craves.

President Donald Trump speaks with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at Memphis Air National Guard Base on March 23. Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

Reaching Trump through a medium he loves

Hegseth, a TV veteran, knows which buttons to push with his boss. His video was fiery, loaded with the kinds of lacerating cultural attacks that endeared him to Trump in the first place. He boasted about driving “the weird and the woke” out of the military. He also adopted the iconography of the assassination attempt that Trump survived in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024, presenting himself as the epitome of the toughness the president’s supporters perceive in their idol.

“He literally took a bullet for this nation,” Hegseth said. “He shook his fist and said ‘fight, fight, fight,’ and so will we.”

Hegseth’s speech was accompanied by a blitz of supportive social media posts by aides in what increasingly looks like an orchestrated campaign to save his job. The message to Trump and the MAGA movement is clear — if Hegseth walks the plank, it will mean an enormous defeat for the president. A senior administration official told CNN’s Haley Britzky on Thursday that “the Pentagon and White House made their positions crystal clear tonight. They are coming out swinging in support of Hegseth and that should tell you everything you need to know.”

It is not the first time the MAGA movement has mobilized for Hegseth. An aggressive pushback when his confirmation push was in deep trouble last year succeeded in saving his nomination.

Yet Hegseth’s latest self-defense may have misjudged the political moment.

He delivered his amped-up speech from the Pentagon steps, with a sign reading “Department of War” over his shoulder — a jarring choice two days after millions of Americans voted to repudiate the nation’s latest foreign entanglement. Such bombast may have worked earlier, at the apex of Trump’s power. Now it seems tin-eared.

After Vance’s break with Trump, it also hints at a leadership vacuum, especially since the commander in chief has spent hours following the election on his personal vanity projects, including the White House ballroom. On Thursday, Trump signed a proclamation designating the Cabinet Room and the Oval Office as national landmarks in an apparent effort to protect his gold-soaked redecorations.

Hegseth’s tactics complicate delicate defense spending push

The depth of Hegseth’s predicament will become clearer next week. Rep. Thomas Massie, an anti-Trump Republican who lost a primary to a challenger backed by the president, is vowing to bring up articles of impeachment.

Republican criticism of Hegseth on Capitol Hill may reach a crescendo when angry GOP lawmakers return to Washington after the electoral rout. What incentive will there be for defeated representatives or survivors who now face life in the minority to stand up for the architect of a war that doomed their careers?

There is no sign yet that there would be a two-thirds majority to convict Hegseth in an impeachment trial in the Senate and remove him from office. But even before this week’s elections, Hegseth’s brash appearances at hearings made him few friends on Capitol Hill. Lawmakers also accuse him of withholding details of Iran war strategy and Iranian attacks on US bases in the Middle East. A wide majority vote for impeachment in the House may make his position politically untenable.

A man walks past an anti-US mural in Tehran, Iran, on September 23. Majid Asgaripour/Wana News Agency/Reuters

Democratic House Minority leader Hakeem Jeffries on Thursday asked on social media, “Why is Pete Hegseth still around?” Last week, this would have been easy to put down to partisan sniping. But Jeffries now speaks as a future speaker of the House. Administration funding requests from next January will run through a Democratic Congress, and the Pentagon will need to play nice with the new majority party.

Even before then, Hegseth may be an impediment to the passage of the administration’s $1.5 trillion defense budget.

“I don’t think he has invested enough in the US Senate or Congress to even get a funding request done,” outgoing North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on Wednesday.

“This is beyond the Iran war; this about trying to provide the funding stream that the DOD needs to move forward,” Tillis said, adding that chairs and ranking members of key committees view the defense secretary as disengaged. “Hegseth is just not the right guy for the job,” he said.

Democrats seem to view the wobbling Hegseth as a chance to wound Trump even before they claim their majorities in the new year.

Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego told CNN’s Jake Tapper on Thursday that Hegseth’s video further undermined his authority. “You’re conducting a war right now, and then you’re reacting as if you’re on Fox News,” he said.

The Arizona senator added: “It’s ridiculous. … If he wanted to make a good argument for him not to be impeached, he literally just doubled down and asked for an impeachment.”

World.title: AI stocks bounce back after $2.5 trillion wipeout, but questions remain
World.content:
An AI-driven stock sell-off that wiped roughly $2.5 trillion in market value off Wall Street eased on Friday, but only after hitting Asian and European markets hard.

US tech stocks staged a modest rebound, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 rising 1.1 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively. The Dow, meanwhile, fell roughly 0.5 percent. Markets often bounce back slightly after a sell-off as some investors step in to buy stocks at discounted prices.

Despite bouncing back on Friday, the S&P 500 still finished the week down roughly 2.7 percent, its worst week since April 2025, when President Donald Trump’s unveiling of tariffs rocked global markets.

Some of Thursday’s hardest-hit US stocks — namely, those tied to the AI trade — rebounded, with Nvidia rising 2.8 percent and SpaceX gaining 8.6 percent. Both companies’ share prices had plunged by roughly 9 percent on Thursday, with Nvidia suffering its worst day since January 2025.

Still, signs of recovery on Wall Street came after bruising Friday trading sessions in Asia and Europe. South Korea’s Kospi index and Japan’s Nikkei 225 index both closed down 6 percent Friday, while Taiwan’s benchmark Taiex index ended 4.5 percent lower.

The moves reflected a retreat among investors from some of this year’s hottest trades. Asian tech companies, which play an integral role in the global electronics supply chain, have been buoyed by insatiable demand for components such as semiconductor chips needed to build massive AI data centers.

European indexes, which aren’t tilted as heavily toward technology stocks, also retreated modestly. The region’s benchmark Stoxx 600 index fell 1 percent, while France’s CAC 40 and Germany’s DAX dropped 0.8 percent and 1.9 percent, respectively.

Stock in ASML, the Dutch maker of chip equipment and Europe’s largest company connected to the AI industry, tumbled 6.6 percent on Thursday, though had trimmed some of those losses by Friday afternoon and was up 2.7 percent.

This week’s big swings in AI stocks underscore growing uncertainty among investors over what the results of the U.S. midterm elections means for the AI trade. Many are concerned that Democrats’ sweeping victories could stymie an AI investment boom that has powered both the economy and markets this year. A Columbia Business School study estimates that AI-related infrastructure investment was driving nearly all observed US GDP growth by the end of last year.

However, backlash against the environmental and community impact of new data centers turned AI spending into a key issue in the US midterm elections. Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, and flipped several other contested state seats.

That sweeping victory has spurred concerns that Democratic representatives could now block or slow spending on new AI infrastructure. Those anxieties kicked off in full force Thursday, when the Nasdaq slumped 5.5 percent, its worst day since April 2025, when Trump announced sweeping tariffs on virtually all of America’s major trade partners.

Asia’s wild tech ride

The recent volatility builds on a year of sharp swings for Asian markets, particularly the Kospi, as investors have grappled with the sustainability of the AI boom, as well as the ultimate profitability of such steep investments.

Jung In Yun, founder and CEO of Fibonacci Asset Management Global, said Friday’s sell-off was likely triggered by investors reassessing expectations around AI investment and policy.

However, he believes demand for computing power will continue to grow, along with the need for memory chips like the ones made by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the two largest publicly traded companies in South Korea.

“South Korea’s tech-heavy market is particularly exposed to shifts in sentiment, so we may see more swings before confidence settles,” he said.

Government officials in both South Korea and Japan acknowledged the recent volatility in their respective stock markets on Friday.

“I am aware share prices, particularly those of AI and chip sectors, are falling sharply,” said Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, adding that the government was closely watching market developments. “We will focus on steps to create a strong economy.”

South Korea’s finance and economy minister Lee Hyoung-il also held a meeting Friday regarding the impact of the US midterm elections on the nation’s economy.

According to the ministry, leaders assessed that an impact on the global markets “cannot be ruled out” and that they would proactively devise measures to prevent overreactions in the Korean stock market.

Following US signals

Tech stocks around the world have been sensitive to sudden shifts in sentiment this year, as retail and institutional investors have both responded to new data or developments in AI.

“If we just focus on AI-related stocks in the market, then I would argue there has been too much of a hype earlier this year,” said Theodore Shou, partner at asset management firm Yiyi Capital in Hong Kong. “I think the market is just moderating itself.”

As excitement around AI has grown, Shou said that Asian tech stocks have become more closely correlated with their US counterparts than ever before.

However, Shou said that some market participants may be banking that a Democrat-led Congress could slow the pace of interest rate hikes, lowering the cost of borrowing, which could help boost both tech and non-tech equities.

As traders await the winners of the US midterm elections to take office early next year, analysts said global markets will likely remain sensitive to changes in tech and monetary policy.

“The thing that markets really don’t like is the uncertainty. And what they’re really saying is, we’re not sure what’s going to happen in January,” said Andrew Sullivan, who writes about Asian equities in his newsletter Asian Market Sense. “So, let’s just take a step back. Let’s put some money into cash that we can then use once the dust has settled, so to speak.”

World.title: Photos: Ahmed Helmy meets his wax double at Madame Tussauds in Dubai
World.content:
Egyptian actor Ahmed Helmy celebrated the unveiling of his own wax figure at Madame Tussauds in Dubai, becoming the first Arab actor to be featured among the museum’s collection of stars.

He was joined at the celebration by his wife, Mona Zaki.

The museum houses between 60 and 70 highly detailed wax figures of international personalities from the worlds of entertainment, sports, politics, and fashion.

It marks the first expansion of the renowned museum into the Middle East since its opening in October 2021.

Helmy returns to cinema

Helmy will mark his return to the big screen after a four-year hiatus with the film “Hadouta,” (Story) set to be released in Egyptian cinemas on November 11.

Written by Ahmed Abdel-Rahman and directed by Mazen Ashraf, the film co-stars Amina Khalil, Maged al-Masry, Rahma Ahmed, Sherine, and Mohamed Abdel-Azim alongside Ahmed Helmy.

The plot of “Hadouta” revolves around a 40-year-old criminal who cannot recall where he has hidden a witness he kidnapped.

He turns to a hypnotherapist to recover the lost information. However to regain his memory, he must confront old enemies, past events – and most importantly face himself.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egyptian, Iranian FMs discuss regional developments, ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty held a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to discuss the latest regional developments and ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Nader Zaki said the two ministers exchanged views on recent regional developments and voiced concern over the prospect of renewed military confrontations and their potential repercussions for regional and international security and stability.

Abdelatty underscored the importance of prioritizing diplomatic solutions and demonstrating the necessary openness to advance a political settlement of the crisis.

He stressed the need for all parties to show flexibility and reach compromises that serve their respective interests, thereby preventing the region from descending into a new wave of escalation that could have serious political, economic, and humanitarian repercussions for the region and the world at large.

World.title: FM heads to Libya
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptians Abroad Badr Abdelatty departed for Libya on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

The foreign minister is scheduled to hold a series of meetings with senior Libyan officials.

As part of the visit, Abdelatty will participate in the proceedings of the 22nd Ordinary Session of the Executive Council of the Community of Sahel-Saharan States (CEN-SAD), hosted by Tripoli, to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation among member states and advance efforts to activate the organization’s mechanisms.

World.title: Qatar issues statement following reports of failed negotiations between the US and Iran
World.content:
A statement by the International Media Office of Qatar said that Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim al-Thani confirmed that the US and Iran are continuing efforts to reach an agreement.

“Reports circulating online claiming that His Excellency the Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs stated that the United States and Iran had failed to reach an agreement are false and misleading,” the statement said.

The statement added that “His Excellency’s remarks have been deliberately distorted by those who benefit from continued war and instability in our region. Many of these claims are being spread by fake accounts trying to undermine diplomatic efforts and push for further escalation. This is deeply irresponsible.”

Bloomberg previously reported, citing the Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, that the US and Iran had failed to reach a “comprehensive agreement,” according to the Hebrew-language newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth.

An official from the US Central Command (CENTCOM) told Al Jazeera that the command would issue an announcement regarding Iran at 8:30 am Saturday (Washington time), though he declined to disclose the nature of the announcement.

Meanwhile, the Iranian news agency Tasnim reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, located in the Arabian Gulf; no official information has yet been released regarding the extent of any potential damage.

World.title: Liberia’s Billion-Dollar Bet: Boakai Sends Record US$1.54 Billion Budget to Lawmakers as Questions Linger Over Revenue Windfall
World.content:
Liberia’s proposed 2027 budget is the biggest in the country’s history, promising higher pay for teachers and police, more money for hospitals and a plan to repay nearly US$60 million owed to the state pension fund. But it rests on a revenue milestone that was lifted in part by a one-off mining payment, and the government has yet to explain how it will keep the money coming.

By Rodney D. Sieh

MONROVIA, Liberia – Liberia’s government on Friday asked lawmakers to approve a US$1.538 billion spending plan for 2027, the largest in the West African nation’s history, betting that a recent surge in tax collections can pay for higher wages, new hospital equipment and a long-delayed fix for public-sector pensions.



Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan delivered the draft budget and President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s budget message to House Speaker Richard Nagbe Koon on November 6. The plan is about 18 percent larger than the current year’s revised US$1.302 billion budget.

Boakai titled his message “A Growing Budget for Bigger Impact,” tying the plan to the ARREST Agenda, his government’s development blueprint. He told lawmakers the budget was bigger not only in size but in its potential to change lives, and urged them to pass it quickly.

The pitch leans heavily on one number. In September, Liberia’s domestic revenue crossed US$1 billion for the first time in its 179-year history. How durable that figure is – and how much of it reaches ordinary Liberians – is likely to dominate the debate in the Capitol over the coming weeks.

The billion-dollar question

On September 16, the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) reported that collections for the year had reached just over US$1.005 billion. That is roughly 63 percent more than the government collected in 2023, the year before Boakai took office, when revenue stood at about US$612 million.

Boakai’s budget message presents the milestone as proof that the state can now finance its own development. Economists and opposition lawmakers are likely to ask how much of it will repeat.

A large share came from a single source. The 2026 budget counted a US$200 million signature bonus from steelmaker ArcelorMittal, part of a renegotiated iron ore deal. The company was the country’s biggest taxpayer this year, accounting for about US$270 million of collections. LRA Commissioner General James Dorbor Jallah has argued that Liberia would have neared the billion-dollar mark even without the bonus.

The underlying trend is more modest. Stripping out one-off payments, the LRA’s monthly collections ran at around US$88 million between January and July – a pace that would yield roughly US$1.06 billion over a full year. The 2027 budget asks for close to US$1.54 billion.

The Finance Ministry’s summary of the budget does not say how much of the 2027 total will come from domestic taxes, how much from donors, and how much from borrowing. Nor does it name new tax measures. Ngafuan disclosed in August that ministries and agencies had initially requested about US$1.92 billion for 2027, showing the pressure on the budget even before lawmakers add their own priorities.

The government is targeting US$1.3 billion in domestic revenue by December; the LRA’s own forecast is higher, at US$1.42 billion. Whether the 2027 plan is built on the target, the forecast or the underlying monthly pace is the first question lawmakers are likely to put to the finance minister.

At the clinic, the classroom and the payslip

For most Liberians, the budget will be judged less by its total than by whether hospitals have medicine, teachers are paid and pensions are honoured.

Health. Spending rises 22 percent, from US$110.9 million to US$135.8 million. The money is meant to staff and equip the New Redemption Hospital in Monrovia, buy dialysis machines and other equipment for the John F. Kennedy Medical Center (US$5.3 million), keep medicines flowing to rural clinics through a community pharmacy programme (US$1 million) and launch a national hepatitis B response (US$800,000). Even so, health takes under 9 percent of the budget, well short of the 15 percent African governments pledged in the 2001 Abuja Declaration.

Education. The sector gets US$163.5 million, up 13.9 percent from US$143.6 million. The headline item is US$7 million to continue renovating the University of Liberia. Public schools in Monrovia, where students have protested over conditions this year, get US$1.5 million for repairs.

The change teachers are most likely to feel is a new pay floor across government schools: US$650 a month for those with a master’s degree, US$400 with a bachelor’s, US$240 with an associate degree or B-Certificate, and US$200 with a C-Certificate.

Wages. The government says more than 17,000 people will benefit from pay changes – nearly 13,000 existing workers getting raises and about 4,350 new hires, including volunteers. They include 1,934 police officers, 616 staff of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency who will get a 15 percent raise, and 358 health workers. From January, no government director will earn less than US$500 a month.

Pensions. In one of the budget’s most significant admissions, Boakai confirmed the government owes nearly US$60 million to the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation (NASSCORP) in employer contributions it never paid. From 2027, the government says it will pay its full 6 percent share on time and clear the arrears in instalments – a promise retiring civil servants will watch closely.

Youth and women. The budget sets aside US$2 million for commercial motorcyclists, including roadside rest stops, and funds 1,400 new recruits for the army and police. It provides US$3 million for the national football team, the Lone Star, plus US$650,000 for former players. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection gets a 77 percent increase, while US$2.5 million is earmarked for small businesses, mostly run by women, and US$3 million for school feeding.

What lawmakers will want to know

The ministry’s summary leaves several gaps that the Legislature’s budget committee is likely to probe in hearings.

It does not give a dollar figure for the 77 percent rise at the gender ministry, or say how much of the total goes to salaries rather than roads, clinics and schools. It does not say over how many years the NASSCORP debt will be repaid. And it is silent on agriculture – the “A” in the ARREST Agenda – a sector that has received less than 1 percent of recent budgets despite employing a large share of Liberians.

The priorities themselves invite scrutiny. The football team’s US$3 million allocation is three times what the government plans to spend keeping essential medicines in rural clinics.

Liberia’s fiscal year now runs from January to December, so lawmakers have less than two months to pass the plan. Boakai has asked them to act quickly. The size of the budget, and the questions over how it will be paid for, suggest the debate will not be brief.

World.title: Liberia Pays £5.95 Million to IMO, Remains Top Financial Contributor to Global Maritime Body
World.content:
Annual contribution accounts for approximately 15 percent of IMO’s operating budget as Liberia reaffirms commitment to safe, secure and sustainable international shipping.

LONDON, United Kingdom — Liberia has paid £5,946,633 (approximately £5.95 million) in annual assessed contributions to the International Maritime Organization (IMO), reinforcing its position as the organization’s largest financial contributor and one of the leading voices in global maritime governance.

Liberia’s Maritime Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer, Cllr. Neto Zarzar Lighe Sr., presented a symbolic cheque for the amount to IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez during a ceremony in London on November 6, 2026.



Commissioner Lighe said the timely payment underscores Liberia’s commitment to the IMO, its institutional programs and the continued development of international shipping.

As the world’s largest ship registry, Liberia contributes approximately 15 percent of the IMO’s annual operational budget through its assessed financial contributions.

Speaking during the presentation, Lighe emphasized that Liberia considers its financial obligations to the organization a serious national responsibility, particularly given its influence in the international maritime industry.

“Liberia takes its obligations to the IMO as a serious national obligation. As a global maritime leader and Category-A member of the IMO Council, we remain firmly committed to fulfilling our responsibilities promptly and supporting the Organization’s vital mission of advancing safe, secure, efficient, and environmentally sustainable international shipping,” he said.

Receiving the symbolic cheque, Secretary-General Dominguez expressed appreciation to the Liberian Government for meeting its financial obligations on time and maintaining its longstanding commitment to the organization.

Dominguez also recognized that Liberia’s contribution to the IMO extends beyond financial support, highlighting the country’s active participation in the organization’s technical working groups, committees and Council deliberations.

He described Liberia’s representation as effective, efficient and highly engaged, noting its important role in advancing the IMO’s mandate and strengthening international maritime cooperation.

Liberia has consistently maintained an influential presence within the IMO, reflecting the country’s strategic importance to international shipping through its extensive ship registry.

Commissioner Lighe was accompanied at the presentation ceremony by Liberia’s Permanent Representative to the IMO, Ambassador Robert Wilmot Kpadeh; Alternate Permanent Representative, Dr. Harry Conway; and other officials of the Liberia Permanent Mission to the IMO.

The latest payment further reinforces Liberia’s standing as a responsible flag State, a dependable international maritime partner and a major contributor to global maritime governance.
