World.title: Merz’s conservatives poised to nominate Germany’s first woman president
World.content:
President of the Bavarian parliament Ilse Aigner arrives at the Christian Social Union party congress in Munich, on Oct. 23, 2026. | Alexandra Beier/AFP via Getty Images

BERLIN — Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner is set to become Germany’s next president, making her the country’s first woman to hold the office, according to two senior conservatives with knowledge of the matter.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservative bloc and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) will nominate Aigner to succeed outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the officials told BILD, which, like POLITICO, is part of the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network. Both officials were granted anonymity to discuss internal party matters freely. Aigner’s nomination will officially be announced Monday, according to the officials.

Aigner, who previously served as agriculture minister under former German Chancellor Angela Merkel from 2008 to 2013, is currently president of the Bavarian State Parliament. She is also a member of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

World.title: Trump’s ‘big, beautiful’ European security plan isn’t convincing Europe
World.content:
The latest U.S. proposal underscores growing anxiety around Trump’s fresh rapprochement with Russia as he ramps up pressure on Ukraine and his administration attempts to revive long-stalled talks to end Moscow’s full-scale war against Kyiv.

POLITICO spoke to 12 NATO diplomats, EU envoys and European government officials, all of whom were granted anonymity to speak freely on the sensitive issue. NATO allies were not briefed about the American plans in advance, according to three alliance diplomats, and many remain skeptical of the idea.

U.S. President Donald Trump late Thursday talked of a “big, beautiful agreement,” after meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev, adding: “It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe.”

“Our objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment,” Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner added soon after.

Kushner said the arrangement would have five goals: “Permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.”

“It is a bit obscure what Kushner meant,” said one NATO diplomat. “The general sentiment in Europe is that any discussion with Russia on the future architecture at the moment will just be used by Moscow to legitimize their arguments ... it will not fly with the European allies.”

World.title: Wave of bomb threats target Irish media outlets and more European flights
World.content:
“We have expected a rise in hybrid threats to Ireland because of our hosting of the EU presidency, and the EPC meeting will be by far the biggest set-piece event of that presidency, so one must presume it’s no coincidence that we’re experiencing this spike in hybrid activity now,” the Irish official said.

The Irish government said the threats against media outlets were probably part of a European-wide pattern of threats that have targeted dozens of airlines this week, including Irish carriers Ryanair and Aer Lingus. Hackers also targeted supermarket refrigeration systems in at least seven European countries.

“It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralized or coordinated effort,” the Irish government said in a statement. “However, these threats come on the heels of the ongoing disruption to aviation around Europe caused by similar threats, and it seems likely that this is a coordinated campaign of disruption.”

Bomb threats also targeted at least 18 European flights Friday, after at least 22 the day before, raising concerns that the hoaxes may be part of a coordinated campaign to disrupt air traffic.

Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares told Spanish public broadcaster TVE on Friday that the bomb threats affecting flights could be “an attempt at hybrid aggression and war in some psychological way.” He added that “it cannot be a coincidence that so many identical events occur with the same modus operandi throughout Europe.”

Luis Gallego, CEO of airline group IAG, said: “It is clear that what they [the perpetrators] are looking for is to create chaos and disruption in the different airports.”

World.title: EU capitals urge Brussels to ‘swiftly’ sign electricity deal with UK
World.content:
A group of countries are now urging the European Commission to wrap up discussions by the end of 2027, according to an EU diplomat granted anonymity to discuss internal discussions.

Proponents say the plan would unlock new renewable energy investment in the North Sea and could cut electricity prices.

But the EU says the U.K. would have to make a contribution to EU cohesion funds as the price of participating in the market — a politically difficult ask for London.

Clean energy hub

The leaders, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten, write that the agreement is “necessary to unlock the full potential of the North Sea” and to “transform it into the largest clean energy hub in the world.”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa give a press conference at the end of a European Union summit at the EU headquarters in Brussels on October 16, 2026. | Nicolas Tucat/AFP via Getty Images

“An agreement will thus enhance Europe’s energy security and contribute to a competitive economy that centres on access to clean and affordable energy,” the letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa states.

“These benefits underline the importance of swiftly concluding the ongoing negotiations. We call on you and the UK to agree during the Summit on a path towards the conclusion of these negotiations.”

World.title: Spain and the Netherlands battle over ECB presidency
World.content:
Exiting European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde gives a press conference in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, on Oct. 29, 2026. | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via Getty Images

Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot are in the hunt for the top job after Christine Lagarde’s exit.

BRUSSELS — The Netherlands and Spain on Friday submitted candidates to succeed Christine Lagarde, who steps down as president of the European Central Bank on Feb. 7.

Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former governor of Spain's central bank, and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot, a former president of the Dutch central bank, were the only candidates to emerge after the 5 p.m. deadline, as expected.

Their candidacies are part of a larger game of musical chairs that includes France and Germany, as Europe’s four economic powerhouses negotiate how to secure their seats on the ECB’s executive board.

World.title: ‘I don’t know if it reassured or worried them’: European envoys quiz Le Pen over lunch
World.content:
The group of ambassadors from the eight countries that share a border with metropolitan France — Germany, Spain, Belgium, Italy, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Monaco and Andorra — already met with conservative presidential candidate Bruno Retailleau in September. They are planning to host meetings with the other presidential hopefuls, including far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, at their respective embassies in the coming months.

“I don’t know if it reassured or worried them,” said an adviser to Marine Le Pen who accompanied her to the lunch. “What is sure is that they can now report back to their capitals what the National Rally wants to do,” the adviser added.

Le Pen was mainly questioned about her plans to downsize the EU and on bilateral issues, as well as U.S. President Donald Trump after his seismic defeat in the midterm elections.

While in the past, the National Rally has been supportive of Trump, the party has progressively distanced itself from the U.S. president. The National Rally’s Jordan Bardella on Wednesday said his party was not affected by the result and suggested that Trump’s popularity was undermined by the war in the Middle East and its economic consequences.



Le Pen has also been campaigning for a harsher approach on migration, which would involve stricter checks at the borders, potentially impacting countries whose envoys she met on Wednesday. All of them, apart from Andorra and Monaco, are part of the Schengen free-movement area.

“There is a general interest on what would her stance be on the key issues of mutual interest and cooperation on which we are working with France,” said one diplomat from a participating country.

“It was a very frank exchange. She told them what she says everywhere and she was able to elaborate on a number of topics a little more at length than she would do on TV,” the same adviser said, adding that Le Pen regularly meets ambassadors.

World.title: Election favorite says Spain should quit as World Cup co-host if Morocco stages the final
World.content:
Feijóo noted that the 2030 World Cup was originally a Spanish-Portuguese bid, until Morocco was invited at a later stage. Despite that chronology, Moroccan officials have been pushing vigorously to stage the final, which is the world’s most prestigious sports event.

Rafael Louzán, Spain’s football chief, told POLITICO in June that he was confident either Madrid or Barcelona would host the final, despite Morocco pouring vast amounts of cash into football infrastructure.

Tensions have flared between the two countries in recent months. Spanish political parties this summer accused Morocco of stoking a migrant crisis in Spain’s North African territory of Ceuta, after 80,000 people surged into the city in late July.

A Sigma Dos poll for El Mundo following the Ceuta crisis found that 84.4% of Spaniards opposed Spain continuing to co-host the World Cup with Morocco.

Leftist party Sumar, the Socialists’ junior coalition partner, said this summer that the World Cup “cannot be shared with a country that uses desperate people for its own geostrategic interests.”

The left-wing party tabled a resolution in parliament that far-right Vox backed in an unusual convergence. The text never made it to a vote because parliament was dissolved ahead of the snap election.

World.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square
World.content:
A gunman who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the shooter was fascinated with "radical" and "far right' ideologies.

At least six people were killed and sixteen injured in a shooting near the main market square in the southern Polish city of Krakow on Saturday.

The perpetrator, a 25-year-old Polish man who acted alone, was wounded during an exchange of fire with police, authorities said.

"Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told reporters in Krakow.

"That's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow," he added.

Deadly shooting in popular Krakow tourist spot To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Shooter aimed at random people, police say

According to Krakow police, the gunman aimed at random people as he drove by the city's main square, which is a popular tourist attraction.

"At around 3 pm (1400 GMT), a man who had driven into the market square in a car began shooting at random people from inside the vehicle," police said on X, adding officers were among the wounded.

"The perpetrator was shot by police ‌officers and is currently being ‌transported ​to a hospital," police said.

Later Saturday evening, Polish police chief Marek Boron said a British citizen was among those killed.

"There are six fatalities: four women and two men; three Polish women, one British national, and two people who have not yet been identified," Boron told reporters.

Authorities later clarified that the man drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each with an automatic weapon.

Police secure an area near the city's main market square Image: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

Bodies found in shooter's house

On Saturday night, Tusk said that the bodies of two women and a man were found in the shooters home by police.

There was "much to suggest that they are members of the (suspect's) immediate family."

The residence is located Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.

"We have the next acts of this tragedy," Tusk told reporters.

Shooter fascinated by 'far-right' views

According to Katarzyna Cislo, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, the shooter wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a long gun in the attack.

Numerous other weapons and ammunition were found in the gunman's car.

Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said that the shooter was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held "very radical views."

Kierwinski also told reporters that five of the sixteen people injured in the shooting were non-Polish nationals.

Police personnel at the site of shooting Image: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

Poland to observe 2 days of mourning

Prime Minister Tusk posted to X that police were investigating the attack and called it a "tragic" incident.

Tusk later said Poland would observe two days of mourning for the victims of the shooting.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki wrote on X that his thoughts were with the victims and wounded, as well as their families.

'Poland does not stand alone,' European politicians show support

The European Union's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland, adding that "Poland does not stand alone."

"I am deeply saddened by the events in Krakow. My thoughts are with the victims and their families," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote on X, adding that "Germany stands alongside Poland as a friend and partner during these difficult times."

Krakow is located about 250 kilometers (155 miles) from Warsaw, the capital of Poland.

With a population of over 800,000, Krakow is Poland's second-largest city, as well as a popular tourist destination.

World.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
World.content:
Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

1976: A hitherto unknown disease breaks out near the Ebola river in the country then known as Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This was the first scientifically documented Ebola epidemic.

Now, 50 years on, the DRC once again finds itself at the center of a major Ebola outbreak. This time the pathogen is the less common Bundibugyo type of the genus Orthoebolavirus. The virus was identified in 2007 during an outbreak in Bundibugyo, Uganda. Another outbreak occurred in the DRC in 2012.

Bundibugyo: Preparations could have been made

How can a virus that has been known for decades continue to infect thousands of people, yet there is still no licensed vaccine or official treatment?

Torsten Feldt, a doctor of tropical medicine at Düsseldorf's University Hospital, sees this as a missed opportunity. "We had come across the Bundibugyo virus in two previous outbreaks: 2007 in Uganda and 2012 in DR Congo. So we had enough time to develop vaccines and therapeutic options. But we didn't make use of this opportunity, meaning crucial time was lost during the current outbreak."

Leonie Mayer from the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) and the Institute for Infection Research and Vaccine Development at the University Medical Center in Hamburg-Eppendorf agrees. "They could of course have developed a vaccine and run pre-clinical trials before," Mayer told DW. She stressed, however, that their effectiveness can only be assessed and confirmed during an actual outbreak.

Mayer is the lead author of a recently published study that examined whether Ervebo, an Ebola vaccine that has already been licensed, can be used against other types of Ebola as well.

Congo's Ebola crisis: Fear, mistrust and a growing outbreak To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why Ebola is a good candidate for vaccine development

From an immunological point of view, and compared to — for example — influenza or HIV, Ebola is a very worthwhile candidate for a vaccine. Influenza viruses are constantly mutating, and the human immunodeficiency virus is particularly good at evading our immune defenses. Ebola is far more predictable.

"I think — and perhaps it's kind of a blessing in disguise — that it will be relatively straightforward to develop a vaccine against Bundibugyo," says Mayer.

Herein lies the paradox. From a scientific point of view, Ebola is a good vaccine candidate, yet there is still no licensed form of prevention against the Bundibugyo variant that is currently circulating.

Mayer explains that vaccines cannot be developed as a precautionary measure against every potential pathogen. Lack of funding or the prioritization of other pathogens often have a role to play. Many researchers had assumed that a fresh outbreak of the Sudan Ebola virus was more likely, and vaccine development for this strain is more advanced.

Different types of Ebola

Another part of the problem is that Ebola is not one single virus. The known, highly dangerous orthoebolaviruses include Ebola virus (EBOV), previously called the Zaire Ebola virus (ZEBOV), the Sudan virus (SUDV), and the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). The existing vaccine, Ervebo, was developed and licensed for use against the Zaire variant. But there is still no approved protection against the others.

This is why the existing Ebola vaccine has been of only limited use to people in the areas of the current outbreak.

Another factor may also be relevant: The Bundibugyo virus appears to be less aggressive than the Zaire variant. At first, that sounds like good news, but it may make it harder to contain, as people remain mobile for longer after being infected, and can pass on the virus without realizing.

Ervebo vaccine: Immune response to Bundibugyo

In the recently published study, Mayer's research team from the DZIF investigated whether the already licensed Ebola vaccine could trigger an immune response not only against EBOV, but against other types of Ebola as well. They found cross-reactive T-cell responses against Bundibugyo, and also, to a lesser extent, against the Sudan virus.

For Mayer, this is already an important finding: "We now know that the immune cells can most likely also recognize the Bundibugyo virus." But she also observes: "Our data does not enable us to answer the question of whether this immune response actually provides protection, or if it results in a milder progression of the disease." This is currently an important gap in our knowledge.

Why the existing vaccine cannot currently be deployed

If there's a vaccine that has already been licensed, and indications that it could protect people, why isn't it simply being deployed?

Mayer explains the dilemma. For one thing, she says, it's not ethical to deploy a vaccine if you're not sure whether or how well it works. Also, if it were used on a large scale, it would no longer be possible to establish whether it actually works: A reduction in cases could also be a result of other measures, or the epidemic might already have passed its peak.

Jürgen May, a specialist in tropical diseases at the Bernhard Nocht Institute, also warns against mass vaccination: "Mass vaccination without proof of efficacy could create a false sense of security, forfeit trust, and, if it does not provide sufficient protection, make study impossible."

It's very important for there to be acceptance on the ground. "If we inoculate people with a vaccine on a large scale, and afterwards it turns out that it was nothing like as effective as we expected, it's very difficult to communicate that to people on the ground," Mayer says. In a worst-case scenario, people could subsequently refuse inoculation with more effective vaccines.

Why Ebola is still so difficult to contain

But the current outbreak also shows that medical innovation alone is not enough. Conflicts, difficult transport routes, attacks on healthcare facilities, and gaps in contact tracing all make it harder to contain.

The DRC has had more than 10,000 cases of Bundibugyo since May. Recently, it has also been reported in Kenya and Nigeria Image: Andrew Kasuku/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

Torsten Feldt says identifying Bundibugyo is no longer a problem in itself. What is often limiting is the practical availability of diagnostic tools. "In remote or conflict-affected regions, samples often have to be transported over long distances," he explains.

Here we see another Ebola paradox. The world is getting ever better at diagnosing infections, but it still struggles to contain outbreaks fast enough. The authors of an article in the current issue of Nature come to the same conclusion: The problem is often not identifying cases, but the speed with which people react. Finding Ebola is often easier now than stopping Ebola, they write.

From a Bundibugyo vaccine to a pan-Ebola one?

Many researchers believe the current crisis could potentially also provide a great opportunity. The so-called Tumaini study, which is testing different vaccine candidates, has now been launched in the DRC.

These include Ervebo, developed by Oxford University, and a Moderna mRNA vaccine. The study aims to provide the first reliable data about their efficacy against the Bundibugyo virus.

Whether these vaccines could still help control the current outbreak is uncertain. There is hope, but experts estimate that, realistically, it will be several months before any such vaccine is available for widespread use; perhaps not until mid-2027.

"Ideally, we will develop cross-reactive pan-Ebola vaccines," Christof Geldmacher, a co-author of the DZIF study, says of their long-term plans. This is also something that is being worked on. For now, though, the focus is on developing an effective vaccine against the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Israeli president picks Gadi Eisenkot to form government
World.content:
President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government, with tricky coalition talks expected.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen Gadi Eisenkot to have the first opportunity to form a new Israeli government, according to a statement released by his office on Saturday evening.

The statement said Eisenkot was informed of Herzog's "intention to task him with forming a government" and would be invited to the president's residence, where a formal ceremony will take place on Sunday.

The decision comes after a neck-and-neck race with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel's October election.

Eisenkot's wide-ranging group, fashioned in opposition to Netanyahu, won 48 of the Israeli parliament's 120 seats in October's elections. Netanyahu's camp secured 53, leaving neither with the required majority of 61 seats.

Former Israeli military chief Eisenkot is the leader of the centrist Yashar party and heads an anti-Netanyahu alliance.

While Netanyahu ruled out working with Arab parties to gain a majority, both Arab majority lists had announced during the week that they would recommend Eisenkot to be next prime minister.

Can Netanyahu survive his last big fight? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What happens next?

The move is the first step toward what will almost certainly be complicated coalition talks.

Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a government, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving premier, whose religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in the election, despite emerging as the largest bloc.

Although Eisenkot was runner up, he managed to secure endorsements from leaders of Arab parties, who are opposed to Netanyahu.

Eisenkot faces a tricky path to forming a government, involving difficult constellations of Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties. He will have 28 days to round up the 61 votes needed to form a government.

Herzog can provide a 14-day extension if Eisenkot comes up short before the mandate must be offered to someone else.

If no candidate succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections.

World.title: Trump offers White House press secretary role to Dana White
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship.

US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that he has asked Dana White, the CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), to serve as White House press secretary.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote on his Truth Social account.

"Dana, please take the job!" Trump said, calling on the longtime fight promoter to bring "assistants" with him "even though some are not from our country."

Dana White has been president of the UFC since 2001 and its CEO since 2023.

The White House does not have a press secretary as yet.

Katie Zacharia left the high-profile job on October 16 after a shaky debut press briefing. She was out as press secretary in less than a week after her appointment to the job.

This is a breaking news story. Please check back for updates.

World.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
World.content:
Although fewer protesters turned out in comparison with previous weeks, several cities saw clashes between police and demonstrators.

Fewer protesters than expected turned out for the fourth weekend of mass demonstrations in France, although clashes with police were reported in several cities, the Interior Ministry said on Saturday.

Authorities had expected up to 170,000 people to protest nationwide, including 60,000 in Paris.

The ministry reported a slightly lower nationwide total of 146,000 people, out of which some 46,000 took to the streets of the French capital, where the afternoon was reported to have remained mostly calm, with some isolated incidents reported in the evening involving the deployment of tear gas.

Protest organizers gave a higher nationwide count of over 250,000 protesters, which is nevertheless fewer than the 320,000 to 500,000 that were reported to have turned out last Saturday.

Clashes between police and protesters were reported in Toulouse, Marseille, Lyon and Bordeaux.

The Interior Ministry reported some 350 arrests nationwide by the evening in connection with the protests.

Trash cans were set on fire in Marseille Image: Justine Meddah/AFP

Fourth week of protests in France

Students and labor unions had called an authorized central Paris march "against the high cost of living and in support of young people."

A protest march began at Place de la Republique Satursday Image: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

In Paris, an authorized march proceeded peacefully from Republique to Nation, but tensions erupted after police said some 200 "violent individuals" attacked law enforcement after a man was arrested for setting fire to a trash can, according to Paris' police headquarters.

Depsite several incidents, French authorities said the protests in Paris were mostly calm Image: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

Separately, the country's so-called "Yellow Vest" movement — which gained notoriety eight years ago by violently protesting a proposed fuel tax hike rejected invitations to join the student rally.

Instead, the "Gilets Jaunes" held a banned event at Paris' Place de la Concorde, close to parliament and the presidential Elysee Palace. Two of its leading figures, Benjamin Ball and Solene Azelma Sigaux, were arrested and taken into custody.

Ahead of Saturday's protests, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 police and security forces would be deployed across the country over the weekend, adding that authorities will "be ready" for "rioters and looters."

France protests turn violent nationwide To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Can France afford to raise wages, invest in schools?

The large police presence comes on the heels of weeks of mass demonstrations that have at times grown extremely violent, most notably on October 17, when France's worst rioting in years resulted in more than a billion euros in damage to private and public property.

On Thursday, police made over 600 arrests during a nationwide strike that included blockades and other protest action.

Authorities say that, for the most part, protests have remained peaceful.

But there have continued to be numerous incidents of violent clashes with police, as outgoing President Emmanuel Macron and his government struggle to address public discontent over the rising cost of living.

Although Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is scheduled to meet with trade and employee unions on Monday, organizers say the only thing that will quell anger will be for the government to bow to their demands.

"The only thing that will bring the protests to an end is a response to the demands that have been put forward for several weeks by workers, civil servants, young people and pensioners," according to an inter-union coalition statement published on Friday.

This latest round of protests began with students calling for improvements to the national education system and unions joining in to call for wage hikes and tax reforms.

Macron's government has said it intends to raise the minimum wage as well as increase funding for schools and teaching staff. But it finds itself in a tight fiscal spot as debt — currently 119% of GDP — continues to run out of control in the EU's second-largest economy.

World.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
World.content:
While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

In early October, Artur Danielyan, leader of Armenia's opposition party Adekvad, was arrested following a Facebook post criticizing Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan.

The incident is part of a growing trend: Over the past two years, Armenian authorities have brought charges against multiple opposition figures, largely based on their social media activity.

Civil society representatives warn that such selective justice signals a worrying turn toward democratic backsliding.

The arrest of Artur Danielyan

The grounds for Danielyan's detention were Facebook posts in which he criticized both Pashinyan and the country's security services.

One point of contention was Pashinyan's stance on a possible prisoner exchange involving an Azerbaijani soldier accused of breaking into the home of a 39-year-old woman in the Armenian village of Shaki and injuring her and her children.

In an interview with Armenian news outlet Infocom, Pashinyan ruled out swapping the soldier imprisoned in Armenia for detained Armenians in Azerbaijan. Danielyan responded with a scathing attack, calling the prime minister a "scumbag" and accusing him of being unwilling to bring his fellow citizens home.

Armenia and Azerbaijan were in conflict for three decades over Nagorno-Karabakh, a breakaway Azerbaijani region populated by Armenians that declared independence in the 1990s. After Azerbaijan's military offensive in 2023, Baku regained control over the territory, forcing over 100,000 Armenians to flee. Currently, 19 Armenian individuals are being detained in Baku, including former high-ranking officials from Nagorno-Karabakh's de facto administration.

Artur Danielyan, leader of the far-right "Adekvat" party, is a controversial figure in Armenia Image: Alexander Ryumin/TASS/dpa/picture alliance

Growing trend of selective prosecutions?

Over a dozen Armenian civil society organizations have condemned the prosecution of the Adekvad party leader, calling it "patently illegal, disproportionate, and politically motivated."

"It is punitive in nature and sends a direct signal to the broader public aimed at silencing dissent, critical views, and undesirable speech", said the joint statement.

Several other criminal proceedings have been launched against activists who criticized the ruling establishment or Pashinyan.

Another prominent case emerged ahead of the parliamentary elections in June. Artur Osipyan, a displaced activist from Nagorno-Karabakh, was arrested after a verbal clash with Pashinyan over his Nagorno-Karabakh policy.

Following the incident, Armenian prosecutors indicted Osipyan for disrupting public order and obstructing the ruling party's campaign. He was also charged with inciting violence against Pashinyan in a social media post from March.

Is freedom of expression in danger in Armenia?

On April 15, 2020, Article 226.2 was added to the Criminal Code of Armenia, penalizing public calls to violence, as well as the public justification or promotion of violence.

After strong outrage by civil society, these offences were subsequently decriminalized. According to a 2025 report by Freedom House, "nearly 95% of court cases concerning incitement to violence under a 2020 criminal code amendment had involved alleged threats against Prime Minister Pashinyan and his supporters, whereas potentially prohibited statements by ruling party members were apparently not subject to the same scrutiny."

Throughout the 2026 pre-election period, the Regional Center for Democracy and Security (RCDS), an independent think tank based in Yerevan, monitored online hate speech targeting Nagorno-Karabakh refugees.

Their reports documented how pro-government bloggers and influential social media users used their platforms to direct hostile rhetoric toward displaced Karabakh Armenians, labeling them with derogatory terms. Despite these findings, law enforcement agencies in Armenia largely refrained from pursuing criminal prosecutions against these activists.

Why doesn't the EU react?

Despite Armenia's efforts to strengthen its ties with the EU, Brussels has given no clear response to the silencing of opposition voices, observers in Yerevan told DW.

"The EU, by and large, has adopted a very pragmatic and geopolitically driven approach," said political analyst Tigran Grigoryan.

"Given various regional developments, including what is happening in Georgia, Armenia has now become the EU's primary partner in the region," he added. "Coupled with the fact that the alternative to Pashinyan is a pro-Russian opposition, there is ultimately no serious response to these criminal cases."

Stefan Meister, Eastern Europe expert at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), echoed this view. European support for Armenia appears to be "mainly driven by the European Russia policy," Meister said. "So it's not so much about Armenia itself, but it is more about strengthening those forces that are undermining Russia's influence in the country and in the region."

He believes that Pashinyan leverages this geopolitical dynamic to label internal political opponents as Russian proxies. However, not everyone who criticizes Pashinyan is pro-Russian, Meister added. He pointed out that "the EU is somehow falling into this trap by accepting that this is the right narrative."

EU: Armenia should deliver on its commitment

Democracy, the rule of law, and fundamental rights are at the core of the EU-Armenia Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the Strategic Agenda for the EU-Armenia Partnership, an EU spokesperson said in a written response to DW's request for comment.

It also pointed out that "the EU is closely following developments in the country, including as regards criminal investigations. In line with Armenia's international commitments and legal framework, such investigations should be carried out in an independent and impartial manner, free from political considerations."

World.title: South Africa's ANC facing worst-ever performance in local elections
World.content:
Near-final results show South Africa's once dominant ANC will see its lowest-ever vote percentage. The party is taking the blame for shoddy municipal services, including water and electricity shortages.

South Africa's African National Congress (ANC) is heading for an historically poor election performance, with the near-final tally from Wednesday's municipal polls showing it coming in with just over 30% of the vote.

The ANC also lost its majority in six of the eight metropolitan regions, South Africa's Electoral Commission said Saturday in sharing the results after 98% of votes were counted.

South African voters in 2026 are angry about water and electricity shortages, with the ANC taking the blame for the poor state of municipalities. High unemployment, crime, and widespread corruption are other pressing issues.

ANC leader, and South African president, Cyril Ramaphosa, has not yet addressed the poor performance as of Saturday evening. However, during the week, he admitted in his weekly presidential letter that "municipal failures have contributed to declining public trust and confidence in democratic governance."

On Saturday, ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula told reporters that the ANC needs to work on winning back public confidence.

"We cannot ask the people to trust us merely because of our history," Mbalula said.

"This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC ... as much as we are the largest party, it has been catastrophic for the movement," he added.

The ANC's steady decline with voters

Although the ANC will still be the single largest party by overall vote percentage, it had governed with an absolute majority for most of its history up until the general election in 2024 saw it lose an outright parliamentary majority for the first time in South Africa's democratic era.

"This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared," political analyst Daniel Silke told the AFP news agency.

"It's the ANC's worst result in history," Silke said, adding that the result will undermine the ANC's ability to exert authority on the local and national level. The results could also provide a bellwether of voter sentiment ahead of the 2029 general elections.

Once led by Nelson Mandela, the ANC was instrumental in ending apartheid, and took and power in 1994 after South Africa became a democracy.

But over the past decade, it has steadily performed worse in one election after another. In 2024, the ANC secured just over 40% in the 2024 national polls and 46% at the previous municipal elections in 2021.

After losing the absolute majority in 2024, the ANC formed a cross-party national unity government with all the parties represented in parliament, which is still in power.

The ANC's decline comes amid disillusionment over corruption, mismanagement and high unemployment. Smaller parties have also emerged across South Africa's political landscape, cutting into the ANC's voter base.

DA opposition holds large cities

South Africa is now looking at complex coalition negotiations for municipal level governing alliances.

Runner up in the polls looks to be the pro-business, center-right Democratic Alliance (DA), coming in at 24% of the votes.

The DA is set to keep control of Cape Town after winning an absolute majority. It also performed well in the capital, Pretoria, and economic hub of Johannesburg, and is expected to form coalitions that exclude the ANC.

"All of the cut and thrust that comes with the election is now over, and it is time now... to put together governments that can actually fix these towns and cities," DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis told reporters.

"We have already reached out to many parties over the last 24 hours and will continue to do so today," he said.

World.title: More than 40,000 gather as Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in Uruguay
World.content:
Massive crowds have turned out for the pontiff as he celebrates the first Mass of his South America tour. A nighttime prayer vigil in Montevideo is expected to draw more than 60,000 young people.

The Vatican and local authorities in western Uruguay say an estimated 40,000 people turned out on Saturday morning to participate in the first Mass of Pope Leo XIV's 12-day, three-nation tour of South America.

The Vatican said 30,000 people from Uruguay as well as neighboring Argentina and Brazil had registered for the event, adding that another 10,000 had braved the rain to attend the religious service, which took place in Paysandu — a city on the Uruguay River, some 375 kilometers (230 miles) west of the capital Montevideo.

Leo, who underwent surgery for lung cancer on October 13, was greeted by throngs of cheering fans as he made his way from the local airport to Paysandu's sprawling Paris London Park.

"He's the representative of Christ but he's human," said Soledad Sanchez, who told France's AFP news agency that she had traveled far to be in Paysandu.

"We weren't sure if he could make it but he pushed through for us," said Sanchez as tears welled up in her eyes, "He made it here to give us a message of peace because he knows our world needs it right now."

What to know about Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why are young people reacting so strongly to Pope Leo XIV?

The 71-year-old US-born pontiff, who holds US, Peruvian and Vatican citizenship, is seeking to raise interest in the Catholic Church in Uruguay, South America's most secular country, as a remedy for helping the nation and its citizens cope with the troubles of the modern world.

Saturday morning's Mass was dedicated to the Blessed Jacinto Vera, who was appointed Uruguay's first bishop by Pope Leo XIII in 1878.

On Friday, the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics spoke of Bishop Vera, noting that he had walked the countryside and helped the poor, adding that those whom he encountered "found something of Christ's goodness" in him.

Leo will underscore the need for that kind of outreach on Saturday afternoon when he visits a Montevideo neighborhood beset by drug violence and in which the Church has invested in public housing and rehabilitation projects for addicts.

At Pope Leo's final event in the country — a prayer vigil in Montevideo's Centenary Stadium that is expected to draw some 60,000 young faithful — the pontiff will call on young people to reject religious indifference and turn to Christ's teachings.

Leo's emphasis on charity and brotherly love has struck a deep chord with young people in Uruguay and elsewhere.

One 18-year-old attendee at Saturday morning's Mass told AFP: "I wouldn't call myself religious, but I like this pope. He has a really good message for humanity. Even for non-believers, there is something to take from his ideas."

On Sunday, Pope Leo will depart for Argentina, where he will meet with President Javier Milei, a libertarian-populist and close ally to US President Donald Trump, who previously lashed out at the leader of the world's largest Christian faith over his calls to end wars and cruel immigration policies.

World.title: El presidente de Israel encarga formar Gobierno al líder opositor Gadi Eisenkot
World.content:
“Ha llegado el momento de formar un Ejecutivo de emergencia nacional”, asegura el exjefe del Estado Mayor, que obtuvo 67 de los 120 apoyos posibles, incluidos los de las dos listas árabes

El presidente de Israel, Isaac Herzog, ha anunciado este sábado que encargará formar Gobierno al principal líder de la oposición, el exjefe del Estado Mayor Gadi Eisenkot. Herzog ha efectuado el anuncio a la conclusión de la jornada sabática, tras unas consultas en las que los distintos grupos políticos dieron a Eisenkot hasta 67 apoyos de los 120 del Parlamento. “Ha llegado el momento de formar un Gobierno de emergencia nacional”, ha escrito el líder opositor, tras el anuncio, en sus cuentas de redes sociales. “Haré todo lo posible para estar a la altura”.

Como era previsible, recomendaron su nombramiento los cuatro principales partidos judíos de oposición: Yashar (el del propio Eisenkot); Beyahad, la que lidera los ex primeros ministros Naftali Bennett y Yair Lapid; Los Demócratas, de Yair Golán, única formación de izquierdas del bloque; y el derechista laico Israel Beitenu, del veterano exministro Avigdor Lieberman. Pero también las dos listas árabes, para apuntalar su candidatura y evitar que el encargo recayese en el primer ministro, Benjamín Netanyahu.

Netanyahu apenas obtuvo 46 síes en las consultas. Menos incluso que su actual coalición con ultraortodoxos y ultranacionalistas, ya que uno de los partidos, Judaísmo Unido de la Torá (que cuenta con siete diputados), se abstuvo de recomendar candidato alguno.

Eisenkot, a quien los principales sondeos daban desde hace meses como previsible vencedor, no fue el candidato más votado en las elecciones legislativas del pasado 27 de octubre. Su lista quedó segunda, con 21 escaños. Ganó, una vez más, el Likud de Netanyahu, con 27, pero su coalición perdió la mayoría parlamentaria y quedó, además, con menos margen de maniobra, como se ha acabado viendo en las consultas con el presidente.

Herzog ha invitado a Eisenkot a la residencia presidencial este domingo a las 17.00 horas (16.00 en la España peninsular) para encomendarle la formación del Ejecutivo, ha informado su oficina en un comunicado. A partir de entonces, dispone de 28 días (y otros 14 de prórroga si fuese necesario) para formar el puzle de un Gobierno sin tener claro aún con qué piezas.

El proceso es, además, una novedad para él. Apenas lleva tiempo en política, tras una extensa y laureada carrera militar. Dirigió el ejército israelí entre 2015 y 2019, con Netanyahu como primer ministro. En un país militarista y con reclutamiento obligatorio para la mayoría de los judíos (tanto de hombres como de mujeres), su imagen de militar fiable, sincero y más preocupado por el bien del país que por el suyo personal ha impulsado su figura, hasta convertirle en líder de facto de la oposición. Todo el mundo sabe, además, que ha perdido un hijo y dos sobrinos cuando servían como soldados dentro de Gaza desde la invasión de 2023. El nombre de su partido, Yashar, significa en hebreo recto u honesto, aunque juega también con la idea del centro político.

El encargo abre ahora un camino incierto, por las divergencias dentro del bloque judío de oposición sobre cómo actuar. El viernes, Eisenkot insinuó la posibilidad de gobernar en minoría, y cada vez gana más peso la opción de pactar con los ultraortodoxos (que hoy gobiernan con Netanyahu), en vez de con los árabes, que han extendido su mano para cambiar la jefatura de Gobierno.

Lieberman ha martilleado en su extensa carrera política contra las dádivas a los ultraortodoxos y su exención del servicio militar. Ahora, sin embargo, se muestra abierto (“dolorosamente”, ha escrito) a negociar con ellos con tal de que el nuevo Ejecutivo no tenga que “depender” de las listas árabes, a las que define como “antisionistas que apoyan el terrorismo”. Son dos: Lista Conjunta y Ra’am, y representan a los palestinos con nacionalidad israelí: dos millones de descendientes de quienes no huyeron o fueron expulsados por las milicias sionistas y el ejército de Israel entre 1947 y 1949. Sus 19 diputados sin precedentes les dan las llaves del poder.

Prescindir de ellas obliga a Eisenkot a la aritmética parlamentaria. Lieberman propone atraer a uno o a los dos partidos ultraortodoxos y confiar en un puñado de tránsfugas del Likud, convencido de que un Gobierno de minoría caería enseguida y solo daría paso a otro regreso triunfal de Netanyahu, “con 70 diputados”, como insistía en un importante mensaje el viernes.

El rechazo de una de las fuerzas ultraortodoxas, Judaísmo Unido de la Torá, de recomendar esta vez a Netanyahu como próximo primer ministro ha abierto en cualquier caso esta puerta inesperada, que Eisenkot tendrá que decidir si franquea.

Poco antes del anuncio presidencial, Netanyahu ha emitido un nervioso e islamófobo mensaje en el que advierte contra todo pacto con los partidos árabes, a los que acusa de islamistas radicales y de desear el fin de Israel. Gobernar con ellos convertiría las calles del país en las de París o Ámsterdam, ha dicho, para argumentar la necesidad de un Gobierno de unidad nacional. “Es el momento de la unidad”, ha dicho.

El partido de Eisenkot ha respondido acusándole de hipocresía. “Si el Likud y sus aliados están, de repente, interesados ​​en la ‘unidad’ y en un Gobierno de amplio espectro, son más que bienvenidos a anunciar públicamente que disuelven su alianza con los extremistas, que aceptan los cuatro principios de Eisenkot y que están dispuestos a formar parte de un gobierno encabezado por el primer ministro Eisenkot”, señala.

Los cuatro principios son condiciones que el exjefe del Estado Mayor viene poniendo, ya desde la campaña electoral, a sus socios potenciales: aceptar el carácter de Israel como Estado judío y democrático y la obligatoriedad del servicio militar o nacional para todos sus ciudadanos, respetar los principios y valores de la Declaración de Independencia y definir a Hamás como una organización terrorista que debe entregar sus armas y dejar de controlar cerca de la mitad de Gaza.

World.title: Todos los ojos se vuelven al norte: lo que pasa cuando se empuja a los creadores
World.content:
Faro Santander, el nuevo espacio cultural y museístico del norte de España, lanza la II convocatoria de Ayudas a la Creación para artistas cántabros de cualquier disciplina, un programa que, además de ayuda económica, provee de asesorías especializadas y garantiza una muestra pública en el museo. Los ganadores de la primera convocatoria cuentan su experiencia

Suelen identificarse solo a toro pasado: aquel momento me cambió la vida. Hay oportunidades, sin embargo, cuyo brillo se deja ver desde el principio. Esta es una de esas. Faro Santander lanza su II Convocatoria de Ayudas a la Creación, un programa que ofrece a los proyectos seleccionados una dotación económica de 10.000 euros, seminarios y mentorías con profesionales, la ocasión de compartir proceso creativo con otros artistas y, como remate, una muestra pública en un espacio tan espectacular como el Edificio Pereda, convertido desde su reciente rehabilitación y apertura en Santander en uno de los grandes focos culturales de todo el norte de España.

Hasta el 15 de febrero de 2027 puede disfrutarse gratuitamente, comisariado por Ane Rodríguez, del resultado de los cuatro proyectos becados en la primera edición. Talento cántabro que, a partir de distintas manifestaciones culturales ligadas a esa verde tierra, ha generado un trabajo variado, muy contemporáneo y de vocación universal. En Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas, Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva recuperan materiales de un archivo de educación sexual de hace décadas; una obra, la que proponen, que cultiva la sensibilidad, que induce a la reflexión sobre gestos cotidianos como el abrazo. En Una forma minúscula, de Salón de belleza, nombre del colectivo formado por Manuela Gutiérrez y Cristina Somavilla, el cine de arte y ensayo sirve como pretexto para encontrarse y hablar, para crear comunidad y traer a la conversación la olvidada contracultura santanderina. La pintora Amaia Bregel, por primera vez en su carrera en piezas de gran escala, en Ludarquías muestra instalaciones y dispositivos impregnados de todo su saber pictórico (“Casi todo el arte contemporáneo es hijo de la pintura”, cuenta). El dúo Casapalma —Irene Atienza y Yoel Molina—, cuya música bucea en el folclore cántabro, ha logrado terminar el rodaje de un documental titulado La Suite de los Riconchos que se estrena el próximo 22 de octubre y nos trae ese ancestral conocimiento que se esconde en las danzas tradicionales y la etnografía.

Entre todos los aspirantes, el jurado escogió proyectos en los que, además de formatos convencionales, cupieran investigaciones artísticas y apuestas valientes: se valora documentación, proceso, método y pensamiento tanto como pieza final. Una característica de este programa de ayudas que los cuatro beneficiarios destacan, por inusual en el panorama nacional: “Ojalá mantengan este espíritu”, indica Germán de la Riva. La visibilidad que les ha otorgado este reconocimiento, sobre todo al verse expuestos en Marisma, en la primera planta de Faro, vecinos a una colección permanente que abarca obra desde El Greco a Frida Kahlo, es el otro gran privilegio que los artistas unánimemente señalan: “Para mí supuso un punto de inflexión”, confiesa Amaia Bregel; para ella, esta ha sido la puerta hacia otras becas o ferias de enorme prestigio, como la de Casa Velázquez o Estampa.

“Animaos a participar, sea cual sea vuestra idea”, ese es el mensaje común de los primeros beneficiarios para quienes les sigan.

Segunda convocatoria Ayudas Plazo de admisión 2026 15 octubre -

09 de noviembre Dotación económica 10.000 euros Beneficiarios Cuatro artistas (o colectivos de artistas) de cualquier disciplina, residentes o nacidos en Cantabria Así funciona el programa de acompañamiento: El proyecto debe desarrollarse en Cantabria, entre enero y junio de 2027

Se priorizarán aquellos que fomenten la generación de tejido artístico en el territorio

Se realizará un encuentro inicial entre comisarios, coordinadores y beneficiarios

Los beneficiarios dispondrán de cuatro seminarios y talleres con profesionales invitados, uno a la semana durante el primer mes de trabajo

Estos encuentros colectivos periódicos que estarán abiertos a otros artistas que deseen inscribirse

Los beneficiarios podrán solicitar tutorías personalizadas y seguimiento continuo

Al final del programa, se organizará una muestra pública en Faro Santander, a partir de septiembre de 2027

Amaia Bregel y

Ludarquías

Cuando Amaia Bregel volvió a Santander en marzo de 2020, con la pandemia, no tenía intención de quedarse. Se había graduado en Bellas Artes en Valencia, donde continuó con un máster de Producción de Arte y Pensamiento Contemporáneo y donde, sin aquel terremoto mundial, seguramente se habría imaginado residiendo todavía. Hoy, sin embargo, reivindica las posibilidades halladas en su ciudad: “Mucha gente de mi generación volvió y entre todos hemos creado una red. Soy la que más defiende Santander ahora mismo”, reclama entre risas.

05:15 Amaia Bregel | Fundación Santander

Al borde de la treintena, la ayuda de Faro ha supuesto para ella un cambio de escala, literal y profesional. Su proyecto, Ludarquías, le ha permitido abordar una producción que no habría podido llevar a cabo en las condiciones con las que venía trabajando. La artista lo resume sin rodeos: «Para mí a nivel profesional es un antes y un después». Ha podido tomar por primera vez decisiones plásticas sin ver constreñida su ambición por cuestiones estrictamente económicas y, además, ha contado, cuando la duda más quemaba, con el consejo de la consagrada artista limeña Andrea Canepa. “Fue un regalazo”, cuenta. Fruto de toda esa meticulosa labor es el objeto pictórico titulado Escalera de Jacob. Uno de los imperdibles de la muestra.

Amaia Bregel y

Ludarquías Las ayudas supusieron la oportunidad para Amaia Bregel de llevar sus objetos pictóricos a unas dimensiones nunca antes experimentadas. En la imagen, parte del trabajo de montaje final de la instalación móvil. (Crédito: Jabata Films) Antes de llegar al objeto pictórico grande, Bregel trabaja con maquetas. La propia escala presenta problemas que ha de ir afrontando en el proceso plástico y que necesitan de ingenio. En este proyecto, contó con la asesoría de la artista peruana Andrea Canepa. (Crédito: Jabata Films) Su obra parte de lo pictórico y lo deriva hacia objetos donde el color y sus vibraciones son habitables. Amaia Bregel sigue considerándose, ante todo, pintora, aunque se maneje en muchos lenguajes y métodos. Esta pieza expuesta en Marisma, en Faro Santander, lleva por título ‘Escalera de Jacob’ y puede contemplarse así, como un cubo completo, o abierta. (Crédito: Jabata Films).

Casapalma y

La Suite de los Riconchos

Su álbum debut, Montañesas (2023), mezclaba canción tradicional con sonidos electrónicos; con JOTAS (2025) profundizan en la importancia de la pandereta y de una música que, sobre todo, estaba hecha para bailar. Y ahí, en todo ese universo —de los ritmos de percusión y los pasos de danza a la alfayatería y los trajes tradicionales— encuentran el germen del documental La Suite de los Riconchos que ahora estrenan en la Filmoteca de Cantabria y que esperan que tenga un gran recorrido por festivales y salas. Música y patrimonio, arte y sociología.

08:08 Casapalma | Fundación Santander

Las ayudas, además del crucial aporte económico para completar el rodaje que finalizaron en agosto (“¡Hacer una película es muy caro!”, exclama Atienza), le han procurado otra experiencia de esas difícilmente olvidables. Tocaron en la inauguración de Faro Santander, pudieron, gracias a la celebración de ese concierto, “subir a un escenario enorme el folclore de Cantabria para que lo viera toda la ciudad”.

Casapalma y

La Suite de los Riconchos Fotograma de ‘La Suite de los Riconchos’, con Yoel Molina (izquierda) a la guitarra e Irene Atienza a la pandereta. Molina se formó en Musikene (País Vasco) y en el Conservatorio Superior de Ámsterdam. Atienza, que vivió varios años en Brasil, regresó a su ciudad, Santander, tras la pandemia. Para la grabación del documental han llevado a cabo una importante investigación musicológica y etnográfica. El baile estaba en el centro del propósito de estas músicas, y esa misma relevancia tiene en la película. Los trajes tradicionales de montañesa suelen componerse de camisa de manca ancha, saya larga de colores con detalles de terciopelo y detalles como pañoleta o faltriquera. La película documental musical, que contó con la asesoría de grandes profesionales coreográficos y estudiosos de la etnografía de la región, se estrenó en la Filmoteca de Cantabria el 22 de octubre y está pendiente de su distribución en festivales y salas.

Para una formación que trabaja con el patrimonio inmaterial, con buena reputación ya bien ganada y una trayectoria importante en el campo de la música, compartir el proceso de su película con otros artistas con métodos y objetivos más abstractos, inmersos en proyectos de lenguajes variopintos, ha sido otro de los aprendizajes más enriquecedores. Cuenta Irene que, tras esta experiencia en común, Aurelio Vélez, vinculado al colectivo etnográfico Brañaflor y asesor fundamental del filme, tomó la determinación de presentar una propuesta sobre costura y cuadros de la colección permanente a la convocatoria que ahora se abre. “Él no se imaginaba que pudiera ser candidato a unas ayudas de arte, pero programas como este son una forma de abrir la mente”.

Salón de Belleza y

Una forma minúscula

Una conversación entre dos amigas, Manuela Gutiérrez y Cristina Somavilla, que eclosiona al abrirla al resto: así podría definirse qué es Salón de Belleza, el colectivo artístico que ambas fundaron y para el que ver películas, discutirlas y cuestionar ideas anquilosadas sobre el gusto o la cultura es la razón última de ser. Una forma minúscula parte de un hallazgo accidental: se toparon con el largometraje de Jesús Garay Manderley (1981) sobre la figura del artista y activista LGTBIQ+ José Pérez Ocaña y se obsesionaron con la peli: “Le pregunté por ella a mi padre”, cuenta Somavilla, “y me contó que él había conocido aquí a Ocaña”. Ahí comienza su investigación, ¿qué relatos de aquella Cantabria habían quedado fuera de la historia oficial? “Hemos abierto fisuras en lo que se supone que es Santander: hay mucho más”, explican.

06:42 Salón de Belleza | Fundación Santander

La ayuda les ha permitido poner en marcha un grupo de investigación intergeneracional en el que la memoria oral y el intercambio de pareceres ha ido hilando una conversación inacabada e inacabable (“¡seguiremos con estos encuentros y clubes en el futuro!”), siempre dispuesta a fluir fuera de cauce y al vaivén de las sorpresas, una investigación recogida parcialmente en textos y materiales de archivo disponibles en la muestra. “Nos gustaría ahora que la gente se acercara al espacio museístico, que Faro Santander se convirtiera en ese lugar de participación y encuentro que ha sido para nosotras”.

Salón de Belleza y

Una forma minúscula Sesión de trabajo del proyecto ‘Una forma minúscula’, en la que, a partir del visionado de una película y de ciertos materiales de archivo, se abre una conversación. Fotograma del drama dirigido por Jesús Garay ‘Manderley’, estrenado en 1981. La trama acompaña a tres jóvenes homosexuales que, en un mal momento personal, deciden pasar un verano juntos en Cantabria. Entre los protagonistas, destaca el ‘performer’ José Pérez Ocaña. Además de la película, las sesiones del proyecto utilizan material que reconstruye el contexto cultural en que surgió el filme para indagar más allá del relato oficial. En la imagen, el informe de calificación por edades de ‘Manderley’ (Archivo General de la Administración). Otro de esos materiales empleados fue el libro del artista e historiador Adolfo Fernández-Punsola ‘Nuestras vidas’, editado en 1996, que recoge fotografías y documentos de las décadas que retrata la película.

Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva y

Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas

Nunca sabe uno adónde le va a llevar abrir unas cajas viejas. Germán de la Riva recordaba vagamente el contenido de las que sus padres habían acumulado en la consulta. Psicólogos, fueron pioneros en materia de educación sexual en Santander en los años 80 y 90, con métodos traídos de su experiencia en Latinoamérica y EE UU. Dentro de las solapas de cartón, películas con imágenes artísticas pero explícitamente sexuales convivían con artículos y tesis científicas, un archivo que resultó idóneo para la labor investigadora que De la Riva lleva tiempo desarrollando junto a la también doctora en Bellas Artes y bailarina de danza contemporánea Itsaso Iribarren. Para ellos, toda su obra empieza en el cuerpo.

06:28 Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva | Fundación Santander

Memoria, sexualidad o cómo nos relacionamos físicamente son cuestiones que se pueden abordar apelando a los sentidos y la intuición. El arte tiene su propio camino hacia el conocimiento y, para Iribarren y De la Riva, mostrar ese proceso junto a la obra puede ser la mejor manera de hacer pedagogía: “El público entiende más o menos lo que ocurrió en las artes hasta las Vanguardias, pero existe un vacío, una desconexión, con las artes vivas y el presente de la creación”. Justo por ello, valoran y agradecen el compromiso de Faro Santander al generar un espacio que puede proveer al espectador de las piezas de puzle que le faltan.

Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva y

Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva, doctores en Bellas Artes y practicantes de danza contemporánea y artes vivas, inician todas sus investigaciones plásticas a partir del cuerpo: el movimiento, el tacto, los sentidos. Es otro de los caminos de conocimiento que permite el arte y que merece exploración. Para documentar el proceso del proyecto ‘Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas’ y generar un resultado expositivo, han empleado, entre otros métodos y lenguaje, la filmación analógica en 16 milímetros. Las artes vivas son una disciplina contemporánea en la que las fronteras genéricas se borran, donde conviven ‘performance’, danza, teatro físico, música, texto y artes visuales. De la Riva y Iribarren aplauden la apuesta de Faro Santander por proyectos así, donde mostrar el proceso creativo es casi más importante que alcanzar un resultado final.

Son cuatro historias, cuatro pulsos creativos distintos que, sin embargo, pintan un mapa justo de los derroteros del arte español de hoy, siempre vivo y siempre a punto del naufragio, sin tablas de salvación como la que ofrece esta convocatoria de Faro Santander. Hay oportunidades que de verdad cambian vidas, instituciones que verdaderamente tienen la capacidad de generar un tejido cultural que cosa todo el norte de España y enseñe el tapiz con lo mejor de nuestra creación fuera.

Para presentarse a la nueva convocatoria no hace falta tener respuestas, tan solo ganas de pelearse con el runrún que provocan esas preguntas que merece la pena hacerse.

World.title: En Argentina florecen los ‘finfluencers’, supuestos expertos que prometen hacerte rico: “Deja de ser una perrita y conviértete en un hombre-gorila”
World.content:
Así como se pasan de generación en generación los secretos para encender con pericia el fuego del asado o la receta de una pasta frola, todo argentino aprende, como quien aprende los rudimentos básicos de la supervivencia, que debe proteger su dinero. En una economía históricamente azotada por la inflación y la incertidumbre, el reflejo de la clase media ha sido convertir cada peso extra en dólares para conservar su valor o, en el mejor de los casos, “invertir en ladrillos”. Es decir, comprar una propiedad. Pero en los últimos años, las nuevas generaciones han mostrado un interés creciente por acceder a alternativas más sofisticadas y han encontrado en las redes sociales una guía para hacerlo. Un país donde los salarios no alcanzan para ahorrar y las perspectivas de progreso dependen cada vez más de la astucia para multiplicar lo escaso, es tierra fértil para los finfluencers.

La variedad dentro de este segmento de creadores de contenido es amplia: desde divulgadores profesionales con formación en ciencias económicas o carreras afines —knowledge creators, en la jerga— hasta asesores que encubren la venta de productos o gurús que prometen trucos rápidos para convertirse en millonario. Este último grupo puede resumirse en el fenómeno “masivo bro”, surgido sobre todo en TikTok y cuyo emblema es Matías Cardozo, el creador de la expresión. Este joven, que graba videos desde Dubái, maneja autos de lujo y lleva relojes destellantes en la muñeca, asegura que entrena mucho, duerme poco y vende cursos para dejar de ser una “perrita” y convertirse en un “hombre-gorila” exitoso como él.

Mostrar interés por estos contenidos y entregarse luego a la oferta del algoritmo implica zambullirse en un universo heterogéneo donde aparecen marcos teóricos para empezar a ordenar las cuentas, instrucciones para acceder a activos concretos como fondos comunes, bonos, acciones o criptomonedas e incluso recopilaciones de ofertas de alimentos en los supermercados. Las latas de atún en conserva fueron, de hecho, el instrumento de ahorro sugerido por Ramiro Marra, finfluencer pionero, parte de la sociedad de bolsa Bull Market y exlegislador del partido de Javier Milei. “Es un producto chico, no tiene fecha de vencimiento cercana y en unos meses ya le saqué un 40% (de rendimiento)”, decía en julio de 2023, cuando la inflación galopaba. Terminaría aquel año en el 211,4%.

Esa espiral inflacionaria es uno de los factores que explica la oleada de finfluencers, entiende Agustín Natoli, el asesor detrás del canal de YouTube Joven Inversor, número uno sobre inversiones en Argentina, con más de un millón de suscriptores. “En Argentina el dinero se te escurría de las manos y todo el mundo se metía en internet para ver qué alternativas tenía para conservar el poder adquisitivo. Aunque eso se frenó un poco, seguimos con regímenes altísimos de inflación en relación con el mundo”, apunta. Este año la inflación acumuló un 23,6% en los primeros nueve meses del año y se estima que cierre en torno del 30%.

El propio presidente ha alentado la curiosidad por las herramientas más disruptivas de inversión. Desde su cuenta X, Javier Milei promovió en febrero de 2025 un proyecto de criptomonedas, $Libra, que dejó un reguero de damnificados y derivó en una investigación judicial. Así como algunos creadores se esfuerzan por ofrecer información valiosa, otros dan margen para que se cuelen masivamente estafas, que permean mejor en sociedades desesperadas.

Nuevos canales

Para Lara López Calvo, economista y magíster en finanzas con más de un millón de seguidores en Instagram, el auge de este segmento se explica, en parte, por la transformación del ecosistema fintech argentino. “Lo que pasó en los últimos cinco años es una revolución y hoy la gente accede a un montón de instrumentos a los que antes solo accedían los que tenían mucho dinero, y lo hace de una forma económica, rápida y con mejores sistemas”, señala.

Hay una democratización de herramientas, pero no del conocimiento para hacer uso de ellas, lo que algunos consideran incluso una de las causas detrás del aumento del endeudamiento, especialmente en plataformas digitales. La educación argentina no incluye la educación financiera, más allá de algunas iniciativas puntuales; internet y sus creadores ocupan el vacío. Algunos apuntan a un target específico, como Sabrina Castelli, que con Mujer Financiera quiso enfocarse en quienes los datos ubican en desventaja. Para esta contable y licenciada en administración, el gran desafío es hacer que invertir sea algo “realmente posible y sostenible dentro de las vidas de las mujeres, cargadas todavía con parte desproporcionada de las tareas domésticas y de cuidado”.

El Gobierno alienta abiertamente la inversión como una vía para canalizar más dinero hacia el sistema bancario, ampliar el crédito y ofrecer una alternativa para reactivar la actividad económica. “Tener los dólares debajo del colchón es un muy mal negocio”, ha dicho el ministro de Economía, Luis Caputo, autor de una amnistía fiscal para que las personas puedan llevar sus ahorros no declarados a los bancos sin sufrir penalidades. La apuesta oficial es ambiciosa porque, en el fondo, apunta a desbloquear un trauma colectivo derivado de la dificultad para proyectar a largo plazo y una desconfianza crónica alimentada por las malas experiencias. El Gobierno busca que los argentinos dejen de atesorar rollitos de billetes en sus casas, pero son los finfluencers los que, mal o bien, se han puesto a la delantera.
