World.title: Parties still compiling candidate lists ahead of March Riigikogu elections
World.content:
Parties are still recruiting Riigikogu candidates with some list places unfilled. The coalition Reform Party will not announce its lead candidates until late on this month.

The opposition Center Party has yet to decide which electoral district party chairman and former Tallinn mayor Mihhail Kõlvart will head up.

The Riigikogu elections take place in March and final candidate lists are due by mid-January, meaning parties are deep into the process of deciding who to run where, to optimize results.

Due to the d'Hondt proportional representation system used in Estonia, parties usually place their vote magnet candidates, usually leading politicians, high up on their ordered lists – excess votes these candidates have after clinching a seat can be distributed to candidates lower down on the list, who may not win a seat in their own right.

Kõlvart is one such vote magnet, and Center's Secretary General Anneli Ott told "Aktuaalne kaamera": "The party chairman would be a major vote-winner in any constituency. But which constituency he will head the list in remains undecided."

The party's two MEPs Jana Toom and Jaak Madison, will head electoral lists, Center, whose traditional bedrock areas include Tallinn and Ida-Viru County, confirmed.

Center Party Chairman Mihhail Kõlvart. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

The Social Democrats (SDE) have made more apparent progress. The party leader, Lauri Läänemets, will run in Järva and Viljandi, while new member, former foreign ministry secregary general and prime ministerial candidate Jonatan Vseviov, is to run in Harju and Rapla. "The regional branches have not yet made their final decisions on the order of candidates or who will ultimately stand," said SDE Secretary General Piret Hartmann

The Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) has finalized leading candidates in half its constituencies, with chairman Martin Helme running in Tallinn's Mustamäe and Nõmme. Helme said the party faces difficulty winning votes in the bigger cities, meaning great efforts must be focused there. "A third of the Riigikogu is elected from Tallinn. So naturally, we are focusing on Tallinn," Helme said. EKRE's traditional stronghold has been southwestern Estonia.

Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu is to run in Harju and Rapla, just south of Tallinn and including the capital's commuter belt, with MEPs Jüri Ratas, a former prime minister, and Riho Terras also standing. Secretary General Andres Metsoja said regional branch proposals matter most when making decisions.

Looking for its first ever Riigikogu seats is Parempoolsed, whose chairwoman Lavly Perling is prepared to run in Harju and Rapla, though the party has not completed all its leads and has even turned some aspirants away. Deputy chairman Siim Kiisler said ideological conviction matters to the party more than profile.

Eesti 200, who in summer saw two MPs defect, is still compiling its full list.

Several of the parties have been hit by a wave of departures of high profile candidates who are not running this time around. SDE has lost Raimond Kaljulaid, a prominent MP who sits on the Riigikogu's national defense committee but is returning to the private sector, as well as MEP Marina Kaljurand. Former education minister Liina Kersna (Reform) is not seeking re-election and neither is Hanno Pevkur, defense minister until September and once a challenger for Reform's leadership. Parempoolsed has lost defense and security expert Rainer Saks, who cannot run due to taking up a post as presidential adviser.

High profile candidates may run for a party even if they cannot then take up the seat won, usually because they hold another post which bars that. MEPs and local government leaders fall into that category for instance. Their votes won will be transferred to candidates lower down the party's ordered list.

Polling day is March 7, 2027.

World.title: Priit Reiska: A rare opportunity to increase the number of people with higher education
World.content:
Universities need certainty that funding will be available for the entire duration of a student's studies. A decision on admissions for one year creates a commitment lasting several years to the young people who enroll, writes Priit Reiska.

The 2027 state budget, which has reached its second reading in parliament, will also shape the educational opportunities available to young people who are currently completing secondary education. Will universities have enough places for a larger generation of school graduates, and can the quality of education be maintained while teaching more students?

Parliament has already expressed its position. In its statement "In Support of Higher Education," lawmakers called on the government to ensure that, beginning with admissions in 2027, at least 1,000 additional tuition-free study places are provided annually over several years in fields important to Estonia's development leap. That statement must now be reflected in the state budget.

"Educating the current large generation of young people carries particular importance."

While about 10,100 young people completed secondary education in 2024, forecasts by the Ministry of Education and Research indicate that the number of graduates will reach 12,500 by 2028. This gives Estonia an opportunity to increase the number of people with higher education, but it requires that opportunities to continue studies grow alongside the number of graduates.

Educating the current large generation of young people carries particular importance. If this opportunity is missed, it will become much more difficult to increase the number of highly educated people later because of declining birth rates. Missing out on higher education can limit a young person's opportunities and leave part of their potential unused for the benefit of society.

Education and Research Minister Kristina Kallas has also warned that insufficient study opportunities could increase the number of young people entering the labor market without professional qualifications and slow the competitiveness of the Estonian economy.

University of Tartu Rector Toomas Asser has emphasized that Estonia's move toward a more knowledge-intensive economy depends on how many people possess the necessary expertise. Training the next generation of top specialists requires a strong higher education pathway that begins with sufficient admissions to bachelor's programs.

I have written previously that the scale of higher education and choices of study fields cannot be determined solely by current labor market needs. It is already difficult to predict workforce needs five or 10 years into the future, and the rapid development of artificial intelligence is increasing uncertainty even further, as developments in recent months and weeks have demonstrated.

In such circumstances, the strength of academic university education lies in broad-based knowledge, critical thinking, independent learning skills, and the ability to create new solutions. Highly educated people also create new jobs and help society adapt to change.

New study places require real additional funding

During spring negotiations over administrative agreements, both the ministry and the universities estimated that creating additional study places would require a total of €146 million over the next four years. Of that amount, €19.7 million is needed in 2027, including €13.3 million for first-cycle higher education places.

The increase in higher education funding planned in the draft state budget amounts to only €3.67 million. Compared with the funding needed for first-cycle study places alone, that is nearly €10 million less. The shortfall is intended to be covered by redistributing the existing operating support of universities and professional higher education institutions. As a result, creating new study places would require reducing funding for existing education.

"Efficiency should also be measured by whether students can successfully complete their studies and graduate."

For young people, this creates a real risk that new study places will be established at the expense of current students' learning conditions. If more students must be taught with the same amount of money, the result may be larger study groups, fewer elective courses, and fewer opportunities for individual guidance and meaningful feedback from lecturers. Besides the number of places, it is important to ask what kind of education students enrolled in those places will actually receive.

This is not the first time agreements on higher education funding and actual budget decisions have diverged. In 2023, universities and parliamentary parties agreed that years of funding shortfalls should be corrected over four years and that a sustainable funding model should be developed.

Since then, the planned increase in operating support has repeatedly been reduced. According to the Council of Rectors, operating support for higher education in the 2027 budget falls nearly €50 million short of the level previously agreed upon.

At the same time, universities have increased admissions, improved on-time graduation rates, and developed new forms of study. The administrative agreements signed this spring also included a commitment to educate more young people.

Universities must, of course, organize their activities efficiently and seek ways to teach better with existing resources. Efficiency should also be measured by whether students can successfully complete their studies and graduate. Expanding admissions will not achieve its goal if lecturers have less time to support students and the risk of dropping out increases.

For this reason, universities need certainty that funding will be available for the entire duration of a student's studies if admissions are to be increased. A decision on admissions for one year creates a commitment lasting several years to the young people who enroll.

Parliament can still change the situation

On October 14 of this year, parliament adopted the statement "In Support of Higher Education" with 65 votes in favor. In addition to creating extra tuition-free study places, the statement calls for continued increases in funding for Estonian-language higher education, competitive pay for academic staff, and improvements in educational quality. Parliament has therefore expressed a clear position that educating more young people and ensuring the quality of higher education must go hand in hand.

"Such an opportunity will not come again for decades. Let us make use of it."

Parliament now has an opportunity during the budget process to translate that position into funding decisions. The Council of Rectors' request is that an additional €19.7 million be added to existing higher education funding in 2027 to create new study places. Redistributing existing operating support will not meet that need.

This amount will not solve all the funding problems in higher education, but it would make it possible to increase admissions without reducing funding for existing education. For today's school students, it would provide more opportunities to continue their studies and confidence that a study place also means a high-quality education.

Parliament has supported the creation of additional study places. The 2027 state budget should therefore include real additional funding to create them.

We currently have an opportunity to provide higher education to a larger generation of young people than before. Such an opportunity will not come again for decades. Let us make use of it.

World.title: 400 Estonian students in Russia face recruitment risk, warns KAPO
World.content:
Despite official warnings, nearly 400 young people from Estonia study in Russia, where they risk being recruited by intelligence services or sent to the front, Postimees reported .

The Russian Embassy in Estonia actively promotes Russian higher education on its website, offering scholarships regardless of academic performance and free language courses to help students enrol.

Neither the Estonian Ministry of Education and Research nor the education information system has data on how many Estonians study in Russia, though UNESCO statistics put the figure at 384 in 2023, the year after the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said going to Russia to study is "one of the strangest and most incomprehensible reasons for traveling there," warning that Estonia's ability to provide consular and other assistance to any of its citizens who found themselves in danger would be extremely limited.

Taro said a foreign national could be taken hostage for instance to exchange for captured Russian intelligence operatives, or placed in a situation where signing a contract with the Russian defense ministry ended up the only way out for them — followed by being immediately dispatched to the frontline in Ukraine.

The Internal Security Service (KAPO) says Estonian residents traveling to Russia attract the attention of Russian intelligence, may be detained, and face unpredictable application of Russian law.

KAPO bureau chief Marta Tuul said those interested in studying in Russia are primarily from Russian-speaking backgrounds, and that Russian universities host intelligence officers working under cover who identify and recruit students.

Tuul said recruits may not be activated immediately, with intelligence services waiting until they reach positions useful to them, and that the fate of African students who have been sent to the front cannot be ruled out for Estonians either.

In August, Postimees reported that Nikita Kuzmin, born in Estonia, enrolled at a university in St Petersburg, was recruited by the GRU, given the choice of cooperation or the front, and gathered information on military and civilian sites in Narva before being caught and sentenced to four years.

Prosecutor Margaret Beres said Kuzmin had no accomplices in Estonia and was caught early on, so no significant damage was caused to Estonia's security.

World.title: New buildings may improve air quality but not always lower energy costs
World.content:
A newly built school in western Estonia has delivered a better indoor environment but also significantly higher electricity and heating bills.

Lääneranna Municipality replaced its old school building with a new facility for Lääneranna High School, but the new building's utility costs have proven much higher than those of its predecessor.

Mayor Tarvi Sits said that part of the increase is due to higher energy prices, but the main reason may be the building's modern ventilation system, which consumes considerably more electricity.

"At the moment, the assumption is that the cause is the ventilation system, because the old and depreciated building did not have such a system at all," Sits said, adding that this remains a preliminary assessment.

Tarvi Sits. Source: Piia Saak

"The energy audit was already planned, but we are now speeding it up so specialists can review all the systems and determine whether this is our new reality or whether there is room to reduce costs through better adjustments and settings," he said.

With winter still ahead, the municipality has budgeted additional funds for the school's heating and electricity costs.

Better indoor climate can mean higher energy use

Riigi Kinnisvara AS (RKAS), Estonia's state real estate company, manages a large portfolio of both old and new buildings. RKAS facility services director Priit Valk said situations can arise where a new building consumes more energy than an older one.

The reason often lies in providing a proper indoor climate, Valk noted.

"The same can happen after renovating an old building. For example, if a building previously lacked a mechanical ventilation system, it may have had poorer indoor conditions, in terms of both temperature and air quality. Adding such a system can increase energy consumption, but working conditions in the building improve significantly," Valk explained.

One of the key goals of constructing a new building or renovating an old one is to ensure that indoor climate standards are met.

"Each building must be evaluated individually, and there is no universal rule that applies to every case," Valk said.

Jarek Kurnitski Source: Erakogu

Good air quality comes at a cost

Jarek Kurnitski, professor and academician at Tallinn University of Technology, who leads the university's nearly zero-energy buildings research group, said school buildings naturally require energy-intensive ventilation.

"In a school, many students occupy relatively small classrooms. The air needs to be exchanged five times per hour, and achieving that requires a substantial amount of electricity," Kurnitski said.

"If the old school building did not have a ventilation system, it is understandable that electricity consumption was very low."

He stressed that energy use is unavoidable when maintaining high indoor air quality and that such systems cannot simply be turned off because poor ventilation directly affects students' learning outcomes.

Another issue is whether the ventilation system has been designed and configured efficiently.

"If rooms are not used intensively throughout the day, a demand-based ventilation system could reduce electricity consumption by about half," Kurnitski said regarding the Lihula school building.

"I do not know whether that option has been used in this specific building, but if the ventilation is running from morning to evening regardless of actual room occupancy, there could certainly be opportunities for savings."

Kurnitski described the reported increases in both heating and electricity costs as counterintuitive and suggested that newly completed buildings sometimes operate inefficiently during their first months because systems have not yet been fully adjusted.

Residents seeing similar surprises

A Tallinn resident who moved from a Soviet-era apartment block in Lasnamäe district to a newly built development in Kopli also reported an unpleasant surprise: an electricity bill roughly twice as high as in the older, unrenovated apartment.

The resident has attempted to lower heating costs by turning off ventilation when leaving home, but Kurnitski said that is not a sensible solution and is unlikely to produce major savings.

Newer and older buildings in Kopli, Tallinn. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"Before switching off ventilation, it is worth checking how the ventilation unit is operating. Sometimes the supply air temperature has been set unnecessarily high. If the incoming air is heated above 18 degrees Celsius, heating that air starts consuming significant amounts of electricity," he said.

Despite such examples, Kurnitski stressed that new buildings are generally much more energy-efficient than old ones. Older buildings often consume two to three times more energy.

"A new building should save at least half of energy costs. That is a typical result that can be achieved without applying any extraordinary measures. The same principle applies to both residential and non-residential buildings," he said.

World.title: Crafts teacher: Handmade 'soul bird' makes a heartfelt Father's Day gift
World.content:
Estonia celebrates Father's Day this weekend, and handicrafts teacher Terje Raudsepa says a handmade bird reflecting the maker's feelings and affection can make a great gift.

Raudsepa explained that a hingelind, or "soul bird," represents a person's emotions, thoughts and wishes, so making one for someone is a way to put those feelings into a personal gift.

"When you make someone a soul bird, you pour all your feelings for that person into it," she said.

To make a felt bird, draw a pattern, cut two identical shapes from felting fabric and place them on a soft surface, such as a sponge. Lay thin strands of felting wool over the fabric and work them in with a felting needle.

Crafts teacher Terje Raudsepa demonstrated how "soul birds" can be made by needle felting. November 2026. Source: ERR

A tiny ball of wool can serve as the eye.

"All the supplies you need are available at craft stores," Raudsepa added.

The birds can also be sewn together, embroidered and decorated with leftover bits of fabric, lace and ribbons.

"You can carry your handmade soul bird with you — in your backpack or pocket — and talk to it," Raudsepa said.

And if someone's dad works as a mechanic? "They can stick it in their pocket too," she added.

Crafts teacher Terje Raudsepa showed off her own personal handmade "soul bird." November 2026. Source: ERR

World.title: Iraqi-Spanish Economic Business Council convenes in Madrid
World.content:
Madrid (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi-Spanish Economic Business Council convened in Madrid on Friday, bringing together Iraqi Ambassador to Spain Ali Shamran Hashim Al-Bayati, a senior government delegation, and executives from major Spanish industrial, trade, and investment institutions.

Hosted by the Spanish Chamber of Commerce, the forum aimed to deepen commercial cooperation between Baghdad and Madrid, broaden bilateral investment opportunities, and establish structured joint ventures across vital economic sectors.

Delegates reviewed pathways to expand Spanish commercial involvement in Iraq, particularly in transport, renewable energy, water management, healthcare, and civil infrastructure.

The Madrid summit reflects ongoing efforts by the Iraqi federal government to diversify foreign partnerships beyond traditional markets, encouraging European corporate participation in post-reconstruction development through direct investment, technical joint ventures, and sustainable cross-border trade frameworks.

World.title: US Embassy in Baghdad warns citizens of security risks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Embassy in Baghdad issued a formal security alert on Saturday, warning American citizens residing in or traveling through the Middle East of heightened operational risks stemming from potential armed attacks by the Iranian-backed Houthis, alongside reported Iranian efforts to target U.S. government personnel and interests across the region.

According to the consular advisory, American diplomatic authorities urged citizens to exercise heightened vigilance and prepare for potential commercial aviation disruptions, including short-notice flight cancellations and intermittent airspace closures.

Travelers were advised to monitor airport operational statuses and coordinate directly with commercial airlines for updated departure schedules. The mission highlighted that retaliatory threats or proxy militia actions could extend to commercial facilities, enterprises, and public venues associated with the United States.

To mitigate operational vulnerabilities, the embassy instructed U.S. citizens to maintain a low profile, avoid large crowds, demonstrations, and sites of heavy security deployment, closely monitor local media for situational updates, and strictly comply with instructions issued by host-nation authorities.

World.title: Iraqi Airways resumes direct flights to Beijing starting November 14
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Airways announced on Thursday the resumption of scheduled direct flights to the Chinese capital, Beijing, starting November 14, 2026, marking a significant step in restoring direct air connectivity with one of Iraq’s primary commercial and economic partners.

In an official statement, Director General of Iraqi Airways Mustafa Talib confirmed that the national carrier will operate two weekly round-trip flights servicing the strategic route (Baghdad – Basra – Beijing).

Outbound flights from Iraq are scheduled every Tuesday and Saturday, with return legs operating out of Beijing on Sundays and Wednesdays.

Talib highlighted that the service reinstatement aligns with directives issued by Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani to expand the national carrier’s international route network and inaugurate high-yield commercial air corridors.

By linking Baghdad and the southern oil hub of Basra directly to Beijing, the route aims to streamline business travel, facilitate bilateral freight and corporate logistics, and support expanding commercial and industrial cooperation between Iraq and China.

World.title: Iraq and Syria sign water accord to coordinate Euphrates inflows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Syria have signed a bilateral technical agreement in Damascus to establish joint mechanisms for managing cross-border water resources and align their diplomatic positions ahead of anticipated trilateral negotiations with Turkey over the Euphrates River basin.

The discussions brought together technical delegations led by the Senior Technical Undersecretary of the Iraqi Ministry of Water Resources, Hussein Abdul-Amir Bakka, and Syria’s Deputy Minister of Energy for Water and Electricity Affairs, Osama Abu Zaid.

The bilateral protocol establishes immediate operational measures, including the deployment of joint hydrological gauging stations along the river, regular technical data exchanges, coordinated water quality testing, and collaborative frameworks for monitoring dam integrity and coordinating reservoir discharges. Both parties agreed to work toward convening a tripartite technical meeting including Turkish representatives in March 2027.

The agreement builds directly on previous bilateral coordination meetings held in Baghdad in late June, aiming to settle longstanding operational frictions between the two downstream nations.

Under their 1989 bilateral quota arrangement, Damascus commits to releasing 58% of Turkish Euphrates water inflows into Iraq while retaining 42% for domestic use. However, seasonal flow reductions and conflicting agricultural timelines frequently lead to operational strain around the Tabqa Dam in Syria and the Haditha Dam in Iraq.

Beyond bilateral synchronization, the Damascus talks represent a unified push by downstream states against Turkey’s transboundary water policies.

Ankara continues to govern Euphrates flows under a temporary 1987 protocol establishing a baseline release of 500 cubic meters per second, a framework severely constrained by upstream impoundments under Turkey’s Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP). Both Baghdad and Damascus are pressing for a permanent, legally binding trilateral treaty aligned with international water law to guarantee equitable baseline quotas.

World.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
World.content:
Tehran – Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme.

Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.

He also said Iran’s forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

“Today, the Islamic Republic’s armed forces… having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war,” he said.

“They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence.”

“Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations,” he added.

– Reward offered –

On Friday, the US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme.

Rewards for Justice, a State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including “facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X.

The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In a statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.”

It did not specify what type of information would warrant a $20 million reward.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear programme.

“If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida.

“If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.”

– Dialogue –

The president also said Iran — which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war — is eager to end the conflict.

“We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said.

Trump called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war.

Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said this week his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Early on Saturday, Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, adding there was no official information about any damage.

Iranian state television reported two explosions on the island.

The Iranian army said early Saturday that its air defences had “struck and destroyed” a US drone that was flying over the island, according to state media. It did not say whether the island was attacked.

World.title: Cavs thump 76ers in James return, Celtics crush Hornets
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Cleveland Cavaliers spoiled LeBron James’s latest homecoming on Friday, beating Philadelphia 119-95 to snap the 76ers’ five-game NBA winning streak.

James, playing his first game in Cleveland since opting to head to Philadelphia as a free agent in June rather than returning for a third stint with his hometown Cavs, was greeted by warm cheers — and scattered boos — when he was introduced.

The four-time NBA champion, playing his 24th NBA season at the age of 41, was cheered again when he exited the game late in the fourth quarter.

In between it was a rough night for James and his Sixers teammates, who suffered just their second defeat of the young season.

The league’s all-time leading scorer finished with eight points on three-of-12 shooting with seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers.

Star center Joel Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the floor, making six free throws for six points.

Jaylen Brown, like James an off-season import, led the Sixers with 20 points, but the Cavaliers seized control early and repelled every Philadelphia surge to halt their two-game slide.

Donovan Mitchell scored 10 of his 23 points in the first quarter. Evan Mobley added 22 points, and Cleveland out-rebounded Philadelphia 56-42 despite the injury absence of center Jarrett Allen.

“I did not feel in a good rhythm offensively,” James said. “We didn’t look like much offensively. We had a couple of spurts. We were able to cut (the deficit) to three in the third quarter. But too many turnovers on my behalf.”

Friday’s games were part of NBA Cup group-stage action. The New York Knicks won the in-season tournament last year before going on to win their first NBA title since 1973.

Group-stage Cup games will be played throughout November, all counting in the regular-season standings. Quarter-finals will be played December 4-5 and semi-finals December 8-9 before the final on December 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana.

The Boston Celtics drained a whopping 24 three-pointers on 44 attempts in a 119-80 blowout of the Hornets in Charlotte.

Jayson Tatum, back after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Bucks, drilled five three-pointers on the way to a game-high 34 points for Boston — who led by as many as 46 points in the wire-to-wire win.

“I thought every shot he took was a great shot,” Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla said of Tatum, who added eight rebounds and nine assists.

– Thunder roll past Grizzlies –

The Oklahoma City Thunder continued their dominance of the Grizzlies with a 128-97 win in Memphis.

Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 35 points and two-time defending NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 28 for the Thunder, who notched a 13th straight regular-season win over the Grizzlies despite missing injured starters Jaylen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren.

The absences were irrelevant as the Thunder jumped to a 71-49 halftime lead.

Memphis dropped their third straight defeat after opening the season with six straight wins.

In Dallas, Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving came alive in the second half to help the Mavericks beat the Utah Jazz 112-100.

Dallas forward P.J. Washington scored 22 of his 26 points in a first half that ended tied 57-57.

Flagg, who scored four points before the break, finished with 21 and Irving, held to two points in the first half, finished with 14 as Dallas used a big third quarter to gain control and held on down the stretch.

World.title: Cyberattack shuts down internet fan fiction library
World.content:
Los Angeles – One of the world’s most popular fan fiction libraries has been dark for over a week after a cyberattack forced it offline, leaving millions of fans without access to their favorite stories.

Since October 29, anyone trying to reach Archive of Our Own — known to devotees as AO3 — has been met with a message saying the site is down for maintenance.

“It’s all over my social feed. People are in withdrawal,” Johanna Sarriot, a writer and co-founder of pop-up romance bookstore Love Love Books in Los Angeles, told AFP.

Fan fiction refers to stories written by amateur authors using characters and worlds from already-existing books, films or TV shows.

Contributors rewrite endings, invent romances or give minor characters their own adventures, then share them online for free.

Once a niche hobby, it has become a launchpad for the publishing industry, generating breakout smashes like E.L. James’s “Fifty Shades of Grey,” which began as “Twilight” fan fiction, and Ali Hazelwood’s bestseller “The Love Hypothesis,” which sprang from the “Star Wars” universe.

Launched in 2008, AO3 has become the genre’s main home, with more than 11 million registered users and nearly 18 million works stored on the platform.

In 2019, it won a Hugo Award for Best Related Work, one of science fiction’s most prestigious prizes.

“We wanted to make sure that there was a place for fans to engage in non-commercial creativity in ways that wouldn’t barrage them with ads, censor them to placate advertisers, sell their data, or do anything but provide a space for fandom,” said Harvard Law School professor Rebecca Tushnet, who helped found the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) which runs the site.

– ‘AO3 is not gone’ –

Romance fans have been among the hardest hit by the outage.

“Romance readers read really fast and they read a lot,” explained Sarriot.

For the bookseller, what is at stake goes beyond a website. Fan fiction is where many future authors learn their craft and where readers disover new writers.

“Writers who were able to cut their teeth on fanfiction, and just write as much as they wanted with all the joy and no constraints, can lead to really great novels,” she said.

OTW says it does not believe the user database, which holds usernames, email addresses and encrypted passwords, was stolen, but cannot rule it out.

“AO3 is not gone! There is no data loss and we look forward to restoring the site as soon as possible,” Tushnet added.

The non-profit says it hopes to have things up and running again within a month.

For web developer Yohan Mebrouk, the timeline is a sign of how serious the attack was.

The delay could reflect limited resources, he explained, or the need for a full software upgrade, which he called “an enormous job.”

Well-run sites keep backup copies of their databases, he added. “If they did things right, everyone will get everything back.”

In the meantime, Sarriot is happy to point stranded readers elsewhere.

“Come to Love Love Books and check out a romance novel!” she said, pointing to her shelves full of paperbacks.

World.title: US offers $20 mn reward for info on Iran’s nuclear program
World.content:
Washington – Washington is offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.

A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X.

The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.

It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward.

Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear program.

“If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.”

But the president also said Iran — which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war — is eager to end the conflict.

“We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said.

Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.

And on Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Earlier this week Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

World.title: Skill subject to offer class X Board students a second chance
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Students may no longer have to fear failing the class X board exams as the CBSE has introduced a new rule that not only enhances the relevance of vocational education but also offers students an alternative pathway to pass. From 2027-28, students who fail a core academic subject such as Maths, Science or Social Science, will be allowed to use a passed skill subject as a substitute.This rule is only for students who have opted for one of the 22 skill subjects in class IX under vocational education. This excludes Kaushal Vikas, which is also a skill subject but is assessed internally by schools.Under the revised framework, class IX students will study nine subjects, combining core and skill-based courses. Vocational education includes 22 skill-based subjects, including AI, Data Science, Information Technology, Financial Markets, Automotive, Retail, Design Thinking, and Health Care.Under the NCF-SE, vocational education is mandatory from classes VI to X.A senior CBSE official says the goal is to expand choices for students and promote competency-based, experiential learning by embedding activity-based life skills alongside core academics.Class X students now have two attempts to pass CBSE boards in class X. If a student still cannot clear one core subject, this vocational component provides a cushion to clear class X and move to the next grade.A student who fails a core subject but passes class X through a skill subject can still sit for an improvement examination in the failed subject. CBSE does not have any regulation on which stream the student enrols in class XI as that is the school's discretion."Even if the student passes the boards using skill subject marks, he will have to pass Math or Science to enrol in science stream in class XI," adds the official.Teachers dismiss the idea that the replacement rule will dilute academic rigour, viewing it instead as a constructive stress buster. "This provision will help reduce examination stress, particularly among academically weaker students," says a teacher from PM SHRI KV NER Bareilly.

World.title: Postgraduate doctors quit premier medical institutes, shows RTI reply
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and

, with AIIMS Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025.

While several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents, Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), said multiple RTI applications filed by its members had revealed postgraduate doctors quitting premier medical institutions despite securing top NEET-PG ranks. He cited complaints of duties extending beyond 36 hours, workplace harassment, toxic work culture and inadequate support.



âResidency is meant to train doctors, not break them. Discipline is not humiliation and dedication is not exploitation,â Mittal said, urging authorities to enforce working-hour regulations, establish independent grievance-redressal mechanisms and fix institutional accountability. UDF has also filed a PIL in the Supreme Court.

However, the figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline.





At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025. Department-wise figures show the highest number of exits in anaesthesiology at seven, followed by ophthalmology at six.

Surgery reported three exits, as did pathology. Ophthalmology had recorded 14 exits in 2024.

JIPMER, Puducherry, also reported a decline in resignations.

A combined count of departures from its January and July batches shows 44 residents resigned in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a fall of nearly 27%. However, exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology, emergency medicine, orthopaedics, pathology and surgery.

The trend is not confined to these two institutions. AIIMS Kalyani reported 15 exits across all three years of postgraduate training in 2025, including 13 from the January and July batches.

Another 11 students from the 2026 batches had left by the time of its reply. AIIMS Raipur reported 19 exits from its 2025 batches, AIIMS Patna 12, while AIIMS Gorakhpur also reported departures. At AIIMS Rishikesh, 30 students across various postgraduate and super-speciality programmes left in 2025.

The RTI also sought details of psychiatric counselling and whether stress, depression or sleep deprivation were recorded as reasons for leaving.

AIIMS Delhi said it had no compiled counselling data, while AIIMS Rishikesh reported six postgraduate students receiving psychiatric counselling in 2026 but maintained no consolidated record of workplace-related stress. AIIMS Raipur reported no residents seeking counselling in 2025 or 2026.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

AIIMS Patna reported 15 residents receiving counselling in 2025 and none in 2026, while AIIMS Kalyani declined to provide the information, citing RTI provisions.

The figures are not directly comparable as institutes provided data for different periods and batches. While they establish that residents are leaving, the reasons remain unclear, with several institutes lacking records that could help explain the departures.

World.title: NMC sounds alarm over fake medical colleges, warns students against paying admission fees without verification
World.content:
The NMC has urged students to verify a medical collegeâs approval for the current academic year and avoid fraudulent admission offers, unauthorised agents and forged documents

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned students and parents against falling victim to fake medical colleges, fraudulent admission offers and forged approval documents, following a Supreme Court case involving a purported medical college allegedly operating from a farmhouse.In an advisory, the medical regulator said some institutions were offering medical and allied courses without the requisite statutory approval or recognition. Misleading s, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers could leave students and parents vulnerable to fraud, it cautioned.The warning follows the Supreme Court's intervention in Ayesha Jain vs Amity University, Noida & Others, in which it directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to alert students and parents against enrolling in institutions without first verifying their authenticity.The NMC has specifically cautioned that a college figuring on its official list does not necessarily mean it has permission to admit students for the current academic year. Students must check the college's approval for the relevant year and its sanctioned intake through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board records.It has also advised candidates not to rely on brochures, websites, s or purported Letters of Permission circulated by institutions.Admissions should be pursued through official counselling channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee wherever applicable, or the respective state counselling authorities.The regulator has warned against making payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries. It has also clarified that approval or affiliation from another authority cannot be treated as NMC permission to run an MBBS course.Students can report suspected fake colleges, forged approval letters and fraudulent admission offers to the NMC, state medical education departments or local police.

World.title: ‘She wanted a traditional ceremony’: DMK leader responds to criticism over Vedic rituals at granddaughter’s wedding
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (

The wedding, held on November 1, was officiated by priests and drew prominent political figures and celebrities from across party lines in Tamil Nadu.

âI had to accept my granddaughterâs wish due to her insistence. I regret the incident. No one needs to make this a political issue or turn it into a subject of debate,â the senior DMK leader told reporters on Friday.

He further explained that his granddaughter, who had studied abroad and married a boy from another caste, wanted a traditional wedding ceremony conducted by priests.



Reaffirming his commitment to the partyâs principles, Duraimurugan said his own wedding and that of his son, Kathir Anand, had been solemnised by former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK patriarch M Karunanidhi without such rituals.

K Veeramani, president of the Dravidar Kazhagam movement, had strongly criticised Duraimurugan, arguing that personal choices should not be allowed to "undermine" the rationalist principles on which the Dravidian movement was founded.

World.title: Why can't Congress break free from Gandhi family? Sonia responds to nepotism charge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader

appeared to sidestep questions about the Gandhi family's continued control of the party and allegations of nepotism during an interview with British newspaper The Guardian, saying the question of its leadership should be put to the party itself.

âYou would have to ask the party,â she told the interviewer when asked why the Congress had not moved beyond the Gandhi family's leadership.

The newspaper said Sonia Gandhi âskates over the question of nepotismâ, quoting her response to the charge that the party is controlled by one family. âWe all fight elections: we win them, we lose them. All of us have,â Sonia Gandhi said in a vague answer to nepotism charge.

The interview was published on Saturday, alongside an edited extract from her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", which is due to be released early next week.



Sonia Gandhi âskates over the question of nepotismâ, the newspaper said.

Gandhi grip amid Congress losses

Sonia maintained that the Congress could still emerge as a credible alternative to the BJP. However, the interviewer noted that many people remained unconvinced after the party's repeated electoral defeats.

The article pointed to the Congress's decline under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. After taking over from his mother, Rahul lost the last three general elections to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The party is now in power in only a few states, while the BJP's Hindutva ideology has become the country's dominant political force.





The newspaper observed that the Gandhi family's continued control had made it difficult for the Congress to shake off allegations of nepotism and leadership by political elites.

Sonia was also defensive when asked about the Congress-led

(UPA) government, which remained in power for a decade until 2014, and the controversies surrounding its tenure.

âIn almost every single instance, the ministers resigned,â she said, responding to the criticism.

Sonia calls Emergency a mistake

The conversation also turned to the Emergency imposed by her mother-in-law, former prime minister

, in 1975.

She described the decision as a âmistakeâ and said she believed Indira herself eventually came to feel the same way.

âI know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her,â the ex-Congress president said.

Sonia said the Gandhi family was âsplit on the decisionâ to impose the Emergency.

According to the newspaper's account, her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, opposed the move and advised his mother to wait for the next election. Her younger son, Sanjay Gandhi, reportedly pushed for a tougher response to the Opposition.

At a family dinner, Sanjay is said to have warned Indira that the Opposition would destroy her, telling her, âThey must be stoppedâ. His influence over his mother became a major source of public controversy.

Sonia recalled that the decision âinflamed tensionsâ within the family. Rajiv reportedly tried to confront his mother, but she refused to listen.

âKeeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed,â it quoted from her book.

Recalling the trauma of assassinations

Sonia also spoke about the personal trauma of losing her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, who was assassinated in 1991. She struggled to recall how she carried on after his death, with her daughter Priyanka also joining the conversation at her residence.

She recalled the assassination of Indira Gandhi in 1984, when she heard what sounded like fireworks before seeing her mother-in-law's body covered in blood and bullet wounds. Indira had been shot by two of her bodyguards.

Sonia described trying to revive her as they rushed her to hospital.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThere was blood everywhere, and I realised she wasnât replying to my questions. It seemed as if she had already gone,â she remembered.

She described the journey to the hospital as âexcruciatingâ. Despite the relatively light traffic, the drive seemed painfully slow. She said she knew Indira might already be dead because she was no longer responding.

Sonia also recalled the trauma and depression that followed, saying she lived âlike a ghostâ. The conversation touched on Rajiv's private expression of grief during that difficult period.

World.title: Hands-on inspection: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw buys tea via UPI, interacts with passengers at Anand Vihar Station
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In an unannounced ground check at Anand Vihar Railway Station on Saturday, Union railway minister

stepped onto the platforms to directly interact with festive commuters, gather real-time feedback, and review seasonal travel arrangements.

Connecting with passengers like a common citizen, the minister shared a cup of tea at a station stall and paid digitally using UPI, showcasing the seamless integration of

initiatives at public transit hubs.

During his walk-through of the station, minister Vaishnaw engaged with a wide cross-section of travellers, including women, children, and youth, to assess ground-level amenities.

Passengers shared positive feedback regarding ongoing facility upgrades, cleanliness, and waiting area enhancements implemented by

.



The minister spent time encouraging young travellers and interacting with children, keeping the inspection informal and accessible.

The visit aimed to verify whether high-volume festive management measures were functioning effectively on the platform level.

Addressing the unprecedented passenger volumes during the ongoing festival period, minister Vaishnaw highlighted the scale of operations deployed across the national network.





"This year, around 18,000 special trains have been operated. The benefits are visible. Because of special trains, many passengers can travel. In this Diwali, Pooja and Rush season, more than 2 crore passengers have been able to travel."

With the festive travel cycle reaching its midpoint, railway authorities are bracing for the next phase of heavy passenger movement.

World.title: West Bengal SIR: Fourth retired judge resigns from appeals tribunals, cites ‘personal reasons’
World.content:
Resignations likely to affect disposal of applications in Murshidabad

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Retired Calcutta high court judge Biswajit Basu has resigned from the West Bengal SIR tribunals, becoming the fourth among the 19 retired judges appointed to head the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) panels in the state to step down.Basu communicated his decision to the chief justice of the Calcutta high court through a letter on Friday, citing personal reasons, PTI reported.His resignation follows those of former Calcutta High Court Chief Justice TS Sivagnanam and retired judges Ranjit Kumar Bag and Indrajit Chatterjee.According to an Election Commission (EC) official, Basu and Chatterjee had been assigned to handle cases from the Murshidabad district.Chatterjee had earlier stepped down, citing the difficulty of travelling around 22 km daily to carry out the assignment. He had initially accepted the responsibility believing it would be a temporary arrangement lasting two to three months. However, the large volume of pending cases eventually prompted him to resign.Bag and Sivagnanam had also resigned from the tribunals, citing personal and family reasons.The resignations of the two tribunal members are likely to affect the disposal of appeals in Murshidabad district, where a large number of voters were excluded from the electoral rolls, an EC official said."With both judges stepping down within a month, the disposal of appeals from Murshidabad voters has effectively come to a standstill, raising questions over the tribunal's ability to clear the backlog," the official told PTI.Basu had earlier acknowledged the challenges involved in disposing of a large number of cases, while emphasising that the tribunals were functioning on the directions of the Supreme Court.He had also called for better infrastructure to ensure more effective case disposal."Resolving lakhs of cases in this manner is a little difficult. Since this has been done on the directions of the Supreme Court, it has to be carried out in this manner," he had said.The EC had constituted 19 appellate tribunals for West Bengal in March in compliance with a Supreme Court order. The SIR resulted in the deletion of nearly 91 lakh voters from the state's electoral rolls for various reasons, including "logical discrepancies".The tribunals are hearing appeals filed by lakhs of voters whose names were deleted.

World.title: 'First apologise to devotees, saints': UP CM Yogi ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's Ram Temple visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister

on Saturday said those who had ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge should apologise before visiting the Ram Mandir, taking an apparent swipe at

chief

, who is scheduled to visit the temple on December 12.

Speaking at the 10th edition of Deepotsav in

Ayodhya

, Adityanath said political leaders who had neglected the temple town and insulted its devotees must first acknowledge their past actions.

"Those who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising. Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints.



Let them repent for their actions," news agency PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.

Though he did not name Yadav or the Samajwadi Party, his remarks came hours after former SP MLA Pawan Pandey announced that the party chief and his wife, Dimple Yadav, would visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi on December 12. The visit would be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024.

Adityanath also criticised previous governments for their handling of the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and the firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya.





Recalling the decades-long temple movement, he said the city was now regaining its former glory following the inauguration of the Ram Temple.

"There was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The chief minister also took aim at unnamed political leaders over their conduct at religious gatherings, questioning whether they understood the decorum of a religious discourse.

"Sometimes I am surprised at these people. When they go to a religious discourse, they do not even know the decorum of a katha (religious narration). Is it a katha or a mushaira (Urdu poetry gathering)?" he said.

World.title: DMK flays govt.’s decision to remit money in lieu of distributing rice to ration cardholders in U.T.
World.content:
Convenor of DMK’s Puducherry unit R. Siva has flayed the AINRC-BJP government for adopting the cash transfer mode instead of distributing free rice under the scheme in the Union Territory.

In a statement, the DMK leader said the government had not distributed free rice through ration shops for the last nine months. Now, the government has remitted money into the accounts of ration cardholders in lieu of free rice meant for six months. The amount remitted by the government was based on a calculation of ₹43 per kg for the rice, he said.

However, the cash remitted was not sufficient for buying rice due to cost escalation. The price of rice has gone up substantially in the open market and the money given by the government would be inadequate for the residents to buy the required quantity, he said.

“The government’s decision to adopt Direct Benefit Transfer mode was a betrayal of the mandate given by the people. The Chief Minister had promised the voters to provide rice through ration shops. If the implementation of the scheme to distribute rice through ration shops would take more time, the government should remit more money considering the market rate of rice,” Mr. Siva said.

World.title: Presidency University expels student for allegedly defacing Vivekananda poster
World.content:
KOLKATA

The Presidency University has expelled two students for allegedly defacing Swami Vivekananda posters inside the campus, official sources said. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad had alleged that Left student factions had vandalised the poster and had filed a police complaint on October 14.

The two female students have been barred from taking admission in any course at the university in the future. The university had formed a committee to investigate the matter and has checked CCTV footage of the campus and heard from various stakeholders to come to a decision. One of them is a current student and the other was an ex-student who had finished her post-graduate course a few months back.

“Two students have been expelled from the studentship/post-studentship academic activities. It has also been decided that they won’t be allowed admission to any future degree program in this university,” official sources said.

“Presidency University always stood for dignified academic discourse and debate on different scientific/socio-political issues. The university is not in a position to tolerate any abuse to any thinkers/ideas/organizations,” Presidency University registrar Debajyoti Konar said.

The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) condemned the expulsion on Saturday (November 7, 2026). “By imposing an expulsion that threatens to destroy the academic lives of these two students, the administration has established a deeply dangerous precedent,” their statement from the SFI Presidency unit added. They also said that students must be punished if they took part in vandalism, but asked for corrective steps and rehabilitation, rather than punitive or retaliatory measures.

Meanwhile, the ABVP student wing welcomed the expulsion and said that such “anti-India” sentiments and anti-national conspiracies do not have a place in the educational institutes.

“If such incidents are repeated in the future, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) will once again stand firmly against them. Our message is clear: ABVP possesses the only vaccine capable of eliminating the Chinese virus of anti-national ideology,” Ananta Barui, State Media In-charge, ABVP told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The ABVP student wing had previously alleged that the Left student wings were conducting the vandalism of their posters. However, the Left student wings of Presidency had issued a statement and denied the allegations.

“ABVP has started the work of cleaning the Tukde-Tukde gang from Jadavpur and Presidency. This work must be continued,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said.

This comes as both Jadavpur University and Presidency University, two of the top-ranking educational institutes of the State, remained embroiled in repeated controversies and face-offs with the right-wing student group. A massive fight had erupted at JU in August as left- and right-wing student groups clashed.

World.title: T.N. government to withdraw G.O. promoting Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar as temporary Director of Legal Studies
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Government has informed the Madras High Court of its decision to withdraw a Government Order (G.O.) issued on September 8, 2026, temporarily promoting Tamil Nadu Dr. Ambedkar Law University Registrar Gowri Ramesh as the Director of Legal Studies (DLS). It said, the vacancy shall be filled up through a regular process as contemplated under the Special Rules for the Tamil Nadu Collegiate Educational Service.

Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan recorded the submission made by Advocate General Vijay Narayan and disposed of a writ appeal filed against a single judge’s October 1, 2026 order granting an interim stay of the G.O. The Bench also closed the writ petition pending before the single judge since nothing survived in it pursuant to the government’s decision to withdraw the G.O.

Vellore Government Law College principal M. Rajeswaran had initially filed a writ petition in the High Court in June 2026 challenging a Government Order issued on March 3, 2026 allocating full additional charge of the post of DLS to Ms. Gowri. Then, he had contended that a full-time Registrar of the Law University could not be given additional charge of the full time post of DLS too and that it was against the service rules.

The petitioner contended that the vacancy in the post of DLS could be filled up only through direct recruitment, transfer or by promoting those holding the post of principal in any of the government law colleges spread across the State. Stating that he was senior to Ms. Gowri, the petitioner had wondered how could she attend the Syndicate meetings in her ex-officio capacity as the Registrar of the university and also as the DLS.

Justice P.T. Asha had entertained that writ petition on June 30, 2026 and stayed the operation of the March 3, 2026 G.O. When that stay order was taken on appeal by the State, the A-G told the first Division Bench that the State government intends to commence the regular process of appointing the DLS in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules and complete it within a period of two months.

The Bench disposed of the writ appeal on July 23, 2026 after taking note that the government had also issued a G.O. on July 21, 2026 giving full additional charge of the post of DLS to a joint secretary in the Law department instead of Ms. Gowri.

Thereafter, the September 8, 2026 G.O. was issued temporarily promoting Ms. Gowri as the DLS by invoking the emergency powers conferred on the government under Section 47(1) of Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016. Hence, Mr. Rajeswaran had filed yet another writ petition in the High Court on September 29, 2026 challenging the latest G.O.

This time, Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar stayed the September 8, 2026 G.O. on the ground that the government ought not to have invoked Section 47(1) of the 2016 Act after having given an undertaking before the Division Bench in July 2026 that the post of DLS would be appointed in accordance with Rule 2(a) of the Special Rules.

When a State appeal against this stay order came up before the first Bench, the latter recorded A-G’s submission that the latest G.O. shall be withdrawn. “The State shall pursue with the promotion process in accordance with law. The statement of Advocate General that in the meantime, the State will take steps to fill up the post temporarily, as was done when the earlier writ appeal was disposed of, is recorded,” the Bench said.

World.title: Locals burn effigy of Christian priests at Basanti in WB
World.content:
A group of locals at Basanti in West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas on Thursday (November 5, 2026) burnt effigy of local Christian priests and submitted a memorandum to the police station against the local priests. Basanti has been on the boil since November 1 after a newly constructed church was vandalised by a mob claiming their allegiance to a Hindutva outfit.

The protest on Thursday (November 5, 2026) was organised by Adivasi Eilya Parishad, a local organisation whose representatives said that Adivasis are being lured for conversion on the promise of curing disease, which should not be allowed.

The West Bengal chapter of National Christian Council (NCC) in a press statement added that effigy of local priests were set on fire at Chowmatha crossing in Basanti.

“Later in the evening, during the Friday prayer service, a group of approximately 20–25 people allegedly surrounded women attending the service. According to the complaints received, the women were forced to break their traditional conch-shell bangles (Shakha) and wipe off their vermilion (Sindoor),” the press statement said.

Father Parimal Kanji, the priest-in-charge at Basanti, stated that the alleged perpetrators were outsiders and not local residents and confirmed that a written complaint had been submitted to the police.

Arpan Rana, State General Secretary of the National Christian Council said that Christian communities in West Bengal do not seek confrontation but justice, equal protection and the rule of law. “The Chief Minister is speaking about religious freedom, yet the practical experience of some minority communities raises serious questions about their safety and protection,” Mr. Rana said.

Herod Mullick, the founding State Secretary of Bangiya Chrisityo Pariseba said that the government and administration’s silence has emboldened attackers, who have shifted from targeting small independent congregations to raiding older, established churches.

“While the police are well aware of the situation and continue to accept written complaints, no legal action is mysteriously being taken against anyone, making the government’s ongoing silence both baffling and suspicious,” he said.

According to Basanti Police Station, an FIR has been registered in connection with the incident of attack on the Church and notices have been issued to some accused.

There has been an increase in attacks on churches and Christian gatherings after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power. According to Christian organisations, U.S.-based research project, India Hate Lab, has documented at least 60 incidents of hate crimes and targeted attacks against Christians in West Bengal across 13 districts between May 13 and September 20 this year.

Earlier this week, a public hearing of survivors of the mob attacks was held in Kolkata where people from several districts participated and shared their experience.

World.title: Providing clean air govt’s responsibility, citizen’s participation important: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
World.content:
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday (November 7, 2026) appealed to the citizens of Delhi to celebrate Deepavali in an eco-friendly and safe manner and urged them to use green firecrackers as per norms and celebrate with diyas, rangoli, sweets and mutual harmony. She said that providing clean air is the government’s responsibility, and citizen participation is equally important for it.

Ms. Gutpa said that Delhi is her family, and ensuring a better life, secure future, and dignity for every member of this family is her government’s highest priority.

“We are continuously moving forward towards building a Viksit Delhi (Developed Delhi). Our endeavour is to ensure that the benefits of development reach the last person in society, making Delhi a leading capital of the country equipped with modern amenities, a clean environment, better infrastructure, and economic opportunities,” Ms. Gupta said.

The CM said that the government’s aim is to connect every area of Delhi to the mainstream of development, provide youth with better education and employment opportunities, and offer every citizen a safe, clean, and convenient life. “We aim to build a Delhi where environmental conservation accompanies development, heritage blends with modernity, and social equality coexists with prosperity,” she said.

Ms. Gupta said the people of Delhi will celebrate Deepavali together at ‘Jugmug Diwali’ at Central Park in Connaught Place with drone show and diyas.

World.title: NDA extends winning streak, set to crush YSRCP in ZPTC and MPTC elections as well
World.content:
The TDP and its allies, the JSP and the BJP, continued their stellar performance in the elections to the Zilla and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs and MPTCs) after crushing the YSRCP in the Urban Local Body (ULB) polls. They were all set to pull off another decisive victory over the YSRCP.

Polling was conducted for 582 ZPTCs and 7,767 MPTCs in 28 districts on November 5 following the declaration of 77 and 2,051 ZPTCs and MPTCs respectively as unanimously elected.

As per information furnished by the State Election Commission (SEC) at 9 p.m. on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the TDP won a total of 229 ZPTCs, including 71 unanimous and 158 contested, JSP 36 (2 unanimous and 34 contested) and BJP 8 (three unanimous and 5 contested), whereas the YSRCP managed to win 20 (one unanimous and 19 contested).

In the MPTCs, the TDP won 4,823 (1,780 unanimous and 3,043 conttested), JSP 644 (107 unanimous and 537 contested), the BJP 130 (53 unanimous and 77 contested) and YSRCP 1,050 (89 unanimous and 961 contested).

State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha stated in a press release that the counting process was still underway and progressing peacefully.

The TDP won most of the ZPTCs and MPTCs in Kadapa district, which had been the stronghold of the YSRCP.

After scoring an impressive victory in the elections to the Pulivendula Municipality, the TDP won the Pulivendula ZPTC also, causing a major upset to the YSRCP, which apparently lost the confidence of the people in what had been the stronghold of the Y.S. Rajasekhar Reddy family.

The TDP was in the driver’s seat in the ZPTC seat of Kuppam (Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s home turf) and in a vast majority of the other ZPTCs, and MPTCs in Chittoor and Annamayya districts.

Reacting to the results that were coming in, IT Minister Nara Lokesh described the TDP-led coalition’s overwhelming triumph in the ZPTC and MPTC elections as the “fruits of their good governance and proof of the perfect coordination among the ruling parties.”

TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Rao said the mood was overwhelmingly in favour of his party and its allies due to their good governance, and it was a profound mandate for welfare, development and social justice.

The results were a testament to the trust placed by the electorate in Mr. Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, and the BJP State leadership, he asserted.

A BJP spokesman said the large number of votes, which the party got, proved that the people believed in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.

Meanwhile, YSRCP leaders alleged that the counting of votes polled in the ZPTCs and MPTCs was fraught with irregularities and the SEC’s response to their complaints was untimely.

World.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
World.content:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh visited members of the armed forces at multiple locations in West Bengal on Saturday (November 7, 2026) and highlighted a changing nature of warfare while describing the northeast as India’s “first edge” rather than its “last edge”.

The security landscape around the country has become increasingly complex and the armed forces must maintain the highest level of operational readiness to effectively counter any threats to national security, he told personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station. Delivering his message on the eve of Deepavali from the key airbase near the frontier with China in the Eastern sector, Mr. Singh, without naming any country, said the adversary now avoids direct confrontation but seeks to exploit certain "vulnerabilities".

He called upon the armed forces to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats, according to the Defence Ministry. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma, and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, Mr. Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence personnel towards safeguarding national interests. He stated that the Air Force personnel deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.

The Defence Minister later reviewed the operational preparedness of the Army’s Trishakti Corps at Sukna, with a focus on infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), deployment of advanced military equipment, and adoption of emerging technologies to enhance combat effectiveness.

Mr. Singh expressed satisfaction with the operational preparedness of the corps and appreciated its contribution to infrastructure development and community welfare initiatives in border areas aimed at strengthening ties with local communities.

Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth, Eastern Army Commander Lt. Gen. VMB Krishnan and Trishakti Corps Commander Lt. Gen. Man Raj Singh Mann were present during the review.

Addressing personnel during a ‘barakhana’ on the eve of Deepawali, Mr. Singh commended their courage, professionalism, and dedication in safeguarding the country’s frontiers under challenging operational conditions.

Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, he said security challenges were no longer confined to conventional exchanges of gunfire and artillery but increasingly involved hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyberattacks, drone incursions, and information warfare.

He cautioned that adversaries were using social media to spread rumours, deploying drones to monitor sensitive locations, and attempting to compromise military systems through cyberattacks. He exhorted personnel to remain vigilant and prepared to tackle emerging threats across all domains.

Describing Sukna as a critical logistics hub for eastern India, Mr. Singh said its geographical sensitivity necessitated round-the-clock operational readiness. He highlighted its importance in the movement of supplies, weapons, food, medical provisions, and personnel to forward locations.

The Defence Minister said budgetary allocations for roads, tunnels, border infrastructure, and modern equipment had been increased as the country progressed towards self-reliance in defence production.

He noted that Indian start-ups and industries were manufacturing drones and anti-drone systems, while the armed forces were increasingly embracing emerging technologies and training in drone operations and cybersecurity.

Mr. Singh also stressed the importance of soldiers’ mental health and emotional well-being, urging them to communicate openly with their colleagues and seek support to deal with stress arising from demanding duties and separation from families.
